[[Lin Shouyi]] |Enemie(s) = Daoist second disciple |Occupation = Swordsman |Former_affiliation(s) = [[Sword Qi Great Wall]] |Cultivation_rank = Peak 13th Tier (on ascending) |Novel = Chapter 88 |Donghua = S2 Ep.1 }} '''A'Liang''' is a swordsman who spent a century at the Sword Qi Great Wall. He is an old friend of the [[Scholarly Sage]] and his disciples, and he escorted [[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]] and the children of the small town on part of their journey to Mountain Cliff Academy. == Appearance == A'Liang looks unremarkable. He wears a conical bamboo hat even when there is no sun or rain, carries a slender saber in a green bamboo scabbard, and keeps an old silver wine gourd at his waist. He travels with a white donkey that he never rides.Chapter 88 The bamboo hat hides his aura, since without it he would draw far too much attention.Chapter 112 == Personality == A'Liang is boastful, playful and lazy about small matters. He jokes constantly, teases the children, and gets annoyed when Chen Ping'an compares him to Zhu He.Chapter 93 Cui Chan noted that unlike scholars, A'Liang never boasted, meaning his wild claims after each battle were simply true.Chapter 161 Behind the joking he is watchful and principled. He tested Chen Ping'an from their first meeting at Dragon Whisker Creek to see what kind of person he was.Chapter 111 He told the children that a strong person's freedom ends where a weak person's freedom begins. He is fiercely loyal to Qi Jingchun and grew furious with anyone who used his friend's name as a shield.Chapter 114 == Background == A'Liang met the Scholarly Sage before Cui Chan did. He first meant to beat the old scholar up but was talked round, and the two became close friends. Among the old scholar's disciples he was closest to Cui Chan, Qi Jingchun and Zuo You, and he fought many great battles for Qi Jingchun and Zuo You. Angered by how the Confucian schools treated the Scholarly Sage, he forced his way into two of them, then crossed two continents and passed Stalactite Mountain to reach the Sword Qi Great Wall.Chapter 115 He honed his sword there for a hundred years, never losing to the great demons of the Upper Five Tiers.Chapter 350 He often ventured deep into Savage World alone to fight its great demons. He came to be known as the one who had killed the most demons at the Great Wall.Chapter 189 In Savage World he also befriended Liu Cha, who tried to give him his sword.Chapter 626 A'Liang sought out Wei Jin of Wind Snow Temple and taught him the sword. Wei Jin gave him the white donkey and the sword nurturing gourd.Chapter 649 He arrived near the small town after Qi Jingchun's death, spoke the town's dialect, and agreed to lead Chen Ping'an, Li Baoping, Li Huai, Lin Shouyi, Zhu He and Zhu Lu south. He told Chen Ping'an that the hairpin Qi Jingchun gave him came from Qi Jingchun's teacher and was a token of their lineage.Chapter 91 At Go Table Mountain he shared out a box of treasures among the group, first come first served.Chapter 104 At Pillow Relay Station he dealt with Zhu He and Zhu Lu after they turned on the group, leaving the donkey, the gourd and other gifts to the children before parting. He then went to the Great Li capital, struck the replica White Jade Capital with his saber, and confronted Song Zhengchun, Luan Changye and Cui Chan. He left his saber, Auspicious Talisman, with the emperor to be returned to Li Baoping. When called from the heavens, his aura rose from the peak of the 12th Tier to the peak of the 13th Tier, and he broke through the sky to fight there. A'Liang had come for a sword that chose Chen Ping'an instead, and before parting he told the boy he expected him to become strong enough to carve characters at the Great Wall someday.Chapter 190 == Trivia == * He introduces himself with the line "Liang as in kindness".Chapter 189 * He taught Chen Ping'an the Eighteen Stops, a breathing technique he had refined himself. * He spent over a hundred years pestering Yin Chen at the Great Wall and boasted of winning more than eight hundred arguments with him.Chapter 650 * Chen Qingdu said A'Liang hoped Wei Jin and others on the same path would one day stand beside him. == References ==

pages.title: Azure Phoenix Nation
pages.content:
The '''Azure Phoenix Nation''' is a nation in the southeastern region of [[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]], ruled by the Imperial Tang Clan. Small by the continent's standards but wealthy and proud, it is known for its many Daoist and Buddhist temples and for the grand debate between Buddhism and Daoism that its emperor staged in the capital. [[Chen Ping An]] passed through it with [[Pei Qian]] after leaving Old Dragon City, and the [[Great Li Empire]] quietly drew it into its plans for the continent.

== Geography ==
The nation lies in the southeast of the continent. Old Dragon City runs a louchuan route to its border.Chapter 373 On that border stands Wasp Tail Ferry Station, a former small town where the Azure Phoenix Nation, Fortune Mountain Nation and Lofty Sky Nation meet. The Imperial Tang Clan has fought its two neighbors over the town for centuries, with both brush and blade. The capital lies around eight hundred kilometers from the ferry station.Chapter 374 A second, slightly larger immortal ferry station sits in the east, with routes to nearby immortal abodes and to the Fishing Platform in the north, where travelers cast lines into a sea of clouds.Chapter 398

The nation borders the lands of the Cloud Forest Jiang Clan. Of the three nations around Wasp Tail Ferry Station it is the strongest, but it is still a minor power when set against the whole continent.Chapter 390

== History ==
The Imperial Tang Clan founded the nation with the help of an earth immortal who called himself Wei Qian. The founding emperor raised pagodas and commissioned portraits for twenty four founding ministers. Wei Qian was ranked low among them, yet he outlived the other twenty three and all their great-great-grandchildren, simply changing his name to Wei Liang.Chapter 399 The founding emperor also named an ancient apricot tree near Wasp Tail Ferry Station the Emperor Tree.

For several hundred years the nation stayed calm, with none of its distant governors or nobles ever rising against the throne.Chapter 376 While war raged across the central region of the continent, tens of thousands of nobles and scholars fled south, and the Azure Phoenix Nation took in more of them than any of its neighbors.

After the Azure Phoenix Nation held a Liberation Rite of Water and Land, its two neighbors answered by holding Heavenly Worship Ceremonies at the same time. Emperor Tang Li responded by announcing a debate between Buddhism and Daoism, with the winner to become the national religion ranked above Confucianism. The debate drew cultivators, scholars and nobles from across the southeast and made the nation the region's main topic.Chapter 389. Scholars who had fled south were furious that Confucianism had been left out. In the end Tang Li named Confucianism the nation's fundamental teaching and left Buddhism and Daoism to settle second and third place. The little-known White Cloud Temple became a royal Daoist temple, and a young monk from White Water Temple began preaching in the streets.

== Government ==
The emperor gives out royal titles without lands. Kings and county kings live in residences in the capital that they may use but do not own, and they lose them along with the title. Five chief military governor offices, in the north, south, east, west and center, handle grain transport, salt and iron, and other vital affairs. The four outer governors earned their posts through military service. The central office has always been held by Wei Liang, who keeps his power hidden and is the one figure the clan's chief guest elder, Zhou Lingzhi, truly fears.Chapter 396

Unlike most courts on the continent, the Imperial Tang Clan deals firmly with the immortals of the mountains and never raises up immortal forces without reason. The emperor sorts out disputes between the two worlds himself.

== Religion ==
The nation has more Buddhist monasteries than any other on the continent, where Buddhism is otherwise rare. Daoist immortals and eminent monks hold court-funded Liberation Rites of Water and Land and Heavenly Worship Ceremonies there, and the walls of the monasteries are covered in the writing of famous scholars and poets. White Water Temple, more than a thousand years old, has a spring famed for brewing tea, while the monks of North Mountain Temple are the most active at court.Chapter 378

== Relationship with the Great Li Empire ==
The Great Li Empire had planted a spy holding a second-rank Peace and Safety Tablet in the nation long before the debate, a sign that it meant to take the Azure Phoenix Nation. [[Cui Chan]] came in person and met Wei Liang first. After hearing the empire's plans, Wei Liang agreed to cooperate. Great Li agents then tried to ruin the retired assistant minister Liu Jingting of the Lion Garden so that he could not unite the scholars who had fled south.Chapter 406 The scheme eventually succeeded, and the migrant clans fell to quarreling over who should lead them.Chapter 414

Li Baozhen of the Green Ripple Pavilion chose the nation as the base for his career. Afterward he used its scholars, officials and martial artists as pieces in an experiment at the grassroots, while Wei Liang watched and set rules that even Li Baozhen had to follow. During this period the nation seemed to be entering a golden age.Chapter 535 Later the Great Li court rated the nation's grain waterway project and moved Liu Qingfeng to a border prefecture, and it seemed ready to promote Wei Liang. Once a remote backwater, the nation had become a place rich in prospects for officials.Chapter 652

== Trivia ==
* Its blue sandalwood Xuan paper is sold on several continents and has made its emperors some of the richest rulers in the southeast.
* Cui Dongshan revealed the nation's martial fortune at a county martial sage temple. One drop of golden rain fell every fifteen minutes, which he judged better than several nations he had seen but far short of the old Lu Empire.Chapter 381
* An earth bull equal to a Dragon Gate Tier cultivator hid in its mountains for more than two hundred years before cultivators tried to kill it.Chapter 375
* Cui Dongshan told Chen Ping'an to try two dishes in the capital, Buddha's Temptation and bittern flapjack. Chen Ping'an bought Pei Qian a sparrowhawk kite, a local specialty.
* People there are known for being especially proud of their nation.

pages.content:
{{Character |header1=Bai Shou |Vital_status=Alive |Gender=Male |Species=Human |Master(s)=[[Qi Jinglong]] |Friend(s)=[[Chen Ping An]]
Xu Xingjiu
[[Pei Qian]] |Occupation=Assassin (former)
Disciple of the Great Emblem Sword Sect |Current_affiliation(s)=Great Emblem Sword Sect |Former_affiliation(s)=Deer Cutter Mountain |Continent=[[Northern Complete Reed Continent]] |Novel=Chapter 536 }} == Appearance == As an assassin of Deer Cutter Mountain, Bai Shou dressed in a black robe and wore a white mask to conceal his identity, a disguise he cast aside the moment his cover was blown.Chapter 536 == Personality == He is brash, boastful, and quick to talk himself up, declaring within moments of meeting Chen Ping’an that he would become a renowned sword immortal within a hundred years.Chapter 536 Underneath the bluster he is fiercely loyal to the one master he considers his true master, the mountain lord who raised him, and he refuses to recognize Qi Jinglong as a real replacement even while grudgingly obeying him.Chapter 539 He has a habit of complaining about nearly everything, from cramped lodgings to his master’s moralizing, yet he quietly keeps a sharp assassin’s vigilance running under his lazy, bored exterior whenever there might be real danger nearby.Chapter 596 He is not actually interested in chasing women despite his claims, simply enjoying being liked.Chapter 596 == Background == Bai Shou grew up at Deer Cutter Mountain, a faceless order of assassins with no fixed base and a strict code of rules, trained from a young age at the side of its mountain master and treated as a promising prospect because of his natural aptitude with the sword.Chapter 536 When his master was sent to kill Chen Ping’an and failed to break through Qi Jinglong’s defenses after being allowed two free strikes, an agreement was struck that Deer Cutter Mountain would send its young prodigy to make one final, face-saving assassination attempt. Bai Shou was that prodigy, and when Chen Ping’an caught him lying in wait in a reed thicket, his attempt failed, binding him by the agreement to become Qi Jinglong’s disciple and leave Deer Cutter Mountain behind for good.Chapter 536 He resented the arrangement bitterly at first, mocking Qi Jinglong’s lectures and insisting he would only ever recognize his old master from Deer Cutter Mountain, even as he grudgingly accepted that his old master had likely engineered the whole situation for his own benefit.Chapter 539 He grew to respect his new life more over time, becoming an official disciple of the Great Emblem Sword Sect and receiving a small cottage of his own on the sect grounds, though he still complained that it was far less luxurious than he had expected of a renowned sword immortal’s residence.Chapter 549 Bai Shou traveled with Qi Jinglong to Stalactite Mountain aboard Osmanthus Island, posing as a scholar’s attendant while secretly keeping watch for danger out of old habit. During the trip, Qi Jinglong arranged to request a Sword Nurturing Gourd from the Spring Banner Inn as a disciple-recruiting gift for him, a treasure so rare that even many sword immortals never owned one.Chapter 595 He also grew noticeably more composed in the presence of senior figures of the sect after an encounter with the ancestral hall’s disciplinary elder, Huang Tong, even if he remained prone to blurting out embarrassing truths about his friend Chen Ping’an’s drinking habits.Chapter 596 When Qi Jinglong emerged from seclusion to face three formidable challengers, Li Cai, Dong Zhu, and Bai Shang, Bai Shou welcomed Chen Ping’an to the Great Emblem Sword Sect in his master’s stead, since Qi Jinglong was occupied receiving a stream of guests and visitors. He delighted in recounting how Qi Jinglong had been forced to turn away most callers, teasing Chen Ping’an about a visit from his acquaintance Xu Xingjiu, who had brought homemade wine all the way from Cloudtop City.Chapter 562 == Trivia == * He has a rivalry of sorts with Pei Qian, Chen Ping’an’s disciple, after being thoroughly embarrassed by her in a sparring match on Downtrodden Mountain, something he has never quite lived down.Chapter 595 * He was unaware for some time that his master’s birth surname was Qi rather than Liu, picking up the truth only through rumors at the sect.Chapter 595 * Despite his complaints, he was given the chance to request a Sword Nurturing Gourd of his own, a gift few disciples of any sect could expect so early in their cultivation.Chapter 595 == References ==

pages.title: Bamboo Scroll Lake
pages.content:
{{Spoilers}}
The '''Bamboo Scroll Lake''' is a vast lake in the central region of [[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]], dotted with roughly a thousand islands and rich in spiritual energy. For centuries it was a lawless haven for vagrant cultivators, ruled by force rather than by any nation or sect. It is where [[Liu Zhimao]] took [[Gu Can]] and his mother, and where [[Chen Ping An]] spent about three years trying to deal with what Gu Can had become. After the [[Great Li Empire]] seized the region, the lake became the seat of the True Realm Sect, the Jade Tablet Sect's lower sect on the continent.

== Geography ==
The lake holds about a thousand islands of every size, scattered across the water like stars. Around half of them are owned or rented by Qi refiners, and Cyan Gorge Island, the base of Liu Zhimao, is the largest.Chapter 206 Its abundant spiritual energy makes the bigger islands ideal private abodes for one or two Golden Core Tier cultivators, especially those with an affinity for water.Chapter 427

The lake lies south of the Stone Brush Nation. Travelers from the north have to cross that nation and pass the Thousand Bird Border Pass to reach it. It also borders the [[Luminous Vermilion Empire]], which made it a prize that both the Great Li Empire and the Luminous Vermilion Empire wanted.Chapter 428 The wider central region is overseen by Lake View Academy.Chapter 431

Four major cities stand on its shores. Pond Water City sits on the western bank and is the third largest of them. Green Parasol City lies near Hibiscus Mountain, an outlying island known across the region for Hibiscus Stone, a prized material for carving seals.Chapter 434 Cloud Pagoda City is also on the lakeshore. Beyond the lake to the south lies a stretch of mountains full of miasma, spirits and evil cultivators.

Three foundational water veins carry most of the lake's water fortune. Palace Willow Island owns one outright, Cyan Gorge Island holds most of a second, and Azure Mound Island, Heavenly Governess Island and Millet Grain Island share the third. Countless smaller branch veins are claimed by the remaining islands.Chapter 456

Autumn and winter bring thick mists and winter mirages.Chapter 437 Locals count rain, snow and dew as "rootless water", so a heavy snowfall is welcomed because it raises the lake's spiritual energy.

== History ==
=== Origins ===
The lake was once an ordinary place with little spiritual energy. That changed when a traveling Confucian sage from the [[Middle Earth Divine Continent]] attained the Great Dao there. The resonance between heaven and earth turned the lake into a blessed land.

=== Era of the island masters ===
The lake never had a lasting ruler. The most powerful native cultivator in its history was Liu Laocheng of Palace Willow Island. After he reached the Upper Five Tiers he was entitled to found a sect, but instead he installed a female cultivator close to him as "ruler of the cultivation world" and left the lake. After she died, Palace Willow Island was left to fall into ruin, and the lake split back into feuding islands.

The islanders guarded that independence fiercely. Once an official Nascent Tier cultivator and a Golden Core Tier sword cultivator held a banquet on one of the islands, declaring themselves the lake's new leaders. The island masters all praised them at the table, then joined forces and killed both of them with close to nine hundred immortal treasures and two hundred cultivators sent to their deaths. Locals still told the story with pride centuries later.

=== Rise of Cyan Gorge Island ===
Liu Zhimao, the River Severing True Lord, built Cyan Gorge Island into the strongest force on the lake. He took Gu Can and his mother there from the small town, and in return [[Qi Jingchun]] barred him from leaving the lake for thirty years.Chapter 24 Gu Can's flood dragon, Tan Xue, killed and devoured cultivators across the islands. After it massacred an entire sect, Cyan Gorge Island became the unofficial leader of every island on the lake.Chapter 304

=== The election and Chen Ping'an's stay ===
When Liu Zhimao seemed close to uniting the lake, around a hundred island masters gathered on Palace Willow Island to elect a new ruler. Behind the scenes, the Great Li Empire had long since infiltrated the region, and [[Cui Chan]] treated the lake as a board on which to test Chen Ping'an. Chen Ping'an arrived around the autumnal equinox and took a post as an honorary elder of Cyan Gorge Island. He read the chronicles and genealogies of the islands and visited them one by one.

Liu Laocheng secretly came back to the lake. He then attacked Cyan Gorge Island and crushed Tan Xue in the waters off its shore, but he spared Gu Can and Chen Ping'an. Liu Zhimao won the title of ruler, yet Liu Laocheng refused to let even that title stand. He declared that the lake would no longer have a ruler at all.Chapter 442 To bargain with Liu Laocheng, Chen Ping'an used a sage's jade tablet to start draining the lake's spiritual energy and water fortune, forcing him to the table.Chapter 444

=== Conquest by the Great Li Empire ===
Great General Su Gaoshan of the Great Li Empire then came to the lake and threw his whip into its water. He gave every vagrant cultivator a choice. They could give up everything they owned and leave, or hand over half and serve with his army. Anyone who refused within ten days would die. Liu Laocheng and a group of outside cultivators staying on Palace Willow Island stormed Cyan Gorge Island and locked Liu Zhimao in a water prison beneath Palace Willow Island.Chapter 452 Island after island surrendered half its wealth and its genealogical records. After that, anyone entering the lake needed a passport, and the Great Li general Guan Yiran held more sway there than Liu Zhimao ever had.

=== The True Realm Sect ===
It later became known that the Jade Tablet Sect of Parasol Leaf Continent had chosen the lake as the site of its lower sect. The new True Realm Sect named Liu Laocheng its chief guest elder and took on Liu Zhimao as a guest elder too. Under Liu Zhimao's restructuring, many islands grew stronger and wealthier. Many former vagrant cultivators also found themselves official immortals of a sect-level force, and the continent's most lawless region turned orderly almost overnight.Chapter 530

The sect built its ancestral hall on Palace Willow Island. When Jiang Shangzhen returned to lead the Jade Tablet Sect, Sword Immortal Wei Ying became the new sect leader. The lake then settled into three camps, with Liu Laocheng leading its old powers.Chapter 642

== Culture ==
Under the old order there was no line between good and evil cultivators, only strength and cunning. People drove out of other places often came to the lake to start over, and the only rule that held was paying the agreed price for breaking a rule. Grudges were expected to end with the enemy wiped out completely, sometimes along with the whole island.

The local dialect differs from the continent's official language, though the official dialect of the Luminous Vermilion Empire is widely understood. The lake is famous for crow caw wine, golden garb crabs (the rarest breed is called the bamboo branch), and shredded whitebait. Liu Laocheng named three of its fish as banquet delicacies in the Luminous Vermilion Empire. One of them, the winter carp, tastes best in the coldest, snowiest weather.Chapter 445 News travels through reports sold by Willow Catkin Island, whose cultivators make their living gathering information.

== Trivia ==
* Early chapters call it Lake Shujian, which literally means a letter.
* The lake's nicknames for Gu Can included "Little Devil Gu" and "Prince of the Lake". He and his friends called themselves the Ten Heroes of Bamboo Scroll Lake even though there were only nine of them.
* According to Gu Can, the longest election for ruler dragged on for almost half a year. The shortest ended within a month, when one island master killed more than twenty of the others in anger and his wife was elected that same day. She was the only woman ever to hold the title.
* In late spring, an old man cast twenty-four bamboo slips into the lake, one for each solar term. Only Jiang Shangzhen, Liu Laocheng and Zhou Fenglu sensed it, and none of them could find him.
* Jiang Shangzhen offered Downtrodden Mountain six islands on the edge of the lake as a gift.

pages.title: Blessed Lands
pages.content:
Blessed lands are significant locations in the narrative, often described as places of abundant spiritual energy and unique opportunities for cultivation.

'''Definition and Nature''':

* Blessed lands are territories with high concentrations of spiritual energy, making them ideal for cultivation.Chapter 249
* They can arise from various sources, including shattered small worlds,Chapter 37 ancient battlefields, or natural formations.
* Some blessed lands are connected to other small worlds, which makes them unique compared to other blessed lands.
* They are considered independent and are often compared to subsidiary nations.
* The sources also describe blessed lands as being like a "small world" or "mystical realm".
* They are not necessarily places of good fortune, and may be dangerous.

'''Formation and Origins''':

* Blessed lands can form when small worlds shatter and fall to earth.Chapter 73
* They can also be created from ancient ruins or battlefields, which are imbued with spiritual energy.
* Some blessed lands may form naturally due to unique environmental conditions.
* They can be the result of unique geography or the presence of powerful natural elements.

'''Types of Blessed Lands''':

* Some blessed lands, like the '''Limpid Pond Blessed Land''', are considered lower quality, while others, such as the '''Cloud Cave Blessed Land''', are considered high-quality.
* The '''Golden Millet Blessed Land''' is unique in that it can reflect one's Dao heart, and it was once a bustling world filled with beautiful people and scenes.
* '''Lotus Flower Blessed Land''' is a medium-grade blessed land known for producing many martial arts prodigies.Chapter 319
* There are also unique blessed lands that form in the human body.

'''Significance for Cultivation''':

* Blessed lands offer a conducive environment for cultivation, as they are brimming with spiritual energy, which is essential for Qi refiners.
* They often contain rare herbs, creatures, and treasures that can greatly enhance cultivation.
* Prodigious figures often come from these blessed lands, and are usually claimed by whichever nation or sect owns the land.
* Some blessed lands are connected to other small worlds, providing unique opportunities for cultivation and growth.
* Cultivating in a blessed land can provide a geographic advantage to a cultivator.
* The quality of a blessed land can greatly influence a cultivator's progress, with higher quality blessed lands providing more resources and opportunities.
* Some blessed lands may have different laws of the Heavenly Dao, which can also impact the resources that are available and how they are used.

'''Fated Opportunities''':

* Blessed lands are often associated with fated opportunities, where cultivators may find rare treasures or insights that can lead to rapid advancement.
* These opportunities can vary greatly, from rare items to opportunities for enlightenment.
* It is said that the best fated opportunities are those that can be grabbed, withstood, and digested.
* Some blessed lands are said to be more likely to give fated opportunities to those who are lucky, while others may provide opportunities based on an individual's ability and perseverance.
* Some blessed lands are said to offer insights into the true nature of one's heart and soul.

'''Control and Ownership''':

* Blessed lands are often controlled by powerful immortal clans or sects.Chapter 129Chapter 360
* Some blessed lands are claimed by nations or empires, who may use them as a source of wealth and influence.
* The control of a blessed land can be a major source of power and wealth.
* Those with control of a blessed land may receive passive benefits without any effort on their part.
* Some blessed lands are open to the public for a fee, while others may be restricted to certain individuals or groups.

'''Challenges and Limitations''':

* Entering blessed lands can be dangerous, and not everyone who enters them will obtain a fated opportunity.
* Blessed lands that are open to the public may have a high turnover rate and may be seen as places to spend money for entertainment rather than as places for serious cultivation.Chapter 67
* Some blessed lands may be damaged or incomplete, which can limit the benefits that they can offer.
* The laws of the Heavenly Dao may differ in blessed lands, which can make them unpredictable and dangerous.
* Some blessed lands may be guarded by powerful entities, making it dangerous for inexperienced cultivators to explore them.
* The flow of time may also differ in blessed lands, which can make it difficult to gauge the amount of time that has passed.

'''Examples of Blessed Lands''':

* '''Jewel Small World''' (now called '''Jewel Blessed Land'''): A former small world that fell to earth and became a blessed land, though its spiritual energy dropped sharply in the process.Chapter 75
* '''Limpid Pond Blessed Land''': A low-quality blessed land controlled by the Divine Edict Sect.
* '''Cloud Cave Blessed Land''': A high-quality blessed land controlled by the Jiang Clan of the Jade Tablet Sect.
* '''Golden Millet Blessed Land''': A blessed land that can reflect one's Dao heart. Only its remnants are left now, and drinking its Forgetting Sorrow Wine has become a stop cultivators make a point of visiting.Chapter 628
* '''Lotus Flower Blessed Land''': A medium-grade blessed land that produces many martial arts prodigies.
* '''Ascending True Immortal Mystical Realm''': Not itself one of the 72 blessed lands, but a damaged mystical realm derived from one of them, still able to rival Jewel Small World in size.Chapter 286

Blessed lands are crucial locations in the narrative that offer both opportunities and challenges for cultivators. They are places of intense spiritual energy, rare resources, and unique fated opportunities, but they can also be dangerous and unpredictable. Control over a blessed land is often a major source of power and wealth, making them central to many conflicts and ambitions. Understanding the nature and significance of blessed lands is key to understanding the dynamics of cultivation and the overall story.

pages.title: Blusher Prefecture
pages.content:
Blusher Prefecture is a complex and significant location within the narrative, characterized by its unique blend of cultural, political, and supernatural elements.

'''Political and Administrative Landscape:'''

* '''Part of Colorful Garment Nation:''' Blusher Prefecture is one of the six prefectures of Colorful Garment Nation. This places it within the administrative structure of a larger political entity, though one that is not considered to be among the most powerful.
* '''Prefectural Overseer:''' The prefecture is governed by a Prefectural Overseer, a high-ranking official responsible for the region's administration. The Prefectural Overseer of Blusher Prefecture, Lord Liu, is a scholar known for his essays. He is also a fourth-rank official.
* '''Official Roads''': The prefecture is connected by official roads.
* '''County Magistrate''':  Dragon Spring County was changed to Locust Yellow County after it became part of Dragon Spring Prefecture. There is also a county magistrate, Yuan, in Locust Yellow County, who is different than the previous magistrate, Wu Yuan.
* '''Imperial Court Influence''': The imperial court of Colorful Garment Nation has a significant influence on the prefecture.
* '''Prefectural Office:''' The prefectural office is a significant administrative building, where important decisions and meetings take place.
* '''Military Presence:''' There is a military presence in the prefecture, with a general (General Ma) and soldiers stationed there. The general is said to have fought in a hundred battles. The general also oversees the prefecture.
* '''Relationship with the Great Li Empire''': There is an indication that the Great Li Empire has spies and influence in the prefecture.
* '''Taxes''': The prefecture has a history of taxation, and one prefectural overseer had to beg wealthy clans for assistance in raising money for a city god statue.

'''Cultural and Social Aspects:'''

* '''Scholarly Arts:''' Blusher Prefecture is known for its passion for scholarly arts, especially Go. There is a strong emphasis on education and intellectual pursuits.
* '''Go Players''': There are many skilled Go players in the prefecture, with an elder known to be the number one player.
* '''Wealthy Clans:''' The prefecture is home to wealthy clans.
* '''Traditions:''' It has a strong sense of local traditions.
* '''Open-Minded''': The prefecture is said to be relatively open-minded.
* '''Lanterns''': Colorful lanterns are used to decorate for events and festivals.
* '''City God Statue''': The city god statue was gilded using gold leaf, but now it is missing.

'''Key Locations and Structures:'''

* '''City Walls:''' The prefecture is surrounded by towering city walls, with guard stations.
* '''City God Pavilion:''' A structure dedicated to the city god, which plays a significant role in the story. The city god has a physical form.
* '''Zhao Clan Residence''': The Zhao Clan residence is located in the center of the city.
* '''Embroidery Alley:''' A location within the city where there have been strange occurrences.
* '''Horse Head Bridge''': A location where there have been strange occurrences.
* '''Dangling Copper Tower''': A location where there have been strange occurrences.
* '''Lake View Academy''': A notable academy near the border of White Mountain Nation, with ties to the prefecture.
* '''Unnamed Temple''': There is a newly constructed temple that needs a couplet.

'''Supernatural and Mystical Elements:'''

* '''Demonic Cultivators''': The prefecture is experiencing a demonic crisis. Demonic cultivators are causing chaos.
* '''City God:''' The city god of Blusher Prefecture plays a role in the events. The city god is a spirit, and his health is tied to the city.
* '''Mountain and River Gods:''' There are nearby mountain and river gods who may be called upon in times of crisis.
* '''Immortals''': There are immortals and cultivators who get involved in the prefecture's affairs.
* '''Heretical Cultivators''': There are also heretical cultivators with unknown backgrounds.
* '''Heavenly Master Seal''': A talisman in the form of a Heavenly Master Seal was placed there two hundred years ago by Mount Longhu's Heavenly Master Residence, which may have contributed to the recent demonic problems in the prefecture.
* '''Yin Energy''': There is dense yin energy at unmarked graveyards, which seems to have been changed by the geomancy map.
* '''Spirit Screens''': There is a reference to spirit screens.

'''Key Figures and Groups:'''

* '''Prefectural Overseer Liu:''' The current Prefectural Overseer, known for his literary talent.
* '''General Ma''': A military leader in the prefecture.
* '''Old Immortal:''' An unnamed old immortal is present in the prefecture during the crisis. He is from a foreign nation and is involved in the Go match.
* '''Chong Miao:''' An old Daoist priest with a Daoist title, whom many suspect is taking advantage of the dire situation.
* '''Xu Yuanxia:''' A cultivator who is also involved in the crisis.
* '''Zhang Shanfeng:''' Another cultivator who is involved in the crisis.
* '''Liu Gaohua:''' The son of Prefectural Overseer Liu, who becomes involved in the events. He is a scholar.
* '''The Aide''': The Prefectural Overseer's aide is experienced and knowledgeable, and he assists the Prefectural Overseer by offering advice.
* '''Spiritual Horn Force:''' A local cultivation force that is expected to arrive in the prefecture to help with the crisis. The Spiritual Horn Force has a colored luan which is used for travel.
* '''Old Demon Mi's Disciples''': Three shop attendants from the rice shop are revealed to be disciples of Old Demon Mi.
* '''Zhao Liu''': Zhao Liu is from Divine Edict Sect.
* '''City God''':  The city god was a scholar who was appointed as a god by the emperor of Colorful Garment Nation. He is also aware of the demonic cultivators.
* '''Chen Ping'an:''' He is drawn into the events of Blusher Prefecture and plays a key role in addressing the demonic crisis.
* '''Gao Shuyi''': A noble of Great Quan Empire who is known to act wantonly, and is related to a duke.
* '''Liu Chicheng''': A scholar who is a great demon who can see other's true forms.

'''Challenges and Crises:'''

* '''Demonic Threat:''' The prefecture is facing a significant demonic threat. There are demons and demonic cultivators causing problems.
* '''Missing Treasures''': A sect treasure of the Spiritual Horn Force goes missing, drawing the attention of the sect away from the prefecture.
* '''Internal Corruption:''' There are implications of corruption and internal issues within the prefectural administration.
* '''City God in Trouble''': The city god is in trouble and needs assistance.
* '''Political Instability''': The prefecture is experiencing political instability.

'''Interactions with the Wider World:'''

* '''Other Nations:''' The prefecture has dealings with other nations, and there are outsiders coming to help with the crisis.
* '''Cultivation World:''' The prefecture interacts with the cultivation world, with various sects and cultivators playing roles in the events.
* '''Great Li Empire''': The Great Li Empire has influence and spies within the prefecture.
* '''Divine Edict Sect:''' A sect is mentioned as having disciples in the prefecture.
* '''Lake View Academy''': The academy is a location visited by officials of the prefecture, indicating that there is influence between the two locations.

Blusher Prefecture is a prefecture within Colorful Garment Nation, which is a place with a complex interplay of political administration, cultural traditions, and supernatural events. It is a place of scholarly pursuits and wealthy clans, but it is also under threat from demonic forces and political instability. The prefecture's story involves a diverse cast of characters, including officials, scholars, cultivators, and city gods, all navigating the challenges of a world where the mundane and the mystical often intersect. The prefecture is also a location of intense conflict and intrigue, drawing the attention of other nations and cultivation forces, and it serves as an important setting for the unfolding narrative.

pages.title: Buddhism
pages.content:
Buddhism in Eastern Treasured Vial Continent faces a period of decline, a stark contrast to the flourishing Daoism and Confucianism. The story depict this waning influence, portraying Buddhism as a less prominent force in the world's power dynamics, yet still retaining unique aspects and attracting devoted followers.

'''Buddhism's Diminished Status:'''

* '''Historical Calamities:''' Buddhism has suffered several great calamities over the past 1,000 years, weakening its power and influence. [1]
* '''Popular Perception:''' A common saying in Eastern Treasured Vial Continent reflects Buddhism's diminished standing: "Hear only about the True Lords and Heavenly Masters; know not about the Dharmapala and Bhadanta." This highlights the dominance of Daoist and Confucian figures in the public consciousness. [1]
* '''Weakest Force in the Town:''' In the specific context of the small town, Buddhism is described as the weakest force, further emphasizing its reduced presence. [2]

'''Unique Aspects and Teachings:'''

Despite its decline, Buddhism retains unique practices and concepts that shape the lives of its adherents and contribute to the world's diverse philosophical landscape.

* '''Karmic Fate:''' The concept of karma plays a significant role in Buddhist teachings. Actions have consequences, and individuals experience the repercussions of their past deeds. [2] This emphasis on cause and effect is evident in the interactions between characters, where their choices and actions influence their destinies.
* '''Vanquishing Distracted Minds:''' Buddhism emphasizes the importance of overcoming desires and attachments to achieve enlightenment. [3] Cultivating a peaceful and focused mind is crucial for spiritual progress.
* '''Observing Past and Future Lives:''' The belief in reincarnation and the cyclical nature of existence is central to Buddhist teachings. [3, 4] This perspective shapes the understanding of life, death, and the interconnectedness of all beings.
* '''Attaining Enlightenment through Renunciation:''' While acknowledged as a simplified concept, the idea of attaining enlightenment by renouncing past evil deeds remains a significant aspect of Buddhism. [5] This suggests a path to redemption and spiritual transformation through recognizing and abandoning harmful actions.

'''Buddhist Figures and Practices:'''

The sources introduce several characters and practices that shed light on the practice and influence of Buddhism in Eastern Treasured Vial Continent.

* '''The Old Monk at Heart Manifestation Temple:''' Residing in Southern Garden Nation, where Buddhism is more prominent, the old monk embodies the teachings of compassion, wisdom, and acceptance. [6, 7] He engages in thoughtful discussions about karma, enlightenment, and the complexities of good and evil.
* '''The Young Monk in White Kasaya:''' This monk's dedicated practice and adherence to Buddhist principles amidst the White River Temple controversy demonstrate the resilience and enduring spirit of Buddhism. [8, 9] His quiet presence and commitment to his faith offer a glimpse into the personal devotion that sustains the tradition.
* '''"Refrain From Looking Outward":''' This Buddhist saying, cited by Chen Ping'an, emphasizes the importance of inner reflection and focusing on one's own spiritual development rather than seeking external validation or comparing oneself to others. [10, 11] This principle encourages self-reliance and a deeper understanding of Buddhist teachings.

'''Buddhism, despite its decline, remains a significant presence in Majestic World.''' Its teachings on karma, enlightenment, and the cultivation of a peaceful mind continue to resonate with certain individuals. The sources portray a nuanced view of Buddhism, acknowledging its diminished status while highlighting its unique contributions to the world's spiritual and philosophical landscape.

pages.title: Cai Jinjian
pages.content:
{{Character
|header1=Cai Jinjian
|image1=Cai Jinjian.png
|Chinese=蔡金简
|Pinyin=Cài Jīnjiǎn
|Titles=Celestial Maiden
|Vital_status=Alive
|Gender=Female
|Species=Human
|Love_interest(s)=[[Qi Jingchun]] (unspoken)
|Allies=[[Fu Nanhua]]
|Enemie(s)=[[Chen Ping An]]

'''Cai Jinjian''' is a cultivator from [[Dawn Cloud Mountain]] who came to the small town in [[Jewel Small World]] hunting for a fated opportunity. Her cruelty toward [[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]] nearly cost the boy his life, and he answered it by killing her in an alley. [[Qi Jingchun]] brought her back, and she returned home a changed woman.

== Appearance ==
Cai Jinjian is a beautiful young woman whose body has been cleansed by cultivation, so that to an ordinary village woman she would look like a goddess.Chapter 18 She carries herself with an easy, natural allure, and a respected senior once said she had "aptitude and beauty in equal measure", which her sect took as a sign she would make a fine Dao partner for someone powerful.Chapter 20 Like most people from Dawn Cloud Mountain, she cannot stand dirt.

== Personality ==
When she first arrives in the town, Cai Jinjian is polished and sweet on the surface and cold underneath. She sees the townsfolk as ants, smiles while she lies, and works hard to keep up the image of a gentle lady in front of Fu Nanhua while privately loathing Chen Ping'an, especially his eyes. She has real restraint and can recite a calming mantra rather than lash out, but once her pride is stung she is capable of ruining a child's life on a whim. She also carries the weight of her sect's hopes, which makes her hungry for any opportunity that could raise her standing.

Dying changed her. After Qi Jingchun revived her and talked with her, she lost interest in scheming and in cultivating only for power's sake. Back home she seemed listless at first, but she was thinking things through, and she later grew calm, steady and increasingly aloof, with a firm Dao heart.Chapter 253 (2) She is quietly sharp as well. When Fu Nanhua tried to pressure her with threats against her sect's trade, she saw straight through them.

== Background ==
=== Dawn Cloud Mountain ===
Cai Jinjian is a disciple of Dawn Cloud Mountain, one of the few immortal forces on Eastern Treasured Vial Continent that uses Buddhist cultivation methods.Chapter 642 (3) The sect practices a technique called Observing the Sea of Clouds and lives off the sale of Cloud Root Stones.Chapter 37 Its leaders spent heavily on her because they hoped she would lift the sect's reputation, and her master dreamed making her mountain master one day. Ten years before entering the town, she had traveled with her father to Lake Shujian and glimpsed the River Severing True Lord from afar.Chapter 17

=== The small town ===
Cai Jinjian entered the town with [[Fu Nanhua]] of Old Dragon City, posing as a relative of [[Gu Can]]'s mother, and she chose Gu Can as the opportunity she would pursue. The two struck an alliance and agreed to be open with each other, though Fu Nanhua had already decided to kill her before they set foot inside.Chapter 9

On [[Clay Vase Alley]] she stepped in a pile of dog dung while walking backward and, furious and humiliated, turned on Chen Ping'an. She tapped his forehead and struck his chest, then smiled and told him he had half a year to live at most before claiming it was a joke.Chapter 10 It was not. The tap forced open his acupoints, leaving his body like a house with no door, and the blow to his chest wrecked the foundations he would need to cultivate.Chapter 42

She was not acting entirely on her own. [[Liu Zhimao]], the River Severing True Lord, was hiding in Gu Can's home as a storyteller. He had a hand in her stepping in the dung, delayed Chen Ping'an's warning by a split second so she would take it as spite, and later fooled her into thinking she had reached enlightenment. Years later, Chen Ping'an accused Liu Zhimao of confusing Cai Jinjian with a secret technique and of planting the words "seek death with resolve" in his own heart, so that he would go after Cai Jinjian and Fu Nanhua and die.Chapter 438 (1)

When she and Fu Nanhua were strolling together, Chen Ping'an charged out of a crossing alley. He drove a sharp porcelain shard into her throat, punched her in the chest and shouldered her into the side alley, leaving her in a pool of blood. Everyone took her for dead.

=== Revival ===
Qi Jingchun stepped in, seeing her soul flicker like a candle in the wind. He brought her back to life and, while her body was still badly hurt, drew her soul out so they could talk in the school. He asked about small things in the outside world, like the price of rice and oil and new printing methods, then answered questions about her cultivation that had stumped her master and pointed her to classic Confucian works. When she asked why he saved her, he told her it broke the rules of the world but fit his beliefs.

Before they parted, Mr. Qi asked her for a favor. She was to carry Fleeting Glance Picture Scrolls to the Sword Qi Great Wall, each one showing part of Chen Ping'an's life after leaving the town. The last scroll held Mr. Qi's farewell message to Miss Ning, asking her to treat Chen Ping'an kindly.Chapter 386 (4) She kept the near-death experience secret from her master and her sect.

=== After returning ===
Cai Jinjian came home empty-handed after spending a whole pouch of gold essence copper coins, and her master became a laughingstock on the mountain.Chapter 253 (1) When she visited Old Dragon City with her sect's elders, Fu Nanhua took her aside to find out why she had been saved and to propose an alliance. She turned him down calmly, though the two later became quite close.

Her cultivation then shot up. Within a few years she was a celebrated prodigy at Dawn Cloud Mountain with standing equal to earth immortals of older generations. She spends most of her time in seclusion and keeps a portrait of Mr. Qi that she painted herself, which she has never shown anyone. She now has her own peak and residence, and in quiet moments she still thinks of the scholar she admired most. She knows her feelings were never returned and is content to hold them anyway.Chapter 417 (2)

== Trivia ==
* Chen Ping'an knew at once that her "joke" about his remaining time was true.
* Chen Ping'an has said that he killed Cai Jinjian for his own sake, while he fought the Mountain-Moving Ape for Liu Xianyang's sake.
* Years later, Chen Ping'an still had the porcelain shards from home and picked out the one he had used on her.
* When Mr. Qi gave her the first scroll, he asked, almost like a shy student, whether sending it would be gilding the lily, then admitted he knew nothing about romance.
* Dawn Cloud Mountain had become one of four sects-in-waiting on the continent.

== References ==

pages.title: Cao Qinglang
pages.content:
{{Character|header1=Cao Qinglang|Vital_status=Alive|Gender=Male|Species=Human|Master(s)=[[Chen Ping An]]
[[Zhong Qiu]] (half-disciple)
[[Lu Tai]]|Friend(s)=[[Pei Qian]]|Occupation=Student
Scholar|Current_affiliation(s)=[[Chen Ping An]]'s lineage, [[Downtrodden Mountain]]|Continent=[[Parasol Leaf Continent]] ([[Lotus Flower Blessed Land]])|Cultivation_rank=Abode Tier|Novel=Chapter 311}} {{Spoilers}} '''Cao Qinglang''' is a young scholar from the Lotus Flower Blessed Land, a medium grade blessed land on Parasol Leaf Continent. His entire family was murdered when he was still a small child, and Chen Ping'an, newly arrived in that world at the time, ended up living beside him and raising him, and later took him on as a disciple. == Appearance == He is once described as a young boy dressed in the plain azure robes typical of a private school pupil. == Personality == As a child Cao Qinglang is consumed by grief and a hunger for revenge he has no way to act on, and for a long time afterward he withdraws into himself, going quiet and numb around people who try to reach him. He teaches himself to cook and keep house rather than lean on anyone, and only slowly warms up again, largely thanks to Chen Ping'an and to Pei Qian, who ends up living in his courtyard for a stretch as a child herself. The two of them bicker constantly and he loses every argument, but he does not hold grudges, and he is generous even when he is the one who comes up short. Grown, he reassures Pei Qian rather than resenting her for once wanting him gone, and shows no interest in competing with her or anyone else for Chen Ping'an's attention. He reads far more than he trains, and he is content to fall behind in cultivation while he does it. == Background == Cao Qinglang's parents and grandparents are killed in his own home by Zhou Shi and Ya'er, acting on the orders of the demonic Paramount Leader Ding Ying, who mistakenly believes that the boy's body is hiding the soul of the otherworldly immortal Tong Qingqing.Chapter 311 Officials take the grieving boy to identify the bodies before he is left to fend for himself in the family home.Chapter 322 Chen Ping'an, who has recently arrived in the Lotus Flower Blessed Land, moves into the alley outside his courtyard and gradually starts looking out for him, and the two of them end up sharing meals in near silence most nights. Cao Qinglang is soon joined in the courtyard by a ragged, sharp-tongued little girl, later revealed to be Pei Qian, and the three of them live together for a time.Chapter 323 Chen Ping'an goes on to defeat Imperial Preceptor Zhong Qiu in a sparring match and kills Ding Ying himself in a brutal duel at Bull Mountain, ending the threat that orphaned the boy.Chapter 326 He later tracks down and deals with Zhou Shi and Ya'er specifically because of what they did to Cao Qinglang's family, something he considers unforgivable regardless of the wider politics involved.Chapter 360Chapter 363 Cao Qinglang is largely raised and schooled by [[Zhong Qiu]], who comes to think of him as something between a student and a disciple, and he is later also taught by Lu Tai, the descendant of the Daoist Lu Chen, who at one point entrusts him with the valuable Five Mountains True Appearance Picture Scroll.Chapter 530 When Chen Ping'an eventually leaves the Lotus Flower Blessed Land, he takes Pei Qian with him as his traveling disciple but leaves Cao Qinglang behind, worried for the boy's safety on the road. Chen Ping'an regrets this for years afterward and never stops thinking of him, and when Pei Qian finally visits again she confirms that Cao Qinglang is recognized as their master's disciple too, not merely a boy he once took pity on.Chapter 560 He is formally listed as a student of Chen Ping'an's household at the founding of Downtrodden Mountain's ancestral hall.Chapter 568 By adulthood Cao Qinglang has reached the Abode Tier, a step behind Pei Qian's Sea Observation Tier, something she needles him about without much effect. He spends most of his time reading rather than training, and does not seem troubled by lagging behind his fellow disciples.Chapter 602 == Trivia == * The Lotus Flower Blessed Land is later split into four pieces, one of which is absorbed into Downtrodden Mountain and renamed the Lotus Root Blessed Land. * Zhong Qiu tells him he hopes he will one day speak up for the world rather than let it be reduced to a Go board where people are treated as disposable pieces. == References ==

pages.title: Cao Xi
pages.content:
{{Character |header1 = Cao Xi |Aliases = Sword Immortal Cao
Great Sword Immortal Cao (self-styled) |Vital_status = Alive |Gender = Male |Species = Human |Disciple(s) = [[Li Liu]] (sword technique) |Relatives = Cao Jun (descendant)
Cao Mao (descendant)
Pillar Cao Clan of the Great Li Empire |Allies = Xu Ruo
[[Cui Chan]] |Enemie(s) = [[Xie Shi]] |Occupation = Terrestrial sword immortal
Overseer of the Mighty Suppressing Pagoda |Current_affiliation(s) = Southern Whirl Continent |Former_affiliation(s) = Cao Clan of Clay Vase Alley |Continent = Southern Whirl Continent |Cultivation_rank = Terrestrial sword immortal |Novel = Chapter 24 }} '''Cao Xi''' is a terrestrial sword immortal of Southern Whirl Continent who was born on Clay Vase Alley in the small town of Jewel Small World. He is one of the two best-known cultivators ever to come out of the town, alongside Xie Shi, and is the most senior ancestor of the Cao Clan. == Appearance == Cao Xi looks like a plump, wealthy man rather than an immortal, and strangers in the town take him for a rich merchant.Chapter 201 He has a moustache and a white, chubby wrist. His bonded flying sword is wound around it like a green rope or bracelet.Chapter 235 == Personality == Cao Xi is loud, crude and shameless, and proud of it. Across Southern Whirl Continent he is known as stingy and unkind, a man who would pluck the feathers off a passing goose. He mocks Xie Shi's reputation for righteousness and claims that upright people like him are the hardest to get along with.Chapter 185 He loves striking deals and treats nearly everything as business. Beneath the bluster, he still feels for his hometown. Standing alone in his old family house, he lamented that he had become an immortal while the warmth of the place had vanished. He also caught rain in a bowl to taste the water of home, then poured it out, grumbling that scholars lie about it tasting better than wine. He remembers the names of all his childhood classmates, though every one of them is long dead.Chapter 191 == Background == Cao Xi grew up on Clay Vase Alley and was a troublesome child. He once urinated into the Iron Lock Well and then threw stones into it for a month. His life is recorded in the town's Local County Chronicle.Chapter 24 Like the other children of the town, he had bonded porcelain. He grew strong enough that, according to Song Changjing, the buyers of such porcelain would treat him as an honoured guest rather than a possession.Chapter 61 He left the town and made his name on Southern Whirl Continent. His swordsmanship is not considered elite among terrestrial sword immortals, but his bonded sword ranks among the ten best weapons on that continent. The sword was refined from an entire river by an ancient deity, and it is regarded as a pseudo-celestial tool.Chapter 225 He is also half the owner of the Sea Suppressing Pagoda.Chapter 194 == Plot == Cao Xi returned to the town around the same time as Xie Shi. Xie Shi had come to act against the Great Li Empire, and Cao Xi sided with Great Li, partly on behalf of the Pure Confucian Chen Clan, with whom one of his descendants had become engaged. He urged Xu Ruo to help kill Xie Shi as a warning to others, but Xu Ruo refused to make that decision.Chapter 187 While in the town, he harshly disciplined the fox spirit that served his descendant Cao Jun. He struck it with twenty wisps of sword qi for speaking carelessly.Chapter 195 He also visited the kiln supervision office, where his descendant Cao Mao served, and advised on its feng shui. Cao Xi then visited Old Man Yang to ask about his mother's soul. Old Man Yang struck a deal with him. In return for the souls of Cao Xi's parents, Cao Xi had to give his old flying sword to [[Li Liu]], teach her his sword technique, and serve as her Dao guardian. He protested that a sword immortal who might reach the 12th Tier should not guard a child, but he agreed once he understood what she was. Before leaving the town, he ordered Cao Jun to join the Great Li army and kill a 10th Tier cultivator or two within a decade.Chapter 243 He went to Lion Peak as Li Liu's Dao guardian and gave her the short sword he had used for 300 years before refining his river sword.Chapter 283 He accompanied her through secret realms and old sect ruins while she gathered treasures.Chapter 367 He later returned to Southern Whirl Continent to keep watch over the Mighty Suppressing Pagoda, leaving Cao Jun in the Great Li army.Chapter 568 == Trivia == * When Old Man Yang named Li Liu as his student, Cao Xi joked that people would one day remember him only as Li Liu's master. * He challenged an 11th Tier swordsman to a duel, then set the date a hundred years away and called it strategy. == References ==

pages.title: Chen Clan
pages.content:
{{Spoilers}}
The '''Chen Clan''' is not a single family but several unrelated clans that share the surname Chen. They range from the impoverished line of [[Chen Ping An]] in the small town of [[Jewel Small World]] to the Yingyin Chen Clan of Southern Whirl Continent, the only clan in the world honored as "Pure Confucian", and the clan of the old great sword immortal [[Chen Qingdu]] at the [[Sword Qi Great Wall]].

== Chen Clan of the small town ==
According to [[Old Man Yao]], the small town once had two branches of the Chen Clan. One moved away long ago. The other, the branch Chen Ping'an belongs to, flourished at some point, but so long ago that no one could say whether it was five hundred, eight hundred or a thousand years. It then split into several sub-branches and slowly dwindled. Many of its graves were forgotten, and some of the mountains where they lay were sealed off by the kiln supervision officials. Old Man Yao said that even immortals could not find the branch's ancestral burial ground. For the past few centuries it had produced no one of note, and its only pride was that it had not become servants of the Four Families and Ten Clans.Chapter 36

Most of the other Chen descendants in the town did become servants, many of them for generations. The steward of the kiln supervision office noted that the Song and Zhao clans treat their Chen servants almost as family, and that their head stewards come from the clan. He remembered only one member who had stayed independent, the son of a highly skilled potter who had been praised by two kiln supervision officials and died young.Chapter 57 That son is Chen Ping'an.

The town's records for the past thousand years only cover this remaining branch. Chen Dui told Chen Songfeng that it shares an ancestor with his Dragon Tail County Chen Clan. Ruan Xiu later told Chen Ping'an that he and Chen Songfeng are distant relatives from several centuries back.Chapter 64

== Dragon Tail County Chen Clan ==
The Chen Clan of Dragon Tail County, also called the Dragon Tail Creek Chen Clan, is a powerful and wealthy clan with more than a thousand years of history. Its eldest grandson Chen Songfeng describes it as a clan of scholars rather than cultivators. Its ancestral rules forbid it from taking part in other sects' and clans' conflicts. It knows of the Yingyin Chen Clan only through a distant relationship.Chapter 61

The clan later set up a private school in the small town. It is free to everyone, even the children of Lu Empire prisoners and refugees.

== Yingyin Chen Clan ==
The Yingyin Chen Clan is also known as the Pure Confucian Chen Clan. Chen Songfeng explains that it is the branch that left the small town long ago and moved to another continent, where it became known as an "archway that assembles the characteristics of all teachings". The steward also recalled that when that branch left, it assigned graveyard attendants to tend its graves. Those attendants were [[Liu Xianyang]]'s ancestors.Chapter 65

The clan was once the smallest of eight branches of the Yimen Chen Clan on the Middle Earth Divine Continent, and it moved to Southern Whirl Continent to escape conflict. After its ancestor appeared, carrying a sun and a moon on his shoulders, the clan was transformed. A Confucian school and an academy were built on its land, and the road to its gates is lined with archways honoring its descendants. It is the only clan granted the title "Pure Confucian". Its descendants were proud enough not to feel ashamed when their patriarch announced that the sun on his shoulder had been borrowed by someone for a hundred years.Chapter 206

Its clan leader is Chen Chun'an, who guards Southern Whirl Continent.Chapter 287 He once came to the Sword Qi Great Wall, where Chen Qingdu counted him among the most interesting outsiders he had met.Chapter 578 Chen Dui, a direct lineal descendant, came to the small town to worship her ancestors and took Liu Xianyang to Southern Whirl Continent. The agreement was that he would return to Ruan Qiong after twenty years.Chapter 571 The clan also used its influence behind the scenes to help Ruan Qiong become overseer of Jewel Small World after Qi Jingchun.Chapter 193

== Chen Clan of the Sword Qi Great Wall ==
The Chen Clan is one of the great clans in the city north of the Sword Qi Great Wall, and its old ancestor is Chen Qingdu. He never left the wall, even for the weddings of his clan's top prodigies or the funerals of its fallen sword immortals.Chapter 575 Like the Dong Clan, its power rests on generations of sword immortals, and its sword technique strengthens the bones.

Its current leader, Chen Xi, is an old sword immortal who engraved the character "Chen" on the wall.Chapter 650 Even so, he still feels like a child in front of Chen Qingdu, so the clan's members are the most reluctant of all the clans to visit the city wall.Chapter 596 After the commotion at Mirage Market, Chen Qingdu summoned the clan leader and wounded him with a single sword strike.Chapter 584 Chen Sanqiu is a young master of the clan. Chen Xi once asked Chen Qingdu in private whether Chen Sanqiu could leave with a Confucian sage to study in the Majestic World.

The clan controls the wall's sword market.

== Other Chen Clans ==
* A Chen Clan village in a province of the [[Azure Phoenix Nation]] produces many armed escorts. Its leader, known as Chen's Archway, is so well known that his name helps his clansmen find work.Chapter 380

== Trivia ==
* The accounts of how the town's Chen branches relate to the Yingyin Chen Clan do not fully agree. Chen Songfeng says Chen Dui's clan is the branch that left the town. Ruan Xiu says her clan is unrelated to the town's Chen Clans even a thousand or two thousand years back. Ruan Qiong also tells an old Pure Confucian scholar that the two town branches have nothing to do with his clan.
* That old scholar was saddened by the state of the town's Chen descendants. In Southern Whirl Continent, he said, no Chen with a name in the genealogy would ever become a servant, however poor.
* Cao Xi suspected that either the Dragon Tail Creek Chen Clan had tampered with its records, or one of its ancestors had been so fortunate that he used up his descendants' luck for dozens of generations.
* Old Man Yao suggested that the fortune of Chen Ping'an's branch may have been taken by the other branch.

== References ==

pages.title: Chen Gong
pages.content:
{{Character|Title=Chen Gong|Vital_status=Dead|Gender=Male|Spouse(s)=[[Chen Mu]]|Relatives=[[Chen Ping An]] (Son)}}

== Appearance ==
Gu Can's mother, a close friend of his wife, recalls that he was "far from a handsome man", and that she never thought he was good enough for his wife.Chapter 17

== Personality ==
Chen Ping'an's father was quiet, withdrawn and awkward with words, but very good to his son. Whenever he returned to town, he brought the boy small gifts such as candy Bodhisattva figures or old porcelain fragments. Ma Kuxuan remembers him as a famous potter who was extremely good at his craft and a very honest person.Chapter 56 He and his wife were known as generous and kind people.

One of Chen Ping'an's few clear childhood memories is of his father saying perhaps the only romantic thing he ever said in his life. As his wife mended clothes with their son on her lap, he asked her whether they would be together again in their next lives. She smiled and answered, "Why not?"Chapter 218 (2)

== Background ==
Chen Ping'an's father belonged to the Chen Clan, which had a long and once-prosperous history. Through two periods of upheaval, the clan fell into decline on Eastern Treasured Vial Continent. By the time he was born, it had been in decay for over a thousand years, as if cursed never to rise again.Chapter 22

He grew up in the small town and worked as a potter. Gu Can's mother believed that, had he not died young, he might have become head potter of a large dragon kiln within twenty years.

Before his son turned six, he shattered Chen Ping'an's [[Natal Porcelain|bonded porcelain]], effectively tearing up the contract tied to the boy's fate. This stripped Chen Ping'an of his fated opportunities in Jewel Small World, but it also left him free, "like a flickering candle in a dark room".Chapter 63 (2) Ruan Qiong later wonders how an ordinary town potter could have known the secrets of bonded porcelain, and why he would smash his son's porcelain at the cost of his own life. He concludes that someone must have deliberately revealed the secrets to him and encouraged him. Old Man Yang admits he first took it for an ordinary clan conflict, and only realised too late that it was "the true kill shot" of a vast plot targeting Qi Jingchun.Chapter 85 (1)

He died suddenly, and his body was never found. Some townsfolk said he slipped into the creek one rainy day while rushing to protect the kiln flames, while others said he trespassed onto a mountain sealed by the imperial court and was killed by wild beasts.Chapter 17 Ma Kuxuan recalls that on a stormy night around that time, he saw his own father return home secretly with a strange expression of delight and fear, while his mother could not stop smiling.Chapter 56 It is later revealed that Ma Kuxuan's parents were deeply involved in the shattering of Chen Ping'an's bonded porcelain. The porcelain had been bought by an unknown buyer, and the Great Li Empire paid that buyer compensation for its destruction.Chapter 530 (2)

After his death, his grieving wife fell ill and died within a year, leaving Chen Ping'an an orphan.

== Trivia ==

* Avenging his parents is one of Chen Ping'an's very few lifelong fixations.Chapter 364 (1) 
* The elderly Aunty Chen grumbles that being a good person did him no good, since his death brought years of hardship to his wife and son. She tells Chen Ping'an not to resent him, but to treat it as a debt from a past life, repaid in this one.Chapter 466 (1)
* Following an old potters' tradition, Chen Ping'an adds handfuls of soil from his travels to his parents' graves.Chapter 158 (2)
* His son was born on the fifth day of the fifth month, which the town's elders considered the unluckiest day of the year.

[[Cui Dongshan]] |Occupation=Member of Downtrodden Mountain
Helper at the pastry shop on Dragon Riding Alley |Current_affiliation(s)=[[Downtrodden Mountain]] |Former_affiliation(s)=Imperial River, [[Yellow Court Nation]] |Continent=[[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]] |Empire=Great Li Empire |Cultivation_rank=Middle Five Tiers Qi refiner, close to the Dragon Gate Tier bottleneck *(Chapter 559 (1))* |Novel=Chapter 163 }} '''Chen Lingjun''' is a water snake of the flood dragon lineage who once ruled the Imperial River of the Yellow Court Nation. Subdued by [[Cui Dongshan]] and given to [[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]], he lives on [[Downtrodden Mountain]], where he is better known as the little boy in azure. == Appearance == In human form Chen Lingjun looks like a little boy, and he likes to dress in azure and green. His hands end in claw-tipped fingers. In his true form he is a huge water snake, big enough to carve a path through mountains and forests as he swims.Chapter 163 == Personality == Chen Lingjun is a show-off with a big mouth and a habit of bragging about his grand connections. He calls himself the "Chivalrous Young Man from the Imperial River," a nickname borrowed from a martial arts hero he idolises, and he worries about bringing shame to it. He loves to boast about his close friendship with the river god of the Imperial River, whom he calls his good brother. Wei Bo has bluntly told him that the river god simply took him for a fool. Beneath the bluster he is a coward in front of real power. When Cui Dongshan revealed what he was carrying, Chen Lingjun dropped to his knees and kowtowed at once, offering to find him beautiful maidservants. Back in the Yellow Court Nation he was considered a sixth tier great demon, yet in the Jewel Small World he was too frightened to go outside in case some passerby smashed him with a single punch.Chapter 242 (2) He has an endless craving for snake gall pebbles and will plead, roll on the floor or threaten to steal to get one. He is smarter and more observant than he lets on. He cannot bear to watch [[Pei Qian]] suffer in her fist training, so he keeps away from the bamboo building when she is in it. When [[Cui Cheng]] once asked why he stayed on Downtrodden Mountain, he answered quietly that it was because of his kind-hearted master.Chapter 557 (2) He often teases [[Chen Nuanshu]], but he is also the one who tells her not to rush her cultivation. == Background == === The Imperial River === For centuries Chen Lingjun lorded over the Imperial River outside a city in the Yellow Court Nation. He lurked on the riverbed waiting for the fire python in the Cao Clan's scripture library to shed its skin so he could devour her before she became a flood dragon. When the young Cui Dongshan arrived at the library, Chen Lingjun tried to recruit him to help eat the python. Cui Dongshan injured him, then pulled out an ancient inkstone holding a sleeping flood dragon. The snoring of the tiny dragon terrified both creatures into submission. [[Lu Chen]] later wanted to take him to the Heavenly World because of some connection between them. When Chen Lingjun refused, Lu Chen left behind a golden lotus seed and asked Chen Ping'an to help the water snake swim along a great river in the Northern Complete Reed Continent and transform into a dragon.Chapter 420 (1) === Downtrodden Mountain === Chen Lingjun and the fire python were brought to Downtrodden Mountain to serve Chen Ping'an, who kept them supplied with snake gall pebbles. When the two finally chose their names, the boy named himself Chen Lingjun, and it was his idea that both take the surname Chen.Chapter 467 (1) Chen Ping'an admitted he had planned to call him Jing Qing, after a line of poetry about clear air after summer rain. Chen Lingjun wanted to inscribe his own "impressive and radiant" name all over the pastry shop to bring it good luck, but Pei Qian stopped him.Chapter 467 (2) He wandered the mountains of the region freely and made friends with cultivators all over the western mountains. One of them, a Dragon Gate Tier cultivator on Yellow Lake Mountain, asked him to find a buyer for the mountain. Chen Lingjun haggled the price down to just ten grain rain coins, and Downtrodden Mountain bought it. Chen Ping'an recorded it as Chen Lingjun's first real contribution to the mountain.Chapter 568 (2) === The river journey === During his travels in the Northern Complete Reed Continent, Chen Ping'an walked along the great rivers to scout a route for Chen Lingjun's future journey.Chapter 540 (3) Back home, he spent a whole night explaining the route along Plenty River while Chen Lingjun took notes in messy handwriting. Chen Lingjun then confessed that he did not want to go at all and just wanted to live out his days on Downtrodden Mountain. Chen Ping'an told him he was not angry, and that the journey could wait until Chen Lingjun truly wanted to make it himself.Chapter 567 (3) Chen Ping'an later gave him one of a pair of Dragon King Baskets found in the Northern Complete Reed Continent. Chen Lingjun first tried to refuse, suggesting it go to the black python of Go Table Mountain instead. Chen Ping'an told him the treasure was too precious to entrust to anyone else.Chapter 569 (1) Chen Lingjun refined his basket long before Nuanshu managed hers.Chapter 640 (1) When Chen Ping'an left for the Sword Qi Great Wall, Chen Lingjun went down to Dragon Riding Alley to help Shi Rou run the pastry shop.Chapter 566 == Trivia == * As a flood dragon, if he reaches the Golden Core Tier he will easily outclass an ordinary Golden Core Tier cultivator. * He keeps a bowl of water that lets him spy on distant places. He once used it to peek at a celestial maiden from a cultivating sect. * He once gave his river god brother a precious Peace and Safety Tablet. * He feels a strong, instinctive dislike for Wei Bo, who regularly punishes him. * He likes to watch the Go games on Downtrodden Mountain and shout advice to the players, even though watching usually puts him to sleep. == References ==

pages.title: Chen Mu
pages.content:
{{Character|Title=Chen Mu|Vital_status=Dead|Gender=Female|Species=Human|Spouse(s)=[[Chen Gong]]|Relatives=[[Chen Ping An]] (Son)|image1=Chen Mu.png|Continent=[[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]]}}
== Appearance ==
Chen Ping'an's mother is described as beautiful. A close friend of hers, [[Gu Can]]'s mother, recalls that she was a bubbly, outgoing woman before her illness. Within less than a year of falling ill, she was reduced to "nothing more than a sack of skin and bones", so emaciated that her neighbours were frightened to see her.Chapter 17

== Personality ==
She is remembered as a gentle, warm-hearted woman with "a fantastic personality". Gu Can's mother cannot recall a single time she ever became angry at anyone. She and her husband were generous and kind, which is why their neighbours in [[Clay Vase Alley]] helped their orphaned son after their deaths.Chapter 189 (1)

She was also self-sacrificing to the end. Throughout her illness, she told her son that it didn't hurt and only made her drowsy, so that he would worry less and do less for her. Chen Ping'an only realised much later that she had been gritting her teeth through terrible agony.Chapter 483 (1) Even in her final days, she felt blessed to have such a good child, and murmured that she could not believe her luck that he was her son.

== Background ==
Chen Ping'an's mother grew up in the small town and married a quiet, awkward potter. In Gu Can's mother's opinion, he was not good enough for her. Their family of three lived a stable, happy life until her husband died young, either by slipping into the creek while rushing to the kilns on a rainy day or by trespassing onto a sealed mountain, depending on the rumour.

One of Chen Ping'an's few clear childhood memories is of sitting on his mother's lap while she mended clothes. His father asked her, in what was perhaps the only romantic thing he ever said, whether they would be together again in their next lives, and she smiled and answered, "Why not?"Chapter 218 (2) She once ate a tartary buckwheat cake, told her son it was delicious, and promised to buy him one for his fifth birthday. Years later, Chen Ping'an tries to buy one to offer at his parents' graves, only to find that the pastry shop no longer makes them.Chapter 85 (1)

After her husband's death, she fell gravely ill. Her young son looked after her alone, standing on a stool to reach the stove, buying and brewing her medicine, and searching the mountains for medicinal herbs to save money.

In the winter she died, her son came home from praying at a temple and asked whether she felt better. She smiled with great difficulty and said it no longer hurt at all, and the boy rejoiced that praying to the Bodhisattva worked. Before she died, it began to snow, and she sent him outside to look at it. Once he had gone, she closed her eyes and prayed with all her might: "Please, please, please, let my little Ping'an be blessed with safety and prosperity." She passed away before the turn of the year.Chapter 50 (2)

Chen Ping'an was left an orphan and endured the greatest hardships imaginable between the ages of five and seven. He cut down his parents' old clothes to fit himself and carefully saved every offcut.Chapter 202

== Trivia ==

* Chen Ping'an once said that if he ever found a girl as good as his mother, he would fight to protect her even if his opponent were the Dao Ancestor.Chapter 203
* Watching her waste away left Chen Ping'an with a lasting fear of illness, and an even greater fear that if he died, no one in the world would remember his parents.
* Years later, the elderly Aunty Chen tearfully tells Chen Ping'an how wonderful it would have been for his mother to see his success, since she had known only hardship all her life.Chapter 466 (1)
* Song Jixin once tricked Chen Ping'an into revoking a vow he had sworn to his mother.
* "Ping'an" (平安) means peace and safety, the very blessing she prayed for her son in her final moments.

== References ==
