Keeper of the mountain's funds |Current_affiliation(s)=[[Downtrodden Mountain]] |Former_affiliation(s)=Scripture library of the Cao Clan's Iris Orchid manor |Continent=[[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]] |Empire=Great Li Empire |Novel=Chapter 163 }} '''Chen Nuanshu''', recorded in Downtrodden Mountain's genealogy as '''Chen Ruchu''', is a fire python who serves as [[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]]'s little maidservant and the tireless steward of [[Downtrodden Mountain]]. == Appearance == In her human form Nuanshu looks like a small girl in a pink dress, which is why she is so often called simply "the little girl in pink." She is rarely seen without a bucket and towel in her hands and a big bunch of keys clinking softly at her waist.Chapter 547 (1) She always seems to have a handful of roasted seeds ready to share. Her true form is a fire python. == Personality == Nuanshu is gentle, shy and endlessly hardworking. Chen Ping'an believes that as long as Downtrodden Mountain exists, she will be busy every single day, and he trusts her more than anyone on the mountain because she is the least likely to make a mistake. She is the one who runs around the mountain the most, cleaning every building, cooking, shopping and keeping accounts. When she goes shopping in the prefectural city, she likes to compare every shop carefully before buying. She is soft-hearted and cries easily. After each of [[Pei Qian]]'s brutal training sessions with [[Cui Cheng]], Nuanshu carried the unconscious girl down from the bamboo building, prepared her medicinal bath and went back up to scrub away the blood, often in tears.Chapter 529 (2) She is also something of a bookworm, having spent years reading in the scripture library she came from. Among the three girls of the bamboo building she is the peacemaker. When Pei Qian and [[Zhou Mili]] squabble, she smooths things over. Pei Qian bosses her around as the senior sister and once remarked that Nuanshu's book does not contain the word "refusal." Nuanshu is fiercely loyal to her master and will not hear a word against him. == Background == === The scripture library === Nuanshu was once a fire python living in the scripture library of the Cao Clan's Iris Orchid manor. She was in the second-to-last shedding of her skin, and if she had succeeded at the next one she would have become a flood dragon. A water snake from the river outside the city, the future [[Chen Lingjun]], was waiting to devour her. The young [[Cui Dongshan]] came to the library, cowed both creatures with an ancient inkstone that held a sleeping flood dragon, and took them away. When the fire python took human form, she became a little girl in a pink dress, curled up in terror at the top of the stairwell.Chapter 163 She and Chen Lingjun were brought to Downtrodden Mountain to serve Chen Ping'an. === Downtrodden Mountain === Nuanshu quickly made herself indispensable on the mountain. Chen Ping'an trusted her with the keys to his friends' houses in the [[Small Town]].Chapter 182 When the two children finally chose their own names, the little girl picked Chen Ruchu, meaning "just like before," because she hoped her bond with her master would stay as good as it was at the beginning. Chen Lingjun had come up with the idea of taking the surname Chen. When Chen Ping'an admitted that he had planned to call her Nuanshu, after the first and last characters of a poem about warm spring sunshine, she was so moved that she went home to cry.Chapter 467 (2) Ever after, she recorded herself as Chen Ruchu in the mountain's genealogy, but she told everyone they could call her Nuanshu. Most of the mountain prefers that name. Chen Ping'an once asked her about partridges in poetry, and she rattled off a long list of poems from memory while Pei Qian nodded off beside her.Chapter 478 When Cui Cheng died, he left a posthumous note on the first floor of the bamboo building with an envelope addressed "To be opened by Nuanshu."Chapter 566 Her safety is a quiet concern for Downtrodden Mountain. Chen Ping'an, Cui Dongshan and [[Wei Bo]] took great care to make sure she could leave the mountain on errands without coming to harm. She carries a sword talisman from the Dragon Spring Sword Sect so she can fly freely, and she wears an illusion-cast Dao robe that once belonged to Cui Dongshan. Chen Ping'an later reflected that whatever danger he and Cui Dongshan faced on their travels, they could always take comfort in the thought of Downtrodden Mountain, and that they had Nuanshu to thank for it.Chapter 567 (1) === Later === Chen Ping'an gave Nuanshu and Chen Lingjun a pair of Dragon King Baskets he had found in the Northern Complete Reed Continent. He told them they were too precious to entrust to anyone else.Chapter 569 (1) After the ancestral hall was established, he handed over all the spare immortal coins he had earned as a travelling salesman to Nuanshu to manage. She discreetly held up two fingers to remind him to ask for an allowance of fifty grain rain coins.Chapter 571 (1) While her master is away at the Sword Qi Great Wall, she cleans the Sky Blue Peak ancestral hall every five days.Chapter 594 (2) When Wei Bo brings a letter from Chen Ping'an, she wipes her sleeves before accepting it with both hands.Chapter 600 Chen Lingjun refined his Dragon King Basket long ago, but Nuanshu's progress is very slow, and Chen Lingjun teases her for it. Even so, her talent is not lacking. [[Lu Chen]] once nearly took her to the Heavenly World to cultivate.Chapter 640 (1) == Trivia == * "Ruchu" means "just like before." * Pei Qian once crowned her the number one Go player on Downtrodden Mountain. * Zhou Mili moved her whole collection of storybooks into Nuanshu's room one night, and Nuanshu simply looked after them without a word. * Downtrodden Mountain refers to her, Chen Lingjun and Zhou Mili as its three demons. * Pei Qian, Zhou Mili and Nuanshu each have their own little bamboo cricket cage and porcelain pot from Chen Ping'an. He suspects Nuanshu will end up tending all three plants. == References ==

[[Sword Qi Great Wall]] (Hidden Official's lineage)|Former_affiliation(s)=[[Old Man Yao]]'s dragon kiln|Empire=Great Li Empire}} '''Chen Ping'an''' is the protagonist of ''Sword of Coming''. An orphan from Clay Vase Alley in the small town of Jewel Small World, he becomes the closing disciple of the [[Scholarly Sage]], the mountain master of [[Downtrodden Mountain]], and later the Hidden Official of the [[Sword Qi Great Wall]]. == Appearance == As a boy, Chen Ping'an is thin and looks frail, though years of hard labour have made him far stronger than he appears.Chapter 72 In the town he wears straw sandals that he weaves himself.Chapter 2 After losing the hairpin Qi Jingchun gave him, he bought a plain jade hairpin and carved the same eight-character phrase onto it himself, and he wears that one in its place.Chapter 138 == Personality == Chen Ping'an is careful, patient and steady beyond his years. He grew up poor and learned early that nobody owes anyone kindness, so he remembers every favour done for him and tries to repay it.Chapter 1 He is frugal to the point that friends call him a miser, yet he gives freely to people he cares about. He thinks before acting and tries to see situations from every side. During his journey with [[A'Liang]], he constantly second-guessed himself and tried to read what the swordsman wanted of him. He later recognised this as one of the hardest tests he ever faced.Chapter 605 He keeps the principles he learns from Qi Jingchun, A'Liang, Old Man Yao and others, and holds himself to them. == Background == Chen Ping'an's parents died when he was very young, leaving him alone in the family home on [[Small Town|Clay Vase Alley]]. He worked as an apprentice at the dragon kilns under [[Old Man Yao]]. His father had shattered his [[Natal Porcelain|bonded porcelain]] before he turned six. This cut him off from the fated opportunities other town children had, but it also freed him from the ties that came with them.Chapter 63 He met [[Ning Yao]] after being brought to his house due to her injuries, and the two grew close.Chapter 15 Before leaving the town, [[Qi Jingchun]] gave him a green jade hairpin as a parting gift. The hairpin came from Qi Jingchun's own teacher.Chapter 24 With the wealth he gained in the town, he bought five mountains from Ruan Qiong's map, including [[Downtrodden Mountain]], which later became the seat of his own mountain.Chapter 80 At fourteen, he set out to escort Li Baoping, Li Huai and Lin Shouyi to Mountain Cliff Academy, travelling part of the way with A'Liang.Chapter 134 Back in his home region, an old man who called himself Cui Chan's grandfather put him through brutal training in fist techniques.Chapter 196 The old man was later revealed to be Cui Cheng, a former head of the Cui Clan. During his travels Chen Ping'an took Pei Qian as his opening disciple.Chapter 377 == Trivia == * He was born on the fifth day of the fifth month. The townsfolk believed it was the unluckiest day of the year, when the five poisonous creatures come out, and some neighbours were wary of him because of it.Chapter 14 * "Ping'an" means safe and sound, and can also mean peace. * As a small child he went to the Yang family medicine shop again and again to buy medicine for his sick mother, often without enough money. Old Man Yang took pity on him and gave him a cheap recipe, but his mother died that winter. * The first time he went into the mountains to collect herbs, the basket was nearly as big as he was. His shoulders hurt so much that he dropped it and cried at the foot of the mountain. * Old Man Yao never formally accepted him as a disciple because of his mediocre talent for porcelain. Liu Xianyang was the master's favourite instead. * He spent 100 taels of silver on four jade hairpins on his first journey. He kept one for himself and carved the other three for Li Baoping, Lin Shouyi and Li Huai, writing "Huaiyin" (locust shade) on Li Huai's so that it would have two characters like the others. * He only began practising fist techniques at around fourteen.Chapter 532 * When he returned to Mountain Cliff Academy, he had become the Scholarly Sage's closing disciple and the junior brother of Qi Jingchun and Zuo You.Chapter 402 Mao Xiaodong greeted him as the junior brother he had long been waiting for. * He once hid his identity under the name "Chen Haoren", which means "good person". * At the Sword Qi Great Wall, people called him the Ning Residence's son-in-law. == References == {{Navbox/Donghua}}

pages.title: Chen Ping An/History
pages.content:
{{Tabs|tab1=Chen Ping An|tab2=History|tab3=Cultivation|tab4=Techniques|tab5=Items|tab6=Relationships|tab7=Fights}}

== Volume 1: Caged Sparrow (Chapters 1 to 84) ==
After the kilns closed, Chen Ping'an earned coins delivering letters at the town's eastern gate. He took in an injured young swordswoman, [[Ning Yao]], and the two became close. When Chen Ping'an's life was in danger, [[Qi Jingchun]] asked the town's old locust tree for a blessed leaf on his behalf. A single leaf fell bearing the character "Yao," and Chen Ping'an vowed to save any member of the Yao Clan connected to his old master, even at the cost of his life.Chapter 23

When outsiders came to the town for its treasures, he killed [[Cai Jinjian]] in an alley with a porcelain shard after she shattered his bridge of immortality. After the [[Mountain-Moving Ape]] of Sun Scorch Mountain left [[Liu Xianyang]] near death, Chen Ping'an used his locust leaf to keep his friend alive and then took on the ape himself. Qi Jingchun arranged for him to receive the Sword Nurturing Gourd, holding the flying swords First and Fifteenth. With the golden copper coins he received, he bought five mountains around the town, [[Downtrodden Mountain]] among them, and lent three of them out.Chapter 84 (2) 

== Volume 2: Traveling Boy (Chapters 85 to 178) ==
At Qi Jingchun's request, Chen Ping'an escorted [[Li Baoping]], [[Li Huai]], [[Lin Shouyi]] and other children from the town to [[Mountain Cliff Academy]] in the Great Sui Nation. He wove a bamboo bookcase for the road and travelled with [[A'Liang]], who taught him the Eighteen Stops, and with [[Zhu He]] and his daughter [[Zhu Lu]].

On the way he met the old scholar, the [[Scholarly Sage]]. Over wine one night, the old scholar asked whether he was willing to follow Qi Jingchun's arrangement and become his disciple.Chapter 154 (2) The young Cui Chan, later known as [[Cui Dongshan]], joined the group. Chen Ping'an agreed to accept him as a student on one condition, that he sincerely protect the children.Chapter 163 After delivering the children safely, Chen Ping'an set off home alone.

== Volume 3: Golden Saber Coin (Chapters 179 to 238) ==
Back home, Chen Ping'an trained under a barefoot old man in the bamboo building on Downtrodden Mountain. The old man was [[Cui Cheng]], Cui Dongshan's grandfather, and he beat Chen Ping'an through countless sessions until he became a third tier martial artist.Chapter 197 (1) Chen Ping'an traded his jade hairpin for the flying sword Fifteenth, then set out south with his swords to find Ning Yao. On the road he travelled with the young Daoist [[Zhang Shanfeng]] and the martial artist [[Xu Yuanxia]], and he helped the ghost scholar Yang Huang and settled the trouble in the Colorful Garment Nation's prefectural city. He then prepares to cross the sea to [[Stalactite Mountain]] to deliver Ning Yao's sword.

== Volume 4: Approaching Sword Qi (Chapters 239 to 295) ==
Chen Ping'an passed through the Water Combing Nation and met the old sword saint Song Yushao. At [[Old Dragon City]] he befriended the Fan Clan and saw [[Zheng Dafeng]] again, and by then he had reached the fourth tier. He sailed from Osmanthus Island to Stalactite Mountain and finally reached the [[Sword Qi Great Wall]], where he was reunited with and confessed his feelings to Ning Yao.

There he met the old great sword immortal [[Chen Qingdu]] and his senior brother [[Zuo You]], and he fought a series of duels on the city wall against fourth tier opponents, among them [[Cao Ci]] of the Great Duan Empire. He then headed north again. He travelled for a time with [[Lu Tai]] of the Lu Clan and passed through Flying Eagle Fortress.

== Volume 5: Dao Observing Dao (Chapters 296 to 359) ==
After parting with Lu Tai, Chen Ping'an stumbled into the [[Lotus Flower Blessed Land]]. The martial artists there fought for a chance to ascend, and he clashed with [[Ding Ying]], [[Zhong Qiu]], [[Yu Zhenyi]] and others. He took the street orphan [[Pei Qian]] under his wing, and on leaving the Blessed Land he broke through straight to the fifth tier.Chapter 327 (1)

Travelling on with Pei Qian, he crossed paths with the Yao Clan of the Great Quan Empire, whose locust leaf linked back to his childhood vow. He passed through [[Fox Town]] and helped the water god of Burial River with the aid of the scholar [[Zhong Kui]].

== Volume 6: Little Teacher (Chapters 360 to 455) ==
Chen Ping'an returned to Old Dragon City, then travelled the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent. He met old friends far from home and took Pei Qian and his companions north to Mountain Cliff Academy. He then went to Bamboo Scroll Lake. There [[Gu Can]] had become the disciple of [[Liu Zhimao]] and killed many innocent people. When Gu Can refused to see his wrongs, Chen Ping'an settled for the next best thing. He stayed on the lake for a long time, tracking down the victims and their families and making amends on his friend's behalf, a period that shook him deeply.Chapter 436 (1)

== Volume 7: Dragon Raising Head (Chapters 456 to 515) ==
After handing Gu Can his account books, Chen Ping'an left Bamboo Scroll Lake and finally returned to Downtrodden Mountain, where Cui Cheng beat him in another round of training. He then travelled to the Northern Complete Reed Continent. He went through Skeleton Wall City and its ghost cities, and on the road he called himself Chen Haoren, a name meant to remind himself not to swing from one extreme to the other.Chapter 509 (2)

== Volume 8: No Evil Thoughts (Chapters 516 to 570) ==
Chen Ping'an escorted [[Sui Jingcheng]]'s group for part of their journey, crossed swords with the sword prodigy [[Qi Jinglong]] and his disciple [[Bai Shou]], and sparred with [[Li Er]]. On Lion Peak he broke through to the seventh tier, the Vajra Body Tier.Chapter 570 (1) He returned home to set up Downtrodden Mountain's ancestral hall, then left again for the Sword Qi Great Wall.

== Volume 9: Moon in the Sky (Chapters 571 to 660 - Ongoing) ==
Chen Ping'an returned to the Sword Qi Great Wall and Ning Yao. He fought a run of challenges from the city's young sword cultivators and became the second shopkeeper of a wine shop. Chen Qingdu agreed to act as his matchmaker in proposing to the Ning Clan.Chapter 578 (2) When the Savage World attacked, he fought on the wall and was badly hurt, falling several tiers as a Qi refiner. Liu Xianyang arrived and taught him his family's sword scripture.

After the previous Hidden Official left, Chen Ping'an was named the new Hidden Official. He was the youngest in the Sword Qi Great Wall's history and had the lowest cultivation base of any who had held the post.Chapter 626 (2) He reorganised the Hidden Official's lineage, survived attempts on his life and led sword cultivators onto the battlefield.

{| class="fandom-table"
!Weapons
!Chapter 
!Notes
|-
|'''Locust Wood Sword (Eliminating Fiends)'''
|
|Initially crafted from a locust branch, it's later revealed to have an incense entity residing within. Chen Ping'an considers it too light for his liking but continues to use it. Chen Ping'an also refers to it as being from Mr. Qi.  He eventually allows Ning Yao to look after the sword for him.
|-
|'''Empty Sword Scabbard'''
|
|Chen Ping'an receives it with a sense of bewilderment, wondering where he would find a sword to put in it.
|-
|'''Wooden Sword'''
|
|He was looking for a branch to craft a wooden sword previously.   The sword is implied to have been a gift of some sort, and Chen Ping'an does not seem to craft it himself.
|-
|'''Green Bamboo Scabbard'''
|
|The scabbard is noted to belong to a boastful swordsman who uses a saber as a substitute for his sword.   The sword in the azure bamboo scabbard is a renowned sword by the name of "Immovable".
|-
|'''Silver Sword Billet (Little Capital/First)'''
|
|Chen Ping'an feels nothing from the sword billet when he first receives it. He speculates that the sword spirit would disappear for a decade to sharpen the blade using a piece of Dragon Slaying Platform. The Scholarly Sage calls it "Little Capital," but Chen Ping'an prefers "First". It becomes a flying sword, and is later stored in a Sword Nurturing Gourd.
|-
|'''Emerald Green Jasper Sword (Fifteenth)'''
|
|It's given as a pocket treasure and a high-quality bonded flying sword. It has a cool aura that turns into warmth once inside Chen Ping'an's body. He learns mantras to control it. It is stored in the Sword Nurturing Gourd.
|-
|'''Subduing Demons (Sword in Sword Case)'''
|
|Chen Ping'an carries this sword in his sword case but does not use it, as it is someone else's. Chen Ping'an does not like the weight of his locust wood sword, and feels he needs a heavier practice sword.  He does not appear to acquire this sword in the text.
|-
|'''Li Baoping's Saber (Auspicious Talisman)'''
|
|Chen Ping'an sharpens the blade of this saber using Dragon Slaying Platform in secret. It's called Auspicious Talisman by A'Liang.
|-
|'''Halting Snow (Slender Saber)'''
|
|It is drawn during an interaction with Yu Zhenyi.
|-
|'''True Martial Sword'''
|
|He later plans to retrieve this sword. Zhang Shanfeng mentions it with hesitation.
|}
.
{| class="fandom-table"
!Items
!Chapter 
!Description
|-
|'''Copper Coins'''
|
|Chen Ping'an earns five copper coins from delivering letters. He later uses copper coins to purchase items and receives them as payment or gifts.
|-
|'''Yellow Paper Talisman'''
|
|Chen Ping'an commissions a daoist priest to write a yellow paper talisman.  He later learns to write talismans himself, even without ink. He uses talismans for healing, protection and to release a spirit from a talisman. Chen Ping'an also uses talismans to open doors for yin entities.
|-
|'''Medicinal Ingredients'''
|
|Chen Ping'an is sent to purchase medicinal ingredients for a woman he is helping. He later gathers medicinal ingredients in the mountains. He also has a medicinal recipe from Lu Chen.
|-
|'''Gold Essence Copper Coins'''
|
|Fu Nanhua offers Song Jixin a pouch of gold essence copper coins for a teapot. Chen Ping'an later comes into possession of multiple pouches . These are considered precious, even by immortals. He later gives some away to others.
|-
|'''Mandrill Teapot'''
|
|Song Jixin offers to sell a mandrill teapot in exchange for gold essence coins and other conditions.
|-
|'''Ancient Book'''
|
|Chen Ping'an finds a book wrapped in parchment paper, that is later revealed to have the character "mountain" on the cover. The book was obtained from Gu Can's house It is an ancient text. He intends to return it someday.  He uses this text for reading practice.
|-
|'''Jade Hairpin'''
|
|Mr. Qi gives Chen Ping'an a jade hairpin.  Chen Ping'an later gives the hairpin to Ning Yao for safekeeping. Chen Ping'an later engraves characters on a white jade hairpin and wears it.
|-
|'''Dragon Slaying Platform Shard'''
|
|Chen Ping'an finds a piece of the Dragon Slaying Platform, which he believes to be very precious.  The sword spirit uses this to sharpen the edge of her blade.
|-
|'''Offering Coins, Good Fortune Coins, and Greeting Spring Coins'''
|
|Chen Ping'an tallies his assets and finds that he has three types of gold essence copper coins: Offering Coins, Good Fortune Coins, and Greeting Spring Coins.
|-
|'''Wooden Figure'''
|
|Chen Ping'an finds a wooden figure that he chops into pieces. He finds red spots and tiny black characters engraved on it.
|-
|'''"Severed Water Cliff" Book'''
|
|Li Huai is in possession of a book called Severed Water Cliff. The book itself isn't valuable, but it is made of a relatively valuable material.  Li Huai uses it to catch a fish. Li Huai also carries this book in his bookcase. Li Huai offers the book back to Chen Ping'an later.
|-
|'''"Blessed Beast and Spirit Album"'''
|
|Cui Chan offers Chen Ping'an a copy of the "Blessed Beast and Spirit Album" as a gift, which he claims is very precious.
|-
|'''Silver Ingot'''
|
|Cui Dongshan gives Li Huai a silver ingot. Li Huai puts the silver in his bookcase. Chen Ping'an later tells Li Huai it is his to keep
|-
|'''Carving Knife'''
|
|A shopkeeper gifts Chen Ping'an a small carving knife used by jade workers. He uses this knife to engrave jade hairpins and bamboo slips.
|-
|'''"Mountain Scouring Album"'''
|
|Chen Ping'an gives the "Mountain Scouring Album" to Lin Shouyi.
|-
|'''Maps'''
|
|Chen Ping'an receives maps from the office of the county magistrate, which were offered to Ruan Xiu. Chen Ping'an later uses the map to determine where Yang Huang's estate is.
|-
|'''Wine Gourd'''
|
|Chen Ping'an carries a wine gourd. He gets it refilled with wine.
|-
|'''Geomancy Map'''
|
|Chen Ping'an gets Liu Gaohua to help him sneak out a geomancy map. Chen Ping'an stamps his mountain and water seals onto it. Later he stamps his water seal onto a geomancy map.
|-
|'''Ebony''' & '''White Bowl'''
|
|Chen Ping'an obtains a piece of ebony and a white bowl. He stores them in his pocket treasure.
|-
|'''Ink Brush Washer'''
|
|Chen Ping'an obtains an ink brush washer with a circle of text on the underside. He likes the character for "spring" on it.
|-
|'''Proper Sword Scripture'''
|
|Zheng Dafeng gives Chen Ping'an a book called Proper Sword Scripture. The title of the book is a display of exceptional calligraphy.
|-
|'''Jade Tablet'''
|
|Zheng Dafeng gives Chen Ping'an a plain jade tablet, which is a minimization treasure. Chen Ping'an is accustomed to using Fifteenth, so he does not use this treasure.
|-
|'''Talisman Papers & Wind and Snow Awl'''
|
|Mr. Qi gives Chen Ping'an an elementary book about talismans, talisman papers, and a Wind and Snow Awl which enables him to draw talismans without ink. Chen Ping'an uses the Wind and Snow Awl to draw talismans.
|-
|'''"Lush Mountain Green Water Copybook" & "Teacher, Please Put More Oil and Salt in Your Dishes" Copybooks'''
|
|Chen Ping'an has two copybooks: the "Lush Mountain Green Water Copybook" and "Teacher, Please Put More Oil and Salt in Your Dishes". The first is a serious copybook, while the other is more absurd.
|-
|'''Small Silver Sword Billet'''
|
|Chen Ping'an has a small sword billet that resembles a silver ingot, which is related to Tassel Mountain of the Middle Earth Divine Continent. The sword billet can light the way at night. Chen Ping'an waits for the sword spirit to return.
|-
|'''Mountain and Water Seals'''
|
|Chen Ping'an owns a pair of Mountain and Water Seals.  He stamps them onto a map. His mountain seal is destroyed, leaving his water seal lonely.  He stamps the water seal on a geomancy map.
|-
|'''"Tranquil Mind Begets Enlightenment" Seal'''
|
|Chen Ping'an possesses the "Tranquil Mind Begets Enlightenment" seal.
|-
|'''Medicinal Recipes'''
|
|Chen Ping'an has a medicinal recipe left by Daoist Lu. He uses the recipe for reference. He gives this recipe to He Xiaoliang, who stores it in her lotus leaf pocket treasure.
|-
|'''Golden Lotus Flower Seed'''
|
|Chen Ping'an obtains a withered golden lotus flower seed on Go Table Mountain. He is unsure of its purpose.
|-
|'''Demon-Binding Chain'''
|
|Chen Ping'an refines a demon-binding chain.
|-
|'''Sword Nurturing Gourd'''
|
|Chen Ping'an owns a Sword Nurturing Gourd.
|-
|'''Sword Edict Talisman'''
|
|Chen Ping'an possesses a Sword Edict Talisman, which is an ancient talisman.
|-
|'''Bamboo Slips'''
|
|Chen Ping'an has bamboo slips from Go Table Mountain, which he engraves with quotes and sayings. He obtains more bamboo slips from the divine mountain in Bamboo Sea Small World. Chen Ping'an cherishes these bamboo slips.
|-
|'''"Mountain and Sea Chronicle"'''
|
|Chen Ping'an has a copy of the "Mountain and Sea Chronicle", an all-encompassing divine book that records information about mystical realms.
|-
|'''Jade Pendant'''
|
|Chen Ping'an has a golden jade pendant that carries the inscription of "nurturing the noble spirit". It can absorb natural spiritual energy, but he can't wear it at the moment.
|-
|'''Cauldron'''
|
|Chen Ping'an purchases a cauldron from Lu Yong for fifty grain rain coins, to use in refining items.
|-
|'''Natural Treasures & Sands'''
|
|Chen Ping'an obtains about fifty types of natural treasures and twelve types of sand from Fan Junmao in exchange for the Nascent Tier food dragon's golden core, to use in the refinement process.
|-
|'''Miniaturization Treasure'''
|
|Chen Ping'an comes into possession of a miniaturization treasure. It is an imperial jade seal of a fallen nation. He is also given a white jade tablet that is also a minimization treasure by Zheng Dafeng.
|-
|'''Golden Core'''
|
|Chen Ping'an receives a golden scholarly core from City God Shen Wen. He later obtains an old flood dragon's golden core, which he gives to Fan Junmao.
|-
|'''"Principles of Life for Children"'''
|
|Chen Ping'an has a book called "Principles of Life for Children". He reads it to understand its deeper meaning, despite its seemingly shallow principles.
|-
|'''"Gently Flicking Iron Sword"'''
|
|Chen Ping'an has the book 'Gently Flicking Iron Sword'. He reads through it and engraves good sentences onto bamboo slips.
|-
|'''Sword Case Containing "Subduing Demons and Eliminating Fiends"'''
|
|Chen Ping'an carries a sword case containing the sword "Subduing Demons and Eliminating Fiends".
|-
|'''Lasting Qi'''
|
|Chen Qingdu originally intends to give the sword Lasting Qi to Ning Yao, but instructs Chen Ping'an to carry it to Parasol Leaf Continent instead. Chen Ping'an later places it back into its scabbard.
|-
|'''White Jade Hairpin'''
|
|Chen Ping'an intends to buy a white jade hairpin. Later, he wears a white jade hairpin, which Jiang Shangzhen notices has an inscription on it.
|-
|'''Picture Scroll'''
|
|Chen Ping'an has a picture scroll that "eats" grain rain coins.
|-
|'''"Authentic Death-Avoiding Book"'''
|
|Chen Ping'an obtains an elementary book about Daoist talismans called the "Authentic Death-Avoiding Book". Chen Ping'an memorizes the book and starts to practice talismans from it.
|-
|'''"Mountain Shaking Guide"'''
|
|Chen Ping'an owns the "Mountain Shaking Guide". He practices the sleeping meditation from this book.
|-
|'''Five-Colored Rope'''
|
|Lu Tai's five-colored rope was damaged in a fight.
|-
|'''Five Mountains Painting White Bowl'''
|
|Chen Ping'an has a white bowl with a painting of the Five Mountains on it.
|-
|'''Talismans Containing Skeletal Ghost'''
|
|Chen Ping'an owns a talisman containing a skeletal ghost. He has a beautiful ghost in a talisman, which he later releases.
|-
|'''"Proper Sword Scripture"'''
|
|Chen Ping'an owns a book called "Proper Sword Scripture", which he studies.
|-
|'''"Lesser Heat Coins"'''
|

pages.title: Chen Ping An/Relationships
pages.content:
{{Tabs|tab1=Chen Ping An|tab2=History|tab3=Cultivation|tab4=Techniques|tab5=Items|tab6=Relationships|tab7=Fights}}
== Friends ==
Chen Ping'an has formed several key friendships throughout the story, each with its own unique dynamics and importance. These relationships are often complex, going beyond simple camaraderie and touching on themes of loyalty, obligation, and mutual growth. Here is a breakdown of some of his most significant friendships:

* '''[[Gu Can]]:''' Chen Ping'an is a significant figure in Gu Can's life. It seems that Gu Can has accepted Chen Ping'an as his only close companion outside his mother. Chen Ping'an also takes on a mentor-like role, advising Gu Can to look after his mother and be careful of his master. This relationship highlights Chen Ping'an's protective nature and his willingness to look out for those who are vulnerable.
* '''[[Ning Yao]]:''' Ning Yao's relationship with Chen Ping'an is complex and evolves throughout the sources. She initially appears as someone who is unwilling to accept help, but later accepts Chen Ping'an's help, stating that she will repay him for saving her life. She becomes more familiar with him, and their interactions are marked by a certain level of banter. She also recognizes his kind nature and makes an agreement to repay him for his help. '''Their relationship is significant because it shows a deep connection and understanding, and it is also suggested that they have some fated ties'''. She openly admits she does not dislike him, but also does not give a clear answer when asked if she likes him. '''She is also the person he intends to account to for any money he spends'''. They are so close that she can understand his character by looking at the gifts he has given her.
* '''[[Liu Xianyang]]:''' While not as extensively detailed as other relationships, Liu Xianyang is mentioned as one of the people whose safety and happiness Chen Ping'an cares about. Chen Ping'an also appears to value Liu Xianyang's friendship, as he was willing to give away three pouches of coins to him. Chen Ping'an acknowledges that they became friends in the first place because of a specific reason, perhaps a shared experience or value. Chen Ping'an is also willing to help Liu Xianyang's business, and to introduce Fan Er to Liu Xianyang if the opportunity arises.
* '''Song Jixin:''' Despite being neighbors, Chen Ping'an does not consider Song Jixin a true friend. Chen Ping'an dislikes Song Jixin because of the way he treats others. '''Chen Ping'an cannot befriend people who are willing to add to the burdens of others'''.  Song Jixin, however, sees Chen Ping'an as someone he should befriend. This relationship highlights Chen Ping'an's strong moral compass and his inability to form genuine connections with those who do not share his values. Chen Ping'an makes a point to highlight how different his relationship with Song Jixin is from his friendship with others.
* '''[[A'Liang]]:''' A'Liang is a complex character who becomes a significant figure in Chen Ping'an's life. '''Chen Ping'an is suspicious of A'Liang, yet he also considers him to be a very interesting person'''. He enjoys A'Liang's company and is willing to have conversations with him.  A'Liang also acts as a mentor figure, giving him advice. A'Liang even seems to be interested in Chen Ping'an's romantic relationships. They have many conversations and A'Liang explains many things, which Chen Ping'an often finds confusing.
* '''[[Li Huai]]:''' Chen Ping'an has a close and caring relationship with Li Huai. Li Huai sees Chen Ping'an as a good person. Chen Ping'an has taught Li Huai important principles and supported him in various ways, and Li Huai recognizes all that Chen Ping'an has done for him. This relationship reflects Chen Ping'an's protective nature and his willingness to guide and support those younger than him.
* '''Lin Shouyi:''' Chen Ping'an's relationship with Lin Shouyi is somewhat different from his relationships with others. Lin Shouyi notes that Chen Ping'an seems to care for Li Baoping more than for him.  Chen Ping'an is aware of this, and he feels he has to explain situations to Li Baoping because he has a better understanding of her. Despite this, Chen Ping'an is willing to give Lin Shouyi valuable items and share his knowledge with him. '''Lin Shouyi recognizes that Chen Ping'an is more seriously injured than others, but that he is hiding his injuries well'''. He is also the person Chen Ping'an chooses to gift the 'Mountain Scouring Album' to.
* '''[[Li Baoping]]:'''  Chen Ping'an has a very close relationship with Li Baoping. Chen Ping'an explains things to her because he feels it's important she understands them. Chen Ping'an prioritizes her understanding and safety, indicating that he feels a sense of responsibility towards her. She is also one of the three people, along with Liu Xianyang and Gu Can, whose happiness and safety he prioritizes above all others. It is also suggested that Li Baoping will get angry for Chen Ping'an's sake if she feels like others are not treating him well.
* '''[[Zhang Shanfeng]] and [[Xu Yuanxia]]''': Chen Ping'an displays a high level of care and loyalty towards Zhang Shanfeng and Xu Yuanxia. He considers them his true friends and would offer help or advice without hesitation. '''When they meet again after some time apart, Chen Ping'an is overjoyed, stating that they are the only ones who would be willing to help him with a thankless task'''. Chen Ping'an also values these relationships so much that he is very willing to go to great lengths to help Xu Yuanxia with a situation, even if it means risking his own safety.
* '''[[Liu Baqiao]]:''' Liu Baqiao and Chen Ping'an have a complicated relationship.  Liu Baqiao is very friendly and considers Chen Ping'an to be a close friend.  Chen Ping'an, however, does not reciprocate the same level of friendship. He does not take Liu Baqiao seriously no matter how much the latter proclaims they are brothers. Despite this, Chen Ping'an still has a positive impression of Liu Baqiao.  '''It is noted that even after only two meetings, Chen Ping'an and Liu Baqiao already seem to be very close friends, while Sun Jiashu and Fu Nanhua could be friends for decades and never be very close'''.
* '''[[Sun Jiashu]]:''' Chen Ping'an and Sun Jiashu's relationship is primarily described in terms of business and strategic value. Sun Jiashu does not see Chen Ping'an as a close friend. Chen Ping'an also states that he is no longer friends with Sun Jiashu because he is not sufficiently earnest when it comes to certain things.  Chen Ping'an notes that Sun Jiashu sets a price tag on everyone he encounters, regarding them as a business asset.
* '''[[Fan Er]]:''' Chen Ping'an has a close friendship with Fan Er, and he is willing to reciprocate those feelings. Fan Er sees Chen Ping'an as a very close friend. Chen Ping'an genuinely envies Fan Er, who never seems to have a care in the world.
* '''[[Cui Chan]]:''' Chen Ping'an is aware that Cui Chan's intentions are not pure. Chen Ping'an does not trust Cui Chan and hopes that he will stay away from him. Despite this, Chen Ping'an and Cui Chan have a complex relationship that has a sense of interconnected fate to it.

These friendships reveal different facets of Chen Ping'an's character. He is loyal, protective, and deeply values genuine connections. He prioritizes the well-being of his friends, and does not form friendships easily with those who do not share his values.  He is also willing to help those in need, and he is often shown giving valuable gifts to those he considers friends. Chen Ping'an also recognizes that he cannot befriend everyone, and that some relationships are merely transactional. His interactions with others highlight his strong sense of morality and his preference for genuine, meaningful relationships over superficial ones.

== Foes ==
Chen Ping'an has a number of key enemies, and these relationships are often complex and deeply intertwined with his personal journey and the larger conflicts in the world around him. These relationships are not just about simple antagonism, but also about exploring themes of fate, justice, and the nature of good and evil. Here is a breakdown of some of his key enemies:

* '''[[Fu Nanhua]]''': Fu Nanhua is a significant enemy of Chen Ping'an, with their animosity stemming from a personal conflict in Chen Ping'an's hometown. Chen Ping'an almost killed Fu Nanhua in their first encounter. Fu Nanhua holds Chen Ping'an in contempt and is determined to kill him. '''Their conflict is personal, but also reflects the clash between different social classes and values, with Fu Nanhua viewing Chen Ping'an as a "piece of scum".''' Chen Ping'an knows he must be careful due to his history with Fu Nanhua.
* '''[[Sun Scorch Mountain]]:''' The people from Sun Scorch Mountain are a major threat to Chen Ping'an. '''They are described as a well-established and reputable sect, with members who are far more powerful than people like Fu Nanhua'''. Lu Zhengchun hates Liu Xianyang and wants to see him dead. Bai Yuan from Sun Scorch Mountain is convinced that Chen Ping'an is a pawn of a powerful mastermind, and is constantly looking for him. The Mountain-moving Ape from Sun Scorch Mountain is also noted as one of Chen Ping'an's mortal enemies that he must exact revenge on. These interactions are indicative of the conflicts between different factions and highlight the dangers Chen Ping'an faces.
* '''[[Ma Kuxuan]]''': Ma Kuxuan is a recurring enemy who detests Chen Ping'an. Their conflict seems to be a matter of fate, with their paths destined to clash. Their relationship is further complicated by the conflict between their fathers, of which Chen Ping'an is unaware. Chen Ping'an dislikes Ma Kuxuan just as much as Ma Kuxuan dislikes Chen Ping'an. They had previously fought to a draw, but Ma Kuxuan has advanced three tiers in a single year, making him an even more dangerous opponent. '''Their conflict represents a clash of destinies, and is possibly indicative of a larger, long-term rivalry that may play out through generations'''.
* '''[[Cui Chan]]:''' Cui Chan is a complex figure who acts as both a potential ally and an enemy. Chen Ping'an does not trust Cui Chan, and believes his intentions are not pure. Despite this, their fates seem interconnected. Cui Chan orchestrated a plot against Chen Ping'an and Qi Jingchun. '''Cui Chan also views Chen Ping'an as an obstacle in his pursuit of the Great Dao'''. He is an extremely cunning individual who is adept at hatching elaborate schemes. Cui Chan had been eavesdropping on Lin Shouyi, and he becomes enraged when he is insulted. Despite not trusting Cui Chan, Chen Ping'an acknowledges he is very intelligent. Cui Chan's motivations and schemes often make him a hidden enemy, whose actions directly affect Chen Ping'an's circumstances.
* '''[[Song Jixin]]:''' Although Song Jixin is Chen Ping'an's neighbor, they are not friends. Chen Ping'an dislikes him because of the way he treats others. Song Jixin was seen encouraging those who were beating Liu Xianyang. Chen Ping'an feels that Song Jixin would add to the burdens of others simply because he thinks it is fun. Song Jixin, however, views Chen Ping'an as someone he should befriend. '''This relationship highlights Chen Ping'an'an's strong moral compass and his inability to form genuine connections with those who do not share his values. While Song Jixin may not be an outright enemy, he represents a type of person that Chen Ping'an cannot accept.'''
* '''The [[Chen Clan]]''': Chen Ping'an's own clan also appears to be his enemies. His clan does not see Chen Ping'an as one of their own, and they are hoping that he will be killed so that they can benefit from his death. Chen Ping'an's branch of the Chen Clan has fallen to a miserable state. The Chen Clan in the small town only has one member who is not a servant or a maid. The enemies of the Chen Clan also see Chen Ping'an as an enemy because of his relation to the clan.
* '''Ding Ying:''' Ding Ying was once considered the most powerful person in the world, and was an enemy of Chen Ping'an. Chen Ping'an ultimately defeats Ding Ying, killing him in a head-on battle. '''Ding Ying is an example of an enemy who represents a large and powerful organization, whose intentions are difficult to discern.''' Ding Ying also mistakenly believed that Cao Qinglang was related to Mirror Heart Hall's Tong Qingqing.
* '''Yu Zhenyi''': Yu Zhenyi is another powerful enemy who allies himself with Ding Ying. However, Yu Zhenyi is also an enemy of otherworldly immortals, meaning that Chen Ping'an is also one of his targets. Yu Zhenyi is only willing to target other otherworldly immortals. Chen Ping'an is one of the people Yu Zhenyi fears most due to his ability to kill Ding Ying. '''Yu Zhenyi's motivations are complex and are tied to his own ambitions and his role in a larger power struggle. Chen Ping'an does not believe that Yu Zhenyi's actions were justified.'''
* '''[[Pei Qian]]:''' Although Pei Qian becomes a companion of Chen Ping'an, she is also described as someone Chen Ping'an genuinely detests. '''Despite traveling together, Pei Qian's actions and behaviors are described as a mirror by which Chen Ping'an uses to look back at himself, which is indicative of their conflicting personalities.''' They have a difficult and complicated relationship.
* '''[[Old Man Yang]]:''' Old Man Yang is not necessarily an enemy, but he is a complex character who is implied to have some connection to Chen Ping'an's past. Old Man Yang was aware of what was going to happen to Chen Ping'an's father, but he did not intervene. Chen Ping'an may resent him for his inaction. The fact that Old Man Yang may have known about the events surrounding Chen Ping'an's father and did not intervene creates a complicated relationship dynamic where he is not necessarily an enemy, but is not a friend either.
* '''Unnamed individuals:''' There are several unnamed enemies mentioned as well. There are assassins from the Case Purchasing Pagoda and Grandmaster Lin Gushan from Colorful Garment Nation who team up to attack Chen Ping'an. There is also a powerful woman in the Great Li Empire who resents Song Changjing and who orchestrated the shattering of Chen Ping'an's bonded porcelain. There are also those who are betting on when Chen Ping'an will be killed.

These enemies and rivalries highlight the complex and dangerous world Chen Ping'an navigates. They reveal a world where personal grievances, political schemes, and the pursuit of power all intertwine. Chen Ping'an is not simply a passive observer in these conflicts, but a significant player whose actions and choices shape his relationships and his own destiny. These relationships also serve to highlight his strong moral compass, as well as the kind of person he is.

== Mentors ==
Chen Ping'an has several key mentors who have significantly influenced his life, each relationship marked by unique intricacies and importance. These mentors have shaped not only his skills, but also his understanding of the world and his place in it.

* '''[[Old Yao|Old Man Yao]]:''' Old Man Yao, a potter, is one of Chen Ping'an's early mentors. Although he was often stingy with his best skills, Chen Ping'an diligently practiced whatever Old Man Yao was willing to teach him. Chen Ping'an would also commit all of Old Man Yao's stories to memory. This relationship highlights Chen Ping'an's dedication and willingness to learn from even the most reluctant of teachers. Despite Old Man Yao's reluctance to fully teach Chen Ping'an, he still had a significant impact on Chen Ping'an's life.
* '''Mr. Qi([[Qi Jingchun]]):''' Mr. Qi is a crucial mentor figure for Chen Ping'an. '''Mr. Qi provides Chen Ping'an with background information about his parents and the world, and gives him the jade hairpin, a representation of the deep relationship between Mr. Qi and his teacher'''. Chen Ping'an trusts Mr. Qi, and believes in the rules Mr. Qi once followed. Mr. Qi also tries to persuade Chen Ping'an not to kill Fu Nanhua. Chen Ping'an deeply respects Mr. Qi.
* '''[[Ruan Qiong]]:''' Ruan Qiong, a blacksmith, takes Chen Ping'an in as a laborer. This relationship is significant because Master Ruan allows Chen Ping'an to purchase five mountains. '''Chen Ping'an relies on the promises and rules set by Master Ruan, but does not necessarily trust him implicitly''', which highlights Chen Ping'an's cautious nature. Master Ruan also gives Chen Ping'an maps.
* '''Cui Chan's grandfather:''' [[Cui Cheng]] teaches Chen Ping'an his fist techniques, although he does not teach Chen Ping'an everything. The less he teaches Chen Ping'an, the more it reflects his lofty expectations of him. '''This mentorship is important because it provides Chen Ping'an with a foundation for his martial arts training''', and suggests a path for growth based on individual experience rather than strict instruction.
* '''[[A'Liang]]:''' A'Liang is an enigmatic figure who also acts as a mentor to Chen Ping'an. He teaches Chen Ping'an persuasive speaking techniques. '''A'Liang's approach is often unconventional, using complicated words and profound reasoning to explain simple things, which helps Chen Ping'an understand complex concepts'''. A'Liang also believes that there are too many distractions on the path to cultivation, and he attempts to help Chen Ping'an in his cultivation. Chen Ping'an respects A'Liang and his knowledge.
* '''[[Zhu He]]:''' Zhu He is a martial arts master and a patriarch of the Li Clan. He provides Chen Ping'an with valuable knowledge about martial arts, and explains the Wooden Fetus Tier. Zhu He also advises Chen Ping'an to cherish his bonds with Master Ruan and Ning Yao. '''His guidance on martial arts and his emphasis on enduring hardship are significant for Chen Ping'an's growth'''.
* '''[[Scholarly Sage]]''': The Scholarly Sage is Mr. Qi's teacher, and is also an indirect mentor to Chen Ping'an. Chen Ping'an is interested in comparing the books of the Scholarly Sage with those of the Second Sage. '''Chen Ping'an respects and admires the Scholarly Sage''', which is evident in his desire to learn from the Scholarly Sage's teachings. The Scholarly Sage offers to take Chen Ping'an as his final disciple.
* '''[[Zheng Dafeng]]:''' Zheng Dafeng becomes Chen Ping'an's Dao mentor, though their relationship is initially marked by friction. Zheng Dafeng does not warm up to Chen Ping'an and views him as too boring. '''Despite this, their interactions lead Zheng Dafeng to recognize Chen Ping'an's unique path, and ultimately to acknowledge him as his Dao mentor'''. Zheng Dafeng acknowledges that Chen Ping'an's path has to be acknowledged for getting him to that point.
* '''External Heavenly Master from Mount Longhu''': This old Daoist priest is an external Heavenly Master from Mount Longhu, who is Zhang Shanfeng's master. This mentor is important because he acknowledges that Chen Ping'an's bonded item is filled with an immortal aura.

These mentors each contribute to Chen Ping'an's development in different ways. Some provide practical skills, others offer moral and philosophical guidance, while others challenge him to grow and question his own beliefs. These relationships highlight Chen Ping'an's openness to learning from diverse sources, and his ability to integrate these lessons into his personal growth.

Dong Sangeng|Enemie(s)=The old man in gray, [[Demon Tribe]]|Cultivation_rank=Sword Immortal|Clansmen=Chen Xi}} '''Chen Qingdu''' is the strongest sword cultivator on the [[Sword Qi Great Wall]] and one of the most powerful beings in existence, said to be only slightly beneath the Paramount Sage, the Dao Ancestor, and Buddha.Chapter 584 He guarded the wall for over ten thousand years without once leaving, not even to attend weddings or funerals within his own [[Chen Clan]].Chapter 571 On the Sword Qi Great Wall, Chen Qingdu was the highest principle there was.Chapter 578 == Appearance == Chen Qingdu is a hunchbacked old man who has been unable to truly straighten his back throughout the past ten thousand years. He habitually clasps his hands behind his back and lives in a thatched cottage at the very top of the Sword Qi Great Wall. == Personality == Chen Qingdu is a man of few words who nonetheless becomes surprisingly chatty around people he is fond of. He has a dry, sometimes vulgar sense of humor, and enjoys needling [[Zuo You]] about his sword skills despite genuinely respecting them. Beneath his detached manner he keeps careful watch over every swordsman on the wall and cares deeply about matters most would consider beneath someone of his stature, such as whether children in the city are learning to read and write, which he sees as addressing the fundamental question of why sword cultivators fight and die at all. He holds firmly to the belief that sword cultivators exist to stand with the weak and challenge the strong. Those who view others as ants, he says, are nothing more than ants themselves.Chapter 649 He is not sentimental about death. In his eyes, no one is above it, including those he cares for.Chapter 615 Yet he is far from cynical. When asked whether humanity had disappointed him over the millennia, he replied that he had seen much more hope than despair.Chapter 633 He once told [[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]] that a person should be willing to act unreasonably once or twice every hundred years, a lesson Chen Ping'an took to heart.Chapter 279 == Background == Chen Qingdu is one of the earliest humans to learn the sword. His sword lineage, one of four original lines, carries the greatest destructive power of any. In the ancient era, he was among the humans who rose up against the deities who had kept humanity as livestock. After that great war ended, the sword cultivators who fought in it were treated as prisoners and exiled to the Sword Qi Great Wall, tasked with holding the line between the Majestic World and the Savage World indefinitely. In the distant past, Chen Qingdu led Long Jun and Guan Zhao to challenge the demon ancestor at Holding Moon Mountain. Guan Zhao was killed. Long Jun's soul was shattered. Chen Qingdu returned alone, and Holding Moon Mountain was left in ruins behind him.Chapter 613 He himself has died once, in a sense, during those ancient battles, though he survived and continued his vigil. For over ten thousand years he never left the wall. The Sword Qi Great Wall was Chen Qingdu, and Chen Qingdu was the Sword Qi Great Wall.Chapter 626 Even visiting sages of the Three Teachings trod carefully around him. A Confucian sage once came to complain about the wall's conduct. Chen Qingdu told him they could talk after a fight. The sage fought three bouts, won two, lost one to the Hidden Official, and departed in low spirits. The Daoist second disciple, for his part, chose not to fight Chen Qingdu at all. During the events of the novel, Chen Qingdu killed Dong Guanpu, a demon tribe spy from a prominent sword cultivator clan, with a single offhand sword strike after Dong Guanpu attempted to act against Chen Ping'an. He later lent his own sword, Lasting Qi, to Chen Ping'an for a critical journey.Chapter 322 When the demon tribe proposed a trade of worlds to avoid further bloodshed, Chen Qingdu flatly refused.Chapter 589 After the Mirage Market assassination attempt on [[Ning Yao]], he wounded the [[Chen Clan]] leader for failing to prevent it. Chen Qingdu took a particular interest in Chen Ping'an's growth. He served as matchmaker for Chen Ping'an and Ning Yao's marriage proposal, helped Chen Ping'an refine his fifth bonded item and nurture his bonded flying sword,Chapter 619 and ultimately appointed him as the new Hidden Official after the previous one betrayed the wall.Chapter 627 He also deliberately suppressed Ning Yao's cultivation advancement using the Sword Qi Great Wall's sword dao, believing it was not yet time for her to break through. He had a complicated relationship with a tall woman who was the spirit of one of the oldest swords in existence. She was his senior by a wide margin, and her former owner had been one of the first people to teach Chen Qingdu the sword. When she visited the wall, she told Chen Qingdu to get lost and said she had come to visit "her master," meaning Chen Ping'an.Chapter 587 [[A'Liang]] spent a hundred years on the Sword Qi Great Wall. Chen Qingdu was fond of him despite comparing his constant chatter to a fly droning beside his ear. When A'Liang finally departed, Chen Qingdu told him not to come back. Chen Qingdu's ultimate opponent was the old man in gray, a manifestation of the Savage World's Great Dao itself. During the battle at the wall, the old man in gray faced one of Chen Qingdu's sword strikes directly. Before the final chapter of the wall's struggle, Chen Qingdu revealed two long-held secrets to Chen Ping'an concerning the true origins of the exiled sword cultivators' hometowns and the nature of the martial arts path as a road to godhood.Chapter 650 He had a habit of passing down the small thatched cottage behind his own to whichever young swordsman he was most taken with at the time. First it went to Cao Ci, then to Chen Ping'an, then to [[Wei Jin]]. == Trivia == * Chen Qingdu's sword is named Lasting Qi, which he once turned into a joke at the old man in gray's expense. * Despite never leaving the Sword Qi Great Wall in ten thousand years, he was aware of events across the Majestic World in remarkable detail. * He offered to teach [[Wei Jin]] sword techniques drawn from the foundation of one of his old friends, but only in exchange for battlefield merit. == References ==

[[Sword Qi Great Wall]] |Novel=Chapter 572 }} == Appearance == Chen Sanqiu is an extremely handsome young man, widely regarded as one of the most good-looking young masters on the city wall.Chapter 572 He carries two swords on his waist, an unsheathed blade called Cloud Pattern with the characters for “Cloud Pattern” engraved onto it in archaic text, and a sheathed sword called Scripture.Chapter 572 He wears a white Dao robe passed down by the ancestors of the Chen Clan of Taixiang Street.Chapter 617 == Personality == He is good-humored, quick with a joke, and genuinely devoted to his friends, even when that means covering their bar tabs or dragging a drunk friend home night after night.Chapter 586 He has carried an unrequited devotion to Dong Huafu’s older sister, Dong Bude, for years without ever being discouraged by her repeated rejection, and he is remembered as a surprisingly heavy drinker whenever his feelings get the better of him.Chapter 574 Despite his status as the young master of a top-notch clan, he treats friends from far poorer backgrounds, such as Fan Dache and the wine shop’s workers, with genuine warmth rather than condescension.Chapter 590 He trains hard out of a quiet determination to keep the gap between his own cultivation and Ning Yao’s from growing too wide, even though he never mentions this openly.Chapter 575 == Background == Chen Sanqiu is the young master of the Chen Clan on Taixiang Street at the Sword Qi Great Wall, one of a close group of young prodigies there that includes Ning Yao, Die Zhang, Yan Zhuo, and Dong Huafu. As a child he idolized the legendary swordsman A’Liang, tagging along after him in hopes of free wine and picking up plenty of bad habits in the process, though he learned little actual swordsmanship from him. Before A’Liang’s departure from the Sword Qi Great Wall, the two shared a drink together, and A’Liang’s parting words left such a deep impression on Chen Sanqiu that he got thoroughly drunk afterward cursing him for sharing them.Chapter 574 He has been in love with Dong Huafu’s older sister, Dong Bude, since childhood, but she has always turned him down, telling her brother privately that she disliked Chen Sanqiu simply because he was too handsome, a reason even her own brother found hard to accept as legitimate. Despite the rejection, Chen Sanqiu has remained popular with many other women, and the local wine shops have long been willing to extend him credit without hesitation.Chapter 574 His sword Cloud Pattern originally belonged to his close friend, Little Ququ, a young man who rose from an impoverished background and shared Chen Sanqiu’s ambition to travel south and earn military merit on the battlefield. After Little Ququ died in battle, Chen Sanqiu inherited the sword, carrying it without a scabbard for years until he eventually bought one from the sword market.Chapter 611Chapter 617 When Chen Ping’an arrived at the Sword Qi Great Wall and began challenging established young sword cultivators, Chen Sanqiu was skeptical of his chances at first but came to accept him as a friend once he saw his resolve, eventually becoming one of his regular drinking companions at Die Zhang’s wine shop.Chapter 575 He helped Chen Ping’an and Die Zhang’s wine shop get off the ground by taking a cut of its profits in exchange for occasionally sending customers their way, and he personally helped Chen Ping’an acquire printed books and essay collections from the Mirage Market.Chapter 590 He played a key role in smoothing over a falling-out between their friend group and Fan Dache, a clan descendant whose drinking and heartbreak over a failed engagement nearly cost him his place among their circle, personally dragging him home and paying for the damages when things got out of hand.Chapter 586Chapter 587 On the battlefield south of the city wall, Chen Sanqiu fights alongside Ning Yao, Die Zhang, Dong Huafu, and Yan Zhuo, coordinating his flying sword with theirs to cover their weaknesses, and he has lost close friends and even his first guardian swordsman to the fighting there over the years.Chapter 574Chapter 617 == Trivia == * He once purchased an exquisite seal inscribed with “My heart is set on my beloved, I think of her and I long for her,” a piece he liked so much he bought it outright rather than simply appraising it.Chapter 590 * His old ancestor, Chen Xi, once appeared unannounced during his sword training to remark cryptically that it was about time for “the old monk who’s been nodding off on the city wall for many years to open his eyes.”Chapter 611 * He lent his original sword to his friend Fan Dache, who struggled for years to break through to the Golden Core Tier.Chapter 617 == References ==

pages.title: Clans
pages.content:
{{Spoilers}}
'''Clans''' are the great families. Many hold dragon kilns, intercontinental ships, armies or mountains, and some are tied by marriage or old debts to sects and empires across several continents. 

== Eastern Treasured Vial Continent ==

=== Four Families and Ten Clans ===
The Four Families and Ten Clans, also called the Four Surnames and Ten Clans, are the leading households of the small town, living on [[Fortune Street]] and Peach Leaf Alley. The four great surnames of Fortune Street are Lu, Li, Zhao and Song, and between them they own ten large dragon kilns.Chapter 90 For centuries the clans schemed and shed blood over the town's thirty or so dragon kilns. After the town became Dragon Spring County, they were forced into an alliance, though each kept its own secret ties to the imperial court.Chapter 127

The Imperial Song Clan secretly favored them. Under a hidden pact with the sages, each clan could keep the bonded porcelains of one to three cultivation prodigies, who were allowed to cultivate inside the small world free of its usual suppression but could not leave without permission.Chapter 471 When Wu Yuan arrived as county magistrate, the clans gave him little help and mostly watched him struggle.

=== Lu Clan ===
The Lu Clan was the head of the Four Families and Ten Clans inside the town, yet the weakest of them outside it, because the empire it backed, the Lu Empire, was destroyed by the [[Great Li Empire]].Chapter 34 Its ties to the fallen empire left it worse off than any other clan after Jewel Small World fell to the ground. Lu Zhengchun left with a lady of the Xu Clan of Light Breeze City and became a direct disciple of that clan's ancestral hall.Chapter 651

=== Li Clan ===
The Li Clan of Fortune Street is led by Li Hong. His children are [[Li Xisheng]], [[Li Baozhen]] and [[Li Baoping]]. Their grandfather became the first cultivator of the Four Families and Ten Clans to reach the tenth tier.Chapter 206 He is a Nascent Tier earth immortal and a secret top guest elder of the Great Li Empire. [[Sun Scorch Mountain]] left [[Tao Zi]] in the clan's care while she was in the town. The Li Clan later moved away, and its two dragon kilns passed to the Wei and Liu clans of Peach Leaf Alley.

=== Zhao Clan ===
The Zhao Clan of Fortune Street keeps quiet about its wealth, unlike the Lu Clan, which likes to show off its power and present itself as a clan of scholars. [[Zhao Yao]] belongs to this clan.Chapter 27 Its head steward, like those of the Song Clan, comes from the town's Chen Clan, and the two sides treat each other almost as family.

=== Song Clan ===
The Song Clan of Fortune Street holds two pouches of gold essence copper coins, the most of any of the Four Families and Ten Clans. It is a separate household from the Imperial Song Clan of the [[Great Li Empire]].

=== Xie Clan ===
The Xie Clan lives on Peach Leaf Alley. Few in number and in decline, it survived for centuries thanks to a pair of incense entities. It was saved from worse when a long-eyebrowed boy of the clan became Ruan Qiong's unofficial disciple.Chapter 187 Its old ancestor is [[Xie Shi]], who returned with the sword immortal [[Cao Xi]] and stayed at the clan's residence. The Wind God Xie Clan of the Lu Empire is a separate family.

=== Wei Clan and Liu Clan ===
The Wei and Liu clans of Peach Leaf Alley took over the Li Clan's two dragon kilns after the Li Clan left the town.

=== Ma Clan ===
The Ma Clan is wealthy and owns two dragon kilns, but its ancestors forbade it from ever moving to Fortune Street or Peach Leaf Alley. [[Ma Kuxuan]] is a member.

=== Chen Clan of the small town ===
Almost everyone in the small town with the surname Chen works as a servant for the Four Families and Ten Clans, many of them for generations.Chapter 57 According to Chen Songfeng, the town once had two Chen Clans. One stayed and became servants, while the other left long ago for another continent and grew into the [[#Yingyin Chen Clan|Yingyin Chen Clan]].Chapter 61

=== Dragon Tail County Chen Clan ===
The Chen Clan of Dragon Tail County, also called the Dragon Tail Creek Chen Clan, is a wealthy scholarly clan with more than a thousand years of history. Its ancestral rules forbid it from taking part in other sects' and clans' conflicts, and it knows of the Yingyin Chen Clan only through a distant relationship. Chen Songfeng is its eldest grandson. It later opened a free private school in the small town that even the children of Lu Empire prisoners could attend.Chapter 188

=== Other small town families ===
* '''Yang Clan''' runs the Yang Family's medicine shop. It is well off but not part of the Four Families and Ten Clans, and every generation keeps a set of ancestral rules. Old Man Yang has watched over it for generations.Chapter 428
* '''Lin Clan''' is a large clan that is not part of the Four Families and Ten Clans and keeps to itself. [[Lin Shouyi]]'s father was a minor official in the kiln supervision office.
* '''Gu Clan''' is the family of [[Gu Can]]. His father Gu Tao became a yin god and later the mountain god of the Great Li Empire's old Northern Mountain.

=== Imperial Song Clan ===
The Imperial Song Clan rules the Great Li Empire. It rose from a small vassal state of the Lu Empire to rule the whole north of the continent.Chapter 189 Its Peace and Safety Tablets carry the clan's cloud pattern on their corners. It is a sworn enemy of the [[#Gao Clan|Gao Clan]] of the Great Sui Nation. See [[Great Li Empire]].

=== Yuan Clan ===
The Yuan Clan is a pillar clan in the capital of the Great Li Empire. Its ancestor Yuan Xie and the Cao Clan's ancestor Cao Hang came from the same place and fought side by side, and the history books call them the "twin jade pendants of scholarship and martial arts". The two clans once intermarried often, but over the past century or so they became hostile.Chapter 191 Wu Yuan married into the Yuan Clan. The new Wenchang pavilion in the small town honors Yuan Xie.

=== Cao Clan ===
The Cao Clan is the Yuan Clan's rival pillar clan. Cao Hang is shown on the door gods of Dragon Spring Prefecture and honored in its martial sage temple. Its most senior ancestor is the sword immortal Cao Xi of [[Southern Whirl Continent]], who outranks even the ancestor who won the clan its title. Only the eldest son of each generation is told.Chapter 201

=== Guan Clan ===
The Guan Clan is a pillar clan of the Great Li Empire whose patriarch oversees the Ministry of Personnel. Its direct grandson Guan Yiran served as the Great Li general stationed at [[Bamboo Scroll Lake]].Chapter 455

=== Yu Clan (Great Li) ===
The Yu Clan is one of two lesser-known pillar clans that rival the Yuan and Cao. It lives in the mountains and seldom takes part in mortal affairs.Chapter 450

=== Gao Clan ===
The Gao Clan, also called the Geyang Gao Clan, has ruled the [[Great Sui Nation]] for all of its 1,200 years. It is a mortal enemy of the Great Li Empire's Song Clan.Chapter 13 Gao Xuan is a member, and the clan's only Unpolished Jade Tier cultivator is an ancestor who works as a storyteller.

=== Cui Clan ===
The Cui Clan has been one of the most respected and highly educated clans on the continent for a thousand years.Chapter 243 It is the clan of [[Cui Chan]], and its old ancestor is the tenth tier martial artist [[Cui Cheng]].

=== Chu Clan ===
Several unrelated clans share this name. The Chu Clan of Prosperous City is an esteemed guest of the Great Li Empire, and its patriarch is deputy sect leader of Rattle Mountain. One of its young masters was beaten by Ruan Xiu.Chapter 94 The Chu Clan of the Yellow Court Nation is that nation's founding clan. The Chu Clan of Phoebe Creek in the Great Sui Nation was one of the clans Li Er named for punishment.

=== Xu Clan ===
The Xu Clan of Light Breeze City is a powerful force on the continent. It schemed for the armor handed down in [[Liu Xianyang]]'s family and won it in the small town.Chapter 65 It is known for its Fox Skin Beauty Talismans and later became a firm ally of Sun Scorch Mountain.

=== Fu Clan ===
The Fu Clan has ruled Old Dragon City for thousands of years. Countless emperors rose in the north of the continent, while the Fu Clan stayed dominant in the south.Chapter 251 Its leader, Fu Qi, is city lord, and Fu Nanhua is his favored heir. The clan owns two of the city's six intercontinental ships, a Treasure Swallowing Whale and a floating mountain known as a miniature [[Stalactite Mountain]].Chapter 252 Fu Nanhua's marriage to a woman of the Cloud Forest Jiang Clan brought a Nascent Tier maidservant and a young flood dragon as dowry.Chapter 361 After Sun Jiashu and the Ding Clan's Du Yan sided with it, the Fang and Hou clans had to follow its orders.Chapter 366

=== Sun Clan ===
The Sun Clan ranks second in Old Dragon City, ahead of the Fang, Hou and Ding clans. Every other major clan in the city has changed many times over the past few thousand years, but the Sun Clan has survived. Its own crises were all linked to the Sword Qi Great Wall. It owns the Mountain and Sea Turtle, and its rules forbid spending on things that are not needed. Its leader, Sun Jiashu, later lent Downtrodden Mountain three hundred grain rain coins.

=== Fan Clan ===
The Fan Clan of Old Dragon City owns the intercontinental ship Osmanthus Island and brews osmanthus wine. Its heir is [[Fan Er]], and his half-sister [[Fan Junmao]], a Nascent Tier cultivator, holds more sway than the whole ancestral hall.Chapter 362 A separate Fan Clan rules Pond Water City beside Bamboo Scroll Lake, where Fan Yan acted the fool while serving the Great Li Empire.

=== Fang Clan ===
The Fang Clan has no Nascent Tier cultivator, but two seventh tier martial artists and a Golden Core Tier swordsman give it great sway over the southern mortal empires. It owns countless banks, escort agencies, pawnshops and inns there.Chapter 260 One of its descendants defiled and killed a woman of the Dust Medicinal Shop, which led Zheng Dafeng to storm its manor.

=== Hou Clan ===
The Hou Clan relies on guest elders of the Middle Five Tiers. Its foothold in Old Dragon City comes from a branch descendant who became a virtuous scholar of Lake View Academy. It also controls the most routes from the city to Northern Complete Reed Continent.

=== Ding Clan ===
The Ding Clan nearly lost its place among the five major clans. A disciple of the Parasol Leaf Sect, Du Yan, married into it and kept it in power. It competes with the Fan Clan.

=== Cloud Forest Jiang Clan ===
The Cloud Forest Jiang Clan was the first prominent clan of the Middle Earth Divine Continent to move to Eastern Treasured Vial Continent. Its manor stands on the southeastern coast and stretches close to twenty kilometers out into the sea. Its marriage alliance with the Fu Clan reshaped Old Dragon City, and the [[Azure Phoenix Nation]] lies beside its lands.

=== Imperial Tang Clan ===
The Imperial Tang Clan rules the Azure Phoenix Nation. It grants royal titles without lands and deals firmly with the immortals of the mountains.Chapter 376 See [[Azure Phoenix Nation]].

== Southern Whirl Continent ==

=== Yingyin Chen Clan ===
The Yingyin Chen Clan, also called the Pure Confucian Chen Clan, was once the smallest of eight Yimen Chen Clan branches on the Middle Earth Divine Continent before it moved to Southern Whirl Continent to escape conflict. After its ancestor appeared, carrying a sun and a moon on his shoulders, the clan was transformed. A Confucian school and an academy were built on its land, and the road to its gates is lined with archways honoring its descendants. It is the only clan granted the title "Pure Confucian". Its clan leader is Chen Chun'an, and Chen Dui is a direct lineal descendant. Liu Xianyang's ancestors were graveyard attendants for the clan, and he went to Southern Whirl Continent to study there.Chapter 571

== Parasol Leaf Continent ==

=== Yao Clan (Great Quan Empire) ===
The Yao Clan commands a border army of the Great Quan Empire. Its plainly armored cavalry is famous along the border.Chapter 330 Chen Ping'an met its troops on his travels through the empire.

=== Huan Clan ===
The Huan Clan holds the Flying Eagle Fortress in Agarwood Nation. It moved there from Lasting Yi Nation more than six hundred years ago to escape war, and its ancestral hall is called Zhongying Hall.Chapter 291 The fortress had once been famous for almost a century, but had long since declined.

== Northern Complete Reed Continent ==

=== Sui Clan ===
The Sui Clan is an old official clan of Five Mountain Nation, led in name by Old Assistant Minister Sui Xinyu. Chen Ping'an escorted four of its members to the Great Seal Script Empire, and its daughter Sui Jingcheng was known as the clan's Jade Person.Chapter 519

=== Yang Clan of Lofty Cloud Palace ===
{{Main|Sects#Lofty Cloud Palace}}The Yang Clan of the Great Origin Empire's Esteemed Mystery Department is known for repaying kindness many times over, and hostility just as fully.

== Pure White Continent ==

=== Liu Clan ===
The Liu Clan is the foremost clan of Pure White Continent and is called the God of Wealth of the Majestic World. It owns the Ape Havoc Estate, one of the four great private residences on Stalactite Mountain.Chapter 269 Its heir is Liu Youzhou, the "Treasure Child". The clan is said to have built its fortune from a single copper coin.

== Middle Earth Divine Continent ==

=== Yu Clan (Shaoyuan Empire) ===
The Yu Clan is an ancient top-tier clan of the Middle Earth Divine Continent.Chapter 597 Its daughter Yu Juanfu, a pure martial artist, came to the Sword Qi Great Wall under Zhou Shenzhi's protection. Once she regains her standing, she is expected to control half the national power of the Shaoyuan Empire.

== Sword Qi Great Wall ==
The great clans of the city north of the Sword Qi Great Wall each hold their own top sword technique. The Chen Clan's strengthens bones, the Dong Clan's cleanses marrow, the Qi Clan's tempers souls, the Ning Clan's sharpens bonded swords, the Yao Clan's nourishes sword qi, and the Nalan Clan's joins sword qi and sword intent.Chapter 277

=== Chen Clan (Sword Qi Great Wall) ===
The Chen Clan is [[Chen Qingdu]]'s clan. Like the Dong Clan, its strength rests on generations of sword immortals.Chapter 574 Its current leader, Chen Xi, has carved a character on the wall, but he still feels like a child before the old great sword immortal. For that reason, its members are the most reluctant of all the clans to visit the city wall.Chapter 596 Chen Sanqiu is a young master of the clan.

=== Dong Clan ===
The Dong Clan rose after its ancestor charged into the Savage World alone and slew three Upper Five Tier great demons. Almost every leader since has slain great demons of the Unpolished Jade Tier or higher.Chapter 272 Dong Sangeng is its old ancestor. When Chen Qingdu killed Dong Guanpu as a demon spy, the clan leader nearly came to blows with him.

=== Qi Clan ===
The Qi Clan's sword technique tempers souls, and its men are famous for their looks. Its sword immortal Qi Tingji has carved a character on the wall. Qi Shou, a young sword cultivator of the clan, fought Chen Ping'an.

=== Ning Clan ===
The Ning Clan is the clan of [[Ning Yao]]. It had fallen from grace by the time Ning Yao's mother married into it, and it offered its Dragon Slaying Cliff as a marriage gift. Both of Ning Yao's parents later died in battle south of the wall.

=== Yao Clan (Sword Qi Great Wall) ===
The Yao Clan is the clan of Ning Yao's mother. It refused to approve her marriage into the declining Ning Clan, and she married without her elders' blessing. Its clan leader is Yao Chongdao, and the old sword immortal Yao Lianyun also belongs to it.

=== Nalan Clan ===
The Nalan Clan is one of the most powerful clans on the wall, though often forgotten because its leader Nalan Shaowei spends so long in seclusion. With the Yan Clan, it leads the wall's trade with the Majestic World.

=== Yan Clan ===
The Yan Clan owes its power to wealth rather than sword immortals. It serves the Sword Qi Great Wall much like a Ministry of Revenue and controls nearly half of the resources moving through it.Chapter 572 Its leader is Yan Ming, and its heir is Yan Zhuo.

=== Guo Clan ===
The Guo Clan of Ritual Baton Street is led by the sword immortal Guo Jia and has about a hundred members. His daughter Guo Zhujiu is an innate sword talent and a future pillar of the clan.Chapter 584 The clan stood by the Ning Residence after its fall.

== References ==
