pages.title: Du Mao
pages.content:
{{Character |header1=Du Mao |Vital_status=Deceased |Gender=Male |Species=Human |Enemie(s)=[[Chen Ping An]]
[[Zuo You]]
The sword spirit |Occupation=Strongest cultivator of the Parasol Leaf Sect |Former_affiliation(s)=Parasol Leaf Sect |Continent=[[Parasol Leaf Continent]] |Cultivation_rank=Ascension Tier |Novel=Chapter 364 }} == Appearance == Du Mao has a short, diminutive frame, to the point that he had to look up slightly even at a younger, towering pure martial artist standing only a couple of steps away from him.Chapter 364 He has a habitual gesture of raising a thumb and wiping it across his own lips whenever he is about to go all out in a fight, a tell recognized by anyone who knew him well.Chapter 365 == Personality == He is arrogant and openly contemptuous of anyone weaker than himself, dismissing a cultivator still below the Upper Five Tiers as worthless trash regardless of potential.Chapter 364 He subscribes wholeheartedly to the idea that power is above all else, and he is willing to try to reason his way out of a losing fight the moment the odds turn against him, showing none of the pride he projects when he has the upper hand.Chapter 365 He is also deeply selfish, ultimately willing to sacrifice an entire small world purely to save himself when cornered, a final act that left even his own sect disillusioned with him.Chapter 631 == Background == Du Mao was the strongest cultivator of the Parasol Leaf Sect and, by reputation, the most powerful cultivator on Parasol Leaf Continent aside from the old Daoist priest of the East Sea. After the sect’s only other Ascension Tier cultivator died, leaving it in a difficult transitional period, Du Mao exhausted the sect’s wealth refining a bonded celestial weapon called the Sword Devouring Ark, forged over six centuries from the complete carcass of a giant ancient Treasure Swallowing Whale, before retreating into seclusion for centuries more. The first thing he did upon emerging was travel to the Jade Tablet Sect atop his ark to challenge an Unpolished Jade Tier sword immortal to a battle to the death, killing him and devouring his bonded flying sword with the ark in the process.Chapter 364 Years later, Du Mao traveled to Old Dragon City on the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent with three goals in mind: to see the swordsman Zuo You’s skill for himself, to test how much Divine Lord Yang of Jewel Small World would tolerate, and to quietly further the Parasol Leaf Sect’s reach into the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent. He also hoped to use the opportunity to sever the Scholarly Sage’s scholarly lineage if the chance arose. To lure Zuo You out, he brutally beat down the pure martial artist Zheng Dafeng, crippling him, and then cornered Chen Ping’an, mocking his weak cultivation and threatening to kill him and take his treasures once Zuo You failed to appear.Chapter 364 Zuo You never came, but a white-robed sword spirit intervened in his place. Du Mao failed to glean anything about her strength through divination, since the area had already been sealed off, and he underestimated her badly, ordering his Sword Devouring Ark to strike her. The weapon instead trembled in open fear and refused to obey him, and when he eventually tried to force it to attack anyway, the sword spirit swatted it down and later destroyed it entirely after amusing herself with its vaunted reputation. Realizing he could not win, Du Mao abandoned his pride and tried to negotiate, but the sword spirit toyed with him regardless, sealing him inside a scenic picture scroll to fight his yang soul avatar to destruction while his true body’s yin soul fled back to Parasol Leaf Continent. He escaped with his life, but at the cost of the Sword Devouring Ark and any hope of intimidating Chen Ping’an or the Scholarly Sage again.Chapter 365 Some time later, Du Mao attempted to force his ascension from the world. Zuo You intercepted him and killed him in a decisive sword strike, ending his ascension attempt for good. In his final moments, Du Mao chose to destroy an entire small world in a desperate bid to survive, a selfish act that disgusted the Parasol Leaf Sect’s own disciples and elders and left the sect leader openly disappointed in him, even though the sect leader admitted he likely would have done the same in Du Mao’s place. Du Mao’s remains scattered as colored glaze golden body fragments, some of which fell to the Parasol Leaf Sect while others were lost elsewhere; Chen Ping’an came into possession of at least one such fragment and later gave it away as a gift.Chapter 631 Without Du Mao’s overwhelming strength to lean on, the once-feared Parasol Leaf Sect fell into sharp decline, having grown too dependent on his domineering reputation and too accustomed to using his name as an intimidation tactic against outsiders.Chapter 631 == Trivia == * His immortal body was later inhabited by a female bone ghost named [[Shi Rou]], who went on to serve as one of Chen Ping’an’s stewards alongside the Far Roaming Tier martial artist Zhu Lian.Chapter 364 * He once offered to make Jiang Shangzhen, then still only at the Golden Core Tier, the next sect leader of the Parasol Leaf Sect if he advanced to the Upper Five Tiers. Jiang Shangzhen turned him down and left for the Northern Complete Reed Continent instead.Chapter 364 * The injury he inflicted on Chen Ping’an with the Sword Devouring Ark left behind energy that continued to eat away at Chen Ping’an’s soul long after the wound itself had healed, proving far more troublesome than an ordinary physical injury.Chapter 364 == References ==

pages.title: Eastern Treasured Vial Continent
pages.content:
'''Eastern Treasured Vial Continent''' is the smallest of the nine continents of the [[Majestic World]] and the homeland of [[Chen Ping An]]. Long looked down on by the larger continents, it is home to countless empires and vassal states. Over the course of the story it comes largely under the rule of the [[Great Li Empire]], and it is later set to become the Majestic World's line of defence against the demon tribe.

== Geography ==
The continent is the smallest in the Majestic World.Chapter 191 [[Parasol Leaf Continent]], its neighbour to the southeast, is far larger.Chapter 261 To the north, a stretch of sea separates it from the [[Northern Complete Reed Continent]], and the [[Middle Earth Divine Continent]] lies across the sea to the west.

The north of the continent is bleak and poor in resources, while the south is rich.Chapter 165 The northern region is home to the Great Li Empire, [[Great Sui Nation]] and [[Yellow Court Nation]], and it once belonged to the [[Lu Empire]]. Before the Great Li Empire built a ferry station on Parasol Tree Mountain, no Kun ship could dock anywhere in the north. The central region holds the [[Luminous Vermilion Empire]], Lake View Academy, [[Southern Stream Nation]], [[Colorful Garment Nation]] and [[Bamboo Scroll Lake]]. [[Azure Phoenix Nation]] and the Cloud Forest Jiang Clan lie in the southeast.

[[Old Dragon City]] sits at the continent's southern tip. It is the largest trading hub on the continent and the link to Parasol Leaf Continent.Chapter 252 All of the continent's intercontinental ships belong to its clans.

== History ==
For a long time the Lu Empire was the strongest nation in the north.Chapter 160 The Great Li Empire began as a small state that the older nations to the south regarded as northern savages. With the help of [[Jewel Small World]], which hung above its territory, it grew into the largest mortal empire on the continent and destroyed the Lu Empire.

After the death of Qi Jingchun, the Great Li Empire turned south. When [[Sects#Ceremony Mountain|Ceremony Mountain]]'s Kun ship was brought down in the central region, Heavenly Lord [[Xie Shi]] of the Northern Complete Reed Continent took up position north of Lake View Academy. This cut the continent in two and left the empire free to take the north.Chapter 235 The Great Li cavalry then marched south. Before long more than half of the continent was under its control.Chapter 469 The Luminous Vermilion Empire fell, and its Central Mountain became the Great Li Empire's own. [[Song Jixin]] was made the empire's feudal lord of Old Dragon City.Chapter 528

[[Cui Chan]] planned to turn the resources of the whole continent into the power of one nation. With Old Dragon City as its anchor, the continent would hold back the demon tribe once the [[Sword Qi Great Wall]] fell. Later the Great Li court gathered the continent's leading cultivators and mountain gods to plan defensive lines against the demon army. It was expected to march north after destroying Parasol Leaf Continent.Chapter 640

== Cultivation world ==
The continent has always been short of powerful cultivators. When Qi Zhen of the [[Sects#Divine Edict Sect|Divine Edict Sect]] reached the Immortal Tier, he became its only Heavenly Lord. Only a handful of Unpolished Jade Tier cultivators could be counted.Chapter 362 Even years later it still had too few Ascension Tier cultivators.Chapter 571 Cultivators from the Complete Reed Continent held the continent in low regard.Chapter 213

The Divine Edict Sect is its leading Daoist sect and oversees Daoist orthodoxy across the continent. [[Sects#Wind Snow Temple|Wind Snow Temple]] and [[Sects#True Martial Mountain|True Martial Mountain]] are the two ancestral temples of the Militarians. The continent had only two Confucian academies, [[Mountain Cliff Academy]] and Lake View Academy, while the Complete Reed Continent had six.Chapter 61 Notable figures include Li Tuanjing of the [[Sects#Wind Lightning Field|Wind Lightning Field]], long regarded as the strongest cultivator below the Upper Five Tiers.Chapter 254 [[Wei Jin]] of Wind Snow Temple became the youngest swordsman in its history to reach the Upper Five Tiers. [[Liu Laocheng]] was its only vagrant cultivator at that level.

As the Great Li Empire expanded, its Five Mountains became the Five Mountains of the continent. [[Wei Bo]] of the Northern Mountain is the only mountain god of the Upper Five Tiers on the continent. Four forces, including [[Sects#Sun Scorch Mountain|Sun Scorch Mountain]] and the Xu Clan of Light Breeze City, became sects-in-waiting under the empire.

== Trivia ==

* Almost all Daoist priests on the continent wear fishtail hats.
* The men of the north are known across the continent for being tall and strong.
* The Great Li Empire was the only empire on the continent that made its Qi refiners serve three years in the army.
* Cultivators from Circling Ascension Continent complained that their own continent was only slightly larger than this one.
* One official dialect is spoken across the whole continent.Chapter 85

pages.title: Emerald Lake
pages.content:
The Emerald Lake is a significant mystical realm with unique origins, notable features, and connections to a larger narrative. It serves as a location for travel, exploration, and interactions among diverse characters, while also hinting at deeper spiritual and cultivation aspects tied to its history and unique characteristics. The lake's beauty and the lore surrounding its origins make it a memorable location within the overall story.

'''General Characteristics:'''

* The Emerald Lake is a '''mystical realm''' that is a remnant of the '''Hanging Flower Blessed Land'''. The Hanging Flower Blessed Land was destroyed due to a backlash from the Heavenly Dao, scattering its remains across the world.
* It is described as a place with a '''vast and rippling surface''' where mists rise.
* The lake is approximately '''three hundred kilometers across'''.
* It is known for containing '''renowned spring water''' that was collected by a female immortal when she was still alive. This water is said to be ideal for brewing tea, particularly if one can identify and draw from the subtle veins that contain its essence.

'''Features and Structures:'''

* There are around '''one hundred pagodas floating above the lake''', each connected to others via small paths. These pagodas serve as residences and locations for various activities.
* Each pagoda is provided with '''two or three small boats''', allowing passengers to explore the lake and enjoy the scenery.
* There are areas with '''large patches of lotus flowers''', where young women row boats and harvest lotus seeds, humming tunes as they work.
* The '''Lingering Shade Mountain Pagoda''' is a notable structure with covered walkways enclosed by white jade railings and a small dock with two small boats.
* There are also shops run by the intercontinental ship within some of the pagodas where passengers can purchase goods.

'''Significance and Lore:'''

* The lake's origin as a remnant of the Hanging Flower Blessed Land gives it a unique mystical quality.
* The '''female immortal''' associated with the Hanging Flower Blessed Land and the spring water adds a layer of lore and importance to the lake.
* It is considered a place where one can find fated opportunities and treasures, and those with a discerning eye may find pleasant surprises.
* The quality of the water from a particular well in the area is considered unusually good, despite well water generally being considered unsuitable for tea.

'''Travel and Commerce:'''

* The Emerald Lake is accessible via a '''ferry station''' located within the '''Treasure Swallowing Whale'''.
* Passengers traveling on the Treasure Swallowing Whale can use high-grade land-shortening talismans in the form of embroidered brocade rugs to quickly reach their destinations, such as the Emerald Lake.
* It is a popular destination for those seeking fated opportunities or a place to reside while traveling.
* There is an intercontinental ship that makes stops in the Emerald Lake and has various shops to sell goods to travelers.
* There are small boats that people can use to explore the lake and enjoy the scenery.

'''Interactions and Encounters:'''

* Characters such as Chen Ping'an, and Lu Tai, visit the Emerald Lake, each with their own goals.
* Lu Tai, an otherworldly immortal, demonstrates his ability to navigate the area and is seen acquiring boxes of makeup while there.
* The lake serves as a location for interactions between travelers and those who live in the mystical realm, where they engage in conversations about life and their perception of the world.

'''Spiritual and Cultivation Aspects:'''

* The spring water is of high quality and has a special essence to it, making it valuable for those who are particular about tea.
* The lake's water may have unique properties due to its link with the Hanging Flower Blessed Land.

pages.title: Factions
pages.content:
=== The Three Teachings ===
The Three Teachings—'''Confucianism, Buddhism, and Daoism'''—are the most influential philosophical and religious forces in Majestic World. They hold significant sway over the lives of ordinary people and the actions of powerful cultivators.

* '''Confucianism''': This teaching emphasizes morality, social harmony, and respect for authority. Confucian schools and academies are scattered across Majestic World, serving as centers of learning and upholding the moral order. They play a crucial role in shaping the laws and governance of mortal empires. '''Confucian sages''' are the highest authorities within Confucianism, possessing immense knowledge and influence.
* '''Buddhism''': Focused on achieving enlightenment and escaping the cycle of suffering, Buddhism is a prominent force with numerous temples and monasteries throughout Majestic World. '''Eminent monks''' and '''Golden Arhats''' are powerful figures within Buddhism, often possessing supernatural abilities and profound wisdom.
* '''Daoism''': Focused on living in harmony with the Dao, the natural order of the universe, Daoism is known for its diverse practices and esoteric teachings. Daoist temples and blessed lands are scattered across Majestic World, often serving as havens for cultivators seeking to refine their Qi and achieve immortality. '''Daoist sages''' are among the most powerful figures in Majestic World, commanding vast knowledge of the Dao and wielding incredible mystical powers.

=== The Militarians ===
Although not considered one of the Three Teachings, the '''Militarians''' constitute a powerful force in Majestic World. They are primarily focused on military strength and martial prowess, with many serving as generals, bodyguards, and military officers in mortal empires.

* '''True Martial Mountain and Wind Snow Temple''': These are the two main ancestral forces of the Militarians. True Martial Mountain is known for its close ties with mortal empires, while Wind Snow Temple is more focused on its own development and exploring ancient battlefields.

=== The Hundred Schools of Thought ===
Beyond the Three Teachings and the Militarians exist the '''Hundred Schools of Thought''', representing diverse philosophical and intellectual traditions. They hold varying levels of influence and often specialize in specific areas of knowledge or practice.

* '''Examples''': The sources mention Commercialism, followed by the five major clans of Old Dragon City, including the Fu Clan and Sun Clan [1]; the School of Naturalists, whose knowledge is said to make up half the teachings in that school, including the Middle Earth Divine Continent's Lu Clan [2]; Mohists, whose artisans are renowned for their craftsmanship [1]; and Fictionists, who can manipulate reality through storytelling [3].

=== Major Clans and Sects ===
Scattered throughout Majestic World are '''powerful clans and sects''', each with its own history, traditions, and goals. They often control vast resources and influence and play significant roles in shaping the political and social landscape.

* '''Examples''': The Cloud Forest Jiang Clan, renowned for its wealth and influence [4]; the Fu Clan of Old Dragon City, the most powerful clan in the city [5]; Parasol Leaf Sect, a powerful sect that lends its name to an entire continent [6]; and Mount Longhu's Heavenly Master Residence, a prominent Daoist faction [7].

=== The Demon Tribe ===
Originating from a different world called the '''Savage World''', the '''demon tribe''' represents a formidable force often seen as antagonistic to the inhabitants of Majestic World. They are known for their powerful physiques, martial skills, and insatiable desire to conquer. Their ongoing conflict with Majestic World is a major source of tension and conflict.

=== Otherworldly Immortals ===
A relatively new faction, '''otherworldly immortals''' are individuals who have somehow entered Majestic World from other realms, like the '''Lotus Flower Blessed Land'''. They often possess unique abilities and knowledge and can disrupt the existing power dynamics. Their origins and motivations are often shrouded in mystery, making them a source of both fascination and apprehension.

pages.content:

Owner of Osmanthus Island | Current_affiliation(s) = Fan Clan | Continent = [[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]] | Cultivation_rank = Fourth tier pure martial artist | Novel = Chapter 256 }} {{Spoilers}} '''Fan Er''' is the heir of the Fan Clan of Old Dragon City and the martial arts disciple of [[Zheng Dafeng]]. He met [[Chen Ping An]] at the Dust Medicinal Shop and became one of his closest friends, and he later put his own money behind Downtrodden Mountain. == Appearance == Fan Er is a good-looking boy, and the women working in the Dust Medicinal Shop often comment on his looks. His clear eyes show every emotion he feels.Chapter 256 By the time Chen Ping'an returns to Old Dragon City, Fan Er has grown into a handsome young man without losing his lively air.Chapter 361 == Personality == Fan Er is cheerful, open and quick to make friends. He told Chen Ping'an about his life after knowing him only a few days. He is smart and well raised, and despite his clan's wealth he is aware of how ordinary people struggle.Chapter 257 He prefers the women of the medicine shop, who treat him like any boy, to the clan's celestial maidens, who see him as the future clan leader. He has a strong sense of right and wrong. When a woman from the Dust Medicinal Shop died after being defiled by a Fang Clan descendant, he protested to his father even though everyone told him it was a trivial matter, and he was confined to the ancestral hall for a month for it. Zheng Dafeng judges him to be sturdy on the outside but fragile on the inside, a result of his easy upbringing. Chen Ping'an envies how carefree he is and wishes he could live the same way.Chapter 259 Fan Er has little ambition. He only studies martial arts because he lacks the aptitude to be a Qi refiner, and all he really wants is to reach the eighth tier so he can fly. When Zheng Dafeng offered to make him the strongest fourth tier martial artist, he said he would rather relax and enjoy life like his teacher. == Background == Fan Er is the second child of the Fan Clan leader. His older half-sister, [[Fan Junmao]], was born to a different mother. He admires her deeply and is fond of her mother, who praises him when he does well and calmly explains his mistakes, while his own mother spoils him. His name simply marks him as the second child, and he is a little embarrassed by it. The character for two is also slang for a fool, and Fan Junmao remarks that their parents named him well. He is the future leader of the clan, and Zheng Dafeng notes that the role weighs heavily on him.Chapter 261 He is also set to inherit Osmanthus Island, the Fan Clan's intercontinental ship.Chapter 263 Fan Er was a third tier martial artist when Chen Ping'an met him. Zheng Dafeng says his foundation is among the best on the continent and his aptitude matches Chen Ping'an's, but his sister calls his aptitude mediocre. When Chen Ping'an left for [[Stalactite Mountain]], Fan Er saw him off at Osmanthus Island. He tried to give Chen Ping'an the gold ingots he had saved from years of New Year money and handed over two flagons of osmanthus wine stolen from his father. He also gave him an osmanthus wood guest badge marked "friend of Fan Er", and they agreed to drink flower wine together one day.Chapter 258 Two years later he greeted Chen Ping'an outside Old Dragon City as a fourth tier martial artist. He told him about the Fu Clan's marriage alliance with the Cloud Forest Jiang Clan and about Zheng Dafeng storming the Fang Clan. The Fan Clan kept him inside the manor during the conflict, where he dug dirt in the yard with a small pickaxe and saved more than ten sacks of it for emergencies.Chapter 367 He saw Chen Ping'an off again when he left for the Azure Phoenix Nation.Chapter 372 Later, Fan Er personally decided to lend [[Downtrodden Mountain]] three hundred grain rain coins for the [[Lotus Flower Blessed Land|Lotus Root Blessed Land]], asking only for periodic interest.Chapter 529 He slipped out of Old Dragon City in secret to join the talks, and Chen Ping'an finally gave him the piece of chinaware he had promised years before, fired at the dragon kiln where he once worked.Chapter 570 The loan drew heavy criticism from the elders of his clan. Some of them argued that he was too rash to be trusted with Osmanthus Island and wanted an older relative to run it for a few years.Chapter 638 == Trivia == * After hearing Chen Ping'an's stories of eating clay as a child, Fan Er dug up a pouch of clay and hid it under his bed. He later tasted some during his punishment and complained that Chen Ping'an had lied to him. * He once tried to stage a "battle for the ages" with Chen Ping'an, only to be dragged off by Fan Junmao. He later let [[Pei Qian]] chase him around a courtyard and praised her "unfathomable powers". * He commissioned a lifelike portrait of Sui Youbian for Zheng Dafeng, which got his teacher nearly cut down by her sword.Chapter 368 * Lady Gui considers him the best match for her disciple Jin Su, but Jin Su dislikes him and prefers Sun Jiashu. * He calls the elderly Golden Core Tier swordsman who drives his carriage Grandpa Ma. == References ==

pages.title: Fan Junmao
pages.content:
{{Character|image1=Zhao Yao.PNG|status=Alive|gender=Male|species=Human|master(s)=[[Mister Qi]]|donghua=Chapter 2}}
==Appearance==
Fan Junmao is frequently called a '''"young mistress,"''' and her appearance is described as captivating and memorable. She is noted for her '''beautiful eyes''' that can appear as "bottomless, pitch-black wells". Her eyes can also be fervent and filled with awe. At other times, she is described as having a '''cold look''' in her eyes. She has a '''fair complexion''' and a '''graceful figure'''. She is also described as stunningly beautiful. Her attire is often mentioned, and she is known to wear a '''green dress''' that is described as spectacular. She also appears wearing a '''black robe''' and when she is on the sea of clouds she is dressed in white. She seems to prefer simple clothing that is not flashy or ostentatious, although upon closer inspection her clothes are refined and of high quality. Fan Junmao is also described as having an '''authoritative''' and '''commanding''' presence, which is in contrast to her youthful appearance. Even though she is young, she has a regal bearing. She has also been described as having a '''disdainful sneer'''.

==Personality==
Fan Junmao's personality is a complex mix of confidence, authority, and a sharp, sometimes abrasive, wit. She is presented as someone who is '''highly self-assured''', often displaying a '''commanding presence''' despite her youth. She is not afraid to speak her mind, and she often does so with a '''disdainful sneer''' or a sharp retort. She can be '''impatient and easily irritated''', especially when dealing with those she considers less intelligent or capable than herself. Despite her seemingly harsh exterior, Fan Junmao is also shown to be capable of '''great insight and strategic thinking'''. She is a shrewd observer of character and is not easily fooled. While she often expresses a cynical view of the world, she is also capable of acts of generosity and kindness, albeit often disguised with a mocking tone. She possesses a '''strong sense of pride''' and does not hesitate to show it, but she is also capable of self-reflection and admitting when she is wrong. Fan Junmao is also portrayed as being '''extremely intelligent''' and is not one to shy away from challenges or difficult situations. She is seen to be fiercely independent and does not like to be controlled. She is also shown to be '''loyal and protective''' of those she cares about, despite her often brusque manner. She can be '''impatient''', and she often speaks her mind directly and without hesitation. She is described as being someone who is difficult to understand. She is also shown to be '''ambitious''' and is not afraid to take risks. She has a deep understanding of power dynamics and often uses her wit and intelligence to manipulate situations to her advantage. She is also '''secretive''', and she is not always willing to reveal her true intentions.

==Background==
Fan Junmao is a character with a mysterious and complex background that is gradually revealed throughout the sources. She is from a poor family in Pine Song Nation, but a traveling senior sister from the Mirror Heart Hall saw potential in her and took her in as a disciple in place of her own master. This led to her becoming the most outstanding disciple of the current generation in the Mirror Heart Hall. '''She traveled across the cultivation world by herself for several years''', which contributed to her unique perspective and formidable abilities. It is suggested that '''she has ties to the old divine lord''', and that the Fan Clan is essentially under his control. Her rapid cultivation base progression has always been extremely strange, and there is clearly far more to her than meets the eye. She is also described as being someone who was originally a spirit, and she '''abandoned her cultivation and grew up naturally''' before eventually becoming Fan Wan'er. '''Half of her soul had been missing''', which led to her appearing hesitant and sluggish as if she was being suppressed by a huge boulder. She is also described as having a close relationship with the old man in the Yang Family's medicine shop.

Fan Junmao is shown to be deeply knowledgeable about the workings of the cultivation world and is not easily fooled. She is also '''highly influential within the Fan Clan''', as she is the one who calls the shots behind the scenes. She is also very familiar with various cultivation techniques, including the art of refining bonded items. She is a formidable force to be reckoned with, and despite her young age, she commands respect from many different people, including even powerful cultivators.

pages.title: Fox Town
pages.content:
Fox Town is a complex location that is much more than what it appears to be on the surface. It is a border town with a blend of ordinary people, petty officials, and hidden elites, a place where the mundane and the mystical intersect. It is a place where both the local residents and outside travelers are aware of hidden agendas, and power struggles are commonplace. The town's unique location, its unusual residents, and the constant stream of travelers make it a place of intrigue and potential conflict within the narrative.

'''General Characteristics:'''

* Fox Town is a '''border town''' of the Great Quan Empire. This location gives it a unique character as a crossroads of different cultures and influences.
* It is considered a '''small town''' with a mix of ordinary residents, petty officials, and hidden elites.
* The town is known to be '''haunted by ghosts and spirits''', which can lead people astray. This has reportedly caused some travelers to go insane.
* The town is not particularly large or significant and is viewed as being unimportant by some of the more powerful figures.
* The town's residents are described as '''spirited people'''. They are not necessarily powerful but are not stupid either.
* The town has a '''local dialect''' that can be difficult for outsiders to understand.

'''Social and Political Landscape:'''

* The town has a '''constable''' named Ma Ping, whose family has held the job for generations. Ma Ping is described as arrogant and egotistical.
* The town's officials are considered '''informal''' and '''petty''', not regarded as true officials. They are described as arrogant and egotistical.
* The town has a mix of '''commoners''', as well as individuals with hidden identities or agendas, including some powerful elites and cultivators.
* There is a sense that the town is not peaceful, with some people believing that the unrest is due to the presence of demons.
* The town residents have a tendency to '''gossip''', creating rumors about various events.

'''Key Figures and Locations:'''

* '''Jiu Niang''' is the innkeeper of an inn in Fox Town and is described as "foxy" and likes to seduce men. She is a respected figure in the town and has the ability to resolve local disputes.
* There is a '''lame young boy''' who works at Jiu Niang's Inn. He is perceptive, and can sense the approach of large cavalry troops.
* '''Third Grandpa''' is a figure of some significance in the town.
* There is a '''pharmacy''' in the town.
* There is a sense that some people in the town '''know more than they reveal''' and that they have witnessed many interesting things.
* The inn where Chen Ping'an stays is described as both '''mystical and sinister''' by the town's residents.

'''Conflicts and Interactions:'''

* '''Outsiders''' are sometimes picked on and bullied by the local children.
* There is a tension between the town's residents and outsiders, with a potential for conflict.
* There have been '''battles''' both inside and outside the inn involving cultivators, which have caused quite a stir in the town.
* The town has been visited by a '''True Dragon''', leading to rumors about the nature of the town and its residents.
* A '''Yao Clan convoy''' passes through the town, with connections to the imperial court.
* Some residents of Fox Town like to visit '''Hanging Armor Military Town''' in order to see the Yao Clan's cavalry.
* There is an awareness of the '''Yao Clan's''' activities and their influence, even at a distance.
* There is a sense that powerful figures are hiding within the town.

'''Mystical Aspects:'''

* There are '''mighty figures''' hiding in the town that are stronger than those seen in Colorful Garment Nation.
* The presence of '''demons''' is believed by some to be the reason for the lack of peace in the town.
* The town's location on the border may make it a place where '''spiritual energies''' gather or mix in interesting ways.
* '''Zhong Kui''', a noble scholar, is keeping an eye on the town, implying that there are forces at play that warrant such observation.

'''Connections to the Wider World:'''

* The town is located on a '''border of the Great Quan Empire''', placing it in contact with other regions and powers.
* The town is a stop on the route to other places, like the capital, and serves as a '''relay station''' of sorts.
* It is located near a well-traveled '''official road''', which implies that the town sees its fair share of travelers and merchants.
* There is knowledge of places like '''Mirage City''' and '''Heavenly Palace Peak''', showing that the town is not entirely isolated.

[[Old Dragon City]] |Continent=[[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]] |City=[[Old Dragon City]] |Cultivation_rank=Sixth tier (Volume 4) |Novel=Chapter 9 |Donghua=Episode 1 }} '''Fu Nanhua''' is the son of Fu Qi, lord of [[Old Dragon City]] at the southern tip of Eastern Treasured Vial Continent. He came to the small town in [[Jewel Small World]] for a fated opportunity, nearly died at the hands of [[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]], and went home to become the clear heir to his father's seat. == Appearance == Fu Nanhua is a tall, strikingly handsome young man whose good looks hold up even in a grimy alley.Chapter 9 He carries a natural regal air and, when he wants to, a warm and easy smile. In the town he always kept a green dragon-shaped jade pendant at his waist, the Old Dragon Rainbringer, until he gave it away to Song Jixin. == Personality == Fu Nanhua is refined, smooth-spoken and calculating. He can bend down to speak eye to eye with a poor boy one moment and quietly plan an ally's murder the next. He decided to kill [[Cai Jinjian]] from the moment he entered the town, even while walking beside her as a friend. When she was struck down in front of him, he felt relief, and his speech about avenging her was aimed at the sages watching over the town.Chapter 21 He is proud and quick to anger when he feels slighted, but he usually keeps his temper in check when his future is at stake. He respects those he sees as equals or betters, such as Song Jixin, and looks down on everyone else. He tends to agonize over hard choices, pacing the room as he weighs them, and his father mocks him for it. Over time he learns to put the clan's interests ahead of his own grudges, which earns his father's approval. == Background == === Old Dragon City === Fu Nanhua was born into the Fu Clan, the rulers of Old Dragon City. He was once just one of several children with a claim to the city lord's seat and was not seen as special, so it came as a surprise when his father chose him to go to Jewel Small World. His older siblings, Fu Donghai and Fu Chunhua, had spent a century handling the clan's dealings with other continents.Chapter 254 (3) === The small town === Fu Nanhua entered the town with Cai Jinjian and the two formed an alliance, though he planned to dispose of her. He was seeking Song Jixin, and when Chen Ping'an refused to tell him where Song Jixin lived, he took the boy as a nuisance. Song Jixin hinted to him that no one would care if the orphan from Clay Vase Alley died.Chapter 10 Fu Nanhua fell in love at first sight with a small Mandrill Teapot that Song Jixin owned. He offered the Old Dragon Rainbringer as a meeting gift and a pouch of Offering Coins, and when Song Jixin pushed back, he tapped the table in a way that caused Song Jixin agony. He held back from killing him for the sake of his future. Song Jixin's terms were three pouches of gold essence coins and a killing on his behalf.Chapter 17 According to Cui Minghuang, Song Jixin could not decide on the target and switched it from Liu Xianyang to Chen Ping'an.Chapter 89 Then Chen Ping'an ambushed Cai Jinjian with a porcelain shard while she and Fu Nanhua were walking together. Fu Nanhua stalked the bleeding boy down the alley, sure of an easy kill, but Chen Ping'an tricked him into looking back and slammed into him. Chen Ping'an pinned him against the wall, choked him with one hand and pressed the shard into his stomach. Fu Nanhua offered to swear an oath, hoping to deceive the boy with a half-truth, and blacked out just as Qi Jingchun arrived.Chapter 22 Qi Jingchun stopped Chen Ping'an, told Fu Nanhua to leave the small world, and gave him an opportunity of some kind, without asking him to promise anything about Chen Ping'an.Chapter 253 (2) On Old Man Yang's orders, Zheng Dafeng took Fu Nanhua back to Old Dragon City. === Return home === The ordeal nearly broke his Dao heart. Fu Nanhua, once known for his wide circle of friends, withdrew and saw few people. Even so, his standing rose quickly: his master was close to a breakthrough, a marriage to the Cloud Forest Jiang Clan was arranged, and he came to be seen as the one most likely to inherit the Old Dragon Robe.Chapter 253 (1) When Cai Jinjian visited the city, he tried to win her over with a plan to raise both of them to power together, but she turned him down. His father then appeared and laid out two paths: kill Chen Ping'an to cut away the knot left in his heart, or let it go and use the Fu Clan's secret method of turning such knots into pearls in the mind. Fu Qi mocked him for being troubled by a dead man and a nobody, and the shaken Fu Nanhua broke down in tears. Later, when Chen Ping'an came to Old Dragon City, Fu Nanhua announced that the boy had to die. His sister Fu Chunhua privately looked down on him as a waste who had reached only the sixth tier despite all the resources poured into him. Soon after, [[Zhi Gui]] arrived at the Fu Clan wrapped in the Old Dragon Robe, called him a pathetic little ant for not daring to kill Chen Ping'an, and left him feeling close to madness.Chapter 254 (4) In the end he chose not to use the clan's power for a private feud. Fu Qi was pleased and told him that the Fu Clan's real strength was money, which had carried Fu Qi himself to the Nascent Tier.Chapter 255 (1) Fu Nanhua stayed a sworn enemy of Chen Ping'an but did not move against him.Chapter 361 (1) === Young city lord === Fu Nanhua married the young woman from the Jiang Clan. On their wedding day the two talked plainly and agreed on the terms of their marriage, and he found her beautiful, far from the rumors.Chapter 364 (1) During the clash between Fu Qi and Zheng Dafeng, he sent a quiet signal that swayed the Ding, Fang and Hou clans, and afterward he personally told them that the Parasol Leaf Sect had also allied with the Fu Clan. By Volume 9 he was certain to be the next lord of Old Dragon City and was on good terms with Song Jixin, who had been posted to the city as a feudal lord.Chapter 571 (1) == Trivia == * Rumors once claimed his bride was shockingly ugly and over thirty. In fact she was at least as pretty as Jin Su. * He once fell for Jin Su of Osmanthus Island, as did Sun Jiashu, and she rejected him outright. * He did not know that Zheng Dafeng was more than a simple gatekeeper of Jewel Small World. * He was not among the clan members chosen to greet the Great Li guests, and he was thrilled to later meet the Mohist Xu Ruo in person. * Chen Ping'an hoped Gu Can would never become like Fu Nanhua, who bullies those weaker than him. == References ==

pages.title: Gao Zhen
pages.content:
{{Character |header1 = Gao Xuan |image1 = Gao Zhen.png |Aliases = Gao Zhen (false name in Jewel Small World)
Xuan'er (by his father) |Vital_status = Alive |Gender = Male |Species = Human |Relatives = Emperor of Great Sui (father)
Gao Zhen (brother)
Old ancestor of the Geyang Gao Clan |Friend(s) = [[Yu Lu]]
[[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]]
[[Dong Shuijing]] |Allies = Wu Yue
[[Wei Bo]] |Occupation = Imperial prince
Royal hostage |Current_affiliation(s) = Forest Deer Academy
[[Great Sui Nation]] |Former_affiliation(s) = [[Mountain Cliff Academy]] |Continent = [[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]] |Novel = Chapter 1 |Donghua = Ep 1 }} '''Gao Xuan''' is a prince of the imperial Gao Clan of [[Great Sui Nation]]. As a boy, he entered Jewel Small World, deep in the territory of his nation's enemy, the Great Li Empire, escorted by the old eunuch Wu Yue. There he introduced himself as '''"Gao Zhen"''', the name of one of his brothers, and claimed two of the small world's greatest fated opportunities: the golden carp and the Dragon King Basket. He later becomes a friend of [[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]], a student of [[Mountain Cliff Academy]] and close friend of [[Yu Lu]]. After the treaty between the two empires, he is sent to Forest Deer Academy in Dragon Spring Prefecture as a royal hostage. ''Note: the name "Gao Zhen" in Volume 1 refers to Gao Xuan. The real Gao Zhen, his brother, is a separate, timid prince who never visits the small town.'' == Appearance == Gao Xuan is a handsome boy who first appears in brocade robes, dressed in a colourful and extravagant manner. Chen Ping'an counts him among the good-looking youths of his age he has met, alongside Song Jixin, Zhao Yao and Lin Shouyi. == Personality == Gao Xuan is friendly, bold and carefree on the surface, but quick to anger when crossed, as when his own servant defies him. He is courageous enough to have travelled into the heart of an enemy nation as a child, which Chen Ping'an considers far more impressive than Song Jixin's later visit to Great Sui. He tells Yu Lu that with women he always tries to show his best side, while with men he can reveal his true self. As a hostage, he outwardly seems calm and carefree, though [[Dong Shuijing]] and Xu Ruo guess at the disheartenment beneath. He is sincere and respectful towards scholars. == Plot == === Jewel Small World === Gao Xuan first appears outside the courtyards of [[Clay Vase Alley]] with an elderly servant, and offers to buy [[Song Jixin]]'s maidservant [[Zhi Gui]].Chapter 1 In an alley, he examines an antique green jade seal carved with coiling dragons and crouching tigers, secretly hoping that a passing young woman with a veiled hat and saber, [[Ning Yao]], will try to take it from him.Chapter 12 When his servant, the old eunuch Wu Yue, suddenly tries to kill the young woman, Gao Xuan introduces himself to her as "Gao Zhen from Yiyang County of Great Sui" and offers compensation. When Wu Yue defies him and pursues her anyway, Gao Xuan is livid, calling Wu Yue an "old, castrated donkey" and shouting that he has committed a crime punishable by death.Chapter 13 Gao Xuan and Wu Yue intercept [[Li Er]] as he is about to sell the golden carp in the Dragon King Basket to Chen Ping'an, and buy both themselves. Zheng Dafeng scolds Li Er for wasting the basket on "that small prince from Great Sui".Chapter 63 (2) Gao Xuan gives Chen Ping'an a pouch of gold essence copper coins as thanks for the opportunity.Chapter 25 === The Name Gao Zhen === Years later, the emperor of Great Sui reveals that Gao Xuan used his brother Gao Zhen's name in Jewel Small World. The girl Wu Yue nearly killed later descended from the heavens with several sword immortals from another continent to seek vengeance against Gao Zhen. She realised she had the wrong person and apologised, but the timid Gao Zhen was deeply traumatised. Wu Yue, meanwhile, judges that Gao Xuan reaped "two enormous pieces of fortune" on the trip, and the emperor concludes that "Xuan'er is more fortunate than I am".Chapter 165 (2) === Friend of Chen Ping'an === At the end of Chen Ping'an's journey to Great Sui, Gao Xuan arrives with an enormous escort and introduces himself under his real name. He brushes off Wu Yue's concerns, saying a name is meant to be called, and personally escorts the group to the capital.Chapter 159 (2) He later catches up with Chen Ping'an outside the capital, insists that they are now friends, slaps palms with him, and gives him a carriage stocked with fine wine, pills and makeup.Chapter 160 Chen Ping'an later realises why Gao Xuan seemed so apologetic about the golden carp: it was originally meant for him. === Mountain Cliff Academy === Gao Xuan often visits Mountain Cliff Academy, accompanying Li Huai and Yu Lu to the city during the Lantern Festival. When Great Li and Great Sui form an alliance, he meets Song Jixin again. Recalling that he once offered to buy Zhi Gui, he asks if the price of 10,000 taels of gold still stands, and tells Li Baoping that he is now good friends with Chen Ping'an. The emperor of Great Sui formally enrols him in the academy. He becomes Yu Lu's roommate and inseparable friend, fishing with him at the lake. Yu Lu eventually confides that he is the former crown prince of the Lu Empire and a seventh-tier martial artist, and Gao Xuan is proud to have chosen such a friend.Chapter 304 (1) === Royal Hostage === Under the treaty between Great Li and Great Sui, Gao Xuan is sent to the Great Li Empire as a royal hostage, accompanied by an eleventh-tier gatekeeper and the old ancestor of the Geyang Gao Clan. He studies at Forest Deer Academy on Cloud Drape Mountain.Chapter 400 (3) To his surprise, no one there treats him as important. The old ancestor explains why, and Gao Xuan understands at once. In his free time, he wanders the mountains of Dragon Spring Prefecture and the streets of the small town with his bookcase, sometimes visiting Li Er's empty old house.Chapter 415 (1) Calling himself a wanderer seeking knowledge, he befriends Dong Shuijing over wontons and rice wine, enjoying a friendship free from transactions. Dong Shuijing hands him his shop keys so he can climb the mountain to watch the sunrise.Chapter 420 (2) Wei Bo counts him among Chen Ping'an's allies in the Great Li Empire.Chapter 461 (2) When Mao Xiaodong leads Mountain Cliff Academy's students on an excursion, the white-haired scholars of Great Sui are finally able to see him. When they bow to him in tears, Gao Xuan, who had not felt especially wronged by his life as a hostage, also tears up, and bows to them in return as a junior Confucian disciple.Chapter 471 (3) == Possessions == * '''Golden carp''': one of the five greatest fated opportunities of Jewel Small World. * '''Dragon King Basket''': the fish basket that held the golden carp, caught by Li Er. * '''Green jade seal''': an antique seal carved with coiling dragons and crouching tigers. == Trivia == * He once offered to buy Zhi Gui from Song Jixin, who named a price of 10,000 taels of gold. * Zheng Dafeng compares Ma Kuxuan's white cat to Gao Xuan's golden carp in significance. == References ==

pages.title: Great Li Empire
pages.content:
The '''Great Li Empire''' is the largest mortal empire on [[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]], ruling the entire northern stretch of the continent. Founded by the Imperial Song Clan after centuries as a vassal state of the Lu Empire, it grew from a small dominion of 70 counties into a continental power and, by the later volumes, the de facto ruler of the entire continent.

== Geography ==
The Great Li Empire occupies the northernmost region of Eastern Treasured Vial Continent. Its people were long looked down upon as northern barbarians by the older civilizations to the south.Chapter 39 The empire's territory expanded dramatically over two to three centuries, eventually swallowing the Lu Empire and sweeping south all the way to Old Dragon City, the southernmost city on the continent.Chapter 550 (4)

The capital city is home to over a million residents and serves as the seat of the emperor, the imperial court, and the Mountain and River Formation that protects the realm.Chapter 84 (2) The empire is also home to [[Mountain Cliff Academy]], one of only two Confucian academies on the continent, which played a major role in raising the empire's reputation from a northern backwater to a civilized power.Chapter 82 (1)

== History ==
The Song Clan's realm spent several hundred years as a vassal state under the Lu Empire, which suppressed and abused it for generations. The Great Li Empire broke free and declared itself a sovereign state in its own right, an event still celebrated in the history books.Chapter 550 (4)

Over the following centuries the empire expanded steadily, and in the fifty years before the novel's start it doubled in size, growing from 70 counties and 800 cities to 140 counties and 1,500 cities. Imperial Preceptor Cui Chan, the "Embroidered Tiger", is credited with half that growth.Chapter 39 The other half belongs to Song Changjing, the Monarch and the empire's supreme martial artist, who personally destroyed the Lu Empire in a single campaign, ending its long reign as the continent's dominant power.Chapter 550 (4)

By the later volumes, the Great Li Empire's heavy cavalry had marched south through every remaining empire and vassal state on the continent. Emperor Song He presided over a realm whose territory had no precedent in the history of the Majestic World, with the seas effectively forming its borders.Chapter 555 (2)

== Government ==
The empire is ruled by the Imperial Song Clan. Three figures hold the real power:
* The '''emperor''', who commands the formal apparatus of court and controls the divine infrastructure of mountains and rivers.
* '''Song Changjing''' (the Monarch), the emperor's younger brother and the continent's preeminent martial artist, who leads the military and conquered the empire's enemies.
* '''Cui Chan''' (the imperial preceptor, nicknamed the "Embroidered Tiger"), who shapes strategy, trains the cavalry, and serves as the emperor's most trusted advisor.Chapter 187 (2)

The empire's administrative hierarchy includes six ministries, with the Ministry of Rites and Ministry of Justice playing prominent roles in relations with divine powers and conquered territories. Six military governor positions were created in the later volumes to administer the newly conquered lands.Chapter 550 (4)

The empire is also supported by six pillar clans, among them the Yuan Clan and the Cao Clan, who wield enormous influence in court.Chapter 13

== Emperors ==
* '''Song Zhengchun''' — the emperor at the time of the story's beginning. He brought Song Jixin (his son Song Mu) back to the capital after the fall of [[Jewel Small World]], and later officially recognized Song Mu as his heir.Chapter 116
* '''[[Song He]]''' — Song Zhengchun's younger son, who inherited the throne and became emperor by Volume 7. Under his reign the empire completed its conquest of the continent.Chapter 550 (4)

== Military ==
The Great Li Empire is renowned on Eastern Treasured Vial Continent for the quality and discipline of its martial artists and cavalry. More martial artists of the Middle Five Tiers serve the empire than any other nation on the continent, with Song Changjing at their head.Chapter 75 Imperial Preceptor Cui Chan's meticulous cultivation of the cavalry over decades gave it a discipline that set it apart from every other army in the Majestic World.Chapter 559 (4)

The empire's intelligence apparatus spans seven agencies, three of which were controlled by a single senior official during the small town era.Chapter 62

== Religion and divine hierarchy ==
The empire maintains tight control over the gods within its borders. All legitimate mountain gods, river gods, and yin gods within its territory are formally appointed by the imperial court and answer to a hierarchy of senior river gods and the Ministry of Rites. Rogue gods and illegal temples were systematically destroyed as the armies marched south.Chapter 556 (2)

The Northern Mountain serves as the formal home of the empire's mountain god hierarchy, with the great mountain god of Cloud Drape Mountain (later [[Wei Bo]]) as one of its most powerful members.Chapter 559 (1)

== Relationship with Mountain Cliff Academy ==
[[Mountain Cliff Academy]], overseen by [[Qi Jingchun]] during his 60-year tenure in [[Jewel Small World]], provided the empire with most of its educated officials and was instrumental in transforming it from a settlement of northern barbarians into a literate, civilized power. The academy's decline after Qi Jingchun's departure threatened the pipeline of talent the empire depended on.Chapter 82 (1)

== Trivia ==
* The empire's territory, spanning 140 counties and 1,500 cities before the southern campaigns, held over 20 million families.Chapter 41
* The Great Sui Nation's royal Gao Clan and the Great Li Empire's Song Clan are hereditary enemies.Chapter 34
* Song Changjing submitted a memorial to the emperor consisting of a single sentence — "There are heroes outside of our Great Li Empire as well" — and the emperor laughed and approved it without revision.Chapter 93 (1)
* Cui Chan wrote the couplets for [[Jewel Small World]]'s county offices and lingered a long while over the names on a wall in the small town's temple.Chapter 85 (1)

== References ==

pages.title: Great Sui Nation
pages.content:
The '''Great Sui Nation''' is a powerful nation in the north of [[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]], ruled for its entire 1,200-year history by the Gao Clan. It was the [[Great Li Empire]]'s strongest rival in the north and a nation that holds scholars in unusually high regard. After [[Qi Jingchun]]'s death it took in Mountain Cliff Academy, and [[Chen Ping An]] escorted [[Li Baoping]], [[Li Huai]] and [[Lin Shouyi]] there on his first long journey.

== Geography ==
The nation lies south of the Great Li Empire. Travelers coming from the Great Li Empire first pass through its subsidiary, the Yellow Court Nation, a journey of about 600 kilometers.Chapter 133 The Yellow Court Nation was one of the Great Sui Nation's twelve subsidiary nations.Chapter 139 Past the Great Sui Pass on the border, the capital is still about 400 kilometers away.Chapter 159

The capital is large and walled. The new Mountain Cliff Academy stands on Eastern Splendor Mountain, also called East Mountain, the most scenic mountain in the city. Iron Tree Mountain is the tallest mountain in the capital.Chapter 162 The city is guarded by a great protective formation nurtured over several centuries. The imperial palace has its own formation, called the Dragon Wall, and secret passages link the palace to the offices of the Six Ministries and the academy.Chapter 169

== History ==
The Gao Clan has ruled the nation since its founding, and Yiyang County is the emperor's home.Chapter 13 One of its founding fathers was the Confucian general Yuan Gaofeng, who gave up a scholar's career to found the nation with the first emperor of the Geyang Gao Clan. He was the first official in its history granted the posthumous title of Civil Justice, and he is now honored as a deity in the capital's Confucian temple.Chapter 407 Working with the Lu Empire, the Gao Clan held back the rise of the Great Li Empire for several decades.Chapter 404

A [[Gao Zhen|prince of the Gao Clan]] entered the small town of [[Jewel Small World]], paying half of the emperor's private treasury, and bought the golden carp and a Dragon King Basket there. After Qi Jingchun's death, the Great Sui Nation took in the remaining teachers and students of Mountain Cliff Academy, with the Great Li emperor's approval.Chapter 160 When the academy's local students bullied the children from the small town, Li Huai's father Li Er stormed into the imperial palace. He fought the chief eunuch, who drew on the capital's dragon qi, until Mao Xiaodong brought the two sides to peace.

Facing the Great Li Empire's march south, the emperor chose not to fight. The Imperial Song Clan and the Imperial Gao Clan sealed an alliance with pacts signed on Cloud Drape Mountain and on East Mountain.Chapter 239 The nation's vassals, including the Yellow Court Nation, switched their tribute to the Great Li Empire. More than a hundred officials resigned, a famous scholar threw himself off a cliff, and a Go master renowned across half the continent burned his favorite Go table.Chapter 283 Gao Xuan went to the Great Li Empire as a hostage in place of his older brother.Chapter 467 An eleventh tier gatekeeper of the capital and the old flood dragon of the Yellow Court Nation went with him to serve as assistant mountain masters of Forest Deer Academy.Chapter 400

The alliance gave the nation more than a century to recover, but both sides kept scheming. After the death of the Great Li emperor Song Zhengchun, many officials and border generals wanted to tear up the pact. Assassins targeted Mao Xiaodong and the students from the Great Li Empire around the Thousand Elders Banquet in the hope of starting a war.Chapter 410

== Government ==
The nation is ruled from the capital by the emperor and the Six Ministries. Its imperial censors hold great power, and the title of heavenly official belongs to the head minister of the Ministry of Rites, rather than of the Ministry of Personnel as in the Great Li Empire. The head minister also serves as the academy's official mountain master. Twelve chief eunuchs guard the palace and kneel only to the emperor. The nation's only Unpolished Jade Tier cultivator is an old ancestor of the Gao Clan who lives as a storyteller and does not excel in battle.

== Culture ==
Scholars are held in very high regard. Women may study at any academy that accepts them before they marry, but may not sit the imperial examination. Almost everyone in the nation speaks the continent's official dialect, unlike in the Great Li Empire. The nation counts itself home to the best Go players on the continent, and Ning Yao remarks that a ninth dan Go official of the Great Li Empire is only equal to a seventh dan expert of the Great Sui Nation.

The Gao Clan's centuries of peace left a wealthy people who are happy to spend. Families in the imperial court hold the same standing their ancestors had two or three hundred years ago, which Cui Dongshan contrasts with the Great Li Empire's open court. He also judges its scholars as more theoretical and less practical than those of the Great Li Empire.

== Mountain Cliff Academy ==
The new Mountain Cliff Academy on Eastern Splendor Mountain is much larger than the old one. When the children from the small town arrived, the emperor met them at the foot of the mountain in his formal robes. Its first students were mostly drawn from wealthy and powerful clans of the nation. Mao Xiaodong serves as head deputy mountain master and runs the academy's teaching. Having moved, the academy lost its place among the 72 Confucian academies. Restoring it was later among the aims raised for the continent's future.Chapter 640

== Trivia ==
* The prince who entered the small town calls himself Gao Zhen in Chapter 13, but the same prince is called Gao Xuan from Chapter 159 onward. The clan's home is called Yiyang County in early chapters and Geyang later.
* Cui Dongshan compares the nation's cavalry to guard dogs raised in a courtyard, while the Great Li Empire's border cavalry are wild dogs with sharp teeth.
* The capital's residents are known in the north for being arrogant and unwelcoming to outsiders.
* Some time after the children's arrival, the nation announced it had gained a powerful tenth tier martial artist. In the south of the continent this was dismissed as a lie and a diversion.

== References ==

pages.title: Gu Can
pages.content:
{{Spoilers|This page contains spoilers beyond what the donghua has adapted. Major spoilers are blurred. Hover over blurred text to read it.}} {{Character |header1=Gu Can |image1=Gu Can.png |Chinese=顾璨 |Pinyin=Gù Càn |Titles=Little Devil of Bamboo Scroll Lake |Aliases=Can'er, Cancan (by his mother) |Vital_status=Alive |Gender=Male |Species=Human |Master(s)=[[Liu Zhimao]] |Relatives=Gu Tao ([[Yin god]])
Mother (Aunt Gu) |Beast_companions=Tan Xue, the "little catfish" (flood dragon, deceased) |Friend(s)=[[Chen Ping An]]
[[Zeng Ye]]
Ma Duyi |Enemie(s)=[[Liu Laocheng]] |Current_affiliation(s)=Cyan Gorge Island |Region=[[Bamboo Scroll Lake]] |Cultivation_rank=Abode Tier (by Chapter 455) |Novel=Chapter 7 |Donghua=Episode 1 }} '''Gu Can''' is a boy from [[Clay Vase Alley]] in the small town of [[Jewel Small World]], raised by his mother and looked after by his neighbor [[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]], who thinks of him as a little brother. Taken away by [[Liu Zhimao]], he grew into the feared "little devil" of Bamboo Scroll Lake before Chen Ping'an came to set him right. == Appearance == As a child in the town, Gu Can is small and scrawny, always with two lines of snot under his nose and a pair of big eyes like black grapes.Chapter 7 He weighed under 40 kilograms but carried an aptitude so heavy that was very heavy.Chapter 8 At Bamboo Scroll Lake he wears a dark green official python robe and has a habit of tucking his hands into his opposite sleeves. A few years later he has shot up to the height of a young man from the north, and in his later travels he carries a folding fan of divine cloud bamboo. == Personality == His mother did not always raise him well, and he learned early to be sharp, sly and watchful as a way of protecting himself. He holds grudges for years and loves to rant about digging up the ancestral graves of anyone who wronged him, such as the drunkard who once kicked him in the stomach and stomped on his head until Chen Ping'an carried him off for help.Chapter 93 (1) He is also patient enough to sit in the blazing sun all day for a single eel. With the two people he trusts, his mother and Chen Ping'an, he is a different child: clingy, quick to cry and eager to please. At Bamboo Scroll Lake that loyalty turned into a belief that anything was allowed so long as it kept his mother safe, and he honestly could not see why killing his enemies, and the people around them, was wrong. After losing Tan Xue and making amends under Chen Ping'an's rules, he became calmer, more measured and far harder to read. He still keeps a list of grudges, but he no longer kills over hurtful words.Chapter 534 (2) == Background == === Clay Vase Alley === Gu Can grew up without his father, and his mother, a sharp-tongued beauty who could hold her own against Granny Ma and the other alley women, raised him alone. She fed Chen Ping'an a bowl of rice when he had nothing, and in return Chen Ping'an stood up for the pair, carried water for them in droughts and treated Gu Can like a younger brother. Chen Ping'an also gave him a small black catfish, which Gu Can kept in his water vat. A storyteller with a bottomless white bowl, who turned out to be Liu Zhimao, the River Severing True Lord of Lake Shujian, found that Gu Can had a great aptitude for cultivation and took him as a disciple on the spot. When Cai Jinjian of Dawn Cloud Mountain came to claim him, Liu Zhimao drove her off. The little catfish was in truth a flood dragon, and formed a close relationship with Gu Can.Chapter 18 Before leaving, Gu Can whispered to Chen Ping'an about the treasures he had hidden at the bottom of his water vat.Chapter 25 Among them was a fist manual, the Mountain Shaking Guide, which became the foundation of Chen Ping'an's fist techniques. Gu Can later refused to take it back. His father Gu Tao turned out to be a [[Yin god]] whose soul had never left. When he later met Chen Ping'an, he thanked him for looking after Little Can all those years.Chapter 134 (2) === Bamboo Scroll Lake === Liu Zhimao took Gu Can and his mother to Cyan Gorge Island at Bamboo Scroll Lake. When a senior brother lured Gu Can away so a guest elder could take his mother as a mistress, Gu Can let the flood dragon swallow the senior brother whole, and told his master he could either kill him and face the dragon or lose one of his many disciples.Chapter 206 (5) From then on he rode the dragon through the lake, wiped out sects that sent assassins after him, and picked beautiful girls for his future harem.Chapter 304 (2) Liu Zhimao named him the future master of Cyan Gorge Island. Chen Ping'an arrived years later and slapped him twice in public in Pond Water City. Gu Can took it without a word and brought him home, and when Chen Ping'an asked about an assassin, Gu Can explained calmly that killing her alone would not deter anyone.Chapter 430 (1) Over dinner he insisted he had done nothing wrong. Unable to kill him or walk away, Chen Ping'an broke his own second bonded item that night and stayed on the island to keep Gu Can from killing again.Chapter 432 (2) When the Upper Five Tiers cultivator Liu Laocheng came to Cyan Gorge Island, he beat Gu Can and the flood dragon to the brink of death, and only Chen Ping'an stepping in kept them alive.Chapter 437 (3) Chen Ping'an later killed Tan Xue, the flood dragon, with his sword for the lives it had taken. Gu Can ran through the snow and knelt outside his door, crying like the snotty boy from Clay Vase Alley for the first time in years.Chapter 442 (3) === Making amends === Some time later, Gu Can asked Chen Ping'an to take his mother away from Bamboo Scroll Lake. Having learned the price of not speaking reason, he wanted to learn the price of speaking it.Chapter 455 (3) His mother went back to Dragon Spring Prefecture, while Gu Can traveled the mountains around the lake with Zeng Ye, and his cultivation sped up once he committed to it, reaching the Abode Tier. Chen Ping'an left him the Hall of the Underworld and a replica of the Colored Glaze Pagoda, which held the souls of people he had killed, along with two years to arrange a Heavenly Worship Ceremony and a Liberation Rite of Water and Land for them. It was both a penance and a test.Chapter 464 (1) Gu Can kept his promise, struck deals with the angry spirits, and slowly earned respect around the lake. Before going into seclusion, Liu Zhimao visited him, passed him the River Severing Sutra, and judged that he had finally learned nuance. Gu Can thanked his master for taking him out of Clay Vase Alley, but he never opened the sutra that night. Afterward he quietly built up wealth and influence, though he privately grieved that the Gu Can Chen Ping'an most wanted to see was gone for good. == Trivia == * He is said to have received more ancestral blessing than almost anyone in the town's history, more even than Liu Xianyang. * He collected snake gall pebbles but only ever took one home at a time. * He never thought of Liu Xianyang as a friend, since Liu Xianyang loved to joke about his mother, but he envied how easily Liu Xianyang fit in anywhere. * He, Liu Xianyang and Chen Ping'an once wrote their names at the very top of a wall in the town's small temple. * Chen Ping'an paid for the couplets and door gods on Gu Can's home every year, though he was poorer than Gu Can's family. * Out of the five fated opportunities of the small town, Gu Can was the first to lose his when Tan Xue died. == References ==

pages.content:

Disciple |Current_affiliation(s)=Guo Clan
[[Sword Qi Great Wall]]
[[Downtrodden Mountain]] |Cultivation_rank=Sea Observation Tier |Novel=Chapter 581 }} == Appearance == As a child Guo Zhujiu was known for running around wrapped in nothing but a bedsheet and climbing in and out of houses through windows and over roofs rather than using doors, a habit she kept up until Dong Bude took her in hand and disciplined her out of it. == Personality == She is headstrong and relentless once she has decided on something, shown by how long and how persistently she pestered Chen Ping’an to accept her as a disciple even after he turned her down.Chapter 581 Underneath the mischief she is also generous and a bit of a schemer for a good cause, as when she talked the local children into buying wine to help Chen Ping’an and Die Zhang’s new shop get started, and left a quiet, affectionate note carved into a wooden tablet there rather than announcing the gesture outright.Chapter 582 She also has real nerve and a protective streak, willing to fight off armed attackers bare-handed to save a stranger’s life.Chapter 584 == Background == Guo Zhujiu is the daughter of Sword Immortal Guo Jia of the Guo Clan, a first-rate clan at the Sword Qi Great Wall, and was seen from a young age as having an innate talent for the sword and a likely future pillar of her clan. As a child she was unruly, until Dong Bude stepped in to discipline her. She latched onto the idea of becoming Chen Ping’an’s disciple and refused to let it go despite his repeated refusals. Chen Ping’an uses a naming-based method to judge whether someone is suited to be his disciple, and he initially felt her name, meaning “bamboo wine,” was not suitable, so he told her to wait three years instead of accepting her outright. Around this time others took to calling her “Lü Duan.”Chapter 581 She helped Chen Ping’an and Die Zhang when they opened a new wine shop, getting the neighborhood children to come buy wine to help the business get on its feet, and left a secret, affectionate inscription on a wooden tablet in the shop without taking credit for it.Chapter 582 The turning point in her relationship with Chen Ping’an came when she stepped in to rescue an emaciated boy being set upon by assassins in an alley, killing one attacker with her bare hands before being struck across the forehead by a flying sword, leaving a deep gash. The attack turned out to be a targeted assassination attempt on her specifically, rooted in rising political tension between the Ning Clan and the Guo Clan, and echoing an earlier, separate assassination attempt made on Ning Yao at the Mirage Market. Her father Guo Jia arrived afterward and negotiated her punishment down to roughly a year of being grounded. It also came out that Chen Ping’an had quietly arranged for Nalan Yexing to shadow and protect her whenever she went out, showing that he had already unofficially treated her as his disciple well before making it official. After this incident he decided to formally take her on as his disciple without further delay.Chapter 584 She met Pei Qian for the first time shortly after, addressing her as senior sister.Chapter 607 She was later formally entered into Downtrodden Mountain’s genealogical records as Chen Ping’an’s disciple. Despite her natural talent for the sword, she chose to train in fist techniques instead. Her cultivation was confirmed at the Sea Observation Tier, and she received a treasure-storage bracelet as a gift from Chen Ping’an, delivered through Cui Dongshan. Pei Qian jokingly referred to her afterward as their master’s “pseudo-closing disciple,” though the actual title of closing disciple belongs to Chen Ping’an himself under the Scholarly Sage, not to her.Chapter 610 == Trivia == Her name, Zhujiu, means “bamboo wine,” which is why Chen Ping’an initially felt it was unsuitable for a disciple under his naming method. She is nicknamed “Lü Duan” by others. She chose to learn fist techniques rather than sword techniques despite being recognized as having natural sword talent. == References ==
