[[Northern Complete Reed Continent]] (current) |Cultivation_rank=Unpolished Jade Tier |Novel=Chapter 40 }} {{Spoilers}} '''He Xiaoliang''' is a Daoist cultivator from the [[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]] whose fortune is spoken of across two continents. She was once the Jade Girl of Divine Edict Sect, the most envied young talent among that continent's Daoist orthodoxy, but she cut ties with the sect and the master who raised her to become a direct disciple of the Daoist Branch Master [[Lu Chen]] instead, later founding the Refreshing Sect on [[Northern Complete Reed Continent]] and advancing to the Unpolished Jade Tier. Lu Chen bound her fortune to [[Chen Ping An]] as part of one of his schemes, tying the two of them together through an uneven, uncertain connection. Chen Ping'an would rather never see her again, while she has come to regard him as both a danger to her Great Dao and the person she is most likely to end up spending her life with. == Appearance == He Xiaoliang is widely considered one of the two most beautiful women on Eastern Treasured Vial Continent, rivaled only by Su Jia of [[Sun Scorch Mountain]], and cultivators across the continent argue endlessly over which of them truly deserves the title. Some say she lacks Su Jia's warmth and comes across as cold and distant instead. During her time in the small town she kept an unusual white deer at her side, one able to transform into a horse. Its white coat was later revealed to be an illusion cast by Qi Zhen, hiding what was actually a Five Colored Deer.Chapter 405 == Personality == He Xiaoliang is composed, distant, and given over almost entirely to the pursuit of the Great Dao, treating most else as unimportant by comparison. Her Dao Heart rarely wavers, and she tends to judge things in blunt, uncompromising terms. She speaks her mind freely, even to her own master, and she can turn ruthless when provoked, as when she kills two of Xu Xuan's maidservants and strips him of his weapons rather than tolerate his pursuit of her. She has said more than once that she understood her own nature from a young age and never had to search for it the way others do. The one thing that reliably unsettles her is Chen Ping'an. Her calm slips when she learns their fortunes have been tied together, and she eventually admits that she cannot stop thinking about him. == Background == He Xiaoliang entered [[Divine Edict Sect]] as an unremarkable initiate with no notable background. Enlightened Saint Profound Talisman, senior brother to sect master Qi Zhen, was the only one who saw promise in her, and he took her on as his sole disciple. Under him she rose at a pace that soon outstripped every expectation, until she was named Jade Girl alongside Qi Zhen's own prized disciple as the new Golden Boy and Jade Girl of [[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]], a pairing the sect hoped would end in marriage between the two. [[Wei Jin]] of Wind Snow Temple loved her for years and was turned down every time. When he finally asked whether she would still go through with becoming Dao partners with someone chosen for her even if she never loved him, she told him she would, and that she would not come to regret it even if it left her unhappy. He left in tears.Chapter 176 As she grew older, her master's regard for her became far less innocent. He began pressing her to become his Dao partner in truth, offering to abandon the sect for her, or failing that, to carry the arrangement on in secret behind the appearance of master and disciple. When she refused, he turned to intimidation and outright coercion to force her hand. She held him off without ever openly retaliating, privately pitying him for choosing a path she viewed as too narrow to ever lead anywhere worth reaching. A fellow senior within the sect, unwilling to see her treated this way, confronted her master over the matter directly, and when Wei Jin passed through the region not long after, her master mistook him for an ally she had summoned, though she turned Wei Jin down just as she always had. In the end she chose to cut ties with Divine Edict Sect entirely rather than depend on anyone else's protection. Qi Zhen declined to brand her a traitor for leaving despite the sect elders' fury, and personally barred her master by force when he tried to chase after her.Chapter 211 == Plot == === Jewel Small World === He Xiaoliang visits the small town together with her junior brother, the Golden Boy, on a mission for their sect. One night by the stone cliff above the Dragon Whisker River, her white deer approaches Chen Ping'an, and she has a little girl translate for her, telling him that he values his own fortune, but that the two of them share too shallow a fate to ever become fellow Daoists.Chapter 40 Chen Ping'an gives her a snake gall pebble before she leaves. === Becoming Lu Chen's Disciple === Having already left her old sect, He Xiaoliang travels onward aboard a Kun ship, where she returns Chen Ping'an's old snake gall pebble for a finer one, only for Lu Chen to pluck her from the ship without warning. He had secretly tested her by nudging her into believing that she and Chen Ping'an were fated to be Dao partners, and only once she works out for herself that the two of them are in truth only loosely connected by fate does she pass his test. Lu Chen accepts her as his sixth direct disciple and permits her to found a sect of her own on Northern Complete Reed Continent. === Founding the Refreshing Sect === He Xiaoliang's swift rise on Northern Complete Reed Continent and the sect she founds there, the Refreshing Sect, draw attention throughout the continent. Watching from the White Jade Capital, Lu Chen notes the threads of fate still linking her to Chen Ping'an.Chapter 494 She later takes in the Deer Rider Divine Maiden, one of the female heavenly officials who stepped out of her own mural at Mural City, as a disciple.Chapter 488 At Skeleton Wall City in Malicious Ghost Valley, she and the city lord Gao Cheng quietly plot against Chen Ping'an. Jiang Shangzhen tries to provoke a reaction out of her, but she stays silent throughout, offering Gao Cheng only a way to build his own cycle of reincarnation before leaving without warning.Chapter 497 She later tells her disciple that a Dao partner shares in one's fortune as much as one's misfortune, and that her presence in a city so opposed to her own nature was meant to grind down the fortune she had built up through her bond with Chen Ping'an. Chen Ping'an later blames this uncertain tie to her for much of the danger he faces on the continent. === Conflict with Xu Xuan === Xu Xuan of the Jade Forest Sect pursues He Xiaoliang, hoping to become her Dao partner, and is willing to abandon his own sect for her. She rejects him, and when he pushes the matter further the two of them fight in open country, reshaping the land for kilometers around. She kills two of his maidservants and takes his saber and sword, leaving them outside the Refreshing Sect's gate for him to reclaim if he dares. The fight sets his cultivation back by years and leaves the Refreshing Sect isolated from its former allies, though He Xiaoliang remains unmoved by the fallout.Chapter 555 === Meeting on the Coast === After reaching the Unpolished Jade Tier, He Xiaoliang nearly slips back down a tier for no clear reason. She seeks out Chen Ping'an on the west coast of Northern Complete Reed Continent, claiming she was simply passing by.Chapter 553 Walking with him through an alley, she asks how he saw through her scheme with Gao Cheng, remarks on how much he has changed since the small town, and suggests that perhaps he has done nothing wrong at all, and is himself the mistake. When he asks whether they might each walk their own path from here on, she tells him to take the question up with her master instead. Chen Ping'an tells her that the Dao she chases holds the same place in her heart that [[Ning Yao]] holds in his. She understands him completely, but says she still cannot bring herself to accept it. After a long silence, she tells him that only now has she come to feel that becoming Dao partners with him would not be an obstacle at all, but the best match she could hope for. She says she will wait for him at the summit of the Majestic World, then leaves, remarking as she goes that romance between men and women is, in the end, a small thing.Chapter 554 * '''Fortune:''' spoken of across two continents as one of the most fortunate cultivators alive, ranked just behind Huang Ting.Chapter 631 * '''Cultivation:''' Unpolished Jade Tier. She expects reaching the Immortal Tier will take her centuries. * '''Treasures:''' a large collection of pocket and minimization treasures, among them a fallen nation's jade seal, an antique inkstone, a jade book, and a lotus leaf. * '''Combat:''' strong enough to defeat Xu Xuan, whose advancement to the Upper Five Tiers was close at hand. == Trivia == * Wealthy cultivators commission face masks made to resemble her, though shops are careful never to make them too accurate.Chapter 230 * It is later remarked that Qi Zhen of Divine Edict Sect should have gone to any length, even crippling and imprisoning her, to keep a disciple as fortunate as her within the sect.Chapter 559 * When Chen Ping'an eventually tells Ning Yao about his history with He Xiaoliang, Ning Yao takes it in stride, remarking only that He Xiaoliang had gone a little too far, and saying she would like to meet her someday.Chapter 581 == References == [[Category:Characters]] [[Category:Female]] [[Category:Alive]]

pages.title: Heavenly World
pages.content:
'''Location and Nature''': The Heavenly World is presented as a realm '''beyond the Majestic World'''. It's a place where Daoist sages reside, and it seems to be the ultimate destination for those who attain the highest levels of cultivation.

'''Daoist Influence''': The Heavenly World is heavily associated with '''Daoism'''. Daoist sages in this world focus on increasing the height of White Jade Capital, adding layer upon layer above its peak, rather than expanding their territories like those in the Majestic World. This suggests a focus on internal development and spiritual refinement over worldly expansion.

'''White Jade Capital''': The White Jade Capital is a significant structure within the Heavenly World. It has '''four floors''' that help cultivators suppress their internal demons using different Daoist techniques. These techniques are described as the most orthodox methods of the Daoist Sect, and they provide a smooth path to suppressing internal demons, which is a dream for many cultivators.

'''Immortal Ascension''': The Heavenly World is the place where cultivators aspire to ascend. In ancient times, there were seemingly Immortal Ascending Platforms scattered around the world to aid Qi refiners in their ascension. The sources describe an ascension as a grand event, accompanied by heavenly maidens scattering flowers, iridescent clouds, and brilliant rays of light. Those who ascend with their complete physical body and soul are seen as having received a high-level fated opportunity.

'''Connection to the Majestic World''': There are mentions of individuals who have traveled from the Heavenly World to the Majestic World. For example, a Daoist priest is said to have traveled to the south from the Heavenly World, where he engaged in a battle and acquired a treasured pearl. Furthermore, there are mentions of a rift between the two worlds. There is at least one individual who has the power to open a path between these two worlds.

'''Rulers and Sages''': The Heavenly World is inhabited by powerful Daoist sages who possess immense power and influence. The Dao Ancestor is said to have a Lotus Flower World which is one of the 36 small worlds, and just a single lotus leaf in that world is larger than the capital city of the Great Li Empire. These sages are focused on developing the White Jade Capital and helping those with a true heart in cultivation, though they also act as gatekeepers.

'''Hierarchical Structure:''' There is a sense of hierarchy and order within the Heavenly World. There is mention of an Etiquette Sage and rules laid down by them. This suggests a well-established social and spiritual order.

'''Relationship with Other Worlds''': The Heavenly World seems to be a realm that stands apart from other worlds, including the small worlds. It seems to be a destination for those who have transcended the limitations of the lower worlds. Some sources suggest that the Heavenly World is a place of immense power and that a chosen few may ascend there, implying a form of reward or recognition for those who achieve a certain level of spiritual progress.

'''The End Tier''': The 13th tier of Qi refinement, known as the Ascension Tier, is considered the End Tier, similar to the 10th tier of pure martial arts. This level of cultivation is associated with the ability to ascend into the Heavenly World.

pages.title: Heavens Beyond Heavens
pages.content:
The "heavens beyond heavens" are presented in the story as a realm or set of realms that exist above the Heavenly World, representing a further level of existence with its own characteristics and powerful beings. 

'''Hierarchical Structure and Vastness'''

* The term itself, "heavens beyond heavens," implies a '''hierarchical structure''' where the Heavenly World is just one layer in a multi-layered universe.
* These realms are described as being '''incredibly vast and expansive''', beyond the comprehension of those in lower realms.
* They are considered the origin point of "true" power, suggesting that even the most powerful figures in the Heavenly World are subject to the rules and forces of the heavens beyond heavens.
* '''Access to these realms is not easy''', and requires immense power or unique circumstances to reach.

'''Inhabitants and Their Powers'''

* The most prominent inhabitants of the heavens beyond heavens are the '''sages and patriarchs of the various teachings and sects'''. These include figures like:
** The '''Dao Ancestor''', whose power is so immense that his disciples' actions can cause shockwaves through lower worlds. He also possesses a "Lotus Flower World" that is said to be bigger than the capital of the Great Li Empire, and may reside in the heavens beyond heavens.
** The '''Buddha''', who is speculated to reside in the western pure land of Sukhavati, which is described as a realm beyond the Heavenly World where scriptures and Buddhism are discussed.
** Figures from the '''Confucian academies''' also reside in the heavens beyond heavens, observing the mortal world.
* These beings possess '''powers that are beyond the scope of those in the Heavenly World'''. They can manipulate reality, influence the fate of worlds, and even alter the fundamental laws of existence.
* It is suggested that beings in the heavens beyond heavens are '''less bound by the limitations of the lower realms''', having transcended ordinary concepts of space and time.
* Some beings in the heavens beyond heavens can also '''see through disguises and illusions''' that would fool those of lower realms, and they are able to peer into different worlds.

'''Interactions with Lower Worlds'''

* The beings in the heavens beyond heavens '''do not frequently interfere directly in the affairs of the lower worlds''', but their influence is still felt.
* They sometimes '''observe the lower realms''', using them as places to test disciples and explore philosophical concepts.
* They may '''bestow opportunities''' upon those in the lower worlds, often in the form of fated encounters and spiritual insights, though these fated opportunities can be both good and bad.
* Powerful beings from lower worlds may '''seek to ascend''' to these higher realms, either to join them or to challenge their authority.
* The '''actions of those in the heavens beyond heavens can affect events''' in lower worlds, with the shattering of the Jewel Small World having ramifications across the world.
* '''Conflicts can sometimes spill over''' from the heavens beyond heavens into the lower realms, though such occurrences are rare.

'''Key Concepts'''

* '''The Great Dao''': The heavens beyond heavens are seen as the origin point of the Great Dao, the ultimate principle governing the universe, so it is often the aim of powerful cultivators to pursue the Great Dao.
* '''Ascension''': The concept of ascension often involves leaving the lower realms and entering the heavens beyond heavens, which is often seen as the ultimate goal for cultivators, though the process for ascension is extremely difficult.
* '''Heavenly Mandate''': The idea that beings in the heavens beyond heavens can grant or revoke the mandate to rule, or can decide the fate of different beings.
* '''Testing of the Heart''': The heavens beyond heavens are presented as a realm where flaws in one's mind's realm are magnified, meaning that inner demons can grow to monstrous sizes when one reaches those high levels.

'''Additional Points of Interest'''

* The heavens beyond heavens are not static, with the Daoist sages in the heavens beyond heavens seeking to '''expand the height of the White Jade Capital'''.
* There are also suggestions that there are '''different types of heavens beyond heavens''', with the Buddhist pure land of Sukhavati being a separate plane of existence.
* The concept of the heavens beyond heavens can also be a metaphor for a '''higher state of consciousness or spiritual enlightenment'''.
* The beings of the heavens beyond heavens '''may or may not conform to traditional concepts of "good" and "evil,"''' as they exist on a plane beyond human morality.
* Some beings in the lower worlds who seek to become as powerful as the beings in the heavens beyond heavens might attempt to create a new heaven, which could be interpreted as a new set of rules for how existence itself works.

The heavens beyond heavens are depicted as a '''complex and multi-faceted concept''', representing a realm of immense power, ultimate authority, and the origin of fundamental principles. They serve as a destination for those who have reached the pinnacle of cultivation and a place of mystery and wonder that motivates those in lower worlds to strive for greater heights.

pages.title: Hundred Schools of Thought
pages.content:
The Hundred Schools of Thought represent a diverse and influential collection of philosophical and intellectual traditions within Majestic World. They encompass a wide range of disciplines, from ethics and politics to warfare and economics, shaping the world's intellectual landscape and impacting the lives of cultivators and ordinary people alike.

'''Key Insights into the Hundred Schools of Thought:'''

* '''Competition and Collaboration:''' While the Hundred Schools are often portrayed as competing factions, vying for influence and power, the sources also highlight instances of collaboration and exchange between different schools. This suggests a dynamic relationship where ideas and practices intermingle, enriching and evolving each tradition. [1-8]
* '''Influence Beyond the Three Teachings:''' Confucianism, Buddhism, and Daoism are acknowledged as the three most prominent teachings in Majestic World. However, the Hundred Schools, despite not reaching the same level of widespread recognition, exert significant influence. They offer alternative paths to cultivation and advancement, attracting followers seeking specialized knowledge or defying the conventions of the three dominant teachings. [2, 9-15]
* '''Practical Applications:''' The Hundred Schools are not merely theoretical frameworks. Their principles and teachings are applied to real-world situations, impacting governance, warfare, commerce, and even interpersonal relationships. This practical focus is evident in the actions of characters like Cui Chan, who employs techniques from various schools to achieve his goals. [3, 7, 8, 16, 17]
* '''Historical Significance:''' The Hundred Schools have shaped the history of Majestic World, influencing the rise and fall of empires, the development of cultivation techniques, and the course of major conflicts. Their legacy is evident in the numerous academies, temples, and historical sites scattered across the continents, serving as reminders of their enduring impact. [18-25]
* '''Diversity of Disciplines:''' The sources mention various schools within the Hundred Schools, each specializing in a particular area of knowledge:
* '''School of Naturalists:''' Skilled in manipulating fortune and karma, often through cultivation techniques. [3, 5]
* '''Fictionists:''' Capable of influencing reality through storytelling, with their power tied to their cultivation level and the scope of their narratives. [11, 20, 26, 27]
* '''Mohists:''' Known for their focus on universal love, logic, and practicality, often engaging in acts of chivalry and contributing to the development of technology. [4, 7, 11, 22, 28]
* '''Commercialists:''' Devoted to the principles of trade and commerce, often viewed as pragmatic and opportunistic, with a significant following despite lacking official endorsement from empires. [8, 29, 30]
* '''Diplomatists:''' Skilled in negotiation and diplomacy, playing crucial roles in inter-empire relations and alliances. [8]

'''Chen Ping'an's Encounters and the Hundred Schools:'''

Chen Ping'an's journey brings him into contact with individuals and teachings from various schools, broadening his understanding of the world and shaping his own philosophical outlook.

* He interacts with scholars and cultivators from the School of Naturalists, Fictionists, Mohists, and Commercialists, witnessing their unique abilities and learning about their principles.
* He engages in discussions about the strengths and weaknesses of different schools, comparing their approaches to cultivation, ethics, and governance.
* He observes how the teachings of various schools are applied in practical situations, from warfare and diplomacy to personal growth and self-cultivation.

Through these encounters, Chen Ping’an gains a nuanced perspective on the Hundred Schools, recognizing their diversity, complexity, and lasting impact on Majestic World. His journey serves as a microcosm of the broader intellectual landscape, showcasing the interconnectedness of different traditions and the enduring relevance of their teachings.

'''The Hundred Schools of Thought, far from being mere historical relics, remain vibrant and influential forces within Majestic World.''' They offer alternative paths to power, enlightenment, and understanding, shaping the destinies of individuals and empires alike. Their teachings continue to be debated, interpreted, and applied, ensuring their lasting legacy in this vast and wondrous realm.

pages.title: Lady Chu
pages.content:
== Appearance ==
Lady Chu is a female ghost who appears in a bright red wedding dress made of real silk, carrying an oil-paper umbrella.Chapter 122 She first approaches along a muddy mountain path, letting the mud stain her dress rather than using her powers to repel it. She can peel the skin from her face with a swipe of her hand and plaster it back on. With it in place, she looks like a beautiful young bride-to-be, apart from her deathly pale, sickly complexion.Chapter 123 She can speak without moving her lips, her voice sounding directly beside her listeners' ears.

After [[Wei Jin]]'s sword strike shatters her barrier, beads of blood seep from her wedding dress.Chapter 126 Later, when she agrees to leave her residence to the Yin god, she is no longer wearing the wedding dress at all. Chen Ping'an later admits he found her too creepy on their first meeting to notice what she actually looked like.

== Personality ==
Lady Chu is proud, volatile and terrifying when angered. When a Daoist priest addresses her as "Young Miss", she roars at him to call her "Lady", since she is wearing a wedding dress, and a storm breaks out over the mountains. Yet she can also appear soft and graceful. She welcomes the trapped children into her residence with a curtsy, calling them esteemed guests and apologising that her husband has not yet returned from a distant journey.Chapter 125 She is described as the type of resolute person who would choose to fight to the death without hesitation if pushed too far.

At heart, her cruelty comes from grief. Once a kind young woman deeply in love with a scholar, she came to believe he had betrayed her, and turned her heartbreak on every scholar who passed through her territory. She killed them and planted their corpses in her backyard as "flowers and plants".Chapter 476 (2) [[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]] later reflects that she loved the scholar very, very much, yet killed many innocent scholars because of it, and that this was a wrong that could not be easily righted.Chapter 200 (2)

== Background ==
Lady Chu rules a stretch of mountains and rivers along the [[Embroidered Flower River]], where the Great Li Empire has long recognised her residence as her territory. Above its gate hangs a plaque reading "Beautiful Water Noble Wind".Chapter 420 (1) A previous emperor of the Great Li Empire became indebted to her, and her residence still displays a Golden Characters Iron Certificate inscribed "Eternal Harmony of Mountains and Rivers". After an "unfortunate event", successive emperors tacitly allowed her to vent her anger on passing scholars.Chapter 124 The Mohist swordsman [[Xu Ruo]] explains that her actions once helped the Song Clan extend the life of the empire, but that the Song Clan later did something that left them feeling guilty towards her.Chapter 129

Long ago, an impoverished, skinny scholar passed her residence on a rainy night, reciting the Confucian classics to keep up his courage, on his way to take the imperial examinations.Chapter 145 (2) The two fell in love. The scholar hoped to earn the title of virtuous scholar through his merits, so that the imperial court would acknowledge his marriage to a ghost. However, before the Great Li Empire's rise, ambitious scholars were persecuted, and he was preyed upon by a descendant of a powerful clan. He died at [[Lake View Academy]], his corpse sinking to the bottom of its lake. Believing he had abandoned her, Lady Chu began killing scholars.

When [[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]]'s group passes along her mountain path, she traps them on a "path to the underworld" and later inside her residence. The [[Yin god]] fights her to a standstill, Wei Jin of Wind Snow Temple shatters her barrier with a single strike, and she is cut apart, retreating into her plaque before reforming.Chapter 127 Xu Ruo warns her that if another scholar vanishes, he will personally take her to the water dungeons.

The [[Yin god]], [[Yin god|Gu Tao,]] later offers her a way out: she may leave to find her scholar's corpse at Lake View Academy and seek revenge, if she hands her residence to him for a hundred years. She agrees. Years later, when Chen Ping'an returns intending to settle their old grudge, he learns that she has gone to Lake View Academy to collect the corpse of a scholar who died there.Chapter 426 Barred from the academy as a ghost, she forced her way in and nearly died. She used the last of her goodwill with the imperial court to take his remains, and learned the truth: he had never betrayed her, and his love for her was what led to his death. The truth drove her insane. After Gu Tao leaves the residence, she returns in mourning clothes with a coffin, telling anyone who will listen that she is waiting for someone.Chapter 567 (3)

== Trivia ==

* Her full name is never revealed. "Lady Chu" is how she asks to be addressed.
* Chen Ping'an counts her, along with [[Zhu Lu]] and [[Ma Kuxuan]], among the very few people he has ever truly detested. His encounter with her left him with a lasting dislike of troublesome ghosts and yin entities.
* For a long time, Chen Ping'an regarded Wei Jin's strike against her barrier as the pinnacle of flying sword strikes, until he saw Zuo You at the Flood Dragon Trench.
* Her residence later falls within the territory of [[Wei Bo]] as Northern Mountain God, although its affairs are managed by the Ritual Office of the Great Li Empire's Ministry of Rites.
* Zhu Lian was disappointed not to learn whether she was beautiful.

pages.title: Large Worlds
pages.content:
Large worlds are a fundamental part of the cosmology of the narrative, representing the most significant and powerful realms in existence.

'''Definition and Nature:'''

* Large worlds are described as realms that '''run through heaven and earth''' and possess an '''abundance of spiritual energy'''.
* They are considered '''bona fide immortal abodes''', making them ideal places for cultivation.
* They are distinct from the 36 small worlds and are much more expansive.
* The rulers of these worlds are '''blessed with immense fortune''', and these worlds have already been divided among the most powerful figures of the three teachings.

'''Number and Organization:'''

* There are '''10 large worlds''' in total.
* These worlds are the '''most significant realms in the cosmology''', and they are usually controlled by powerful figures or groups.
* They are often contrasted with the smaller, less stable mystical realms.
* The ten large worlds are often referenced as a group when compared to the thirty-six small worlds.

'''Significance and Power:'''

* Cultivating in large worlds can significantly '''speed up a Qi refiner's progress''' due to the abundant spiritual energy.
* The '''most powerful figures in the three teachings''' have already divided the large worlds among themselves, making it difficult for others to gain control over them.
* Large worlds are seen as the '''ultimate destinations for cultivators''' seeking to reach the highest levels of power and enlightenment.
* They are '''the source of power for many major forces''' and are often the heart of the most important events and conflicts.

'''Comparison with Small Worlds:'''

* While both large and small worlds can possess significant spiritual energy, large worlds are generally considered to be '''more stable and more complete'''.
* Small worlds are often described as damaged or incomplete compared to the '''pristine nature''' of the large worlds.
* Large worlds are '''more vast''' and hold more spiritual energy than small worlds.
* The ten large worlds are usually the '''center of power for major factions''', while the 36 small worlds are often hidden and more independent.

'''Examples of Large Worlds'''

* The sources do not explicitly name all ten of the large worlds.
* However, one source mentions the '''Middle Earth Divine Continent''' as being like "the glowing gem that was Middle Earth Divine Continent" and that several major empires exist on that continent.
* It is also mentioned that the '''Lotus Flower World''' is one of the 36 small worlds, and legend states it is where the Dao Ancestor goes to relax. It is not one of the ten large worlds, despite its size.

'''Rulers of Large Worlds'''

* The rulers of large worlds are described as people '''blessed with immense fortune''', and they belong to the most powerful figures of the three teachings.
* The sources imply that these rulers are some of the '''most powerful beings in the cosmos''', and their control over the large worlds is absolute.

'''Relationship to Cultivation:'''

* Large worlds provide an environment where Qi refiners can significantly '''accelerate their cultivation''' due to the abundance of spiritual energy.
* The division of the large worlds among the most powerful figures suggests that control over these worlds is key to '''attaining immense power and influence'''.

The text implies that to become a Sage, one must occupy and control a large world.

The large worlds are '''the most powerful and significant realms in the story'''. They are the pinnacle of cultivation, offering unparalleled resources and opportunities for those who can access them. They are the focus of much of the power struggle in the narrative and are essential to understanding the cosmology and dynamics of the world. The immense fortune, the vast territory, and the control over these worlds make them central to the ambitions of cultivators and the overall narrative. They are also the benchmark against which all other worlds are compared, highlighting their immense importance in the grand scheme of the cosmos.

Li Clan of Fortune Street |Continent=[[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]] |Novel=Chapter 7 }} '''Li Baoping''' is the youngest child and only daughter of Li Hong, the leader of the Li Clan of [[Fortune Street]] in [[Jewel Small World]]. She is one of [[Qi Jingchun]]'s five direct disciples and travels to [[Mountain Cliff Academy]] in Great Sui Nation under the protection of Chen Ping'an, whom she calls her "junior uncle". == Appearance == Li Baoping is a small girl with her hair in two braids and cheeks often flushed from running. She wears a red jacket as a matter of habit. Setting out for the academy, she carries a small basket on her back topped with a conical bamboo hat, with no fewer than seven or eight embroidered pouches hanging all over her body. Her bamboo bookcase, which is the earliest of the three that Chen Ping'an made, crafted from ordinary green bamboo, stays as verdant as the day it was made even years later.Chapter 86Volume 7, Chapter 384 == Personality == Li Baoping is bright, direct and relentlessly curious. She chatters freely, asks questions without end, and does not let an unsatisfying answer go. She has a strong sense of fairness and is quick to step in on behalf of anyone she thinks is being wronged. When Li Huai's classmate at Mountain Cliff Academy snatched a book from him, Li Baoping announced she would tear it in half and give each of them a piece — and when the other child agreed, she tossed the book to Li Huai and beat the thief up instead. An old scholar watching from a distance laughed heartily at her solution.Volume 6, Chapter 310 She is also stubborn, competitive and not above gloating. Li Huai is her habitual sparring partner in both argument and mischief. None of the children at the private school could match her in a fight. Her affection for Chen Ping'an is genuine. She calls him "junior uncle", repeats things he says, holds him to his own principles, and tells him bluntly when she thinks he is wrong. When he sends letters to the children at Mountain Cliff Academy, she convenes the whole group using a self-carved "alliance leader badge" before reading each letter aloud in order, saving his letter to her for last, and she has read it nine times through.Volume 4, Chapter 210 == Background == Li Baoping is one of five children from the private school whom Qi Jingchun took as direct disciples, giving each of them the character Qi before he died. The others are Li Huai, Lin Shouyi, Shi Chunjia and Dong Shuijing. Cui Chan considered it remarkable that she, out of all of them, was Qi Jingchun's true direct disciple.Volume 3, Chapter 235 She grew up in the Li Clan manor on Fortune Street. Her grandfather, the Li Clan patriarch, is a Nascent Tier earth immortal and a top-level guest elder of the Great Li Empire — a status the clan kept private for many years. He is openly devoted to her, adoring her more than both grandsons combined. Her father Li Hong loves her best of all his children. Her older brother Li Xisheng taught at the private school and watched over her from a distance, while Li Baozhen sent her letters from the capital that she treasured and read eagerly. She and Chen Ping'an first properly encountered each other when the old locust tree in Clay Vase Alley was uprooted. She had gone to look at it instead of going to school, and he found her there. He gave her three of the locust leaves he had collected, and she kept them.Chapter 7 She was close to Zhu Lu, the Li Clan maidservant who taught her about martial arts and whom she had once followed everywhere. == Plot == === Journey to Mountain Cliff Academy === Li Baoping set out from [[Jewel Small World]] with Chen Ping'an, accompanied by Zhu He and Zhu Lu, bound for Mountain Cliff Academy in Great Sui Nation. Ruan Xiu packed her basket with maps, books and travel money. She left in high spirits, jumping for joy when Chen Ping'an gave the word to depart.Chapter 86 On the road she and A'Liang got along easily, in contrast to almost everyone else he travelled with, and she gave him a thumbs up when others refused to engage with him. At Go Table Mountain she and the group survived the attack of the black and white pythons, and she witnessed Zhu Lu's panicked decision to free Wei Bo and Zhu He's inability to hold his daughter accountable.Chapter 99 At Pillow Relay Station, Zhu Lu attempted to assassinate Chen Ping'an on Li Baozhen's secret instructions. Chen Ping'an told Li Baoping the truth, believing she needed to know what the people around her had done. She was deeply hurt.Chapter 110 She eventually reached Mountain Cliff Academy and settled into life there, attending classes on her own, climbing trees and buildings, squatting by the lake to watch fish, and generally puzzling her classmates with her habits. In her own assessment, she was having a decent time.Volume 6, Chapter 310 === At Mountain Cliff Academy === When Chen Ping'an sent letters to the group from afar, Li Baoping gathered everyone with her wooden alliance leader badge, read all letters aloud, and distributed them — except to Li Huai, who had not been written to, much to his humiliation.Volume 4, Chapter 210 She and the other Mountain Cliff Academy students attended the Night Travel Banquet hosted by the Great Li Empire's Northern Mountain as a group excursion, led by Mao Xiaodong, where she was reunited with Jiu'er, a young girl she had befriended earlier and missed greatly. When Chen Ping'an visited, Li Baoping met Pei Qian, his attendant. The two girls took to each other immediately. In a later meeting, Pei Qian launched herself at Li Baoping the moment she saw her, and Li Baoping patted her on the head and teased her about growing taller. Li Baoping, Pei Qian and Cui Dongshan ended up sitting together on a branch at the mountain summit, and Li Baoping felt it was a shame her junior uncle was not there to join them.Volume 9, Chapter 601 == Trivia == * Li Baoping is said to have been born unable to sit still, always darting around — a quirk her family attributed fondly to her constitution.Chapter 87 (1) * She once built a pond in the Li Clan courtyard for Li Xisheng by collecting pebbles from Dragon Whisker Creek over many months. When he tried to help with the physical work, she refused.Volume 3, Chapter 181 * The three bamboo bookcases Chen Ping'an made (for Li Baoping, Li Huai and Lin Shouyi) were crafted at different times. Li Baoping's was made first, from ordinary green bamboo. The other two were made after Go Table Mountain, using the courage bamboo Wei Bo had given them. All three remained as green as ever years later. == References == [[Category:Characters]] [[Category:Female]] [[Category:Alive]] [[Category:Human]]

pages.title: Li Baozhen
pages.content:
{{Character |header1=Li Baozhen |image1=Li Baozhen.png |Vital_status=Alive |Gender=Male |Species=Human |Relatives=Li Hong (father)
[[Li Xisheng]] (older brother)
[[Li Baoping]] (younger sister) |Allies=[[Cui Chan]] |Enemie(s)=[[Chen Ping An]] |Occupation=Leader of the southeastern division, Green Ripple Pavilion |Current_affiliation(s)=Green Ripple Pavilion
[[Great Li Empire]] |Continent=[[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]] |Novel=Chapter 127 }} == Appearance == He is a young man from [[Fortune Street]], described as truly young and filled with unrestrained vigour when he appears in the Azure Phoenix Nation, where he speaks its official dialect fluently.Chapter 396 (3) Chen Ping'an had never actually seen him before their encounter on the road near Lion Garden. Li Baozhen calls himself "nothing more than a scholar who can't withstand a single punch".Chapter 398 (2) == Personality == Li Baozhen is charming, clever and ambitious. Within the Li Clan he is far more likeable than his quiet elder brother, Li Xisheng.Chapter 181 He is widely regarded as the smartest of the three Li siblings, and he is his mother's favourite. She keeps every letter he sends her in a small red box.Chapter 206 (3) He is also impatient, reckless and unwilling to admit fault. His father complains that he promised to follow the rules and avoid hidden schemes after leaving the small town, then "decided to act first and ask later".Chapter 127 Li Xisheng says that his brother has never been willing to acknowledge his mistakes since childhood.Chapter 191 (1) He is shrewd and ruthless; Shi Rou, who met him, regards him as such. He sees others as pieces on a Go board, and openly delights in other people's misfortune. Cui Chan, his patron, judges that Li Baozhen's pursuits are nothing special: all he wants is to accumulate merits and climb the official hierarchy.Chapter 406 (2) Despite his arrogance, he can be candid about his own fears. He admits to a carriage driver that he has never been a courageous person, given how many powerful beings lived in his hometown.Chapter 397 (2) == Background == Li Baozhen is the second son of Li Hong, leader of the Li Clan of Fortune Street, the younger brother of [[Li Xisheng]] and the older brother of [[Li Baoping]]. After leaving the small town for the capital of the Great Li Empire, he quickly made a name for himself, finding a powerful backer who arranged for him to study at the imperial academy. That backer later fell from power.Chapter 132 It was under Li Baozhen's secret direction that the Li Clan maidservant [[Zhu Lu]] tried to assassinate [[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]] at Pillow Relay Station. A hidden message in his letter to Li Baoping spurred the infatuated Zhu Lu to act "for the sake of love".Chapter 392 (1) Li Xisheng offered Chen Ping'an his peach wood talisman as an apology in his brother's place, and Chen Ping'an promised Li Xisheng that he would spare Li Baozhen once. Under Imperial Preceptor [[Cui Chan]], Li Baozhen joins the Great Li Empire's intelligence agency, the Green Ripple Pavilion, as leader of its southeastern division. Cui Chan offered him three postings, and he was sent to the Azure Phoenix Nation to work under the scholar Liu Qingfeng.Chapter 398 (1) When Chen Ping'an unexpectedly appears on the road near Lion Garden, Li Baozhen laments that the intelligence reports have "screwed him over", then secretly reaches for a talisman. Chen Ping'an pins his talisman to the carriage wall with his flying sword, beats him with a single punch, and keeps his promise to Li Xisheng by sparing him. He confiscates Li Baozhen's Dragon Palace jade pendant and Day and Night Wandering Deity True Body Talisman, an heirloom passed down by the Li Clan's ancestors, and later gives both to Li Baoping. By doing so, Chen Ping'an separates Li Baozhen from the rest of the Li Clan in his mind.Chapter 408 Li Baozhen goes on to complete his task in the Azure Phoenix Nation, undermining the northern scholars' alliance leader Liu Jingting.Chapter 414 (3) He later runs an ambitious grassroots experiment there, sending promising scholars, martial heroes and cultivation prodigies into the region's sects so that even immortal sects could one day be governed by mortal empires. Liu Qingfeng allows it to proceed, observing every step.Chapter 535 (3) == Trivia == * Li Baozhen's and Li Baoping's names both contain the character "bao" (宝), while Li Xisheng's does not, a detail that later proves significant to the secret of Li Xisheng's birth.Chapter 563 (1) * According to Li Baozhen himself, Zhu Lu fled to him in the capital in tears after her failure, and he nearly killed her with a single slap. * Chen Ping'an regards him as a grudge he cannot avoid, alongside Zhu Lu. * Liu Qingfeng, Li Baozhen and Wei Liang are later named as three people in the Azure Phoenix Nation whose actions could have implications even beyond Eastern Treasured Vial Continent. == References == [[Category:Characters]] [[Category:Male]] [[Category:Fights]] [[Category:Alive]] [[Category:Human]]

pages.content:
{{Tabs|tab1=Li Er}}{{Character|Vital_status=Alive|Gender=Male|Species=Human|Novel=??|image1=LiEr.jpg|Donghua=??|Chinese=李二|Pinyin=Lǐ Èr|Age=??|Hair_color=Black|Eye_color=Dark Brown|image2=Unsheathed-novel-1.webp|image3=|image4=|Love_interest(s)=|Title=Li Er|Relatives=[[Li Huai]] (Son) 
[[Li Liu]] (Daughter)|Cultivation_rank=10th(current)}}Li Er is a side character of the series [[Donghua|Sword of Coming]].

== Appearance ==
Li Er is a rugged, middle-aged man with a sturdy and burly build that reflects a life of manual labor. He has a weather-beaten face, simple black hair usually kept in a practical style, and dark, unassuming eyes. He is almost always seen wearing coarse, drab commoner’s clothing made of hemp or linen, typically in shades of brown or grey. His most recognizable feature is the large bamboo basket he carries on his back, often appearing barefoot or in simple straw sandals, which makes him look like a typical laborer rather than a legendary figure.
== Personality ==
Li Er is exceptionally stoic and low-key. He has no interest in the fame or politics of the immortal world and prefers to live a quiet, unremarkable life. He is a man of very few words, but he is defined by a fierce, silent loyalty to his family. While he is a protective father to his son, Li Huai, and his daughter, Li Liu, he is also known for being humorously submissive to his wife. He approaches conflict with a blunt, "straight-line" logic, relying on his overwhelming physical presence and fearless attitude to settle matters directly, often willing to challenge entire sects or empires if they threaten his children.

== Background ==
Li Er’s background begins in the mysterious Lizhu Cave Heaven, the same small town where the story starts. While many youths in the town were recruited by great sects for their spiritual potential or scholarly talent, Li Er took the difficult path of a Pure Martial Artist, focusing entirely on physical tempering and endurance. He eventually left the small town to settle at Lion Peak in the Southern Baoyue State. Throughout the story, he serves as a symbol of peak physical strength, proving that a person who looks like a common worker can command enough power to rival the world's strongest beings. He appears early in both the novel and the donghua, initially blending into the background as just another ordinary resident of the town.

== Trivia ==

[[Xie Xie]] |Occupation = Student |Current_affiliation(s) = [[Mountain Cliff Academy]] |Former_affiliation(s) = Qi Jingchun's private school |Continent = [[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]] |Novel = Chapter 67 }} {{Spoilers}} '''Li Huai''' is one of the last five students of [[Qi Jingchun]]'s private school in the small town, and the youngest member of the group that [[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]] escorts to [[Mountain Cliff Academy]] in [[Great Sui Nation]], alongside [[Li Baoping]] and [[Lin Shouyi]]. He is the son of [[Li Er]], a man the whole town dismisses as a useless drunkard, but who is secretly one of the three End Tier (tenth tier) martial artists on [[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]]. Loud, lazy and sharp-tongued, Li Huai is often treated as comic relief and consistently ranks last in his classes. Yet he is surrounded by an almost absurd amount of good fortune: treasures, spirits and even a white deer seem to fall into his lap without effort. [[Cui Dongshan]] calls him the luckiest person alive, and Old Man Yang considers his fortune greater than that of the most famously fortunate cultivators of the age. == Appearance == As a child, Li Huai is the youngest and smallest of the group, poor enough that his toes poke through his worn boots when the journey begins. He almost always carries the small green bamboo bookcase Chen Ping'an made for him, and for special occasions he wears a black jade hairpin engraved "Huaiyin". By the time he is a teenager at the academy, he has grown taller than his sister [[Li Liu]]. == Personality == Li Huai is cheeky, talkative and quick with insults, loves to stir up trouble, and has a habit of "offering" his sister in marriage to anyone he admires. Nobody can beat him in an argument, and even Mr. Qi struggled to get him to listen. He is lazy about study and training, dozes in class, and openly wishes for a shortcut that would make him an immortal overnight. [[A'Liang]] sums him up as a little tyrant at home and a coward outside: bold with friends and family, but timid around strangers, crowds and ghosts. He takes this trait after his mother. As a child he was so afraid of the dark that Chen Ping'an accompanied him every time he needed to relieve himself at night, sometimes being shaken awake to do so. Beneath the mischief, he is kind-hearted, never holds a grudge, and always remembers who has been good to him. Chen Ping'an describes him as having a tongue coated in honey but dipped in arsenic, while being fundamentally pure and kind. He worries for his family, fearing his quiet father and sister will be pushed around once his mother is too old to argue for them. The journey to Great Sui and his early bullying at the academy make him noticeably more mature. Mao Xiaodong observes that although Li Huai learns slowly, he genuinely absorbs what he understands rather than just memorising, which is why his teachers like him despite his grades. As a teenager, he tells his sister that passages he once couldn't memorise have become impossible to forget after his travels. == Background == Li Huai grew up in a poor house on the west side of the small town. His father was mocked as a timid good-for-nothing and his mother was famous for out-arguing everyone. Li Huai was teased at school because of his father and was long ashamed of him. Li Baoping was the only classmate who never mocked Li Er and greeted him as "Uncle Li", which is why Li Huai never resents her beatings. When he was small, Li Er worked at the Yang Family Medicine Shop, and Li Huai often ran around its backyard, a place almost nobody else was allowed into. He would roll in the mud, wet himself, and then sit for hours watching Old Man Yang smoke his pipe. [[Zheng Dafeng]] often carried him there on his back. Without telling him, Li Er also bathed him in medicinal wine every month, which made him far tougher than an ordinary child. Li Huai remembers a night when a neighbour scratched his mother's face and his father seemed to do nothing. Li Er calmly said he was "going out of the mountains", left, and came back weeks later with presents. In truth, Li Er had left Jewel Small World and fought his way up a powerful sect's mountain to destroy its ancestral hall. Shortly before the story begins, his parents and sister left the town, and Li Huai was left with an uncle and aunt who treated him harshly.Chapter 67 (2) == Plot == === Leaving the Small Town === After Qi Jingchun's death, Li Huai sets off with the other four remaining students and [[Ma Zhan]] on an excursion to Mountain Cliff Academy. When [[Cui Minghuang]] kills Ma Zhan, it is Li Huai who finds him dying. Back in town, the children trick a suspicious coach driver: Li Huai claims to know Chen Ping'an and leads the driver on a long detour while Li Baoping warns Chen Ping'an.Chapter 84 (1) Li Huai refuses to go to the capital to join his family and instead follows Chen Ping'an's group. === Journey to Great Sui === Li Huai bickers constantly with A'Liang, offering him his sister for his wine gourd. While inspecting him, A'Liang discovers that his true condition is hidden by an advanced concealment technique, with purple qi rising in him like a mountain range.Chapter 96 At Go Table Mountain, Li Huai throws a tantrum in the mud and only stops when Chen Ping'an promises him a bamboo bookcase. During the white snake attack, he turns back to yell at the frozen [[Zhu Lu]] to run. When the mountain's treasures are shared out, he takes a painted puppet and the yellow ebony box they came in.Chapter 104 In [[Red Candle Town]], Chen Ping'an buys him the book ''Severed Water Cliff'', which turns out to be an old book inhabited by silverfish; A'Liang also seals a green darkness fish into it. Li Huai weeps when A'Liang leaves for battle and is left caring for his white donkey. On the Embroidered Flower River, Chen Ping'an makes him apologise for the donkey frightening a child, then defends him when the child's family threatens them anyway. After the encounter with the ghost [[Lady Chu]], [[Wei Jin]] sees through the barrier on Li Huai's aptitude, judges it better than Lin Shouyi's, and gives him five small clay statues that may come to life if nurtured.Chapter 128 The [[Yin god]] escorting them privately reveals that Old Man Yang sent him specifically to protect Li Huai.Chapter 130 Once [[Cui Chan]] joins the group, Li Huai receives a "bug silver" from him and later wins a dancing glass figure. At the Autumn Reed Inn, Chen Ping'an carves him the "Huaiyin" hairpin, and Li Huai shows him the sheet bearing the character "Qi" that Mr. Qi gave each student as final homework. When he tucks it into ''Severed Water Cliff'', the book's silverfish and fish swim into the paper as if returning to water.Chapter 141 Qi Jingchun later reveals that giving his students the character "Qi" was how he passed part of his remaining fortune to them. === Early Academy Years === Chen Ping'an leaves without saying goodbye, and Li Huai cries alone in his dormitory. His dorm mates mock his poverty, steal his puppet and clay statues, and beat him. Li Baoping confronts them with her saber, Lin Shouyi is badly hurt in the escalating conflict, and Yu Lu eventually takes matters into his own hands.Chapter 162 (2) Li Huai moves into Lin Shouyi's dormitory, gets his belongings back, and spends an afternoon quietly writing his family members' names in the dirt. His family then visits. Li Huai praises Chen Ping'an at length, no longer feels ashamed of his father, and apologises to him for how he treated him.Chapter 168 (2) Without Li Huai's knowledge, Li Er breaks through to the tenth tier, forces Great Sui's powerful clans to answer for the bullying, and realises that Old Man Yang had been deliberately suppressing Li Huai's aptitude.Chapter 170 (1) Before leaving, Li Er gets Li Huai drunk and grips his wrist as if about to do something important; what he did is not revealed directly. Over the following years, Li Huai's family moves to the town at the foot of Lion Peak on [[Northern Complete Reed Continent]], where his sister begins cultivating. At the academy, Li Huai makes two close friends, the bold, poor and talented Liu Guan and the timid rich boy Ma Lian. The three become sworn brothers in a ceremony using sparrows in place of chickens and pages torn from library books in place of yellow paper, and are beaten by their teacher for it. Li Baoping makes him "division leader" of his dormitory in her imaginary martial-arts alliance, a title he takes very seriously. === Chen Ping'an's Visit === Almost three years after arriving, Li Huai climbs the academy's mountain alone and tries to write Chen Ping'an's name in the dirt, believing that writing his parents' names is what brought them to visit. Li Baoping keeps wiping it away until he cries, then makes him write it neatly. Chen Ping'an arrives at the academy that very day.Chapter 400 (3) By then, the academy's leadership regards Li Huai as the least talented of the group academically but the most dangerous to provoke. Li Huai is overjoyed, greets him with "Grandmaster Li's Invincible Fist Technique", and immediately tries to make him his brother-in-law. He also becomes fast friends with Chen Ping'an's disciple [[Pei Qian]], who convinces him she is a lost princess. The two hold a "showdown for the ages" comparing their treasure collections on the mountain summit, which Li Huai loses, and play pranks such as staging a mock assassination of Cui Dongshan. They promise to travel the cultivation world together hunting treasure and to split the spoils evenly. During an assassination attempt on the academy, Li Huai, Li Baoping and Pei Qian are locked in a study for safety. Afterwards, the white deer of the scholar Zhao Shi chooses Li Huai of its own accord, and Zhao Shi gives it to him. Cui Dongshan calls it a slice of immense fortune falling into his lap.Chapter 411 Before Chen Ping'an leaves, Li Huai stars in a farewell performance as "Paramount Fists and Feet Hero Li", wearing a bamboo hat and riding the white deer in imitation of A'Liang. Chen Ping'an also teaches him that while Chen Ping'an can bend certain rules, Li Huai should not assume he can until he understands them. === Visit to Dragon Spring Prefecture === Li Huai returns home on an academy excursion led by Mao Xiaodong to watch the Night Travel Banquet. He brings Liu Guan and Ma Lian to his empty family house, then bursts into the Yang Family Medicine Shop with a gift of tobacco for Old Man Yang. He scolds Zheng Dafeng, smacks Old Man Yang on the head, and lectures him about his health, astonishing the shop's new apprentices. Old Man Yang, unusually, smiles and tells him there are indeed a few items set aside for him, to be discussed later.Chapter 471 (4) === Later Years === Chen Ping'an later stays with Li Huai's family at Lion Peak and sleeps in the room prepared for Li Huai. He sends Li Huai a wooden deity statue through Li Liu, and earlier passed him a veiled clay statuette, likely part of the same set as Wei Jin's gift. Old Man Yang reflects that Li Huai attracts fortune more naturally than even Huang Ting and [[He Xiaoliang]], and that he truly likes the boy.Chapter 530 (1) As a teenager, Li Huai still struggles with his studies, but loves the long journeys the academy organises with its teachers. When Li Liu visits with a bag of treasures disguised by restrictions, he tells her to stop giving things to her family once she marries, so she will not be looked down on by her husband. He admits he only thought of this after talking to Chen Ping'an.Chapter 569 (2) When Chen Ping'an and Pei Qian visit again, Li Huai is outraged that Chen Ping'an kept his new mountain, [[Downtrodden Mountain]], a secret from his "sworn brother", and demands to become its chief guest elder. He is equally outraged when Li Baoping hands her title of alliance leader to Pei Qian. == Abilities == He imitates Chen Ping'an's walking meditation and fist stances only half-heartedly. His aptitude, however, is remarkable: * It was hidden by an advanced concealment technique, which A'Liang saw through. * Wei Jin judged it better than Lin Shouyi's and highly prized by Militarians. * Old Man Yang deliberately suppressed it, and said his sister was talented while Li Huai was blessed with great fortune. * His father's medicinal wine baths gave him unusual stamina; he walked to Great Sui without getting a single blister. == Possessions == * '''Bamboo bookcase''': made by Chen Ping'an from courage bamboo given by [[Wei Bo]]; it stays green years later. * '''Straw sandals''': several pairs made by Chen Ping'an, which he treasures. * '''Black jade hairpin''': engraved "Huaiyin" by Chen Ping'an, one of his three most prized possessions with the bookcase and sandals. * '''Painted puppet''': from the Go Table Mountain treasures; his "number one general". * '''Yellow ebony box''': turned red from centuries underground, still fragrant. * '''''Severed Water Cliff''''': an old book home to silverfish and a green darkness fish. * '''Mr. Qi's "Qi" character''': now inhabited by the book's spirits. * '''Five clay statues''' from Wei Jin, plus a veiled female statuette from Chen Ping'an. * '''Bug silver''' and a '''dancing glass figure''', both from Cui Chan. * '''White deer''': formerly Zhao Shi's. * '''Wooden deity statue''': a gift from Chen Ping'an via Li Liu. * '''Bag from Li Liu''': treasures disguised by restrictions. * '''Ma Lian's bamboo case''': a case of items Ma Lian's family treated as junk. Like most things that come to Li Huai, the text implies they are real treasures. * '''White donkey''' (formerly): A'Liang's donkey, later reclaimed by Wei Jin. == Trivia == * 槐 (huái) means locust tree (Chinese scholar tree); "Huaiyin" means "locust shade". * He once answered a teacher who asked whether the drumstick or the ruler tasted better that both were fine if one came with the other. * He and Pei Qian redrew fish and cages onto Cui Dongshan's priceless antique paintings, and played jacks with his priceless Vibrant Cloud go stones. * His parents call him "Huai'er". His mother is never given a full name; Chen Ping'an addresses her as "Aunt Liu" when he meets her at Lion Peak. == References == [[Category:Male]] [[Category:Characters]] [[Category:Alive]]

{{Character |header1 = Li Liu |image1 = Li Liu.png |Aliases = Little Willow (by Zheng Dafeng)
Esteemed Founder (by Lion Peak) |Vital_status = Alive |Gender = Female |Species = Human (reincarnated) |Master(s) = [[Old Man Yang]] (Dao mentor) |Disciple(s) = Huang Cai (from a past life) |Relatives = [[Li Er]] (father)
Aunt Liu (mother)
[[Li Huai]] (brother) |Friend(s) = [[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]] |Allies = [[Cao Xi]] (Dao guardian)
[[Zheng Dafeng]]
[[Zhu Lian]] |Enemie(s) = [[Ruan Xiu]] (ancient rival) |Occupation = Founder of Lion Peak |Current_affiliation(s) = Lion Peak |Continent = [[Northern Complete Reed Continent]] |Cultivation_rank = Nascent Tier (as of Volume 8) |Novel = Chapter 73 }} {{Spoilers}} '''Li Liu''' is the older sister of [[Li Huai]] and the daughter of [[Li Er]]. To her family and neighbours she is a quiet, gentle and pretty girl who never speaks much. In truth, she is the reincarnation of one of the most powerful ancient beings of the heavens, born with the full memories of her countless past lives. She has a deep connection to water and an ancient grudge against [[Ruan Xiu]]. Through all of this, Li Liu cares about very few things in the world, and her family, above all her little brother, is at the top of that list. == Appearance == Li Liu is slender, delicate and soft-looking, often compared to a willow branch in spring. She is not the kind of beauty who stuns at first glance, but one who grows more beautiful the longer she is looked at, with particularly lovely eyes. She is described as resembling her mother in looks while taking after her father in temperament. When she smiles, her eyebrows curve into crescents. At Lion Peak she carries a golden lion seal and a short sword at her waist, both hidden by concealment restrictions. == Personality == At home, Li Liu is mild, patient and obedient. She accepts her mother's open favouritism towards Li Huai without complaint, takes every scolding with a smile, and quietly helps in the family shop. She almost never gets angry or laughs loudly. Her mother calls her a lump of soft dough that anyone could bully. Outside her home, she is a completely different person. Having lived through so many lifetimes, she regards most of the world with indifference and treats lesser beings, even powerful cultivators and water gods, with cold disdain. She can be shockingly ruthless, as when she gouges out a fox spirit's eye on a whim. She has little patience for sentiment, saying she has experienced too many joys, sorrows, separations and reunions to feel much about them anymore. She also openly dislikes sword users of every era. The one thing that reliably softens her is Li Huai. Whenever her brother is mentioned, her expression turns gentle and she looks like the young girl who used to carry water to the town well. She also reflects that the small town was the only place in all her lives where she met many "genuine people", and she thinks of it with longing. == Background == Li Liu was born in the small town in a birth deliberately arranged by Old Man Yang of the Yang Family Medicine Shop, who placed her family close to his shop. Unlike other reincarnated beings he guided, she never needed her memories unlocked, because she was born with them.Chapter 530 (1) Old Man Yang told her plainly that if she kept cultivating in her old way, changing bodies and climbing quickly each life, she would remain stuck at the Immortal Tier forever, "a half-assed individual who couldn't even act like a human". Her real assignment in this life, as she sees it, is not to advance in cultivation but to learn how to be a person.Chapter 557 (1) Old Man Yang is her Dao mentor, unlike Li Er and [[Zheng Dafeng]], whom he only calls his disciples.Chapter 253 (1) He once said that Li Liu was talented while Li Huai was blessed with fortune. Her talent is that she was born with intuitive knowledge.Chapter 206 (4) In the town, Li Liu kept a low profile. She had no close friends, never went to school, and often went to the private school to fetch Li Huai, carrying herself with natural grace. Both [[Lin Shouyi]] and [[Dong Shuijing]] fell for her. Qi Jingchun only ever nodded at her through the classroom window. The one time he spoke to her was when he came to drink with Li Er. He told her that what defines a person is not their decaying body but how they live, and he raised his bowl of cheap wine to pay respects to "her kind", as the reason for the existence of his own kind and the world itself. == Plot == === Early Appearances === Li Liu is first mentioned as Li Huai's older sister, who left the town with their parents.Chapter 73 Li Huai repeatedly "offers" her as a bride to people he admires, including [[A'Liang]] and [[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]]. Her family later returns to visit Li Huai at Mountain Cliff Academy. There she quietly helps her brother, refuses the painted puppet he tries to give her, and sews him cloth shoes. Lin Shouyi can barely look at her.Chapter 168 (1) As her family leaves the academy, her eyes meet those of [[Cui Dongshan]]. It is later revealed that she made a deliberately provocative gesture at him, knowing exactly who he was, and Cui Dongshan recalls it with alarm years later. === Journey North === On the ship to [[Northern Complete Reed Continent]], her father cripples a group of cultivators who harass the family, then claims the ship's overseer simply scolded them. Li Liu has to suppress a smile at her father finally learning to lie. Meanwhile, Old Man Yang arranges a deal with the sword immortal [[Cao Xi]]: the souls of Cao Xi's parents are in Li Liu's possession, and in return for them, Cao Xi must give her his old flying sword, teach her his sword technique and act as her Dao guardian.Chapter 235 (2) A young scholar surnamed Situ travels with the family for part of the journey, and Li Liu's mother hopes in vain that he will marry her. === Lion Peak === The family settles at Lion Peak, whose master claims a connection to Old Man Yang. Li Er opens a shop in the small town at the foot of the mountain, and a Lion Peak immortal "coincidentally" discovers Li Liu's aptitude. In reality, Li Liu is the reincarnation of the founder of Lion Peak. After seeing her parents off, the entire leadership of the mountain bows to her as "Esteemed Founder". She walks into a sealed cave whose restrictions even earth immortals cannot break and comes out wearing a golden lion seal. When Cao Xi hands her his short sword, she casually unleashes a stroke of sword qi that splits the sky, having stepped straight into the Middle Five Tiers.Chapter 283 (2) The current mountain master, Huang Cai, was a starving beggar boy she took in during a past life. He became her only direct disciple and has guarded Lion Peak ever since. Over the next years, Li Liu becomes the second most important figure on Lion Peak, even treated with great respect by the sage of Great Cormorant Academy. Cao Xi follows her to secret realms and old sect ruins, where she simply "picks up" one treasure after another. Her mother is kept completely in the dark, since Lion Peak's cultivators are forbidden on pain of death from approaching the shop, and she believes Li Liu is a lowly maidservant to some mediocre old immortal. Li Liu happily hands over thirty taels of silver of her "allowance", saved for Li Huai's marriage, while her real wealth would astonish the sword immortals of Southern Whirl Continent.Chapter 367 (2) When news comes that Zheng Dafeng has been badly hurt, she smoothly covers for Li Er so that her mother does not realise he is going off to fight. === Mural City and Treasure Mirror Mountain === At Mural City on Skeleton Shoal, Li Liu appears alongside a young man who kneels before the murals with an ancient jade tablet, presenting the Rain Bringer Divine Maiden with a dilemma. The divine maiden goes pale on seeing her: the immortal realm in the murals was once one of Li Liu's own summer residences. When the martial artist Yang Chongxuan (in truth Yang Ningzhen of the Great Origin Empire's Lofty Cloud Palace, one of the continent's top ten young cultivators) attacks the divine maiden at Treasure Mirror Mountain, Li Liu intervenes. She claims to have personally given the Yang Clan's founding ancestor the prophecy about the mountain's treasure mirror when he was still a child in patched open-crotch trousers. In the battle that follows, she sacrifices her golden lion seal and a Dao saber but beats him decisively, takes the treasure mirror from the mountain, and hands it to him so that the Yang Clan owes her another favour.Chapter 496 (6) She then rips out an eye of the fox spirit Wei Taizhen, but changes her mind with a gentle smile when she remembers that Li Huai will soon be travelling and needs a maidservant. She replaces the eye and claims Wei Taizhen for him. She also forces Wei Taizhen's brother to choose between killing his father or dying himself, and, when he chooses to die, approves of it as "the stupidest method, but the most correct choice". Finally, she burns away the thread of love between the Rain Bringer Divine Maiden and her lover, binding the divine maiden to a sixty-year promise.Chapter 496 (7) === Return to Dragon Spring === Li Liu returns to the Yang Family Medicine Shop to meet Old Man Yang. He urges her to set aside her ancient grudge with Ruan Xiu, a conflict between water and fire from the age of the gods, saying both sides made enormous mistakes. The text reveals that if Li Liu wanted to settle that grudge, she would first need to kill Chen Ping'an, who stood in for her against Ruan Xiu and has a strong affinity with water. She refuses, because it would grieve Li Huai. She also tells Old Man Yang that her mother never needed to go north. She then visits Ruan Xiu herself with keys to old shattered realms. Ruan Xiu, who has lost her memories, asks who won their final battle, and Li Liu answers that they both lost. The two share Ruan Xiu's desserts while trading threats about eating each other one day.Chapter 530 (2) At [[Downtrodden Mountain]], she explains the workings of the newly split Lotus Root Blessed Land to [[Zhu Lian]] and recognises his Great Dao as within reach. Zhu Lian, in turn, tells her it is a shame she is not joining Downtrodden Mountain. === The Water Dragon Sect === Li Liu deliberately seeks out Chen Ping'an at the Water Dragon Sect on the Plenty River. She passes on news of Downtrodden Mountain's debts and shows him a painted scroll revealing a painful truth connected to him.Chapter 548 (2) The sect's hidden water official, Li Yuan, kowtows to her: the Dragon Palace Small World was another of her summer palaces, and the sect's founding was her doing. She arranges a private island for Chen Ping'an to cultivate on and gives him her "Three Feet Sweet Rain" jade tablet as repayment for his kindness to Li Huai, then slips away so he cannot return it. Every river, lake and sea in the world is described as her territory.Chapter 549 (3) When Chen Ping'an leaves the tablet behind anyway, she gives it to Li Yuan. She also heals the water goddess Shen Lin and promises her a future promotion, and plays Go with Spiritual Master Fire Dragon, who treats her as half friend, half enemy. === Chen Ping'an at Lion Peak === When Chen Ping'an arrives at Lion Peak, Li Liu's mother tries to match him with her daughter, and the town assumes they are lovers. Li Liu tells him calmly that she likes neither Lin Shouyi nor Dong Shuijing, and that she has never thought about marriage. While Li Er trains Chen Ping'an at the founder's cave, she brings them meals. During a walk on the mountain, Chen Ping'an makes a light joke: there could be no grass in [[Clay Vase Alley]], because the hens would eat it. Li Liu suddenly bows and thanks him for his guidance, leaving him completely puzzled. That night she asks her father what the family will do when she must one day take back her true body and her divinity outweighs her humanity. Li Er answers that they will treat her like a child who has become extraordinarily successful, still their daughter, and asks only that she always treat her mother well. She agrees.Chapter 558 (2) Before Chen Ping'an leaves, she mends his Dao robes and hides another precious jade tablet among her mother's gifts for him. === Visiting Li Huai === At their mother's request, Li Liu visits Li Huai at Mountain Cliff Academy, now that he has grown taller than her. She brings a bag of treasures disguised to look ordinary. Li Huai complains that a maidservant to an old immortal can't save anything good, urges her to reach the Abode Tier quickly, and lectures her not to keep giving gifts to her family once she marries. She smiles throughout, telling him only that he has grown up. == Abilities == * '''Memories of past lives:''' Li Liu is born with complete memories of her previous incarnations, so for her death is little more than a change of body. In one past life she was a sect leader at the peak of the Immortal Tier. She has died at the hands of a tenth-tier martial artist and has also killed tenth-tier martial artists. * '''Knowledge:''' Her understanding of blessed lands, small worlds and ancient history rivals Jiang Shangzhen's. She has managed several blessed lands before, including the now-shattered Ripple Small World and Emerald Tide Blessed Land. * '''Cultivation:''' In this life she entered the Middle Five Tiers in a single step and casually advanced to the Nascent Tier, where she stayed for a time. * '''Water dominion:''' Any body of water is effectively her territory. She can travel thousands of kilometres instantly by entering a river, heal a water goddess's shattered godly body by touch, and command ancient water officials. * '''Combat:''' She beat Yang Ningzhen, one of the continent's top ten young cultivators, with punches, kicks, immortal treasures and countless mystical abilities. She can draw a golden circle that imprisons others, and hide her aura so that it resembles another person's. == Possessions == * '''Golden lion seal''': retrieved from her old cave at Lion Peak; sacrificed in the fight at Treasure Mirror Mountain. * '''Cao Xi's short sword''': carries 300 years of nurtured sword qi. * '''Dao saber''': also sacrificed at Treasure Mirror Mountain. * '''Hornless dragon jade tablet "Three Feet Sweet Rain"''': the original on which the Water Dragon Sect's tablets are modelled; later given to Li Yuan. * '''Jade tablet "The old flood dragon quells the storm"''': given secretly to Chen Ping'an. * Several former abodes: Lion Peak, the Dragon Palace Small World, the Southern Fragrance Water Palace, and the immortal realm of Mural City. == Trivia == * 柳 (liǔ) means willow, which is why Zheng Dafeng calls her "Little Willow". * Li Huai boasts that he has a 100% win rate against her at jacks. * The town's women avoid the family shop when she is minding it, because they feel plain beside her. Chen Ping'an suggests hiring less beautiful Lion Peak maidens to shop there in clothes made from the shop's fabric. * Spiritual Master Fire Dragon names her among the young cultivators of the age whom no one will be able to stop. == References == [[Category:Female]] [[Category:Alive]] [[Category:Characters]]
