Talisman master |Current_affiliation(s)=Li Clan of Fortune Street |Continent=[[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]] |Cultivation_rank=Sixth Tier (Qi refiner) |Novel=Chapter 127 }} '''Li Xisheng''' is the eldest grandson of the Li Clan of [[Fortune Street]] and the older brother of Li Baozhen and [[Li Baoping]]. A gentle, quiet young Confucian scholar who teaches at the town's private school, he is one of the few people Chen Ping'an instantly feels close to, alongside Mr. Qi. He rose through the cultivation tiers with astonishing speed despite the restrictions of Jewel Small World, and he is talented enough that the Daoist [[Lu Chen]] personally orders his protection. Li Xisheng later reveals to [[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]] that the Great Dao fortune he enjoyed had originally belonged to Chen Ping'an, and that he himself may not truly be a Li at all. == Appearance == Li Xisheng is a young scholar in azure or green robes, usually with a gentle smile "as warm as the spring breeze". In later appearances he wears Confucian robes and carries a bamboo hiking pole, with a simple, elegant peach wood talisman made of two pieces of wood hanging at his waist. == Personality == Li Xisheng is warm, patient, humble and courteous to everyone. Compared with his charming younger brother, he seems pedantic and quiet, and the clan's servants find him less likeable. Their mother, too, is closer to Li Baozhen. He loves books, and he fills the margins of everything he reads with his own understanding in black ink and his questions in red. He has a strong sense of fairness and balance. He believes that whenever someone gains, someone else must lose, and he cannot rest until he has set right any imbalance he discovers, especially one he caused himself. He holds that pure principles are worth passing on even when they seem useless. Chen Ping'an lists him among the people who left a warm impression from the very first meeting, like Mr. Qi and Zhang Shanfeng. == Background == Li Xisheng grew up in the Li Clan manor on Fortune Street. His father, clan leader Li Hong, often reads with him, while drinking with Li Baozhen. Their grandfather, who advanced greatly once the small world's restrictions were lifted, won two protected official appointments in the Great Li Empire for the clan. Li Xisheng turned his down, while Li Baozhen accepted.Chapter 206 (3) As a boy, Li Xisheng once saw his normally kind mother turn cold at the idiom "a peach for a plum", and furious at "the peach tree withers in place of the plum tree". The memory stayed with him as a faint unease. == Plot == === The Small Town === Li Xisheng is first named in passing as a scholar in azure of the Li Clan.Chapter 127 When Chen Ping'an returns from Great Sui, Li Xisheng greets him at the manor gate as Li Baoping's brother. He takes in the mountain crossing carp Chen Ping'an has brought for her, gives him several annotated books, and invites him to visit freely.Chapter 181 When the swordsman Cao Jun, a descendant of the sword immortal Cao Xi, confronts Chen Ping'an and the two children in [[Clay Vase Alley]], Li Xisheng steps in front of them, declaring that reasonable discussion should come before drawn swords.Chapter 182 Although he is only a sixth-tier Qi refiner facing a ninth-tier swordsman, he defends himself with a host of spring leaves, summer thunder, autumn wind and winter snow trinkets, and Cao Jun cannot break through. Li Xisheng calls it his first fight and admits he was flustered.Chapter 184 Visiting Downtrodden Mountain, Li Xisheng answers Chen Ping'an's questions about the Bai Ze Suppressing Pagoda. Speaking the name "Bai Ze" aloud draws the attention of Master Bai himself from the far side of the continent, and Li Xisheng apologises in his direction.Chapter 189 (2) He later climbs the mountain with his young scholarly attendant, Cui Ci. He tells Chen Ping'an that he will soon leave the small town, and offers his peach wood talisman as an apology for his brother Li Baozhen's role in [[Zhu Lu]]'s assassination attempt. Chen Ping'an refuses it.Chapter 191 (1) He explains that Fortune Street (福禄) is a homonym of "talisman" and that [[Fortune Street|Peach Leaf Alley]] refers to peach wood talismans. He describes a strange dream in which he played Go with someone and learned the secrets of the peach wood talisman. Since Chen Ping'an still refuses the talisman, Li Xisheng spends the night inscribing talismans and poetic phrases on the walls of the bamboo building with his brush. His characters are so powerful that the whole mountain slowly sinks.Chapter 192 These inscriptions later help keep Cui Cheng lucid, and greatly strengthen the building. He also gives Chen Ping'an the brush itself, the Wind and Snow Awl, engraved "Writing as if Assisted by the Gods", along with gold and yellow talisman paper and the ''Authentic Death-Avoiding Book''. Rather than teaching specific talismans, he teaches Chen Ping'an the principles of drawing them, saying it is better to teach a man to fish.Chapter 216 Meanwhile, the Daoist envoy Xie Shi demands three people from the Great Li Empire: He Xiaoliang, Ma Kuxuan and Li Xisheng.Chapter 199 Lu Chen later orders Xie Shi to protect Li Xisheng, swearing to return from the White Jade Capital and break the rules of both worlds if anything happens to him.Chapter 235 (1) Cui Dongshan later speculates that Lu Chen may have shaved a layer off the river of time in Jewel Small World for the sake of Li Xisheng, whom he calls one of Lu Chen's "so-called senior brothers".Chapter 385 (2) === Promise Concerning Li Baozhen === Chen Ping'an promises Li Xisheng that he will spare Li Baozhen once. Li Xisheng gives Li Baozhen a farewell gift, the Day and Night Wandering Deity True Body Talisman. When Li Baozhen later confronts Chen Ping'an, Chen Ping'an keeps his word by sparing him, and confiscates the talisman. From then on he regards Li Baozhen as separate from the Li Clan of Li Baoping and Li Xisheng.Chapter 408 He hopes to ask Li Xisheng to repair the damaged talisman. === Northern Complete Reed Continent === Li Xisheng travels north to [[Northern Complete Reed Continent]] with Cui Ci. He buys a small house on Cave Immortal Street in a provincial city of the remote Sweet Wormwood Nation. He briefly secures a post in the provincial education office by quietly leaving behind some "knowledge" for the commissioner, then loses it without concern. He plans to stay there for thirty to forty years, and spends his time listening, through an enchanted picture scroll, to the lectures of an obscure old virtuous scholar, to whom he pays a grain rain coin in thanks.Chapter 559 (2) Through Li Er of Lion Peak, he sends Chen Ping'an a message: the peach wood talisman had been meant to settle a great karmic debt between them, so Chen Ping'an should not come to him out of gratitude. === The Truth === When Chen Ping'an visits, Li Xisheng explains everything. Qi refiners struggled to cultivate in Jewel Small World, yet he had progressed faster than even Ma Kuxuan. Over time he traced the reason: the Great Dao fortune that should have belonged to Chen Ping'an had fallen upon him instead. The peach wood talisman was the foundation of his own Great Dao, which is why he tried to give it to Chen Ping'an in return. The talisman papers and the ''Authentic Death-Avoiding Book'', he adds, were simply thanks for escorting Li Baoping to Great Sui. He then reveals a deeper secret. Across the street from him lives a Confucian scholar named Chen Baozhou, a few years older than Li Baozhen. Chen Ping'an understands at once: Li Xisheng should have been Chen Xisheng of Cave Immortal Street, and Chen Baozhou should have been Li Baozhou of Jewel Small World. This also explains why a model tree, a symbol of wisdom and virtue, had grown from the Chen Clan's ancestral grave in the mountains. Chen Ping'an tells him that his sorrow is understandable but should not run so deep, and Li Xisheng says he feels truly consoled. The two then play Go.Chapter 563 (1) == Abilities == * '''Qi refiner:''' reached at remarkable speed inside Jewel Small World. * '''Talismans:''' an advanced talismanic master whose inscriptions could sink a mountain. * '''Defence:''' able to control a large number of objects at once, enough to hold off a ninth-tier swordsman. Cao Jun notes that this should be impossible for someone of his tier. * '''Scholarship:''' Zheng Dafeng counts him among the three most learned people in Jewel Small World, alongside Mr. Qi and Old Man Yang. == Trivia == * Unlike his siblings Li Baozhen and Li Baoping, his name does not contain the character "bao" (宝), a detail that weighs on him. * Kiln Supervision Official Cao would change out of his official robes to sit in on Li Xisheng's lessons. * The peach wood talisman is the foundation of his Great Dao, refused by Chen Ping'an. * He gave his Wind and Snow Awl (a calligraphy brush that forms ink from breath), Authentic Death-Avoiding Book, and talisman paper to Chen Ping'an. * '''Day and Night Wandering Deity True Body Talisman''' (given away): given to Li Baozhen, later held by Chen Ping'an. == References == [[Category:Characters]] [[Category:Male]] [[Category:Alive]] [[Category:Human]]

'''The Swords (剑来 Unsheathed)''' is a novel written by '''Feng Huo Xi Zhu Hou (烽火戏诸侯)'''. The main protagonist is [[Chen Ping An|'''Chen Ping An''']]. It has been mistranslated as "Sword of Coming" on many sites.

==Biography ==
'''The Swords''' is an online fantasy novel by [[Light Novel/Author|Fenghuo Xi Zhuhou]], serialized on the '''Zongheng Chinese website'''. The story features the protagonist, [[Chen Ping An|Chen Pingan]], who wields a sword with immense power. The novel has been highly recognized, winning top awards, including the 4th Chenggua Online Literature Award and the 2nd Pan-Chinese Online Literature "Golden Keyboard" Award for Best Story Creativity in 2020. It was also recognized as one of the top ten animation IPs with great potential.
==Creative background==
When Fenghuo Opera Princes was making an outline for "The Swords", he put forward two requirements for the book: The first is his self-requirement, which is to build a complete and logical world of fairy tales, which is obviously a It is a fictional world, but all the joys and sorrows in this work must be connected with reality. It should allow readers to have a series of resonances and a sense of empathy that is not inferior to that of a book with realistic themes. The second point is "different". The princes of Fenghuo Opera specially emphasized these three words.

==Synopsis==
The boundless universe was filled with all sorts of wonders.

I, Chen *Ping’an, only have one sword, to move mountains, turn the seas upside down, suppress demons, deal with gods, pluck stars, break rivers, destroy cities, and open the heavenly abode!

My name is Chen Ping’an, Ping’an* of Peace, and I am a swordsman.

The Midland world was full of wonders.

In the center of the world, there was a scholar who had once used a sword to slash out a waterfall of the Milky Way. This was the person he was the most proud of.

At the edge of the East Sea’s cliffs, there was a nameless Daoist who was unwilling to ascend to the peak of a mountain. He only wished for a cool breeze to brush against his face.

In the Western Pure Land, there was an old monk who liked to treat people to chicken soup and tell stories.

In the southern border of the Wilderness, there was a blind painter who controlled golden-armored puppets that were as tall as mountains to move the hundred thousand mountains, creating an embroidered picture.

An impoverished youth who grew up in the north. One day, he saw tens of thousands of Sword Kinesis Immortals above him, like a swarm of locusts crossing the border.

He wanted to see for himself the scholar that the storyteller had mentioned, the surging tides of the East Sea, the vast swamps of sand in the west, and the majestic mountains of the Southern Wasteland.

Thus, one day, the youth picked up the wooden sword and began to descend south.[https://www.novelupdates.com/series/unsheathed/ Novel Updates]

==Wuxiaworld==
Chen Ping’an had grown up his entire life in a mundane little town, leading an impoverished yet peaceful existence. However, the arrival of a group of outsiders quickly turned his mundane life on its head. Before long, all types of strange occurrences were taking place in the town, and Chen Ping’an was made to realize that things are not what they seem. As it turned out, the stories of immortal cultivators, mighty dragons, and unfathomably powerful beings that had always been told in the town as folklore were all true, and Chen Ping’an was inadvertently swept up into this world that he had no business being a part of. Having been forced onto a path that Chen Ping’an had never thought he would walk, he commences his journey to the top…[https://www.wuxiaworld.com/novel/unsheathed Wuxiaworld]

==Biography==
Fenghuo Opera Princes , whose real name is Chen Zhenghua. Born on November 8, 1985 in Chun'an County, Hangzhou City, Zhejiang Province. A popular writer on the rich list of Chinese Internet writers, a columnist on Zongheng Chinese website , and a new generation of popular writers of online novels. His representative works are "The Best Young Master", " Chen Ergou's Evil Life ", " God Descends to Earth ", " The Fighting Sword in the Snow ", and " I'm a Toad ".  His contributions to internet literature have earned him several awards, including the Golden Keyboard Award in 2018.

''Sword Comes'' (剑来) is one of Fenghuo Xi Zhuhou's well-known works, set in a world of martial arts and fantasy. The story follows the protagonist, Chen Ping An, as he navigates a journey filled with swordsmanship, adventure, and self-discovery. It explores themes of fate, cultivation, and the pursuit of power. ''Sword Comes'' was recognized for its deep character development and intricate world-building, earning it a place in the 2017 ''China Online Novel Ranking'' and adaptations into other media.
==Writing Style==
Fenghuo Xi Zhuhou's writing is characterized by intricate world-building, complex character development, and a deep exploration of martial arts philosophy. His narratives often blend elements of traditional Chinese culture with imaginative fantasy, creating immersive and engaging stories.

pages.content:
{{Character |header1 = Lin Shouyi |image1 = LinShouyi.png |Vital_status = Alive |Gender = Male |Species = Human |Age = 12 (Chapter 134) |Master(s) = [[Qi Jingchun]] (teacher)

[[Li Huai]]
[[Li Baoping]]
[[A'Liang]] |Allies = [[Xie Xie]]

Student |Current_affiliation(s) = [[Mountain Cliff Academy]] |Former_affiliation(s) = Qi Jingchun's private school
Lin Clan |Continent = [[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]] |Cultivation_rank = Qi refiner (Lower Five Tiers) |Novel = Chapter 72 }} {{Spoilers}} '''Lin Shouyi''' is one of the last five students of [[Qi Jingchun]]'s private school in the small town, and the eldest of the three children whom [[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]] escorts to [[Mountain Cliff Academy]] in [[Great Sui Nation]], alongside [[Li Baoping]] and [[Li Huai]]. An illegitimate son of the Lin Clan, he is cold, proud and reserved, but sharp-minded and deeply loyal to those who earn his respect. He becomes a Qi refiner on the journey thanks to [[A'Liang]]'s wine and a Daoist lightning scripture, and later grows into one of the most celebrated young cultivation prodigies in Great Sui's capital. He has been in love with [[Li Liu]], Li Huai's older sister, since childhood. == Appearance == As a child, Lin Shouyi is fair-skinned from his privileged upbringing and first appears wearing a black fox fur coat with a cold, aloof expression. He grows into a handsome, elegant young man who dresses plainly, wearing the jade hairpin Chen Ping'an carved for him. By his later years at the academy, he is described as a refined young master with an ethereal air, and young women from the capital's leading clans come to the academy just to catch a glimpse of him. == Personality == Lin Shouyi is cold, taciturn and proud, and he struggles to open up to people. He dislikes being in anyone's debt, especially to people he distrusts. He prefers owing favours to good people, whom he can repay on his own terms, rather than to schemers like Cui Dongshan. He is calm in danger, quick to see through people, and comfortable viewing the world in the most negative light possible. His sense of self is shaped by his background. As an illegitimate child despised by his own family, he once said he didn't care if he died. He is sensitive about money and status, and was the "biggest misfit" in the travelling group, quietly feeling left out while appearing indifferent. Yet he has a strong sense of right and wrong, is kind-hearted beneath his aloofness, and, in his own words, never resents someone for treating others better than him as long as they treat him kindly. His name, 守一, means "remaining loyal to one thing", which fits his single-minded devotion to cultivation and to Li Liu.Chapter 119 (1) == Background == Lin Shouyi is from the Lin Clan, a large but low-profile clan of the small town that is not among the Four Families and Ten Clans. His father was a low-ranking official in the kiln supervision office who quietly held more power than he showed, and served three successive kiln supervision officials. Lin Shouyi is his illegitimate son, the child of a maidservant according to [[Zhu Lu]], and both his father and his mother treat him coldly. At school, he had beautiful handwriting that Mr. Qi praised, did not get along well with the other children, and was openly scornful of rich children from [[Fortune Street]] like Li Baoping. When Mr. Qi gave his last students each a sheet with the character "Qi" as homework, Lin Shouyi kept his safely at home. == Plot == === Leaving the Small Town === On the excursion with [[Ma Zhan]], Lin Shouyi is the only child who distrusts [[Cui Minghuang]] from the start. After Ma Zhan's murder, he suspects the coach driver was involved, and it is his idea, refined into a plan by Li Baoping, to trick the driver. When the five children swear a pact before carrying it out, he declares that as a despised illegitimate child, he doesn't care if he dies.Chapter 84 (1) Afterwards, he and Li Huai catch up with Chen Ping'an's group and insist on going to the academy, admitting frankly that they would never make it there alone. === Journey to Great Sui === Lin Shouyi is the first of the group to sense that A'Liang is far more than he appears. After his first sip from A'Liang's wine gourd following a sighting of demons, he grows close to A'Liang, drinking a little every day and discussing everything from swordsmanship to Chen Ping'an's hidden injuries. A'Liang tells him he is the first person to realise there are benefits to befriending him, and that he has good intuition on the path of cultivation.Chapter 100 (2) When Chen Ping'an offers to make Li Huai a bamboo bookcase after his tantrum on Go Table Mountain, he turns and offers to make one for Lin Shouyi too. This small gesture means far more to Lin Shouyi than anyone realises at the time. When the Go Table Mountain treasures are shared out, Lin Shouyi tears his eyes away from a beautiful saber and chooses an ancient Daoist book, the ''Recite Atop Clouds Scripture'', saying he is not suited to martial arts.Chapter 104 The scripture turns out to be a secret manual of the Five Lightning Righteous Technique. In [[Red Candle Town]], he receives a curt letter from his father containing a 300-tael banknote, telling him to wait to be collected and adding that his corpse would not be worth the transport fee. That night, a woman on a pleasure boat singles him out. She is the grand elder of the Palace of Eternal Spring, a major immortal sect of the Great Li Empire, and later offers to take him as a disciple. Lin Shouyi politely refuses, saying that while he cannot choose his clan or surname, he can choose his own path.Chapter 110 Before leaving, A'Liang gives him a stack of yellow paper talismans and assigns a [[Yin god]] to escort the group, and Lin Shouyi becomes the one who communicates with the Yin god. On the ship along the Embroidered Flower River, Lin Shouyi reveals that A'Liang's wine is what made him a Qi refiner, and is quietly hurt that Chen Ping'an clearly favours Li Baoping and Li Huai. He watches nervously as Chen Ping'an hacks quickly at precious bamboo for his bookcase, pleading with him to add curves and take care. Chen Ping'an teases him by threatening to make his last, and in the end it is the best of the three. During the encounter with the ghost [[Lady Chu]], the Yin god tells Lin Shouyi to use a Barrier Shattering Talisman, which leads the group out of the "path to the underworld" on the mountain road.Chapter 124 Afterwards, Chen Ping'an gives him the ''Mountain Scouring Album'' that a blind old Daoist priest gave in exchange for a snake gall pebble. Lin Shouyi buys a Go set and teaches Chen Ping'an to play, and later plays against [[Xie Xie]], [[Yu Lu]], and the spirit of the Azure Maiden Temple, who gives him a precious Go manual. He is furious when he learns that drunken scholars had defiled her temple, and salutes her statue before leaving. At the Autumn Reed Inn, Lin Shouyi angrily accuses Chen Ping'an of being insane for spending 2,000 taels of silver on one night's lodging, not realising it was for the sake of his own cultivation.Chapter 138 Cultivating greedily in the inn's rich spiritual energy, he nearly overloads himself until [[Cui Chan]] stops him. By then he has reached the peak of the third tier within a few months, thanks to his aptitude and A'Liang's wine.Chapter 140 (2) He later apologises to Chen Ping'an, having expected a beating that never came. On the final stretch, he drives off bandits with his lightning technique and fights a horde of ghosts in a burial ground, looking like a divine lightning general wreathed in purple qi. === Mountain Cliff Academy === At the academy, Lin Shouyi skips lessons to read in the scripture library, where he is drawn to everything except the Confucian classics. His plain dress and cold manner make him wildly popular with female students. The Confucian scholar Dong Jing, a renowned expert in both Confucianism and Daoism, takes him under his wing, taking him to Iron Tree Mountain during thunderstorms. Dong Jing believes Lin Shouyi has a realistic chance of reaching the tenth tier. When Li Huai's belongings are stolen, Lin Shouyi gives him money from his father's banknote to offer as a reward.Chapter 162 (2) He then steps in when Li Baoping is insulted. After beating two local students, he fights the eldest grandson of the Chu Clan, who wields an heirloom Cloud Lightning Zither, and holds his own before losing. Soon afterwards, the son of the late general Pan Maozhen takes a lightning strike head-on and beats Lin Shouyi badly, spitting on him as he leaves.Chapter 165 (1) Lying injured, Lin Shouyi finally understands how heavy a burden Chen Ping'an carried in making every decision on their journey. He later reveals he knowingly risked his entire cultivation future by helping Li Huai. During Li Huai's family visit, he can hardly bring himself to look at Li Liu, drinks with Li Er, and is left holding an undelivered letter as she leaves, murmuring "next time". === Rising Prodigy === Over the following years, Lin Shouyi becomes the academy's most celebrated prodigy, balancing study and cultivation and attracting the attention of officials across Great Sui's capital. A respected teacher secures a private courtyard for him and teaches him lightning techniques. On a three-month trip to Great Sui's Northern Mountain, the teacher catches lightning by hand and gives Lin Shouyi a Thunder Belly Bottle full of it.Chapter 400 (2) Still, he often thinks of Li Liu and of the long-gone days on the road, sensing that the group has drifted apart since Chen Ping'an left. When Chen Ping'an returns to the academy, he gives Lin Shouyi a rare, incomplete lightning scripture. Lin Shouyi accepts it, explaining that he knows he will one day repay it with something more valuable.Chapter 403 (2) He agrees to cultivate each morning in Cui Dongshan's courtyard, insisting that the invitation come from Chen Ping'an so that he owes the favour to him rather than to Cui Dongshan. During an assassination attempt on the academy, Lin Shouyi can do little as a sword cultivator attacks, and nearly loses consciousness from being dragged in and out of the river of time. Chen Ping'an deliberately sits beside him afterwards so that he won't feel useless. Cui Dongshan notes that Lin Shouyi's cultivation is deliberately being held back by Dong Jing, and that he will eventually overtake Xie Xie if she doesn't work hard. Finally, Lin Shouyi reveals why he is so grateful to Chen Ping'an. It was the offhand offer of a bookcase in the mud on Go Table Mountain, which made him feel included when he was the group's misfit. He adds that he doesn't resent Chen Ping'an for loving the others more. Chen Ping'an, in turn, tells him what he is most grateful for: Lin Shouyi once told him that not all parents are good parents, which made Chen Ping'an realise how rich he was in the love of his own parents.Chapter 417 (1) === Later Years === On an academy excursion to Dragon Spring Prefecture, Lin Shouyi visits the kiln supervision office where his father worked. His clan has moved to the Great Li capital, and he and his family remain mutually estranged. They show no interest in his growing fame.Chapter 471 (2) Meanwhile, [[Dong Shuijing]], his rival for Li Liu, admits he could never match him academically, but claims he would take it better if Li Liu chose someone else. Officials of the Great Li Empire responsible for recruiting talent have contacted his father about him, only for his father to deny having such a son. Mao Xiaodong judges him the most well-rounded of the five students, but worries his cultivation is going so smoothly that he may abandon his studies.Chapter 570 (1) When Chen Ping'an announces Downtrodden Mountain's new ancestral hall, Lin Shouyi offers his congratulations and is invited to cultivate on its mountains. He narrowly misses Li Liu's visit to her brother, to his great disappointment. Li Huai, now his good friend, can't understand what he sees in her. == Abilities == * '''Qi refining:''' Lin Shouyi became a Qi refiner through A'Liang's wine and reached the peak of the third tier within months. As of the assassination attempt (ch. 410), he had not yet reached the Middle Five Tiers, partly because Dong Jing deliberately restrains his progress. * '''Five Lightning Righteous Technique:''' He learned it from the ''Recite Atop Clouds Scripture'', guided by Dong Jing and another academy teacher. He is especially gifted at the calculation and deduction needed to use the scripture's sparse instructions. * '''Talismans:''' A'Liang's stack of yellow paper talismans, including the Barrier Shattering, Pearl Within a Plate, Fiery Rain and gold dust talismans. * '''Intellect:''' He is a skilled strategist and a strong Go player, though Xie Xie, Yu Lu and Cui Chan all outclass him. == Possessions == * '''''Recite Atop Clouds Scripture''''': a Daoist manual of the Five Lightning Righteous Technique. * '''A'Liang's yellow paper talismans.''' * '''''Mountain Scouring Album''''': an illustrated bestiary of mountain spirits, given by Chen Ping'an. * '''Azure Maiden's Go manual.''' * '''Incomplete lightning scripture''': a solitary copy from Stalactite Mountain's Ganoderma Inn, given by Chen Ping'an. * '''Thunder Belly Bottle''': filled with lightning by his academy teacher. * '''Bamboo bookcase''': made by Chen Ping'an from Go Table Mountain courage bamboo, the best of the three. * '''Jade hairpin''': engraved "Shouyi" by Chen Ping'an. * '''Mr. Qi's "Qi" character''': kept at home. == Trivia == * 守一 (shǒu yī) means "remaining loyal to one thing". When Chen Ping'an threatens to make his bookcase last, Lin Shouyi protests that someone named Shouyi can't go back on his word. * Li Huai gives conflicting reports on his family's preferences: he once says his mother prefers Dong Shuijing and his sister probably prefers Lin Shouyi, and later says his mother prefers Lin Shouyi and his father prefers Dong Shuijing. * Before Chen Ping'an left Great Sui, he asked Li Baoping in his farewell letter to keep in touch with the aloof Lin Shouyi so their bond would not weaken. == References == [[Category:Male]] [[Category:Characters]] [[Category:Alive]]

'''Liu Xianyang''' is [[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]]'s oldest and closest friend from the [[Small Town]]. He was once [[Old Yao|Old Man Yao]]'s most gifted kiln apprentice and later studies with the Pure Confucian Chen Clan on the Southern Whirl Continent.

==Appearance==
Liu Xianyang is tall and broad, about half a head taller than Chen Ping'an in their youth. He is strong enough to snap a plank bed simply by sitting on it the wrong way. Years later, Chen Ping'an still describes him as a sturdy young man, though he carries himself in a more mature and reserved way than he did in the small town.Chapter 536 (2) 

==Personality==
Liu Xianyang is bold, talkative and almost impossible to rattle. As a boy he never seemed bothered by living alone or by anyone's opinion of him, and Chen Ping'an envied this fearlessness more than his talent or strength.Chapter 4 He makes friends easily, fits into new places without trouble, and likes to brag and show off, especially when a girl is watching. He was openly infatuated with [[Zhi Gui]] for years, though she never returned his feelings.

He can be careless and thoughtless. He took three of four buns for himself and left Chen Ping'an one, and he often joked about [[Gu Can]]'s mother until Gu Can chased him in tears. These fights usually ended with Liu Xianyang apologising with a grin.Chapter 534 (3) He rarely holds a grudge, does not bully people with his strength, and does not care much about winning an argument.

Under the jokes he is loyal and stubborn about things that matter. He refused to give up his family's sword scripture even when it nearly cost him his life. As an adult he is relaxed about right and wrong in a way Chen Ping'an is not, and he openly tells his friend to worry less and enjoy life more. He dislikes wine and prefers a plain bowl of noodles.

==Background==

=== Early life ===
Liu Xianyang was raised by his grandfather. After the old man died he ran wild and became the leader of the children around Apricot Blossom Alley. He left the private school and turned down the teacher's offer of free lessons, saying he only wanted to earn money. Townspeople claimed his ancestor had been a deserter who married into a local family. Liu Xianyang insisted the ancestor was a general, and he treasured an ugly, warty suit of scaled armour along with a sword scripture handed down in his family.

As a boy he was trapped in an alley by Lu Zhengchun and his friends and beaten almost to death. A small orphan's cries for help saved him. That child was Chen Ping'an. Liu Xianyang repaid him badly at first and bullied him. Then one winter he saw the orphan would not survive, felt guilty, and got him work at the dragon kilns. From then on he looked out for Chen Ping'an and taught him to fish, set traps and make bows.

He was Old Man Yao's favourite apprentice and learned in half a year what took Chen Ping'an three years.Chapter 1 After the kilns closed he went to work for [[Ruan Qiong]] at his blacksmith shop. Ruan Qiong's remark that he had come only to forge swords won Liu Xianyang's complete admiration.Chapter 7

=== The armour and the sword scripture ===
Outsiders soon came after his heirlooms. Lu Zhengchun, now working for the Xu Clan of Light Breeze City, begged him to sell the armour and ended up kneeling and kowtowing in Clay Vase Alley.Chapter 34 Liu Xianyang agreed to sell the armour but would not part with the sword scripture.Chapter 42 Soon after, he was struck down at the covered bridge by the [[Mountain-Moving Ape]] of Sun Scorch Mountain and left close to death.Chapter 43 Chen Ping'an used his locust leaf to keep him alive, and [[Qi Jingchun]] later confirmed that someone had stepped in to save him.Chapter 58

His rescuer was Chen Dui of the Chen Clan, which Liu Xianyang's ancestors had once served as graveyard attendants. While he recovered, he told Chen Ping'an he would leave town with her.Chapter 64 The Pure Confucian Chen Clan agreed to take him to the Southern Whirl Continent on the condition that he return to Ruan Qiong after twenty years.Chapter 571 (2) The armour he sold later helped the head of the Xu Clan become a Nascent Tier cultivator.

=== Southern Whirl Continent ===
At the Chen Clan he was given a folding fan of divine cloud bamboo, and he often spent evenings on a cliff above the river talking with an old scholar who called himself a teacher.Chapter 206 (6) He lived frugally, made friends among the clan and the academy's scholars, and became a proper student. He also kept training in secret. In his dreams he faced a swordsman whose strikes jolted him awake. This practice with the sword in his sleep made him an expert in swords. When [[Zhang Shanfeng]] brought him an old sword from Chen Ping'an, he could read its secrets just by watching its blade. He sent gifts to [[Downtrodden Mountain]], and he scolded Chen Ping'an by letter for breaking a promise to give him Golden Sweet Wine.

=== Sword Qi Great Wall ===
Liu Xianyang later came to the [[Sword Qi Great Wall]] and turned up unannounced at Chen Ping'an's table, where they drank and argued as they had at home. He told his friend bluntly to stop carrying so much guilt over Gu Can and won [[Ning Yao]]'s approval in the process.Chapter 619 When Chen Ping'an asked about his cultivation, he refused to answer and teased that the truth would make him cry.Chapter 620 (1)

On the city wall he showed he was a sword cultivator. His swords were never seen, yet demons kept dying along his stretch of the wall. While fighting, he taught Chen Ping'an his family's sword scripture in full.Chapter 622 Even his friend Chen Shi had not known he could use a sword. Before returning to help defend the Southern Whirl Continent, he said he meant to challenge Sun Scorch Mountain, and he brushed off Chen Ping'an's warning to wait for him.Chapter 632 Chen Ping'an gave him a seal inscribed "From Great Sword Immortal Chen Ping'an, to Brother Liu Xianyang," which amused him on the voyage home.

==Trivia==

* He once tried to leap across the creek after hearing a story from his grandfather. He fell in, and the much smaller Chen Ping'an jumped farther than he did.
* He was a better diver than Chen Ping'an and once brought up a huge snake gall pebble just to show off.
* He scoffed at the name "Zhi Gui" and insisted that her real name was Wang Zhu.
* After Old Man Yao overheard him calling himself a prodigy, the old man gave him a rare beating, and Liu Xianyang never used the word again.
* As children, he, Chen Ping'an and Gu Can wrote their names at the very top of a wall in a small temple. Liu Xianyang stole the ladder, and his name was written the largest.
* [[Song Jixin]] considered asking [[Fu Nanhua]] to kill him before choosing a different target.
* Ruan Qiong later admitted that Liu Xianyang was the one he had most wanted as a disciple.
* Gu Can never thought of him as a friend. To Gu Can, Liu Xianyang was only ever Chen Ping'an's friend.

pages.title: Liu Zhimao
pages.content:
{{Character |header1=Liu Zhimao |image1=Liu Zhimao.png |Chinese=刘志茂 |Pinyin=Liú Zhìmào |Titles=River Severing True Lord
Island Master of Cyan Gorge Island
Ruler of the cultivation world of Bamboo Scroll Lake (former) |Aliases=The storyteller |Vital_status=Alive |Gender=Male |Species=Human |Disciple(s)=[[Gu Can]] (final disciple)
Tian Hujun (most senior disciple) |Subordinates=Zhang Ye |Allies=[[Chen Ping An]] (temporary)
Tan Yuanyi |Enemie(s)=[[Liu Laocheng]]
Zhou Fenglu |Occupation=Vagrant cultivator
Guest elder of the True Realm Sect |Current_affiliation(s)=Cyan Gorge Island
True Realm Sect |Continent=[[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]] |Region=[[Bamboo Scroll Lake]] |Cultivation_rank=Unpolished Jade Tier (Upper Five Tiers) |Novel=Chapter 7 (as the storyteller) |Donghua=Episode 1 }} '''Liu Zhimao''', known as the '''River Severing True Lord''', is a vagrant cultivator and the master of Cyan Gorge Island in Bamboo Scroll Lake. He first turns up in [[Jewel Small World]] disguised as a storyteller, takes [[Gu Can]] as his final disciple, and quietly works against [[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]]. Years later, with Gu Can and his flood dragon beside him, he rises to rule Bamboo Scroll Lake, loses everything to Liu Laocheng, and climbs back to become one of the few vagrant cultivators of the Upper Five Tiers on [[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]]. == Appearance == Liu Zhimao is an old man with a beard. In the small town he poses as a wandering storyteller carrying a plain white bowl that can pour out more water than a whole vat can hold. == Personality == Most people in Bamboo Scroll Lake see Liu Zhimao as a quiet man who always wears a smile. Those close to him know a crueler side, and the late master of Heavenly Governess Island summed him up as "a phony of a True Lord, a smiling Buddha with a blade of slaughter concealed up his sleeve".Chapter 438 (1) He is patient, calculating and quick to bow to anyone stronger, and he despises the "official immortals" of established sects. He calls vagrant cultivators like himself wild dogs who have to scrap for every meal. He is also hard to rattle. Locked in a water dungeon with his acupoints sealed, he laughed at his jailer and lectured him on how much tougher a vagrant cultivator's mind is than an official immortal's.Chapter 456 (4) == Background == Liu Zhimao practices a heretical cultivation technique, and his title of True Lord was never granted by any empire. He started out as a mere Sea Observation Tier vagrant cultivator, and over a century of fighting and dealing he built Cyan Gorge Island into a real power, though his reputation stayed poor and his friendships shallow.Chapter 206 (5) His oldest follower, Zhang Ye, was with him from the days when the two of them were young and their first island was sunk to the bottom of the lake. == Plot == === Jewel Small World === Disguised as a storyteller, Liu Zhimao found that Gu Can had received a locust leaf with ancestral blessings and that the boy's aptitude was too heavy for his secret technique to lift, so he decided to take him as a disciple. When [[Cai Jinjian]] of Dawn Cloud Mountain came for Gu Can, he pulled rank by naming her sect master and sent her away. He then had Gu Can's mother tell him everything about Chen Ping'an, and from it he worked out that the boy's father had not died in an accident.Chapter 17 To secure Gu Can and the catfish, he meddled three times on Clay Vase Alley at the cost of several decades of cultivation. He made Cai Jinjian step in the dog dung, delayed Chen Ping'an's warning by a split second so she would take it as spite, and planted a false sense of enlightenment in her.Chapter 18 [[Qi Jingchun]] later told Chen Ping'an that the storyteller was Liu Zhimao and that he was the real cause of the trouble with Cai Jinjian.Chapter 23 When a divination backfired and made him spit blood, Qi Jingchun caught him in a Halted Realm. Liu Zhimao, though a Daoist of an unorthodox school, bowed as deeply as he could in the Confucian manner, begged for mercy and left town at once with Gu Can and his mother.Chapter 24 That brief divination of the town's formation cost him several decades of his lifespan. '''Contains Spoilers''' === Master of Cyan Gorge Island === Back at Bamboo Scroll Lake, one of his guest elders wanted Gu Can's mother as a mistress, and Liu Zhimao neither agreed nor refused. When Gu Can let his flood dragon eat the senior brother who had lured him away, Liu Zhimao's face darkened, then he laughed and patted the boy on the head. He did nothing even after his first disciple was killed, killed every assassin who came for Gu Can, and then led Gu Can and the dragon to wipe out the sect that had sent them.Chapter 304 (2) At a banquet he declared that only Gu Can could inherit his true teachings and become the next island master.Chapter 429 (1) With the flood dragon now at the Nascent Tier, Cyan Gorge Island cut off the lineages of its eleven subsidiary islands and swept across the lake, and Liu Zhimao was hailed as the ruler of its cultivation world. Observers noted that he himself was stuck at the Nascent Tier and owed much of his rise to Gu Can and the dragon.Chapter 435 (1) === Chen Ping'an at Bamboo Scroll Lake === When Chen Ping'an arrived, he sent Liu Zhimao a jade tablet to hold until he left. Liu Zhimao first took it for a fake, but once he confirmed it was real, he was badly shaken.Chapter 431 (1) He ordered Tian Hujun to keep the island's cultivators in line during Chen Ping'an's stay, the first time she had ever seen him show restraint. In private, Chen Ping'an accused him of confusing Cai Jinjian with a secret technique and of planting the words "seek death with resolve" in Chen Ping'an's own heart, so that he would go after Cai Jinjian and Fu Nanhua and die. Liu Zhimao also let Chen Ping'an hear, through his bowl of water, a conversation he had with Gu Can's mother, and privately regretted not taking her by force when she first arrived. After Liu Laocheng beat Gu Can and the flood dragon nearly to death, Liu Zhimao's hold on the lake began to slip. He drank with Chen Ping'an several times, and offered to repay him handsomely if he could obtain a Peace and Safety Tablet for him.Chapter 442 (3) Chen Ping'an made him lift the secret restrictions he had placed on Gu Can's mother, and the two became uneasy allies alongside Tan Yuanyi, a spy of the Great Li Empire. In two separate deals, Liu Zhimao gave Chen Ping'an a walnut bracelet and a high-grade secret technique. === Imprisonment === Liu Laocheng then attacked Cyan Gorge Island. After Liu Zhimao lost the fight and tried to flee, a group of hidden cultivators trapped him with a formation of immortal treasures, and he was dragged off to the water dungeon under Palace Willow Island. Zhang Ye slipped away to tell Chen Ping'an.Chapter 452 (1) Someone even used Liu Zhimao's own flying sword to send Chen Ping'an a warning. Zhou Fenglu of the Jade Tablet Sect came to his cell three times to press him into service. Liu Zhimao told him that serving the Great Li Empire would make him a free-roaming dog, which beat being caged, and laughed in his face. Then Jiang Shangzhen arrived with Liu Laocheng and offered him a place as a guest elder of the Jade Tablet Sect. He accepted, joined the sect's new lower sect, the True Realm Sect, and in time regained Cyan Gorge Island. === Upper Five Tiers === Before going into seclusion, Liu Zhimao visited Gu Can. He told him he had asked Jiang Shangzhen to give Cyan Gorge Island and White Fish Island to Gu Can if he broke through, handed him the River Severing Sutra, his most prized possession for centuries, and drank with him through the night. He told Gu Can that a man must seek joy while he is still young.Chapter 534 (2) He then broke through to the Unpolished Jade Tier, becoming the second vagrant cultivator of the Upper Five Tiers on the continent after Liu Laocheng.Chapter 559 (4) Downtrodden Mountain pointedly sent no congratulations. Later he rebuilt his residence on Cyan Gorge Island and admitted to Li Fuqu over tea that even Liu Laocheng was afraid, and that the Great Li Empire could make use of all of them. == Abilities == * '''Cultivation:''' Unpolished Jade Tier of the Upper Five Tiers, previously a Nascent Tier cultivator a step away from breaking through. * '''Heretical techniques:''' He practices the heretical method recorded in the ''River Severing Sutra''. * '''Divination and mind techniques:''' He reads fate from the lines of his palm, confuses people's minds and can plant thoughts in a person's heart. * '''Water bowl:''' His white bowl holds far more water than it should, and he uses its surface to replay what was said elsewhere. == Trivia == * The early translated chapters call Bamboo Scroll Lake "Lake Shujian". * He longed to reach heights where he could drag the third-generation disciples of the Buddha, the Dao Ancestor and the Confucian Hierarch into a realm of his own. * He recognized Chen Ping'an's wine gourd as a premium Sword Nurturing Gourd and confirmed it to Tian Hujun in secret. * He later gave his most treasured scripture, the ''River Severing Sutra'', to Gu Can. * He later secured Cyan Gorge Island for Gu Can's future. * He worked with Gu Can's mother to raise Gu Can and kept her under secret restrictions until Chen Ping'an made him remove them. * Although Chen Ping'an saw him as an enemy from the small town, he became an uneasy ally at Bamboo Scroll Lake. Chen Ping'an once told him they were half alike, friends or foes aside. * He paid a skilled master to secretly refine the skin the Gu Can's little catfish shed on reaching the Nascent Tier into the dark green robe Gu Can wears. * His walnut bracelet, an old bracelet with eight remaining beads carved with rain gods and thunder gods, was later given to Chen Ping'an. == References == [[Category:Characters]] [[Category:Male]] [[Category:Alive]]

pages.title: Lotus Flower Blessed Land
pages.content:
The Lotus Flower Blessed Land is a dynamic and multifaceted setting with its own intricate system of governance, culture, and power dynamics. Its connections to other worlds and the presence of otherworldly immortals make it a significant location in the narrative. The challenges, opportunities, and unique characteristics of the Lotus Flower Blessed Land make it a compelling setting for conflict, growth, and exploration.

'''General Characteristics:'''

* The Lotus Flower Blessed Land is described as a '''medium-grade blessed land'''. This is according to otherworldly immortals, who consider factors like the abundance of spiritual energy and the population of the world.
* It is considered small by otherworldly immortals.
* It is one of the '''72 blessed lands'''.
* The blessed land is linked to the '''Lotus Flower World''', a small world where the Dao Ancestor is said to relax. This connection is unique, with only one other such place existing in the four worlds.
* The Lotus Flower Blessed Land is not particularly famous compared to the Cloud Cave Blessed Land.
* The land is described as a '''labyrinth''' in a small area, making it difficult for those with cultivation to move around and act as they normally would.
* The rules of the Heavenly Dao are difficult to manifest within the Lotus Flower Blessed Land.
* The flow of time within the Lotus Flower Blessed Land can vary compared to the Majestic World depending on the mood of a certain person.
* The land is known for producing martial arts prodigies and is used by otherworldly immortals to temper their minds.
* Entering the Lotus Flower Blessed Land is said to be more difficult than entering other blessed lands. It depends on the mood of a certain individual or their first impression.
* It is possible to ascend from this blessed land.

'''Political and Social Landscape:'''

* The Lotus Flower Blessed Land contains several nations, including the '''Northern Jin Nation''' and the '''Southern Garden Nation'''.
* These nations have their own political structures, military forces, and cultural practices [See the previous overviews of these nations].
* There is a complex interplay of power between the different nations.
* The land is influenced by the presence of otherworldly immortals, who often arrive to temper their minds.
* There are various sects and factions with their own goals and ambitions.
* The land's elites are known throughout the Lotus Flower Blessed Land [See the previous overviews of the Northern Jin Nation and Southern Garden Nation].

'''Key Figures and Groups:'''

* A mysterious person, represented by a '''young child holding a plantain fan''', is responsible for overseeing the Lotus Flower Blessed Land and interacts with those who have the right to know about the blessed land.
* '''Ding Ying''' is a prominent figure in the Lotus Flower Blessed Land, knowledgeable about otherworldly immortals and has fought them. He is considered a peerless martial artist. He was once considered to be the strongest martial artist in the world.
* '''Zhou Fei''' is an otherworldly immortal who has retained his true body and soul within the Lotus Flower Blessed Land. He is the leader of the Jiang Clan from the Jade Tablet Sect and controls the Cloud Cave Blessed Land.
* '''Yu Zhenyi''' is a leader of the Lake Mountain Faction and is a significant figure within the Lotus Flower Blessed Land.
* '''Zhong Qiu''' is a powerful figure, serving as the imperial preceptor of the Southern Garden Nation.
* '''Lu Tai''' is an otherworldly immortal who became one of the Upper Ten Elites within the Lotus Flower Blessed Land.
* '''Wei Xian''' is the founding emperor of the Southern Garden Nation.
* '''Sui Youbian''' is a female sword immortal who is considered to be very fortunate.
* There are various other powerful martial artists and cultivators, as well as many ordinary people and scholars.

'''Interactions with Other Worlds:'''

* The Lotus Flower Blessed Land is linked to the '''Lotus Flower World''', a small world associated with the Dao Ancestor.
* Otherworldly immortals come to the Lotus Flower Blessed Land to temper their minds and navigate challenges.
* People from the Majestic World view the Lotus Flower Blessed Land as small and limiting.
* There is an awareness of other blessed lands, such as the Cloud Cave Blessed Land and the Limpid Pond Blessed Land.
* The Great Li Empire and other forces from the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent are known.
* The Lotus Flower Blessed Land is known in the Majestic World.
* There is interaction between the Lotus Flower Blessed Land and the Middle Earth Divine Continent.

'''Unique Aspects and Challenges:'''

* The Lotus Flower Blessed Land is a complex area with many powerful figures.
* The rules of cultivation, and the understanding of the world, are different than what is found in other places, like the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent.
* The land has a unique link to the Lotus Flower World.
* There are conflicts and power struggles between various factions and individuals.
* The Lotus Flower Blessed Land is influenced by the mood of a certain person, which can impact the flow of time and the events that occur within it.
* The presence of otherworldly immortals creates unique challenges and interactions within the blessed land.
* There are a number of fated opportunities in the Lotus Flower Blessed Land, but they are difficult to obtain.
[[Category:Locations]]

pages.title: Lu Baixiang
pages.content:
{{Character |header1=Lu Baixiang |Aliases=Little Bai |Vital_status=Alive |Gender=Male |Species=Human |Disciple(s)=Yuan Bao
Yuan Lai |Friend(s)=[[Chen Ping An]]
[[Zhu Lian]]
[[Wei Xian]]
[[Sui Youbian]]
[[Pei Qian]] |Occupation=Martial artist
Founder of a sect subsidiary to Downtrodden Mountain |Current_affiliation(s)=[[Downtrodden Mountain]] |Former_affiliation(s)=[[Lotus Flower Blessed Land]] (founder of its demonic forces) |Continent=[[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]] |Cultivation_rank=Pure martial artist (peak of the sixth tier) |Novel=Chapter 311 }} == Appearance == Lu Baixiang is described as tall, with a sturdy and handsome build. He is usually seen in a Confucian robe, with the saber Halting Snow hanging at his waist, its tip often resting against the ground as he leans on the hilt.Chapter 334Chapter 568 == Personality == Lu Baixiang is calm, composed and easygoing, able to strike up a conversation with almost anyone. He is also a jack of all talents outside of martial arts, skilled at the guqin, Go, calligraphy and painting, and takes a quiet pride in all of them. Despite his relaxed manner, he carries a sharp, dangerous edge underneath, and in the history of the Lotus Flower Blessed Land he was known for his ruthlessness and decisiveness as the founder of its demonic orthodoxy. He is patient and good-humored with the people he is close to, including as a teacher, but he can turn cold and openly threatening when someone close to him might be betrayed.Chapter 334Chapter 400Chapter 559 == Background == Lu Baixiang grew up an orphan in the Lotus Flower Blessed Land and had a hard early life, at one point killing a man in self-defense and being thrown in jail before leaving his hometown to survive on his own. Finding that the martial arts world of his time had no true righteous or demonic factions, just sects competing for impressive-sounding names, he founded his own demonic orthodoxy as a kind of game, deliberately holding it to higher standards than any righteous sect for the novelty of it. He eventually became the most powerful martial artist in the Lotus Flower Blessed Land and achieved invincibility for decades, but his unmarried, wandering lifestyle eventually left him vulnerable, and he was ambushed and killed by dozens of elite cultivators working together.Chapter 311Chapter 314Chapter 400 His cultivation base survived afterward as one of four picture scrolls kept in the Lotus Flower Blessed Land, alongside Wei Xian, Sui Youbian and Zhu Lian. Chen Ping'an brought him out of his picture scroll and back to life in the Majestic World during the battle at Old Dragon City, where Lu Baixiang fought General Xu Qingzhou and was badly wounded before the battle ended.Chapter 334Chapter 337 Afterward, he stayed close to Chen Ping'an and the other three revived martial artists, acting as a strategist, companion and occasional teacher to Pei Qian during their travels, and eventually settled on Downtrodden Mountain. He later took in a pair of twins, Yuan Bao and Yuan Lai, as his in-house disciples after leading a group of former soldiers against a reclusive demonic sect, and brought them to Downtrodden Mountain to broaden their horizons. He also helped recover a dragon boat and a water palace for Downtrodden Mountain, and set up his own sect as a subsidiary to it, splitting his time between Downtrodden Mountain and travels through the cultivation world.Chapter 483Chapter 567Chapter 568 == Trivia == *Pei Qian nicknamed him "Little Bai," using the character for elephant in his name as a pun.Chapter 481 *He is a frequent Go opponent of Sui Youbian and considered himself close to unrivaled at the game during his years in the Lotus Flower Blessed Land.Chapter 334 == References ==

pages.title: Lu Chen
pages.content:
{{Character |header1=Lu Chen |image1=Lu Chen.png |Aliases=Daoist Lu |Vital_status=Alive |Gender=Male |Species=Human |Master(s)=Dao Ancestor |Disciple(s)=[[He Xiaoliang]] |Relatives=[[Lu Tai]] (descendant) |Occupation=Branch Master of the Daoist Sect
Fortune teller |Current_affiliation(s)=Daoist Sect
White Jade Capital |Cultivation_rank=Branch Master of the Daoist Sect
Limited to 13th-tier Qi refiner strength in the Majestic World |Novel=Chapter 15 }} '''Lu Chen''' is the third disciple of the Dao Ancestor and one of the three Branch Masters of the Daoist Sect, which dominates the [[Heavenly World]]. He is the current master of the White Jade Capital. Born in the Majestic World but raised in the Heavenly World, he is a carefree, mischievous figure who appears as a young Daoist priest in a lotus flower hat. He likes running fortune-telling stalls, reading young women's palms, and setting up grand games of Go across the world. To Chen Ping'an, he first appears as "Daoist Lu", the kindly fortune teller who saved Ning Yao and wrote him a medicinal recipe. Later, Chen Ping'an realises that Lu Chen schemed against him several times, and Lu Chen becomes someone Chen Ping'an deeply distrusts. == Appearance == Lu Chen looks like a young, carefree Daoist priest, wearing Daoist robes and a lotus flower hat. He can split himself into multiple clones at once. == Personality == Lu Chen is playful, lazy and shameless. He haggles with a rival fortune teller, eats as a guest while being made to cook, and flirts openly with young women while reading their palms. He cares little for Confucian rites or even for the strict rules of Daoism. His first senior brother is meticulous and his second careful, but Lu Chen has always been scolded for ignoring the rules.Chapter 212 Beneath this, he is a supreme schemer whose plans span centuries, and who treats the world like a Go board. Whether people receive fortune or misfortune from him depends largely on his mood. He describes himself as someone who "holds grudges the best". He can be genuinely kind, as with the little boy in azure, but also coldly ruthless, as when he contemplates crushing his own junior brother. Many of the Dao principles he promotes seem foolish at first, but prove profound after hundreds or thousands of years. == Background == Before ascending, Lu Chen loved to sail the four seas in a small boat. His boatman, who was in his thirties when they set out, returned to land alone after Lu Chen ascended in the North Sea, only to find that his home nation had long since vanished.Chapter 265 That boatman later became the first boatman of Osmanthus Island, and he warned Chen Ping'an not to ruin his Great Dao. Lu Chen's descendant, Lu Tai, deliberately chose a name meaning "land rising", in opposition to his ancestor's "land sinking". Under the rules set by the Etiquette Sage, when Lu Chen enters the Majestic World, he can use at most the power of a thirteenth-tier Qi refiner. == Plot == === Daoist Lu === Lu Chen introduces himself as "Daoist Lu" with no Dao title, running a fortune-telling stall in the small town. He saves [[Ning Yao]] when she is close to death.Chapter 15 He tells Chen Ping'an that he can survive if he goes to the south of town and becomes the disciple of the blacksmith Ruan.Chapter 23 He reveals to Chen Ping'an the sinister things [[Cai Jinjian]] had done to him, and that Chen Ping'an was already brimming with an aura of death at the time.Chapter 42 He leaves Chen Ping'an a three-page medicinal recipe in plain, regulation-style handwriting that Ning Yao finds soulless, stamped with an azure jade seal reading "Signed, Lu Chen".Chapter 70 Chen Ping'an is deeply grateful and practises his handwriting from it. Years later, when Chen Ping'an writes Lu Chen's name in the snow while imitating it, Master Bai turns around from far away, and heaven and earth seem to turn upside down.Chapter 175 Lu Chen also tells Chen Ping'an that the snake gall pebbles in the Dragon Whisker River can be sold, starting him gathering them. === Return to the Small Town === Lu Chen returns to [[Clay Vase Alley]] with his disciple-to-be [[He Xiaoliang]], whom he tricked into leaving Divine Edict Sect. He discusses the Dao with [[Wei Bo]], and tells He Xiaoliang of a "senior brother" of his, who is also her true junior uncle. He predicts that this senior brother will one day surpass him at Go and fortune telling, and defeat the demon of White Emperor City.Chapter 201 (2) He sets up his stall again, where the dying Emperor Song of the Great Li Empire comes to him. Lu Chen mocks him over the replica of the White Jade Capital he built without permission, and remarks that he could extend the emperor's life by a thousand years. He also confronts [[Song Jixin]], calling him by his real name, Song Mu.Chapter 206 (1) He later visits Zhi Gui and tells her he extracted a promise from Song Zhengchun that he wanted. Through He Xiaoliang, he returns a snake gall pebble to Chen Ping'an, declaring that they no longer owe each other anything. His real plan is revealed later. The snake gall pebbles and the recipe pages form the "banks of a river", creating a bridge of fortune between Chen Ping'an and He Xiaoliang, so that the fortune released by the fall of Jewel Small World would be split evenly between them.Chapter 211 (2) He then formally accepts He Xiaoliang as his disciple, and explains that his second senior brother chose [[Ma Kuxuan]] because their personalities were alike. He also solemnly orders Xie Shi to protect [[Li Xisheng]], threatening to return from the White Jade Capital and break the rules of both worlds if anything happens to him.Chapter 235 (1) === Chen Ping'an's Grudge === During the battle at the Flood Dragon Trench, a "decree of Lu Chen" restrains the participants. Chen Ping'an later says that Lu Chen plotted against him two or three times in that battle, and that he retaliated by making Lu Chen deliver his final words to a friend. Chen Ping'an later calls him "that bastard" who screwed him over. In Chen Ping'an's eyes, Lu Chen's bridge of fortune with He Xiaoliang and his attempts to lure him to the White Jade Capital left lasting negative marks. === Master of the White Jade Capital === Back in the Heavenly World, Lu Chen oversees the White Jade Capital. He watches events in the Majestic World from its railings, casually severs a thread of fate, and drives away a crowd of immortals with palm strikes. He guides the Dao Ancestor's final disciple, a young Daoist priest who has suffered at the bottom of the world, enjoyed the White Jade Capital's fortune, and died once. Lu Chen tells him it is now time to learn how to live a good life, and that a few decades or a thousand years would both be normal.Chapter 522 (4) Lu Chen reveals that Qi Jingchun's final game of Go was described to the Dao Ancestor by Qi Jingchun himself. He also urges his junior brother not to lose to someone surnamed Qi again. == Abilities == * '''Cultivation:''' A Branch Master of the Daoist Sect, among the most powerful beings in the Heavenly World. In the Majestic World he is limited to the power of a thirteenth-tier Qi refiner. * '''Divination and calculation:''' A master fortune teller who weaves plans across centuries and continents. * '''Mystical abilities:''' He can create clones, drag others into small worlds, travel instantly across vast distances, and "scoop" people to his side from afar. * '''Name:''' Even writing or speaking his name draws the attention of the world's most powerful beings. == Trivia == * According to rumour, Lu Chen captured a male oriole, while the founder of Syncretism raised the female. * His name, 陆沉, is a phrase meaning "a continent sinking". * He haggles with a fellow fortune teller over the price of advice and pays with a real piece of silver. * Zhi Gui complains that he was "quite unkind" to give Long Eyebrows a pagoda without explaining its downsides. == References == [[Category:Characters]] [[Category:Male]] [[Category:Alive]]

pages.title: Ma Kuxuan
pages.content:
{{Character |header1=Ma Kuxuan |image1=Ma Kuxuan.png |Vital_status=Alive |Gender=Male |Species=Human |Relatives=[[Ma Lanhua]] (grandmother)
Unnamed father and mother |Master(s)=Unnamed swordsman (first master, deceased)
True Martial Mountain's Dao guardian (second master) |Enemie(s)=[[Chen Ping An]]
[[Song Jixin]]
the Sea Tide Cavalry (destroyed) |Love_interest(s)=[[Zhi Gui]] (one-sided) |Occupation=Militarian cultivator
Disciple of True Martial Mountain |Current_affiliation(s)=[[True Martial Mountain]] |Former_affiliation(s)=[[Apricot Blossom Alley]], the small town |Continent=[[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]] |Novel=Chapter 42 }} == Appearance == Ma Kuxuan is a skinny, tanned boy with notably large eyes, short in stature as a child but quick and explosive in his movements, often compared to a nimble monkey. His face is capable of a dazzling, sometimes mocking smile, though when badly hurt he fights on with blood seeping from his mouth, ears and nose without making a sound. He keeps a white cat as a companion, a creature with an unusual nature of its own.Chapter 54Chapter 370 == Personality == Ma Kuxuan is quiet and keeps to himself, having grown up pretending to be slow-witted while bullied by the other children of the small town, though Chen Ping'an recognizes early on that he is anything but. He is cold and calculating, willing to feign weakness to lure an opponent into a trap, as he does in his first fight with Chen Ping'an. He has an intense dislike of being underestimated and takes pride in his vow to never lose to anyone of the same cultivation level after entering [[True Martial Mountain]]. As he matures he becomes more ruthless and unpredictable, killing on a whim and treating the deaths of strangers as inconsequential, yet he holds to his own private code, such as never killing someone he considers truly innocent, however thin that distinction can be in practice. Beneath the arrogance and cruelty, he remains capable of real tenderness, which only ever shows through with his grandmother and in his one-sided feelings for Zhi Gui.Chapter 42Chapter 223Chapter 642 == Background == Ma Kuxuan grew up in [[Small Town|Apricot Blossom Alley]] in the small town, raised by his grandmother, a local midwife known to the other residents simply as [[Ma Lanhua|Granny Ma]], after his father proved unreliable and uncaring. He first appears as a strange, friendless boy who spends his days alone throwing and skipping stones, a habit that conceals formidable precision and power. He confronts Chen Ping'an after he tracked down Chen Ping'an and Ning Yao for a bounty, leading to a fight in which Ma Kuxuan was defeated and only saved from being killed when a swordsman from True Martial Mountain intervened, taking Ma Kuxuan on as his soon-to-be disciple.Chapter 42Chapter 54Chapter 56 Shortly afterward, his grandmother was killed, slapped to death by a visiting cultivator, the granddaughter of the Sea Tide Cavalry's leader. Grief-stricken, Ma Kuxuan demanded his new master help him find her spirit, but was told her soul had already disintegrated from a lifetime of accumulated sins, including years of quietly attacking passing cultivators and spirits. He swore to avenge her regardless of the rules binding him as a Militarian cultivator.Chapter 57Chapter 59Chapter 571 {{Spoilers}} He left the small town to formally join True Martial Mountain, one of the Militarian ancestral forces of the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent, and rose quickly there, earning a reputation as a one-in-a-century prodigy and remaining undefeated against opponents of equal cultivation. He later crossed paths with Chen Ping'an again on the streets of the Colorful Garment Nation and fought a rematch, deepening his one-sided rivalry.Chapter 191Chapter 223 Ma Kuxuan was later given to the sharp-tongued maidservant Zhi Gui as a "fated opportunity" by the fortune-teller Lu Chen, and he willingly agreed to serve and obey her, given his feelings for her even as she needled him for not yet being powerful enough to impress her. His cultivation continued to advance at a startling pace, including killing two Golden Core Tier swordsmen of the Luminous Vermilion Empire in life-and-death duels while still short of twenty years old, a feat that made him the most talked-about young cultivator on the continent, ranked behind only the legendary Li Tuanjing and Wei Jin.Chapter 415Chapter 452 It later came out that Ma Kuxuan's own parents, who secretly controlled the Ma Clan's dragon kiln in Apricot Blossom Alley, had been directly involved in arranging for Chen Ping'an's bonded porcelain to be shattered when he was still a child, selling out his fortune for their own profit. His grandmother had tried and failed to stop them, the one notable act of conscience the otherwise selfish old woman performed, and Ma Kuxuan had woken during the scheme as a child and absorbed part of the truth, which is part of why he always paid close attention to Chen Ping'an afterward.Chapter 530 In retaliation for his grandmother's death, Ma Kuxuan hunted down and annihilated the entire Sea Tide Cavalry, killing the former leader personally and sparing only his granddaughter, whom he took captive and renamed Shudian, keeping her as a maidservant who travels everywhere with him afterward. He visited his resurrected grandmother, now risen to Dragon Whisker River Guardian and threatened on her behalf until she was granted recognition and a temple as the Iron Talisman River Goddess. He continues to travel with Shudian in a cruel, controlling way, and killing indiscriminately by his own whims while insisting he never kills the truly innocent.Chapter 559Chapter 642 == Trivia == *He is a Militarian cultivator, a cultivation path distinct from the orthodox immortal sects and from pure martial artists.Chapter 223 *He has a habit of snacking on brined soybeans.Chapter 223 *He has promised himself to one day kill Song Jixin, who in turn has vowed to kill him over his feelings for Zhi Gui.Chapter 415 *He secretly watched Chen Ping'an from a distance on at least one occasion in their childhood without revealing himself.Chapter 642 == References ==

pages.title: Ma Lanhua
pages.content:
{{Character |header1=Ma Lanhua |image1=Ma Lanhua.png |Aliases=Granny Ma |Vital_status=Deceased (ascended as a river deity) |Gender=Female |Species=River deity (formerly Human) |Relatives=[[Ma Kuxuan]] (grandson)
Unnamed son and daughter-in-law |Occupation=Iron Talisman River Goddess
Former river guardian of the Dragon Whisker River |Current_affiliation(s)=Dragon Whisker River |Continent=[[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]] |Novel=Chapter 59 }} '''Ma Lanhua''', known in the small town as '''Granny Ma''', is the grandmother of [[Ma Kuxuan]]. She was a notoriously foul-tempered old woman of [[Apricot Blossom Alley]] and one of the town's most skilled trash talkers. After being slapped to death by a cultivator, she was made the river guardian of the Dragon Whisker River by Old Man Yang, purely for her grandson's sake. She was later promoted to river goddess. Timid and obsequious towards the powerful, petty and vindictive towards everyone else, she nevertheless loves her grandson deeply. She also showed a rare flash of conscience over the shattering of [[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]]'s bonded porcelain. == Appearance == As a living woman, Granny Ma was a frail old woman. As a river deity, her appearance grows more youthful by the day. She appears with long hair spreading across the riverbank, or as a clump of waterweeds swaying in the river. == Personality == In life, Ma Lanhua was infamous in the small town. [[Zhi Gui]] calls her "far too detestable", possessing every bad habit common and uncommon among women of the common class, and has long wanted revenge on her for her spiteful behaviour at the Iron Lock Well. She was one of the few people who could rival Gu Can's mother in an argument, although Gu Can's mother sent her home to "reflect" time and again.Chapter 202 As a deity, she remains timid and obsequious before anyone stronger, calling Old Man Yang "Great Immortal" and fawning over him. Towards those weaker, she is greedy and petty: she demands bribes from passing mountain spirits, and kills an old tortoise in a fit of anger. Yet she cares deeply for Ma Kuxuan, and she endured everything she suffered as a deity largely so he would not be left alone in the world. == Background == Ma Lanhua lived on Apricot Blossom Alley with her son and daughter-in-law, who managed to control a dragon kiln. The couple were deeply involved in the shattering of Chen Ping'an's bonded porcelain, along with the Great Li Empire's imperial concubine and the late emperor. In a rare display of conscience, Ma Lanhua tried everything she could to stop them, but her son and daughter-in-law were consumed by greed and she failed.Chapter 530 (2) == Plot == === Death === Granny Ma is slapped at her doorway by a cultivator who does not control their strength, and dies from the blow. Ma Kuxuan finds her body with her cheek swollen black and blue. A deity tells him that her soul cannot be found because of the sins she committed in life. Ma Kuxuan suspects it is the girl whose cultivation he disturbed on the covered bridge, and enraged, beats up the girl. He later leaves True Martial Mountain to seek out the commander of the Sea Tide Cavalry in connection with her death.Chapter 224 === River Guardian === Old Man Yang grants her soul the indestructible body of a river guardian. He explains what she must do to win a temple, a golden statue and recognition in the empire's genealogical records. When she asks whether he protects her only because of her grandson, he openly admits that he does. When she presses him on why he let True Martial Mountain take Ma Kuxuan instead of teaching him himself, he punishes her with agonising pain.Chapter 63 (1) As a river guardian, she becomes younger and stronger. When a group of mountain spirits travelling along the Iron Talisman River approaches her for help, she bluntly demands a gift from each of them before she will escort them west.Chapter 96 === River Goddess === Ma Lanhua is promoted to formal river goddess of the Dragon Whisker River by the Great Li Empire, and can now briefly come ashore. She begs Old Man Yang for even a small, empty shrine, but he sneers that with her reputation, she would get vats of spit rather than incense. Swimming past the blacksmith shop, she now feels she has turned Ruan Xiu from an enemy into a friend, considers herself half a helper to the Militarian sage, and privately thinks of herself as Old Man Yang's secret disciple.Chapter 118 (2) When Chen Ping'an returns home with the little boy in azure, who starts a fight in her river, she meets him for the first time as a deity. She hides her identity, telling him that a river deity must sever her mortal past, while privately resenting his good fortune.Chapter 180 (1) Old Man Yang orders her to go to the source of the Dragon Whisker River and disperse half of her godly body into the water, to increase its yin energy for Ruan Qiong's sword forging. The agony and damage to her Great Dao are immense.Chapter 185 (1) Soon after, the haughty Iron Talisman River Goddess, [[Yang Hua]], her superior, visits the waterfall for the first time and leaves without acknowledging Ma Lanhua's timid greeting, to her silent indignation.Chapter 201 (2) === Reunion with Ma Kuxuan === Years later, Ma Kuxuan returns home and goes first to the river rather than to his parents. Ma Lanhua then emerges from the river, rejuvenated in appearance, and sits with her grandson on the bank, holding his hands. She nags him, badmouths everyone who has wronged her, and pokes his forehead for not listening to his elders. == Abilities == * '''River deity powers:''' She can travel through and control the Dragon Whisker River, appear in the water, and, as a river goddess, briefly come ashore. * '''Yin water:''' She can turn the river's water "dark", producing water essence beneficial for forging swords. * '''Indestructible body:''' Her river guardian body was granted by Old Man Yang. == Trivia == * 马兰花 (mǎ lán huā) is the name of a flower, the Chinese iris. * The mountain spirits she extorted were outraged that a "lowly river guardian" demanded bribes after they politely called her a river god. == References == [[Category:Characters]] [[Category:Female]]

[[Cui Chan]] |Occupation = Janitor of the town school
Teacher |Former_affiliation(s) = [[Mountain Cliff Academy]]
Small town school |Continent = [[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]] |Novel = Chapter 67 }} '''Ma Zhan''' is the junior brother of [[Qi Jingchun]] and an unofficial disciple of the [[Scholarly Sage]]. He worked as the janitor of the school in the small town and was killed while escorting the last of its students to Mountain Cliff Academy. == Appearance == Ma Zhan is an old man with white hair. On the day he led the students out of town, he dressed in a scholar's robe much like Qi Jingchun's, with a jade pendant at his waist, a tall hat, and his hair neatly combed.Chapter 71 == Personality == At the school the children knew him as a kindly old man. Once Qi Jingchun was gone, he became stern and commanding, and silenced Li Huai with a single glare when the boy tried to get Li Baoping in trouble. He held firmly to his teacher's words and could not accept Qi Jingchun's choice to stay in the town and give up his future for its people. He blamed Buddhist ideas for leading his senior brother astray and grew angry when Qi Jingchun said their teacher was not right about everything.Chapter 67 He enjoyed scholarly talk and drinking, and he quickly warmed to Cui Minghuang over shared discussion of the classics.Chapter 84 Cui Chan considered him ambitious beyond his ability and the weakest in mind among the Scholarly Sage's students, and said he betrayed his companion for the promise of becoming a mountain master.Chapter 149 The Scholarly Sage judged that one wrong step led Ma Zhan into many more, and that although he came to his senses, he chose to make amends only through his death.Chapter 594 == Background == Ma Zhan first met Qi Jingchun about 80 years before the story, when both studied under the same teacher. Before they left for Mountain Cliff Academy, their teacher gave each of them a saying, and Ma Zhan's was about heaven and earth raising a ruler who in turn governs them. In his student days he and Mao Xiaodong were too intimidated by Zuo You's cold manner to approach him.Chapter 580 He later served as the janitor of Qi Jingchun's school in the small town. While sweeping the yard, he often noticed a boy crouching under the window to listen to lessons, and he later told the coach driver about this boy, Chen Ping'an. Shortly before leaving, Ma Zhan sat outside Qi Jingchun's study and argued with him over whether to stay in Jewel Small World. Qi Jingchun gave him a reply about knowing when to retreat and when to hold firm, which left Ma Zhan puzzled, and then asked him to take the children to Mountain Cliff Academy. Ma Zhan agreed. He told the students that Qi Jingchun had stepped down as teacher and mountain master and that he would lead the trip in his place. He set off with Li Baoping, Li Huai, Lin Shouyi, Dong Shuijing and Shi Chunjia, travelling alongside [[Cui Minghuang]] of Lake View Academy.Chapter 73 On Cui Chan's orders, Cui Minghuang befriended him and convinced him that he could succeed Qi Jingchun as mountain master, and then that he should break with Mountain Cliff Academy altogether to become the first mountain master of a new academy.Chapter 82 While checking the children's homework one day, Ma Zhan said he needed to talk over their route with Cui Minghuang. Neither came back, and Li Huai later found Ma Zhan badly wounded and bleeding heavily. Kept alive briefly by the three ancestral locust leaves Li Baoping carried, he held her hand and told her to secretly warn Chen Ping'an not to trust anyone from Lake View Academy or the Great Li capital. According to Cui Chan, Ma Zhan finally saw that he had been fooled and that Qi Jingchun had known of his betrayal all along. He gave up his chance at reincarnation to injure Cui Minghuang so the children could get back to the town. The children buried him on the road. During his last walk through the town, Qi Jingchun visited the grave of his junior brother.Chapter 85 == Trivia == * Li Huai joked that Cui Minghuang must be Ma Zhan's illegitimate son or grandson because of how close the two seemed. * The Scholarly Sage suspected that Ma Zhan's betrayal hurt Qi Jingchun more than all of Cui Chan's plots. * The Scholarly Sage described Ma Zhan as a piece moved by the real schemer behind the scenes rather than a player in the game himself.Chapter 154 == References ==

pages.content:
{{Character |header1 = Madam Xu |Aliases = Mistress Xu
Miss Xu
the lady of Light Breeze City |Vital_status = Alive |Gender = Female |Species = Human |Relatives = Xu Hun (husband and Dao partner)
