[[Chen Ping An]] |Occupation = Mistress of the Xu Clan |Current_affiliation(s) = Xu Clan of Light Breeze City |Continent = [[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]] |Novel = Chapter 2 |Donghua = Episode 1 |Spouse(s)=Xu Hun|Love_interest(s)=Xu Hun}} '''Madam Xu''' is the wife of the leader of the Xu Clan of Light Breeze City. She came to the small town in Jewel Small World with her son and schemed to take the Liu Clan's ancestral armor from [[Liu Xianyang]]. == Appearance == Madam Xu is a middle-aged woman.Chapter 2 She is described as beautiful and full-figured.Chapter 7 In town she carries herself with calm dignity.Chapter 35 Years later she appears at Sun Scorch Mountain as an elegant woman in a palace dress.Chapter 533 == Personality == Madam Xu is shrewd and calculating, and is called the calculating mistress of Light Breeze City. She treats every dealing like business. She once explained to her son that favours given now and then earn gratitude, while favours given all the time breed resentment. She also told him that people in small places are not as foolish as they look.Chapter 34 With her son she is patient and indulgent. She never minds when he shouts at her, because a powerful figure had declared at his birth that he was fierce and highly gifted.Chapter 44 With others she is gracious on the surface but quietly threatening. When Lu Zhengchun swore loyalty to her alone, she smiled and suggested he repeat those words in front of her husband, and he fell to his knees. She does not dismiss danger easily. Even when the Mountain-moving Ape scoffed at [[Chen Ping An]], she stayed uneasy and believed he would dare to seek revenge. == Background == Madam Xu is the Dao partner of the leader of the Xu Clan, who is later named as Xu Hun.Chapter 457 She entered the small town with her son, a boy in a large red robe, at the same time as the [[Mountain-Moving Ape]] and [[Tao Zi]] of Sun Scorch Mountain. She had paid a great price to come, and her standing in Light Breeze City, along with her hopes of one day running the city, depended on the trip paying off. Her target was the Liu Clan's scaly armor. Working in secret, she let Sun Scorch Mountain know about the armor and sword scripture in Liu Xianyang's family. She also told them that his bonded porcelain had gone to their enemy, the Wind Lightning Field. She then let the Mountain-moving Ape act as her decoy. She used Lu Zhengchun as a go-between with Liu Xianyang. After the ape struck down Liu Xianyang, she obtained the armor and planned to give it to her husband to make up for his weak constitution. She took Lu Zhengchun into the [[Clans|Xu Clan]] as part of a larger deal with the fallen Lu Empire's imperial clan, who had taken refuge in Light Breeze City. When she learned more of the situation, she went to the kiln supervision office and offered to return the armor as an apology. Chen Dui of the Yingyin Chen Clan declined, saying the Xu Clan could not have known Liu Xianyang's true background.Chapter 65 Chen Ping An later counted her among the people who left a bad impression on him at first sight.Chapter 226 With the armor, her husband became a formidable Nascent Tier cultivator and purged rival branches of the clan. The Xu Clan sold its holdings in Dragon Spring Prefecture, including Cinnabar Mountain, at a loss. Cinnabar Mountain later passed to Chen Ping An.Chapter 528 To make up for this, they married a daughter of the clan to an illegitimate son of the [[Clans|Pillar Yuan Clan]] of the [[Great Li Empire]].Chapter 571 Madam Xu spent years trying to arrange a marriage between her son and Tao Zi, without success. During a visit to Sun Scorch Mountain, she told the Mountain-moving Ape that Chen Ping An must die before he could become a threat. Liu Xianyang and Chen Ping An both hold a grudge against her clan over the armor. Liu Xianyang described Light Breeze City and Sun Scorch Mountain as places that chase only profit and not the Great Dao.Chapter 620 == Trivia == * She is mostly called "the woman" or "the lady" of Light Breeze City's Xu Clan. * Lu Zhengchun addressed her as Mistress Xu when he pledged his loyalty. * Ma Kuxuan's greatest regret was that she had been too lenient and failed to kill Liu Xianyang.Chapter 642 * Liu Chicheng described her and her husband as a perfect match. One devotes himself to cultivation while the other runs the clan and makes money.Chapter 651 * The Xu Clan she helps run is famous for Fox Skin Beauty Talismans and later became one of the sects-in-waiting under the Great Li Empire. == References ==

pages.title: Majestic World
pages.content:
The Majestic World is a vast and complex place with diverse geography, demographics, cultures, politics, and economies. Here's a deep dive into what the sources reveal about it:
[[File:Screenshot 2025-01-24 5.30.09 PM.png|center|thumb|525x525px]]

== '''Geography:''' ==
* The Majestic World has '''nine continents''', including Eastern Treasured Vial Continent, Complete Reed Continent, Southern Whirl Continent, Pure White Continent, and Golden Armor Continent.
* '''Middle Earth Divine Continent''' is described as the "glowing gem" and is the central and most significant of these continents. Several major empires exist on this continent.
* The Majestic World contains '''four lakes and five seas'''.
* There are '''ten large worlds and thirty-six small worlds''' that are considered blessed paradises due to their high levels of spiritual energy. These worlds include Paradise Small World, Astral Winds Small World, Jewel Small World, and Island Small World.
* Small worlds are also referred to as mystical realms. These are often formed from ancient ruins or battlefields. They have a history that is complex and can be incomplete.
* '''Blessed lands''' are also part of the Majestic World. They are larger than small worlds and often produce many prodigious figures who are then taken by the nations or sects that own the land.

== '''Demographics:''' ==
* The Majestic World is populated by a variety of beings including humans, immortals, Buddhas, deities, demons, and ghosts.
* There are different groups such as '''Qi refiners''', who cultivate spiritual energy, '''pure martial artists''' and '''swordsmen'''.
* There is a clear distinction between people from "the mountains" (immortals and cultivators) and people from "outside the mountains" (mortals).
* The population is distributed across the nine continents, with varying levels of cultivation and societal development.
* '''Immigrants''' from other worlds also exist in the Majestic World. These “otherworldly immortals” often have unique abilities and knowledge.
* There are also '''demonic cultivators''' who utilize sinister techniques and can cause chaos.

== '''Cultures:''' ==
* The Majestic World is influenced by several major schools of thought: '''Confucianism, Buddhism, Daoism, and Militarianism'''. The Mohists also exist with their own set of values.
* Different continents and regions have their own unique cultures, customs, and dialects.
* '''Language''' and dialect proficiency can be an indicator of one's social status.
* There is a significant emphasis on cultivation, with many people striving to reach higher levels of power and longevity.
* The '''arts and sciences''' exist in the Majestic World, including geomancy, divination, and literature.
* Many stories and legends have developed around the world, with popular figures and places.
* There are cultural practices such as worshipping deities, ancestors, and powerful figures.
* There are different schools of thought, including the School of Fiction, which explores different cultures and customs.

== '''Politics:''' ==
* The political landscape is characterized by a complex interplay between '''empires, nations, and powerful sects'''.
* The '''Great Li Empire''' is one of the major powers in the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent. It has expanded its territory significantly in recent years.
* There are also other powerful entities, like the Lu Clan, known for their knowledge and philosophy.
* The '''imperial courts''' are central to the political structure. The imperial court is organized into six ministries.
* The position of '''city god''' exists in the night realm, mirroring the roles of governors in the living world. City gods rule over the beings and entities in the realm of the night.
* '''Political conflicts''' between different factions and schools of thought are common.
* The leaders of the various worlds are said to be blessed with immense fortune.
* Some rulers focus on expansion and power, while others are more focused on their people's well-being.
* The '''relationship between the imperial court and immortal forces in the mountains''' also influences political dynamics.

== '''Economy:''' ==
* '''Trade''' is a significant part of the economy, with goods and treasures exchanged between different regions and worlds.
* The value of land is determined by the presence of spiritual energy and the potential for profit.
* There are '''various industries and sectors''', including the creation of porcelain, geomancy, cultivation, and travel.
* Certain resources, such as spiritual energy, are highly valued.
* '''Immortal treasures and spirit tools''' have high economic value.
* The collection of merit is important for deities and political achievement for officials.
* '''Intercontinental ships''' transport people and goods between different continents and worlds.

This overview provides a glimpse into the multifaceted nature of the Majestic World, with its vast geography, diverse populations, rich cultures, complex politics, and thriving economies.

pages.title: Mao Xiaodong
pages.content:
{{Character |header1 = Mao Xiaodong |image1 = Mao Xiaodong.png |Aliases = Little Dong
Mountain Master Mao
Senior Brother Mao |Vital_status = Alive |Gender = Male |Species = Human |Age = Over 90 |Master(s) = [[Scholarly Sage]] (unofficial) |Allies = [[Qi Jingchun]] (senior brother)
[[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]] (junior brother)
[[Li Er]] |Occupation = Deputy mountain master of Mountain Cliff Academy
Teacher |Current_affiliation(s) = [[Mountain Cliff Academy]] (Great Sui Nation) |Former_affiliation(s) = Mountain Cliff Academy (Great Li Empire) |Continent = [[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]] |Cultivation_rank = Nascent Tier |Novel = Chapter 160 }} '''Mao Xiaodong''' is the true backbone of [[Mountain Cliff Academy]] and a secret, unofficial disciple of the [[Scholarly Sage]]. He stood beside [[Qi Jingchun]] when the academy was founded in the Great Li Empire, led its teachers and students into exile in [[Great Sui Nation]] after Qi Jingchun's death, and became the sage presiding over the new academy on Eastern Splendor Mountain. Stern, upright and fiercely protective of his students, he looks after [[Li Baoping]], [[Li Huai]], [[Lin Shouyi]] and the other children of the small town. He greets [[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]] as his long-awaited junior brother, and personally guides him through the refinement of his golden scholarly core. == Appearance == Mao Xiaodong is a tall, sturdy old man with a bright red nose, which makes him very recognisable. Although over ninety years old when first introduced, he looks only fifty or sixty. He always carries a redwood teacher's ruler at his waist, which he massages when thinking, and which also stores treasures. He has a habit of dozing in the academy's halls and stroking his beard. == Personality == Mao Xiaodong is principled, protective and plain-spoken. He treats everyone equally, regardless of whether he is teaching them or simply talking. He can be sharply sarcastic, especially with Cui Chan. He follows the rules in all he does, which the Scholarly Sage says is the one thing still holding him back from his teacher's level. Of all the Scholarly Sage's disciples, he is the most like his teacher when it comes to teaching and answering questions.Chapter 450 (2) He cares deeply for the academy's people, saying that its heart lies in its students and teachers, not its name. He is wary of Chen Ping'an straying too far towards Legalism and repeatedly reminds him that laws are merely tools of governance. He has one vice he hates himself for: he cannot give up Go. == Background == Mao Xiaodong was by Qi Jingchun's side when Mountain Cliff Academy was founded in the Great Li Empire, and is regarded as the academy's undisputed top figure in cultivation, seniority and morality alike. After Qi Jingchun's death, he played a pivotal role in leading the academy's original teachers and students out of the Great Li Empire to the new academy in Great Sui. He is known as one of the Scholarly Sage's "secret disciples".Chapter 160 == Plot == === The Academy in Great Sui === When Great Sui's officials complain that the children from the small town are poor students, Mao Xiaodong asks them whether Qi Jingchun was a better scholar and judge of students than all of them. He bluntly tells them that it is Great Sui that expects the children to be geniuses who will pledge allegiance to it.Chapter 162 (1) Through a little girl's translation, Cui Chan delivers to him two messages: a parting message from the old scholar, and Qi Jingchun's final words, which Chen Ping'an was originally meant to pass on.Chapter 164 He bickers constantly with Cui Chan, now calling himself Cui Dongshan. He tells him not to wreak havoc on Eastern Splendor Mountain and threatens to call himself Cui Chan's grandson if he so much as glances at him.Chapter 167 (1) When Cui Chan clashes with the cultivator Cai Jingshen, Mao Xiaodong withdraws the academy's protective formations and lets them fight. When [[Li Er]] arrives over his son Li Huai's mistreatment, Cui Dongshan introduces Mao Xiaodong as Qi Jingchun's junior brother and the one who truly calls the shots. Li Er, who had ignored everyone else, greets him warmly as "Li Huai's father", an honour owed to Qi Jingchun's opinion of Mao Xiaodong.Chapter 169 As Li Er fights his way through the imperial palace, Mao Xiaodong walks deliberately slowly through the secret passageway, then tells the emperor that it is time to end the farce. He brings Li Er before the emperor and the court's storyteller, trying hard not to laugh.Chapter 170 (2) Afterwards, he reminds Li Er not to burn bridges while his son studies there, and remarks that Li Er has truly understood life. He tells Cui Dongshan that, whatever Great Sui does, the children who left the Great Li Empire with him are still the academy's students.Chapter 171 (1) He warns that he will personally kill the young imperial preceptor if Great Sui wrongly blames the academy and talks fail. When an unknown Nascent Tier cultivator attempts an assassination inside the academy, he chases the attacker off, his voice thundering across the sky.Chapter 304 (1) As a Nascent Tier mountain master, he wields the power of an Unpolished Jade Tier cultivator within the academy's grounds.Chapter 345 (2) === Senior Brother to Chen Ping'an === When Chen Ping'an arrives at the academy, Mao Xiaodong leads him sternly to his study, then smiles and bows to him, thanking him for protecting the children of the scholarly lineage. He calls him "Junior Brother" and says he has been waiting for him for a very long time.Chapter 402 (1) He has already gathered most of the natural treasures needed to refine Shen Wen's golden scholarly core into a bonded item, and agrees that Chen Ping'an can repay their market value within twenty years.Chapter 402 (3) He takes Chen Ping'an through the capital, to a small restaurant famous for its rice wine, and to the Confucian temple to secure scholarly fortune. He urges Xu Yuanxia to visit one day as an unofficial teacher. When assassins strike during their outing, he tells Chen Ping'an to focus on protecting himself, teases him that he will beat him in their teacher's place if he is still a "worthless Nascent Tier" at Mao Xiaodong's age, and complains that Chen Ping'an still calls him "Mountain Master Mao" rather than "Senior Brother Mao".Chapter 409 Afterwards, he privately warns Chen Ping'an about Cui Dongshan, and when the assistant mountain master who had invited Zhao Shi to lecture resigns in protest and insults him, Mao Xiaodong sets Cui Dongshan on him. On the mountain's summit, presiding over the academy as its sage, he guides Chen Ping'an through the refinement of the golden scholarly core, pouring the scholarly fortune of ceremonial artifacts into the cauldron. When the core transforms into a tiny Confucian scholar that speaks, he asks what it means, and is satisfied by Chen Ping'an's answer.Chapter 414 (2) He then recites poems to guide him and chats with him daily. In a rare moment, he tells Cui Dongshan that while he admits he is inferior to Qi Jingchun, he is not inferior to Cui Chan. == Trivia == * He threatens to call himself Cui Chan's grandson, then his son, if he continues their pointless arguments. * He laments, "Why have scholars become businessmen?" * Conspirators plotting against the academy once rallied each other with cries of "Death to Mao Xiaodong!" * Mao Xiaodong leads an academy excursion to the Great Li Empire to watch Wei Bo's Night Travel Banquet, visiting Forest Deer Academy and meeting Prince Gao Xuan. * Although he is at the Nascent Tier, with the power of the Unpolished Jade Tier within Mountain Cliff Academy. * He can turn the academy into its own small world, observe everything within it, and control part of the river of time there. * He has deep knowledge of refining scholarly cores, learned in part from obscure books. == References == [[Category:Characters]] [[Category:Male]] [[Category:Alive]]

pages.title: Martial Arts
pages.content:
Martial arts, as presented in the sources, is a distinct path of cultivation focused on physical and spiritual development through combat techniques and rigorous training. It differs significantly from Qi refinement, though there are some overlaps, especially in the early stages of training. 

'''Core Principles of Martial Arts'''

* '''Body as a Tool:''' Martial artists view the body not merely as a vessel for Qi, but as a powerful tool to be honed and perfected.
* '''Physical Prowess''': The focus is on developing physical strength, speed, agility, and endurance through specific training regimens.
* '''Qi as Power''': Martial artists cultivate and manipulate their internal energy (True Qi) to enhance their physical abilities and combat techniques.
* '''Meridians and Acupoints''': Martial artists focus on specific points in the body to channel energy through meridians, expanding and smoothing them.
* '''Combat Orientation''': The primary focus is on combat, self-defense, and the ability to defeat opponents in battle.
* '''Step by Step Progress:''' Martial artists progress slowly and steadily through rigorous training, not by relying on luck or fated opportunities.
* '''Inner Strength''': Though often seen as crude, martial artists seek to develop a strong inner self through discipline and endurance.
* '''Self-Reliance''': Unlike Qi refiners, martial artists emphasize self-reliance, refining their souls and bodies by their own power.
* '''Seeking the Extreme''': Some martial artists pursue an extreme path of breaking the old to establish the new, destroying acupoints to forge a new path.
* '''Dao of the Fist''': Some martial artists, particularly those at higher levels, seek to elevate their martial arts to the level of Martial Dao.

'''Tiers of Martial Arts'''

* Martial arts is divided into nine tiers, with some claiming a '''tenth tier''' exists.
** Above the nine tiers, there is a legendary 10th tier where one becomes the peak of the mountain.
* The nine tiers are further grouped into three major tiers: '''Physique Refining, Qi Refining, and Spirit Refining'''.
* '''Physique Refining Tier'''
** Focuses on physical development and is further divided into three tiers:
** '''Clay Embryo Tier''': This initial tier is about laying the foundation, where the body is rough and unrefined. Reaching the peak of this tier results in a strong foundation where one's Qi will descend to the Dantian, and the practitioner becomes immovable.
** '''Wooden Fetus Tier''': This tier focuses on refining the physique, expanding meridians, and improving the pathways for Qi flow. This tier is also called the Mountain Carving Tier because of the hard work that must be invested to open the meridians.
** '''Mercury Tier''': At the peak of the third tier, a martial artist must undergo a tribulation, sometimes referred to as the "clay Bodhisattva crossing the river". The blood in one's body will become like mercury.

'''Qi Refining Tier'''

* Involves more than just bodily refinement, and also includes refining Qi. The tiers within this are focused on the souls, the spirit, and the gall. This tier is associated with the three immortal souls.
* It is believed that those at the sixth tier can begin to nurture their soul.
* Martial artists in the Three Qi Tempering Tiers will be elevated to encompass Qi refinement as well.

'''Spirit Refining Tier'''

* This tier is associated with the later stages of martial arts training.
* The seventh tier is the '''Vajra Body Tier''', where a martial artist attains a body like a Buddhist vajra or a Daoist glazed body. At this point, one is considered a Lesser Grandmaster.
* The eighth tier is the '''Wing Formation Tier''', or the Far Roaming Tier, where martial artists can fly.
* The ninth tier is the '''Mountain Summit Tier''', which is the ultimate endpoint of the path of martial arts. Those at this level are referred to as Ultimate Grandmasters.

'''Training Methods'''

* '''Standing, Walking, and Sleeping Meditations''': These practices strengthen the body and improve the flow of Qi. Sleeping meditation focuses on breath and accumulation within acupoints.
* '''Fist Techniques''': Martial artists practice various fist techniques, and some focus on sword techniques as well.
* '''Sparring''': Sparring is a way for martial artists to test and refine their skills. Sparring can be between master martial artists, or between martial artists and Qi refiners.
* '''Hardship''': Enduring hardship is essential for progress, especially in the Wooden Fetus Tier.
* '''Combat''': The process of breaking through is aided by combat, where martial artists transform the energy within their acupoints.
* '''Tempering the Body''': The body is tempered with medicinal baths and other methods.

'''Examining the Dragon''': One must understand how the spine allows one to generate explosive power and utilize True Qi.

'''Drawing Talismans''': Drawing talismans can be a method to temper one's physique and train the soul.

'''Sword Techniques''': Some martial artists also practice sword techniques, which are often considered more graceful than fist techniques.

'''Finding the Qi''': Martial artists need to find the initial burst of qi within their bodies.

'''Acupoint location''': A martial artist must find the most suitable acupoint for their qi to reside in.

'''Key Concepts'''

* '''True Qi''': This is the internal energy that martial artists cultivate and use.
* '''Martial Dao''': The ultimate goal for martial artists is to achieve the Martial Dao, which is a profound understanding of their art.
* '''Fist Intent''': Martial artists use their fist intent to reach higher levels of understanding and power.
* '''Soul, Spirit, and Gall''': These aspects are developed in the middle tiers and become interconnected at the seventh tier.
* '''Heroic Spirit''': Militarian cultivators can nurture a heroic spirit that doesn't disperse after death.
* '''Mental State''': The mental state of a martial artist is important, particularly when advancing to the fourth tier.

'''Militarian Path:''' This path is considered a shortcut, and it is dangerous because martial artists may fall into demonic ways.

'''Cumulative Training''': Training is a cumulative process, and it subtly tempers one's mind and heart.

'''No Second in Fist Techniques''': This saying relates to the idea that martial artists do not rely on external items, and so the winner is easy to guess.

'''Challenges and Limitations'''

* '''Limited Lifespan:''' Compared to Qi refiners, martial artists have a shorter lifespan.
* '''Slower Progress''': Martial arts training is seen as more step-by-step and dull compared to the fated opportunities that often drive Qi refinement.
* '''Physical Limitations''': The focus on the physical body is sometimes seen as a limitation, making it difficult to reach the same heights as Qi refiners.
* '''Difficult Breakthroughs''': Advancing between tiers is difficult, especially from the third to the fourth tier, which is likened to a "clay deity crossing the river".
* '''Risk of Injury''': Martial arts training can be damaging to the body if not done correctly.
* '''Demonic Ways:''' There is always the risk of a martial artist falling to demonic ways.
* '''External Interference''':  Martial artists who rely too much on their physical power and disregard their souls and minds may become unstable.

'''Limited Scope''': Some believe that martial arts is unrelated to the concept of Dao.

'''Hardships''': The path of a martial artist involves a great deal of hardship, and there are no shortcuts.

'''End Tier:''' There are very few people who reach the 10th tier of martial arts.

'''Competition''': There is competition between martial artists of the same tier, and those at lower levels will have difficulty competing with those at higher tiers.

'''Differences from Qi Refinement'''

* '''Focus''': Martial arts emphasizes the body, while Qi refinement focuses on the spirit.
* '''Progression''': Martial artists progress through hard work, while Qi refiners depend on fated opportunities and the bestowal of the heavens.
* '''External Items''': Qi refiners use external items to aid in their cultivation, while martial artists tend to eschew such items.

'''Qi''': Martial artists and Qi refiners take different routes when it comes to Qi refinement.

'''Body as Vessel vs. Tool''': Qi refiners treat the body as a vessel, whereas martial artists view the body as a tool.

'''Lower Tiers:'''  Qi refiners in the lower tiers focus on refining their body, which is similar to martial arts training.

'''Unique Aspects'''

* '''Swordsmanship''': Some martial artists use swords, and swordsmanship is considered a graceful fighting style.
* '''Militarian Cultivators''':  These martial artists use combat experience to enhance their cultivation.

'''Heroic Spirit''':  Some martial artists can cultivate a heroic spirit.

'''Feng Shui''':  Practicing martial arts is likened to a feng shui master searching for acupoints.

'''Deity Drumming Technique:''' Intense training sessions can be a way to temper one's mind and heart.

Martial arts is a demanding path of self-improvement, emphasizing physical prowess, rigorous training, and the cultivation of inner strength through combat. Although it is seen as limited in some ways compared to Qi refinement, the sources present martial arts as a respectable and powerful path in its own right, especially for those who value self-reliance and a step-by-step approach to progress.

pages.title: Mi Yu
pages.content:
{{Character |header1=Mi Yu |Vital_status=Alive |Gender=Male |Species=Human |Relatives=Mi Hu (older brother) |Occupation=Sword cultivator
Member of the Hidden Official’s branch |Current_affiliation(s)=[[Sword Qi Great Wall]] |Cultivation_rank=Unpolished Jade Tier |Novel=Chapter 607 }} == Appearance == Mi Yu is a sword immortal popular with women both on and off the Sword Qi Great Wall, having gotten into numerous romantic entanglements over the years despite, or perhaps because of, his pretentious reputation.Chapter 607 == Personality == He comes across as pretentious and mediocre to most of the sword immortals around him, and he is widely looked down upon despite his genuine cultivation base, becoming something of a running joke on the Sword Qi Great Wall for being sincere in a way that nobody credits him for.Chapter 623 Underneath the mockery, he is more thoughtful and conscientious than he is given credit for, willing to risk his own safety to save someone else even when badly outmatched, and quick to call out hypocrisy or cruelty even when it makes him uncomfortable to do so.Chapter 630 He has a habit of taking things for granted when life goes smoothly for him, something that has cost him at least one genuine relationship in the past.Chapter 627 == Background == Mi Yu only managed to reach the Unpolished Jade Tier after burning through an enormous amount of immortal coins, resources made available largely thanks to the sacrifices of his far more talented older brother, Mi Hu, who could otherwise have already reached the Immortal Tier himself. Because of this, Mi Yu is widely regarded on the Sword Qi Great Wall as pretentious and undeserving of his own status, a reputation that has nothing to do with his actual swordsmanship or cultivation base. He was counted among the Sword Qi Great Wall’s handful of unique personalities for this very reason, specifically for failing to be recognized for his sincerity no matter what he did.Chapter 607Chapter 623 When Zuo You caught him mocking the Scholarly Sage’s lineage in front of Cui Dongshan and his companions, Mi Yu was left too frightened to even move, his sword formation torn apart with a single strike and his composure shattered in front of onlookers.Chapter 607 When the Hidden Official’s branch was reorganized to include outsider swordsmen during the war against the Savage World, Mi Yu found himself the only Upper Five Tiers cultivator among a group of far weaker but sharper-minded strategists, led by Chen Ping’an after he was unexpectedly named the new Hidden Official. Mi Yu was initially given the task of liaising with the Sword Qi Great Wall’s own native swordsmen rather than the more prestigious Upper Five Tiers sword immortals, a decision that stung his pride until Chen Ping’an gently explained that the established hierarchy among sword immortals would only work against him in that role.Chapter 626Chapter 627 Mi Yu often accompanied Chen Ping’an personally as a bodyguard of sorts during this period, and when the sword immortal Lie Ji suddenly launched a surprise attack meant to assassinate Chen Ping’an, Mi Yu immediately intervened, knocking Lie Ji’s flying sword just enough off course to spare Chen Ping’an a direct hit to the heart before drawing his own blade against Lie Ji. Despite his efforts, Lie Ji’s attack still appeared to kill Chen Ping’an outright, with Lie Ji sacrificing his own yin soul to guarantee the kill, leaving Mi Yu to be detained under suspicion of complicity in the plot.Chapter 630 He was ultimately spared full punishment and kept close by the sword immortal Chou Miao, only for Chen Ping’an to reappear very much alive shortly after, revealing that the entire incident had been engineered to draw out a traitor. Mi Yu was furious and deeply unsettled to learn how coldly calculated the scheme had been, openly confronting Chen Ping’an about whether he ever felt guilty manipulating even those closest to him, including his own disciple, Guo Zhujiu.Chapter 630 == Trivia == * His bonded flying sword is named Radiant Sunset, and his high-caliber longsword was a gift from his brother, Mi Hu.Chapter 630 * He drinks regularly with fellow underappreciated sword immortal Lie Ji to commiserate about their shared lack of respect on the Sword Qi Great Wall, which made Lie Ji’s betrayal all the more shocking to him.Chapter 630 * A female Nascent Tier cultivator from the Middle Earth Divine Continent became so infatuated with him that she took on the thankless job of administering an intercontinental ship just to stay near him, only to be left heartbroken and vengeful when nothing came of it.Chapter 630 == References ==

pages.title: Middle Earth Divine Continent
pages.content:
'''Middle Earth Divine Continent''' is the largest of the nine continents of the [[Majestic World]]. It sits at the centre of the world and is home to the Confucian temple, [[Sects#Mount Longhu|Mount Longhu]] and [[Sects#White Emperor City|White Emperor City]]. Cultivators from the other eight continents often regard it as the place where the strongest figures and the oldest powers are found.

== Geography ==
Middle Earth is so vast that only the other eight continents put together can match its size.Chapter 565 It has the richest resources of any continent, and is described as being worth eight continents on its own.Chapter 558 Several major empires stand on its land, and the [[Great Li Empire]] would need to swallow half of the [[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]] before it could compare with any of them. The ruins of a great nation that was once one of the nine major empires of the world also lie there.Chapter 258

A sea separates Middle Earth from Eastern Treasured Vial. Tassel Mountain stands near the eastern coast, and a deity in golden armour sits upon it.Chapter 208 This deity is one of the gods of the continent's Five Mountains and is said to have the worst temper on the whole continent.Chapter 351

The continent's most famous waterway is a great river, and White Emperor City is built on its banks.Chapter 455 Mirage Lake is another well known body of water. It is governed by a lake lord of the Upper Five Tiers whose water residence is called Mianchi Palace.Chapter 552

== History ==
After the ancient war that ended the age of deities, the Majestic World built the Confucian temple in Middle Earth and raised nine Mighty Suppressing Pagodas that tower between heaven and earth.Chapter 588 Since then the temple has been the seat of Confucian authority across all nine continents. Its seventy two sages are honoured there, and the [[Scholarly Sage]] was once given the fourth seat among them.Chapter 346 The Confucian school on Middle Earth also holds the power to approve the ranks of mountain and water deities.Chapter 374

Many figures who shaped events elsewhere began their lives here. [[Qi Jingchun]] left Middle Earth to found [[Mountain Cliff Academy]] in Great Li.Chapter 402 [[Zuo You]] is also from Middle Earth, and he is remembered there for crippling many young sword prodigies of the continent.Chapter 591

== Cultivation world ==
Middle Earth has more academies than any other continent and is home to many large Daoist and Confucian powers.Chapter 209 [[Sects#Mount Longhu|Mount Longhu]] is home to the Heavenly Master Residence of the Zhang Clan, whose Daoist line stands apart from the branches of the Heavenly World. White Emperor City is ruled by a city lord who is both a feared demonic cultivator and a Go master so strong that no tenth dan is ever awarded in his lifetime.Chapter 229

The list of the top ten cultivators of each continent is compiled by Middle Earth, and its own list is treated as the most prestigious.Chapter 270 The [[Northern Complete Reed Continent]] calls itself the strongest continent outside Middle Earth, which shows how far above the others Middle Earth is held to be.Chapter 525 In martial arts, [[Cao Ci]] is regarded as peerless among the young martial artists of the continent. The Shaoyuan Empire is known for its many sword cultivators, much like the Luminous Vermilion Empire of Eastern Treasured Vial.

== Trivia ==

* Cultivators from Middle Earth speak an official dialect of their own, and many look down on cultivators from smaller continents such as Eastern Treasured Vial.Chapter 571
* [[Chen Ping An]] asked [[Spiritual Master Fire Dragon]] to sell most of his colored glaze roof tiles to the Colored Glaze Pagoda of White Emperor City.
* [[Cui Dongshan]] says that it is remarkable if even one or two people from the other eight continents can squeeze into Middle Earth's top ranks.

== References ==

pages.title: Militarians
pages.content:
The Militarians are a distinct group of cultivators in Eastern Treasured Vial Continent, known for their unique approach to cultivation and their significant role in the empires and the wider cultivation world. They are distinct from Confucianists, Daoists, and Buddhists, though they can also be cultivators, Qi refiners, martial artists, and swordsmen.

'''Key Characteristics of Militarians:'''

* '''Emphasis on Physical and Spiritual Strength:''' Militarians cultivate both their physical bodies and their spiritual power, making them formidable in battle. They value strength, discipline, and a pragmatic approach to conflict.
* '''Close Ties to Empires:''' Militarians often serve in the armies and governments of the empires, acting as generals, bodyguards, and military officers. They are seen as essential to maintaining order and defending the empires from internal and external threats.
* '''Pragmatic and Adaptive:''' Militarian rules and practices are described as "broad but hollow" [6], allowing for flexibility and adaptability in different situations. This pragmatism sets them apart from other groups like the Confucianists, who are more bound by tradition and strict rules.
* '''Tolerance of Karmic Consequences:''' Unlike some other cultivation paths, Militarians are less concerned with the karmic repercussions of their actions, particularly when it comes to killing. This willingness to act decisively, even if it means incurring karmic debt, contributes to their reputation as ruthless and effective warriors.

'''Cultivation Methods and Techniques:'''

* '''Seeking Fortune and Avoiding Calamity:''' Militarians have an almost instinctive ability to predict the near future and sense danger, allowing them to seek out opportunities and avoid potential threats. This ability is seen as a key advantage in battle and in navigating the dangers of the cultivation world.
* '''Nurturing Heroic Spirits:''' A powerful, though controversial technique, Militarians can cultivate a heroic spirit within their bodies, merging their own soul with the powerful yin soul of a deceased warrior. This fusion grants them immense strength and combat prowess.

'''Notable Militarians and Institutions:'''

* '''True Martial Mountain:''' A sacred land for Militarians in Eastern Treasured Vial Continent. It is a training ground for aspiring Militarians and a source of knowledge and power for those who follow this path. Disciples of True Martial Mountain are known for their independent nature and their adherence to a loose set of rules.
* '''Song Changjing:''' An influential military leader in the Great Li Empire, responsible for enforcing a rule that restricts Qi refiners from participating in battles. This rule highlights the complex relationship between Militarians and other cultivators within the empire.
* '''Ruan Qiong:''' A high-ranking Militarian who plays a pivotal role in establishing order and governance in the town. His actions demonstrate the pragmatic and adaptive nature of Militarian leadership, as he sets rules and negotiates with various factions to maintain stability.
* '''The Militarian Swordsman:''' A character who serves as a mentor to Ma Kuxuan, a young aspiring Militarian. He embodies the values of strength, discipline, and pragmatic action that characterize this path.

'''Strengths and Weaknesses of the Militarian Path:'''

'''Strengths:'''

* '''Unmatched Combat Prowess:''' Their focus on both physical and spiritual cultivation makes them incredibly powerful warriors, capable of facing down even the most formidable opponents.
* '''Decisiveness and Ruthlessness:''' Their willingness to act without hesitation and their tolerance of karmic consequences make them effective in achieving their goals, even if it means resorting to violence.
* '''Strategic Acumen:''' Their ability to predict the future and assess situations allows them to make strategic decisions that give them an advantage in conflicts.

'''Weaknesses:'''

* '''Potential for Corruption:''' The emphasis on power and the tolerance of killing can lead some Militarians down a dark path, turning them into ruthless tyrants or bloodthirsty warmongers.
* '''Lack of Moral Restraint:''' Their disregard for karmic repercussions can have negative consequences in the long run, as their actions may generate karmic debt that will eventually need to be repaid.
* '''Overreliance on Strength:''' Their focus on physical and martial might can sometimes blind them to more subtle approaches to resolving conflicts. This can make them less effective in situations that require diplomacy or compromise.

'''The Militarians play a complex and multifaceted role in the world of Eastern Treasured Vial Continent.''' They are both protectors and potential threats, wielding their power to maintain order and defend the empires, but also capable of great violence and destruction if they succumb to their darker impulses. Their pragmatism and adaptability make them valuable assets in a world fraught with danger and uncertainty, but their disregard for karmic consequences and their potential for corruption make them a force to be reckoned with.

pages.title: Mirage City
pages.content:
Mirage City is a complex and multifaceted location with significant political, cultural, and mystical importance. It is a place where the fate of the Great Quan Empire is decided, and where various powerful figures and factions compete for influence. The city is a hub of activity, with a unique blend of tradition and modernity, where both mundane and mystical elements intersect. The city is a place of beauty and grandeur but is also a location where conflicts and tensions are always lurking beneath the surface.

'''General Characteristics:'''

* Mirage City is the '''capital city''' of the Great Quan Empire.
* It is a '''major political and cultural hub''', drawing in various influential people and factions.
* The city is known for its '''complex social dynamics''' with a mix of powerful officials, wealthy clans, scholars, and cultivators.
* It is described as a '''prosperous city''', with a high level of activity and a wide range of people from different backgrounds.
* The city has a '''scholarly temple and city god pavilion'''.
* The city is so large that people who live there their entire lives may not have seen all of it.
* It is a place where the local inhabitants look down on people from other places, making it difficult for newcomers.

'''Political and Imperial Significance:'''

* Mirage City is the seat of the '''Great Quan Empire's imperial court''', making it a center of political power.
* The city is home to the '''emperor''' and various '''high-ranking officials''', including powerful ministers and generals.
* The city is a place where the '''emperor's authority''' is centralized, and decisions that impact the entire empire are made.
* There are a lot of officials and nobles in the city who are competing for power.
* The city is home to the '''Green Roving Residence''', which is being promoted to a palace, a move that reflects the influence of a noble scholar.

'''Key Figures and Factions:'''

* '''Duke Gao Shizhen''' is a significant figure in the city, described as shrewd and selfless, with a close relationship with the emperor. He has a son, Gao Shuyi, who is known for acting wantonly.
* '''The Yao Clan''' is an influential military clan that has a strong presence in the city. They have connections with the imperial court, and their arrival in the city is met with great fanfare. Yao Zhen is a prominent member of this clan.
* '''The Xu Clan''' is a powerful military clan that has been established in Mirage City for generations.
* '''A noble scholar''' is residing in Mirage City, who is a key reason for the Great Quan Empire's prosperity.
* There are also '''numerous other powerful officials, nobles, and cultivators''' that reside in or frequent the city.
* There are also powerful figures such as '''Du Hanling''', the Temple Master of the Golden Summit Daoist Temple, who are influential in the city.

'''Social and Cultural Aspects:'''

* The city is known for its '''gardens and scenic spots''', some of which are described as unmatched in beauty.
* There are unique cultural practices, such as the construction of '''clay statues of gods''', with different styles associated with various clans.
* There is a '''strong emphasis on scholarly pursuits''', with a scholarly temple and influential scholars.
* The city is a place where '''various people from different backgrounds come together''', creating a diverse cultural environment.
* There are many '''wealthy people''' in the city, but also many depraved gamblers.
* The city has its own unique traditions and customs that newcomers must become accustomed to.

'''Conflicts and Tensions:'''

* There is a sense of '''political intrigue and power struggles''' among the various factions in the city.
* There are those who seek to '''undermine the authority of the emperor and the imperial court''', creating a tense atmosphere.
* There are various '''conflicts and battles''' taking place in and around the city, with powerful individuals and factions vying for control.
* The city is a place where '''those with ill intentions may visit''', while those with good intentions might avoid.
* There is an awareness that the peace and prosperity of the city might be threatened.

'''Mystical and Spiritual Elements:'''

* The '''mountain god''' has a shrine nearby the city where people can go to enjoy the view.
* There is a '''noble scholar''' living in the city who appears to be connected to the rise of the Great Quan Empire.
* It is suggested that some places in the city, like the Green Roving Residence and the Burial River God Temple, have '''spiritual significance'''.
* It is a place where '''geomancy''' is considered important, and that the placement of some places in the city may have significance.

'''Connections to the Wider World:'''

* Mirage City is '''connected to other regions and powers''' through trade and diplomacy.
* The city has an immortal ferry station that allows travel to other regions.
* There are individuals from other regions who come to the city for various reasons, including those seeking fated opportunities, making it a place of diverse interactions.

pages.title: Mountain Cliff Academy
pages.content:
Mountain Cliff Academy is a prominent educational institution in the sources, with a rich history, complex internal dynamics, and a significant role in the political landscape.

'''Historical Background and Founding:'''

* '''Founder:''' Mountain Cliff Academy was founded by '''Qi Jingchun'''. He was a dedicated scholar who, despite coming from a poor background, overcame many hardships to gain admittance into the academy.
* '''Original Location:''' The academy was originally established in the northern wilderness of the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent, within the Great Li Empire. It was founded in an effort to educate the general public and elevate the Great Li Empire from its former status as a settlement of northern savages.
* '''Move to Great Sui Nation:''' Due to political turmoil and the death of Qi Jingchun's teacher, Mountain Cliff Academy was moved to Great Sui Nation. It was constructed on the most scenic mountain in Great Sui Nation’s capital city, Eastern Splendor Mountain.
* '''Significance:''' The academy is considered one of the 72 academies of Confucianism, and was once the equivalent of the imperial academy of the Great Li Empire.

'''Curriculum and Teaching:'''

* '''Confucian Teachings:''' The academy focuses on Confucian principles and the way of managing a nation. It emphasizes the importance of knowledge as a vessel for carrying the Dao.
* '''Emphasis on Books:''' The academy has a vast book collection that is considered the best on the continent. Students are encouraged to read extensively.
* '''Open to All:''' Qi Jingchun offered lessons to everyone in the continent while residing in the Great Li Empire.
* '''Rule of No Food''': Accommodation is provided, but not food, so students from impoverished backgrounds would earn money by copying scriptures. This rule is more lenient at the new academy in Great Sui Nation.
* '''High Standards''': Mountain Cliff Academy has produced many high-ranking officials. It is a very selective school, and many powerful clans try to send their most promising young members to study there.

'''Key Figures and Internal Dynamics:'''

* '''[[Qi Jingchun]]:''' The founder and first mountain master of the academy. He was a revered figure, and his teachings and ideals are still influential even after his death.
* '''[[Mao Xiaodong]]:''' A former junior brother of Qi Jingchun and the deputy mountain master of the new academy in Great Sui Nation. He effectively oversees the educational affairs of the academy.
* '''Mountain Master of Great Sui Nation''': The head minister of Great Sui Nation’s ministry of rites is the mountain master in name only.
* '''Teachers''': The academy employs many reputable and knowledgeable teachers.
* '''Students''':
** '''[[Li Baoping]]:''' A spirited young girl who deeply admires Qi Jingchun and is eager to study at the academy. She is confident and outspoken
** '''Li Huai:''' A student who traveled from the Great Li Empire and has a strong sense of loyalty and determination.
** '''[[Lin Shouyi]]:''' A diligent student who is also a cultivating prodigy. He is often seen reading in the scripture library.
** '''[[Yu Lu]]''': A student who came from the fallen Lu Empire, and traveled with Cui Chan to the academy.
** '''[[Xie Xie]]''': A student who came from the fallen Lu Empire, and traveled with Cui Chan to the academy. She is also a prodigious cultivator.
** '''[[Cui Dongshan]]:''' Though not officially a student, he is considered Chen Ping'an's "pupil" and has a strong presence in the academy. He is also known as the Myriad Treasure Immortal and Cai Clan's Ancestor. He is handsome and cheerful, making him a popular figure at the academy.
** '''[[Gao Zhen|Gao Xuan]]:''' A member of the imperial family of Great Sui Nation, who has been officially enrolled in the academy.
* '''Factions:''' Like the imperial court, there are factions within the academy. Students from the Great Li Empire are often given preferential treatment, creating some discontent among local students of Great Sui Nation. There is also conflict between those students who traveled from Great Li Empire and those who had already been studying at the academy.
* '''Disciples of Qi Jingchun''': The academy places a great deal of importance on Qi Jingchun's direct disciples.

'''Political and Strategic Significance:'''

* '''Relationship with Great Li Empire:''' The academy’s move to Great Sui Nation reflects the ongoing conflict between the two empires.
* '''Great Sui Nation's Hopes:''' The Great Sui Nation has high expectations for the new academy and hopes that it will bring about a new generation of scholars.
* '''Puppet Academy:''' The Great Li Empire is attempting to create a new academy on Cloud Drape Mountain to take the place of the Mountain Cliff Academy. The new academy will be overseen by a puppet of the Great Li Empire.
* '''Potential for Conflict:''' The academy is a potential source of conflict between the Great Sui Nation and the Great Li Empire, with both sides vying for influence. The academy is being carefully watched by the imperial court of Great Sui Nation.
* '''Neutral Stance''': The academy attempts to remain neutral in the conflict between the Great Sui Nation and the Great Li Empire.
* '''Preservation of Heritage:''' Even though the Mountain Cliff Academy has been stripped of its status as one of the 72 academies, it is seen as important to preserve its heritage..
* '''Impact on Great Li Empire:''' The loss of the Mountain Cliff Academy is seen as a severe blow to the official hierarchy of the Great Li Empire.

'''Challenges and Changes:'''

* '''Loss of Status:''' Mountain Cliff Academy was stripped of its status as one of the 72 Confucian academies.
* '''Internal Conflict:''' There are some tensions and conflicts within the academy, particularly between students from different backgrounds.
* '''Instability:''' The academy has experienced some turmoil since its move to Great Sui Nation, including an assassination attempt.
* '''Adaptation:''' The academy is working to adapt to its new environment in Great Sui Nation and trying to maintain its identity while also dealing with the political changes.

Mountain Cliff Academy is more than just a school; it is a symbol of knowledge, tradition, and resilience. It is deeply embedded in the political and social fabric of the world, and its story reflects the complex interplay of power, ambition, and the pursuit of wisdom. It serves as a microcosm of the larger conflicts and changes occurring in the world of the sources.

pages.title: Mountain-Moving Ape
pages.content:
{{Character |header1=Bai Yuan |image1=Bai Yuan.png |Aliases=Mountain-Moving Ape
Grandpa Yuan
Senior Yuan |Vital_status=Alive |Gender=Male |Species=Great demon (white ape) |Allies=[[Tao Zi]] |Enemie(s)=[[Wind Lightning Field]] |Occupation=Guardian of Sun Scorch Mountain
Guest elder of Peace and Tranquility Mountain (formerly) |Former_affiliation(s)=Peace and Tranquility Mountain |Current_affiliation(s)=[[Sun Scorch Mountain]] |Continent=[[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]] |Cultivation_rank=Immortal Tier |Novel=Chapter 45 }} '''Bai Yuan''', known throughout Eastern Treasured Vial Continent as the '''Mountain-Moving Ape''', is a great demon of [[Sun Scorch Mountain]] and the devoted guardian of [[Tao Zi]], the granddaughter of the sect's Pure Yang Sword Patriarch. He spent over three thousand years as a guest elder of Peace and Tranquility Mountain on Parasol Leaf Continent, guarding its well prison, before betraying the sect during a great calamity. He is one of the most powerful beings Chen Ping'an encounters in the small town of [[Jewel Small World]]. == Appearance == Bai Yuan is a white ape as tall as a grown man. He chooses to maintain his original ape form rather than taking on human appearance, and is almost always seen in black robes with a sword carried across his back. Despite his size he moves with startling speed, capable of changing direction mid-leap and clearing rooftops in a few strides. His true form is an ape 3,000 meters tall, said to be capable of uprooting a mountain and carrying it on its back, though whether this has ever actually been witnessed is disputed.Chapter 45 == Personality == Bai Yuan is blunt, proud and quick to anger. He makes no effort to conceal his contempt for those he considers beneath him and will insult powerful figures to their faces without hesitation. He provoked Qi Jingchun at length, calling out his master's disgraced legacy and daring him to retaliate, and was visibly unsatisfied when Qi Jingchun declined to rise to the bait.Chapter 63 (1) He is also capable of loyalty and real devotion. His bond with Tao Zi is genuine as he kneels before her in shame when he fails her, speaks to her gently, and explains things he technically should not be telling her because he feels she deserves to know.Chapter 45 Tao Zi calls him "Grandpa Yuan" and trusts him completely. Despite his ferocity, he has enough self-control to walk away from a fight when the stakes demand it. He knew Light Breeze City was using him to kill Liu Xianyang and understood the trap, yet went in anyway because Sun Scorch Mountain's interests required it — and then accepted the consequences.Chapter 45 == Background == Bai Yuan is the guardian of Sun Scorch Mountain and deeply invested in its centuries-old war with Wind Lightning Field. The root of that war is a female ancestor of Sun Scorch Mountain who challenged the master of Wind Lightning Field, died fairly in battle, and was never returned to the sect. Her body still lies on Wind Lightning Field's sword sparring arena with a sword driven through her skull, a humiliation that has shaped Sun Scorch Mountain for 300 years. Every sword immortal the sect has produced since has felt that weight.Chapter 45 He served Peace and Tranquility Mountain on Parasol Leaf Continent for more than 3,000 years as a guest elder and warden of its well prison. In recognition of his unparalleled service, the sect leader of that era awarded him one of the sect's four ancient swords — a rare honor over which many objected.Chapter 350 (2) He was in seclusion attempting to break from the Unpolished Jade Tier to the Immortal Tier when a calamity struck Peace and Tranquility Mountain. He exited seclusion early, having already broken through, and turned against the sect.Chapter 350 (1) == Plot == === The Small Town === Bai Yuan arrived in [[Jewel Small World]] accompanying Tao Zi, sent to retrieve a sword scripture that the traitor who defected to Wind Lightning Field had originally stolen from Sun Scorch Mountain. Light Breeze City had manipulated events to engineer a confrontation between Bai Yuan and Liu Xianyang, knowing Bai Yuan would be the one to bear the consequences. Bai Yuan understood the trap and jumped in regardless, striking Liu Xianyang down and nearly killing him.Chapter 45 Chen Ping'an, who had watched Liu Xianyang grow up with him, resolved to respond. He climbed to a rooftop above Clay Vase Alley and shot an arrow at Bai Yuan's eye from point-blank range. The arrow pierced Bai Yuan's palm when he raised it to block, drawing blood and leaving the old ape shaken despite the trivial nature of the wound. A long rooftop chase followed, with Chen Ping'an luring Bai Yuan onto a derelict house whose roof collapsed under the ape's weight.Chapter 48 Bai Yuan eventually unleashed his true form (a 3,000-meter ape) in an attempt to carry a mountain out of the small world. Qi Jingchun intervened. With a single stomp, he drove Bai Yuan into the earth. A second stomp sent him deeper. Bai Yuan surrendered and left, though not before raising a thumb toward Qi Jingchun's back as he walked away. === Peace and Tranquility Mountain === During the calamity that struck Peace and Tranquility Mountain, Bai Yuan emerged from seclusion having already attained the Immortal Tier. He used the ancient sword the sect had awarded him to bring the mountain-protection formation to a temporary halt, then used it to kill Zhong Kui, a noble scholar of Great Subduing Academy at the Nascent Tier, who had come to defend the mountain. Bai Yuan cut him in two at the waist and noted, without apparent emotion, that it was "a heroic and righteous death."Chapter 350 (1) == Trivia == * Tao Zi had hoped Bai Yuan would be able to carry a mountain out of [[Jewel Small World]] as a gift to her as he had apparently done this before, bringing a mountain all the way to Sun Scorch Mountain as a private estate for her.Chapter 48 * Liu Baqiao of Wind Lightning Field said he was not afraid of "an old monkey" from Sun Scorch Mountain, but those who witnessed Bai Yuan knew better.Chapter 45 * Ning Yao, who clashed with Bai Yuan outside the town, described him as the most powerful of the outsiders who had entered the small world at that time, this was more dangerous to her than even the eunuch from Great Sui who had injured her on arrival.Chapter 46 * He was not originally from Peace and Tranquility Mountain, and many within the sect resented the ancient sword being given to an outsider demon.Chapter 350 (2) == References == [[Category:Characters]] [[Category:Male]] [[Category:Alive]]

pages.title: Mountains near the Small Town
pages.content:
{{Spoilers}}
The '''mountains near the Small Town''' are the peaks of the former [[Jewel Small World]], which became Dragon Spring County and later Dragon Spring Prefecture after the small world fell to the ground. After the fall, the [[Great Li Empire]] put 61 of them, apart from Cloud Drape Mountain, up for sale.Chapter 75 The smallest cost a single gold essence copper coin, and the largest, such as Divine Elegance Mountain and Incense Mountain, cost 25 to 30 coins each.Chapter 76 [[Chen Ping An]] bought five of them, the beginning of [[Downtrodden Mountain]]. 

=== Dragon Head Mountain ===
Dragon Head Mountain is hidden by a formation that keeps mortal eyes from seeing it. From the small town, it can only be seen from the summit of Cloud Drape Mountain, and reaching it is counted as a fated opportunity.Chapter 66

=== Cloud Drape Mountain ===
Cloud Drape Mountain is the tallest mountain in the region. A Heavenly Master Seal is said to have been buried under it long ago to suppress the dragon qi of the small world.Chapter 54 Cui Minghuang chose it as the site of a new academy, later named Forest Deer Academy, which was meant to become one of the 72 Confucian academies within fifty years.Chapter 82

When the small world fell, the emperor wanted to break the rules and raise Cloud Drape Mountain to the Northern Mountain of the empire.Chapter 117 The court first appointed formal mountain gods to Cloud Drape Mountain, Incense Mountain and Downtrodden Mountain.Chapter 118 In the end, Wei Bo, once the mountain lord of Go Table Mountain, became the formal god of the Great Li Empire's Northern Mountain.Chapter 190

=== True Jewel Mountain ===
True Jewel Mountain is the smallest mountain the Great Li Empire offered, little more than a hill, and its price was a single Greeting Spring Coin. It was the first mountain Old Man Yao took Chen Ping'an to when they went into the mountains to search for soil. Chen Ping'an bought it and planned to keep it for himself for 300 years.Chapter 84

=== Divine Elegance Mountain, Lamp Bearer Mountain and Gallant Spear Mountain ===
[[Ruan Qiong]] asked the Great Li Empire for these three mountains as the site of his future sect.Chapter 77 Lamp Bearer Mountain and Gallant Spear Mountain lie about ten kilometers west and north of Divine Elegance Mountain, and the three stand in a triangle like three giants.Chapter 78 Bonus artifacts were attached to Divine Elegance Mountain, and Lamp Bearer Mountain was given a mountain god. Divine Elegance Mountain became the home of the Dragon Spring Sword Sect's ancestral hall.Chapter 569

=== Treasured Scripture Mountain, Rainbow Cloud Mountain and Immortal Herb Mountain ===
These three mountains lie within fifty kilometers of Ruan Qiong's mountains. Chen Ping'an bought them along with True Jewel Mountain and Downtrodden Mountain. Immortal Herb Mountain is barely larger than True Jewel Mountain, but it is lush and full of tall trees. Ruan Qiong said he would have chosen Treasured Scripture Mountain over Gallant Spear Mountain if not for the needs of his sect's protective formation. Before leaving the town, Chen Ping'an planned to leave Downtrodden Mountain, Treasured Scripture Mountain, Rainbow Cloud Mountain and Immortal Herb Mountain to Liu Xianyang, Gu Can, Ning Yao and Ruan Xiu if he never returned. He later lent the three mountains to Ruan Qiong's sect for 300 years.

=== Lamp Flame Mountain and Yellow Lake Mountain ===
Lamp Flame Mountain and Yellow Lake Mountain are two of the five mountains near Ruan Qiong's peaks. Yellow Lake Mountain has a small lake partway up its slope. It later became the newest subsidiary mountain of Downtrodden Mountain, where the old Daoist priest Jia spends most of the year.Chapter 642

=== Downtrodden Mountain ===
{{Main|Downtrodden Mountain}}Downtrodden Mountain is the mountain Chen Ping'an bought almost by accident. It grew into the seat of his own mountain force.

=== Incense Mountain ===
Incense Mountain is one of the largest mountains offered by the Great Li Empire. Old Man Yang said that apart from Cloud Drape Mountain and Incense Mountain, Downtrodden Mountain was the most interesting of them all. Incense Mountain was given one of the empire's three new formal mountain gods.

=== Dragonspine Mountain ===
A large piece of natural Dragon Slaying Platform appeared halfway up Dragonspine Mountain, which is the real reason the surrounding mountains were sealed off. The Great Li Empire granted the Dragon Slaying Platform to Wind Snow Temple and True Martial Mountain to share. Ruan Qiong warned that not even an Upper Five Tier cultivator would dare to claim the mountain without powerful backers.

=== Go Table Mountain ===
Go Table Mountain lies on the smallest of the three official roads running north from the Great Li Empire's southern border. The road was once used for porcelain, tea and salt, and its stretch across the mountain runs more than 150 kilometers through four prefectures, including Eternal Splendor Prefecture and White Cloud Prefecture. Its summit is a wide, flat plateau that looks like a grain-sunning ground, as if an immortal had sheared off the peak with a sword. Red Candle Town lies to its south.Chapter 97

Its ruler was Wei Bo. The last emperor of the Divine Water Nation had named him a mountain god in charge of thousands of kilometers of land around the mountain.Chapter 102 The Great Li Empire demoted him to a mountain lord for secretly protecting refugees fleeing the Divine Water Nation's wars, but the people of Red Candle Town still praise him for it.Chapter 105 Two pythons, one black and one white, grew strong on the mountain under his watch. With no official title, he needed them to keep the mountain's spiritual energy from being taken by others.Chapter 101

Chen Ping'an crossed the mountain with A'Liang and the children on his way to the [[Great Sui Nation]]. A'Liang's sword strike there broke the restrictions on Wei Bo. The white python was killed, and the black python later moved to Downtrodden Mountain.Chapter 188 A hidden patch of bamboo on the mountain grew very slowly for centuries under generations of mountain lords. It was later revealed to be descended from courage bamboo, one of the ten celestial bamboos of the Bamboo Sea Small World.Chapter 461 Chen Ping'an made the frame of [[Lin Shouyi]]'s bookcase from this bamboo. Wei Bo also found a golden lotus seed on the mountain while fleeing the fall of the Divine Water Nation.

=== Parasol Tree Mountain ===
The peaks of the whole Parasol Tree Mountain range have been sliced flat. A ferry station for ships that sail across the sea of clouds stands there, west of the town, and it is where Chen Ping'an boarded Ceremony Mountain's Kun ship.Chapter 205

=== Ox Horn Mountain ===
Ox Horn Mountain is a low, gentle mountain owned by a cultivator from [[Southern Stream Nation]], with buildings winding from its foot to its peak. It is home to the Cloth Wrapper Shop, and with Divine Elegance Mountain it was one of the two most important mountains in the region.Chapter 199 Chen Ping'an later bought it after the Cloth Wrapper Shop left.

=== Other mountains ===
* '''Cool Wind Mountain''' has the busiest mountain god temple in the western mountains because it lies close to the prefectural city. Dong Shuijing's wonton shop is near it.
* '''Gray Veil Mountain''' is very large and the closest mountain to Downtrodden Mountain. Chen Ping'an bought it later, along with Cinnabar Mountain (formerly held by the Xu Clan of Light Breeze City), Ao Back Ridge, Exuberant Dawn Peak and Sword Worship Plateau.Chapter 529 Gray Veil Mountain and Ao Back Ridge were later leased to Bejeweled Hairpin Island.
* '''Golden Stalk Mountain''' lies just north of Downtrodden Mountain and Gray Veil Mountain. Ruan Qiong bought it to build a new forge.

pages.title: Natal Porcelain
pages.content:
Natal Porcelain, also called "bonded porcelain", is the system through which the small town's most gifted children are identified, claimed, and controlled by outside cultivators and sects.

== Origins and Process ==
Every child born in the small town is given a secret code name recorded in a hidden document. At some point after birth, a specific drop of that child's heart's blood is extracted through a secret technique and sealed into a piece of porcelain fired for them in one of the town's dragon kilns. A girl's porcelain must be fired for six years, while a boy's must be fired for nine, with the kiln fire kept burning without a single day's interruption.Chapter 23

Once a child reaches that age, six for girls and nine for boys, their fate is effectively decided. If an outside buyer has taken an interest in them by then, they are taken from the town to be raised and trained elsewhere. A boy who reaches nine without being claimed by a porcelain buyer is considered to have lackluster cultivation potential and is left in the town, considered to hold little further value.Chapter 20 The piece of porcelain belonging to a child judged to have no potential is removed from the kiln, shattered, and discarded on a mountain of broken porcelain outside the town built up from these failures. No one in the town seems to know what becomes of the children themselves once this happens, beyond assuming nothing good follows.Chapter 61

== The Porcelain Buyers ==
A piece of natal porcelain is bought and sold like any other asset, and "porcelain buying rights" can change hands between outside sects and clans more than once over a person's life, sometimes through outright extortion between rival powers.Chapter 44 The clans inside the town that control the most dragon kilns are also the ones best positioned to supply natal porcelain to the outside world, and a buyer who ends up with a particularly gifted piece of porcelain will often reward the clan that sold it to them with a substantial additional payment on top of the original price.

Whoever holds a person's natal porcelain holds power over that person's life for as long as they live. If the porcelain's owner needs help with something that threatens their clan or sect's survival, the person bound to it is obligated to provide it, and refusing means having their porcelain smashed. This leash holds even for people who go on to become extraordinarily powerful; two such natives of the small town, the Daoist True Lord Cao Xi and the sword immortal [[Xie Shi]], are said to be strong enough that most porcelain buyers would rather treat them as honored guests than as owned property, yet neither can escape the arrangement entirely.

== Consequences and Fate ==
Whether or not someone sold as natal porcelain goes on to achieve great cultivation, the price for it is steep. Once such a person advances to the Middle Five Tiers of cultivation, they lose the right to any afterlife or reincarnation unless they can advance further still, to the Upper Five Tiers. Should they fail to do so, their soul is said to shatter and vanish entirely, beyond saving even by the Dao Ancestor or the Buddha.

Breaking or destroying a person's natal porcelain early severs this bond outright. It is described as a double-edged act: the person loses access to whatever fated opportunities the arrangement might have brought them, but is also freed from the porcelain buyers' control. [[Chen Gong|Chen Ping'an's father]] discovered the truth behind natal porcelain after his own piece had already been tampered with by frustrated buyers who had written him off as worthless, and in response he secretly shattered his young son's porcelain, a porcelain paperweight, before Chen Ping'an turned six. [[Liu Xianyang]]'s bonded porcelain, by contrast, changed hands between rival outside powers, including one buyer who extorted it away from a rival, without ever being destroyed.

[[Nalan Yexing]] (Grandpa Nalan)|Enemie(s)=The demon tribe of the Savage World|Occupation=Sword Cultivator|Continent=[[Sword Qi Great Wall]]}} Ning Yao is the main female protagonist of the series [[Donghua|Sword of Coming]]. == Appearance == Ning Yao first appears in the small town as a black-clothed girl in a veiled hat that covers her face, with a white-scabbarded sword and a green-scabbarded saber at her waist. In her later years at the Sword Qi Great Wall she is often seen in a dark green robe, usually resting a hand on her scabbards.Chapter 15 == Personality == Ning Yao is blunt, proud and supremely confident, firmly believing she will become the most powerful sword immortal under the heavens, not merely one of the most powerful. She speaks her mind without much concern for anyone's feelings, including Chen Ping'an's, and rarely explains herself twice. She has a strong, almost old-fashioned sense of fairness, telling Chen Ping'an early on that in her hometown no one cares whose parents you have, only whether you can win the fight fair and square. She rarely gets truly angry, but when she does, the people around her know to tread carefully, as seen in how harshly she punished friends over an offhand joke at Chen Ping'an's expense. She deliberately avoids discussing her parents' deaths and dislikes being pitied for it, preferring to treat the subject matter-of-factly rather than let outsiders make her a figure of tragedy. Underneath the bluntness she is deeply loyal, patient with the friends she trains, and quietly besotted with Chen Ping'an even while needling him constantly.Chapter 52Chapter 275Chapter 577 == Background == Ning Yao's name combines her father's and mother's surnames, Ning and Yao. Her parents, Master Ning and Mistress Yao, were both twelfth-tier Sword Immortals of the Sword Qi Great Wall, where the Ning and Yao Clans lived only two streets apart but were famously estranged. Mistress Yao married into the then-declining Ning Clan against her own clan's wishes, after a Daoist sage's reading of their compatibility came back unfavorable, and the Yao Clan never fully reconciled with her for it. Ning Yao's birth began to thaw the rift, and in a family lottery over her surname, held between a dowry dagger and a piece of Dragon Slaying Platform, the infant Ning Yao drew the Dragon Slaying Platform, securing her the Ning surname and visibly delighting her mother.Chapter 574 She was recognized as a top-tier sword prodigy from birth and left home to travel the world, eventually arriving badly wounded when she was in the small town, where the Daoist priest Lu Chen saved her life and left Chen Ping'an to nurse her back to health. During her recovery she stayed in Chen Ping'an's home, bonding with him despite her guarded manner, and helped him deal with threats from outsiders such as the Mountain-moving Ape of Sun Scorch Mountain, at one point offering to use her bonded treasure, a mark on her forehead gifted by her mother, as a trump card against him. She left the small town suddenly after receiving a letter from Stalactite Mountain, borrowing Chen Ping'an's sword scabbard.Chapter 15Chapter 53Chapter 71 It turns out both of her parents had been killed, in connection with a battle in which the Sword Qi Great Wall itself nearly fell to its enemies. Her childhood friend Dong Huafu, nicknamed Charcoal, felt honor-bound to personally defend her after her parents and her teacher A'Liang were both gone, and her remaining elders on the Wall, Bai Lianshuang and Nalan Yexing, took on the role of her guardians.Chapter 253Chapter 275 Chen Ping'an traveled to the Sword Qi Great Wall years later to personally deliver a sword forged for her by Ruan Qiong, and the two reunited there, where he confessed his feelings for her for the first time, and she returned it. After giving him ten years to get stronger, he returned on a later visit, having spent the intervening years growing stronger and more sure of himself, and their relationship deepened. On his second return, Ning Yao had become the undisputed top prodigy of her generation at the Sword Qi Great Wall, regarded by the old great sword immortal and the sword cultivator A'Liang as being in a class of her own. She was still working through her Golden Core Tier bottleneck on the way to the Nascent Tier, slowed less by her qi refinement, which came easily to her, than by the item refinement side of her cultivation.Chapter 270Chapter 271Chapter 577 Chen Ping'an ultimately asked her guardians, Bai Lianshuang and Nalan Yexing, for permission to formally propose marriage to her according to the customs of the Sword Qi Great Wall, offering his sword Sword Immortal and his celestial robe Golden Sweet Wine as betrothal gifts despite their value, and naming the reclusive old great sword immortal, [[Chen Qingdu]], as his intended matchmaker. Around the same time, he fought and defeated her rival suitor Qi Shou in single combat after Qi Shou was accused of coveting the Ning Clan's Dragon Slaying Cliff through her, cementing his place among her circle of friends and rivals at the Wall.Chapter 575 == Trivia == *Her bonded treasure is hidden in a mark on her glabella, a gift from her mother.Chapter 53 *She once got drunk and declared she could beat up a hundred Chen Ping'ans with one hand, a boast her friends never let either of them forget.Chapter 572 *Her father once nearly named her "Yao Ning" instead of "Ning Yao," leading to the only real argument he and her mother ever had.Chapter 574 *Her friends at the Sword Qi Great Wall have taken to physically punishing anyone who brings up her parents' deaths around her.Chapter 574 == References ==
