pages.title: Northern Complete Reed Continent
pages.content:
[[Category:Locations]]
'''Northern Complete Reed Continent''', often called simply the '''Complete Reed Continent''', is one of the nine continents of the [[Majestic World]], lying north across the sea from the [[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]]. It is famous for its sword cultivators and its harsh, proud culture, and it was the main setting of [[Chen Ping An]]'s later travels.

== Geography ==
The continent actually lies in the northeast of the Majestic World. It still calls itself the northern continent, which leaves [[Pure White Continent]], the true northern continent, without the title.Chapter 210 A stretch of sea separates it from the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent. Its southern tip and the north of the [[Great Li Empire]] are the closest points between the two.Chapter 513

Skeleton Shoal in the far south is one of the continent's ten major ancient battlefields. Its ferry station is the main hub of the southern region, and the [[Sects#Flax Robe Sect|Flax Robe Sect]] stands above it.Chapter 485 Nearby lies Malicious Ghost Valley, a small world held in a vortex of time and ruled by ghosts.Chapter 489 The Great Origin Empire is the largest empire in the central region.Chapter 494 A great river runs through the centre of the continent from east to west, and the [[Sects#Water Dragon Sect|Water Dragon Sect]] is built upon it.Chapter 542 Other powers include the Great Seal Script Empire and the Tail Feather Empire, one of the largest on the continent.Chapter 283 [[Sects#Ceremony Mountain|Ceremony Mountain]] lies in the southwest.Chapter 207

== History ==
Sword immortals of the continent once led the charge to [[Stalactite Mountain]], among them the patriarch of the Hulü Clan.Chapter 213 For a long time the continent had no full Daoist Heavenly Lord. [[Xie Shi]], its Dao Master, was on the verge of becoming the first.Chapter 191 [[He Xiaoliang]] of the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent later founded the [[Sects#Refreshing Sect|Refreshing Sect]] there, becoming the youngest sect leader in the continent's history.Chapter 487

As the war at the [[Sword Qi Great Wall]] worsened, an army of the continent's swordsmen flew south to reinforce it. By [[Cui Chan]]'s count, half of its top sword cultivators had been drawn away.Chapter 479 Another two hundred sword cultivators went to Pure White Continent, and the leaders of sects such as the [[Sects#Great Emblem Sword Sect|Great Emblem Sword Sect]] left for the Great Wall.Chapter 526

== Cultivation world ==
Sword cultivators make up the largest share of the continent's cultivators. Strength is valued above all. A single look can start a fight, and many people travel under false names.Chapter 367 The imperial courts favour martial arts over scholarship, and the sages who guard its Confucian academies are unusually strong fighters. Once a sword cultivator reaches the Unpolished Jade Tier, other sword immortals almost always challenge them.Chapter 508 The strongest sword immortal of the north is Bai Shang of the [[Sects#Jade Forest Sect|Jade Forest Sect]].

Buddhism has more followers than Daoism on the continent. The Lofty Cloud Palace of the Great Origin Empire acts much like the head of the Daoist orthodoxy there.Chapter 496 Its young talents are ranked as the ten dragons and phoenixes, and its strongest as the top ten cultivators of the mountains. Its cultivators, and especially its sword cultivators, are known for looking down on everyone else.Chapter 506 They held the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent in particular contempt.

== Trivia ==

* The novel gives two counts of its Confucian academies. One passage says six, another says three.
* The Flax Robe Sect of Skeleton Shoal alone has three Unpolished Jade Tier ancestors, a sign of how deep the continent's foundations run.
* Chen Ping An chose to travel there because it was the place most like the Sword Qi Great Wall.Chapter 280

== References ==

pages.title: Northern Jin Nation
pages.content:
The Northern Jin Nation is a complex entity with a rich history, powerful military, and unique culture. Its position in the Lotus Flower Blessed Land makes it a key player in regional conflicts and a point of interaction for people from various other regions and continents. The nation also faces internal challenges and is influenced by both earthly powers and otherworldly forces.

'''Geographic and Political Location''':

* The Northern Jin Nation is located on the '''Parasol Leaf Continent'''.
* It has a long border with difficult mountain paths.
* It is situated near a large lake known as the Four Hundred Kilometer Lake, which contains an island with an illegal temple.
* It is one of the four nations in the Lotus Flower Blessed Land, alongside the Southern Garden Nation, Pine Song Nation, and others.
* The nation has a '''vastly renowned Tathagata Temple'''.
* The Mirror Heart Hall has influence in the imperial court of the nation.
* It is a powerful nation with a history of conflict with the Southern Garden Nation.

'''Culture and Society''':

* The nation's culture is distinct from that of the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent.
* It is known for its martial arts.
* The younger generation lacks elites to inherit the skills and power of the previous generations.
* The nation has a complex political structure with various clans and factions vying for power.
* There are many powerful families in the nation.
* There is a '''Tathagata Temple''' which is renowned, and has a large rock called the Stone Lotus Platform where a Bodhisattva is said to have attained enlightenment.
* The capital of the nation is a grand city.

'''Military and Power''':

* The Northern Jin Nation has a strong military, including a powerful cavalry.
* '''Dragon General Tang Tieyi''' is a pillar member of the nation and a powerful general.
* The nation has a border army that is considered very powerful.
* The nation has elite military scouts and reconnaissance teams.
* The '''Yao Clan''', originally from the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent, serves in the border army of the Northern Jin Nation.

'''Key Figures and Groups''':

* '''Tang Tieyi''' is the most powerful general in the nation, known for his skill with sabers.
* '''Yu Zhenyi''' is the leader of the Lake Mountain Faction, one of the Upper Ten Elites.
* The Mirror Heart Hall focuses on infiltrating the imperial court rather than interfering in the cultivation world.
* '''Lu Fang''' remained on Bird's Eye View Peak and did not involve himself in worldly matters.
* '''Ding Ying''' is a significant figure who is knowledgeable about otherworldly immortals and has fought against them.

'''Conflicts and Challenges''':

* The nation is engaged in conflicts with other nations, such as the Southern Garden Nation.
* There are internal power struggles among the various factions.
* There is a presence of otherworldly immortals who descend into their world.
* There are issues with corruption and abuse of power by officials.
* A great demon in the lake has appointed itself as a water god, and the imperial court is unable to punish it.
* The nation is in competition with the Southern Garden Nation which was once renowned for its powerful mounted troops.
* The imperial court of the nation has faced challenges with rebellions.

'''Interactions with Other Regions''':

* The nation is aware of and interacts with the Great Li Empire.
* It is also aware of the Southern Garden Nation and other regions within the Lotus Flower Blessed Land.
* The nation's elites are known throughout the Lotus Flower Blessed Land.
* The nation's elites often look down upon those from the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent, with the exception of people like Cui Chan and Qi Jingchun.
* There are connections with people from the Middle Earth Divine Continent.
* There are also connections to the Great Quan Empire, especially through the Yao Clan, which originated from the Great Li Empire.

'''Unique Features''':

* There is a large rock called the Stone Lotus Platform that wobbles with the presence of just one person, which no one can explain.
* The nation's border is extremely long and the mountain paths are difficult to traverse.

pages.title: Old Dragon City
pages.content:
Old Dragon City is a complex and dynamic location characterized by its immense power, rich history, and unique geographical location. It is a place of great wealth and commerce, but also a place where power struggles and conflicts are commonplace. The city is a major hub for trade and travel, and its connections to other continents make it a significant location in the narrative. The presence of powerful clans, mystical elements, and a constant state of tension and change make Old Dragon City a central location for many of the events that unfold in the story.

'''General Characteristics:'''

* Old Dragon City is located in the '''southernmost region of the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent'''. This location gives it a unique position, distinct from the northern regions of the continent.
* It is a '''massive city''', so large that a person could spend their entire life exploring it without seeing everything.
* The city is divided into the '''outer city, the inner city, and the Fu city''', each with its own distinct characteristics.
* It is described as the '''most prosperous city''' on the entire Eastern Treasured Vial Continent.
* The city is a '''central hub connecting three continents''', making it a very diverse and complex place.
* Old Dragon City is known for having a '''long and illustrious history''', producing prodigious and powerful cultivators.
* The city has a '''unique feature''': a sea of clouds that floats above it. This sea of clouds is a '''pseudo-celestial tool''' of the city. The city also has an '''underground dragon channel'''.
* It is said that the city is the burial place of the last true dragon in the world.

'''Social and Political Landscape:'''

* The city is dominated by '''powerful clans''', with the '''Fu Clan''' being the most powerful. The other major clans include the '''Sun Clan''', '''Fang Clan''', '''Hou Clan''', and '''Ding Clan'''.
* These clans have deep roots in the city, and they often compete with each other for power and influence.
* The Fu Clan is traditionally the '''dominant force in the south''', with a history spanning thousands of years.
* The '''Sun Clan''' is known for its immense foundation and exceptional business reputation, and its Nascent Tier patriarch. The Sun Clan is also known for its generosity, as they purchase goods from the villages they oversee for higher than market price.
* The city has a '''complex social hierarchy''', with powerful cultivators and wealthy merchants at the top and ordinary citizens below.
* The clans in Old Dragon City are '''followers of Commercialism of the Hundred Schools of Thought''', and their revered figures are different from Confucian sages.

'''Key Figures and Groups:'''

* '''Fu Nanhua''' is the eldest young master of the Fu Clan, described as shrewd and insightful. He is also set to marry a descendant of the Jiang Clan in order to form a marriage alliance.
* '''Fu Qi''' is the city lord of Old Dragon City and the leader of the Fu Clan. He is an earth immortal and is described as both easygoing and unforgiving.
* '''Sun Jiashu''' is a member of the Sun Clan who is very wealthy and has a unique ability to see the wealth that has slipped through someone's fingers. He has a complex relationship with Chen Ping'an.
* '''Zheng Dafeng''' is a powerful ninth-tier martial artist who has a close relationship with Old Man Yang. He is also considered a Dao mentor.
* There are also powerful figures such as '''Chu Yang''', the Fu Clan’s premier guest elder who cultivates on the Dragon Scaling Platform.
* '''Fan Er''' is a member of the Fan Clan.
* There is an individual from the '''Jiang Clan''' who is set to marry into the Fu Clan.
* There are many '''Qi refiners and martial artists''' in Old Dragon City, with many at the middle five tiers.

'''Economic and Commercial Aspects:'''

* Old Dragon City is the '''largest business hub''' on the entire Eastern Treasured Vial Continent.
* It is a major '''trade center''', with ships leading to any place where money can be made.
* The city's economy is driven by the '''five major clans''' and various smaller businesses.
* The '''Sun Clan''' is especially renowned for its business reputation.
* There is a '''street owned by the Sun Clan''' in the outer city.
* The city has many shops and merchants who trade goods from all over the continent.

'''Mystical and Spiritual Elements:'''

* The '''sea of clouds''' above the city is said to be a powerful entity that has been there for thousands of years. It acts as a defensive treasure.
* The city is believed to be the burial place of the last true dragon, and this is said to be the reason for the city's unique characteristics.
* There is a '''Dragon Scaling Platform''' in the city, which is a restricted area. The summit of the platform can only be seen from a ship in the sky.
* Old Dragon City has four '''pseudo-celestial tools''', two of which are in the possession of the Fu Clan's leader.
* The city is described as having abundant '''yang energy''' due to the number of Qi refiners.
* The area around the Sun Clan's ancestral residence is considered a renowned paradise.

'''Conflicts and Tensions:'''

* There is a constant tension among the five major clans as they struggle for power.
* There have been conflicts and power struggles between the Fu Clan and other major clans.
* There is an awareness of the potential for a large-scale conflict that could damage the city.
* There are also conflicts between the city and outside forces, as well as threats from demonic cultivators.
* There are many '''strange occurrences''' that take place in Old Dragon City.

'''Connections to the Wider World:'''

* Old Dragon City is a major '''connection point''' between Eastern Treasured Vial Continent and Parasol Leaf Continent.
* It has '''intercontinental ships''' that can travel to other continents, such as Stalactite Mountain.
* The city is a place where powerful figures from other continents often visit.
* There are ships from the city that travel to the Sword Qi Great Wall, although these are few in number.
* The city has connections to the Great Li Empire.

pages.title: Old Man Yang
pages.content:
{{Character |header1=Old Man Yang |image1=Old man Yang.png |Vital_status=Alive |Gender=Male |Disciple(s)=[[Li Er]]
[[Zheng Dafeng]]
[[Li Liu]] (Dao mentee)
Shi Lingshan
Shi Lingshan's senior sister |Occupation=Medicine shop resident (guise) |Current_affiliation(s)=[[Jewel Small World]] |Continent=[[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]] |Novel=Chapter 50 }} '''Old Man Yang''' is a wrinkled old man who sits in the backyard of the Yang Family Medicine Shop in the small town, smoking a bamboo pipe and rarely speaking except to insult someone. The townspeople see him as an odd old employee of the shop. In truth, he is one of the most powerful and ancient beings connected to Jewel Small World. Ruan Qiong, Cui Chan and the sages of the Three Teachings treat him with wary respect, and he has spent some ten thousand years "sitting in this cage". He is the master of [[Li Er]] and [[Zheng Dafeng]], and the Dao mentor of [[Li Liu]]. He was once the maker of the town's bonded porcelain, and he quietly guides reincarnated ancient beings back to their old paths. He places "bets" on many people of the town, Chen Ping'an among them. == Appearance == Old Man Yang's face is as wrinkled as the bark of the old locust tree. He is almost always seen with his bamboo smoking pipe and a cloth pouch of tobacco at his waist, usually seated on a stool or the steps of the medicine shop's backyard. When he goes into the mountains, he seems far more energetic than his age suggests. == Personality == Old Man Yang is aloof, sharp-tongued and openly contemptuous of most people, mocking even his own disciples. He tells Zheng Dafeng that he isn't successful because he is ugly. He has little patience for bravado, and does not hide his disdain for the scheming of powerful figures. He calls himself "decent when it comes to judging the character of others", and Ruan Qiong knows he has accumulated countless secrets. He is, however, scrupulously fair in his dealings, and much of what he does takes the form of "transactions". He refuses to accept free medicinal herbs from Chen Ping'an, throwing them into the street, but will buy them. He has a soft spot for a few people: he allows the young [[Li Huai]] into his backyard, smiles when Li Huai lectures him about smoking, and admits he truly likes the boy. Old Man Yang says he finds entertainment where he can, since he has been sitting in a cage for ten thousand years. == Background == The text gives only glimpses of Old Man Yang's true nature. He describes himself as having sat "in this cage for ten thousand years", and he once spent nine thousand years trying to work out a problem that Cui Chan's philosophies finally helped him understand.Chapter 428 (3) The making of bonded porcelain, the porcelain linked to the lives of the town's children, was his "supreme ability", and the rise of the Great Li Empire can be traced back to transactions made in Jewel Small World.Chapter 530 (2) He has guided many reincarnated beings "step by step to that ancient path", unlocking their memories. He has instructed "prisoners and sinister remnants" to wrap themselves in a human heart, the reverse of gilding a statue with gold. Many sages of the Three Teachings have visited his shop over the years. When Zheng Dafeng prays to him, he gestures as if plucking three sticks of incense out of the air, as though offering incense to a god. == Plot == === The Small Town === When Chen Ping'an carries the injured Ning Yao to the shop, Old Man Yang asks her how many characters are written on the wall of the small temple, and asks if she "ate" the last one. With a little guidance he helps her advance a tier on the spot, then charges them a pouch of Offering Coins for the medicine.Chapter 60 Watching the rain with Zheng Dafeng, he notes the stark contrast between his two disciples, Li Er and Zheng Dafeng.Chapter 61 He scolds Li Er for catching the golden carp and trying to sell it to Chen Ping'an, orders Zheng Dafeng to escort Fu Nanhua to Old Dragon City, and remarks that no one ever said the three of them were his only disciples.Chapter 63 (2) At Azure Cow Ridge, he offers the drowned old woman in the creek, the reborn [[Ma Lanhua]], a choice between remaining a pitiful catfish or becoming a flood dragon, and sends her swimming down the river.Chapter 71 (1) He then confronts a Confucian scholar from an academy, asking whether it was he who forced Qi Jingchun step by step into sacrificing himself, and tells him he should never have come.Chapter 71 (2) On the mountain of porcelain, he faces down a powerful youthful-looking cultivator of the Upper Five Tiers with only a puff of pipe smoke, while even the newly eleventh-tier Ruan Qiong is uneasy.Chapter 77 Before the small world settles, he takes away the little temple whose walls bear the names of the town's children, telling Ruan Qiong a secret in return.Chapter 85 (2) === Guiding Pieces from Afar === Old Man Yang assigns a [[Yin god]] to secretly protect Li Huai on the journey to Great Sui.Chapter 130 He later suppresses Li Huai's aptitude, saying Li Liu is talented while Li Huai is blessed with fortune. He orders the river goddess of the Dragon Whisker River to disperse half her godly body into the river to help Ruan Qiong forge his sword. In exchange, he offers to help conceal [[Ruan Xiu]]'s true identity for thirty years.Chapter 185 (1) He obtains the golden incense girl that lived in Chen Ping'an's locust wood sword, something Qi Jingchun had secretly possessed and Old Man Yang had long coveted. In return, he agrees to guard Chen Ping'an once. He reveals that the Sword Suppressing Pagoda was originally an ascension platform, and that the children who wrote their names in the small temple and survived have all become extremely powerful.Chapter 195 (2) He tells the sword immortal Cao Xi that the souls of Cao Xi's parents are held by Li Liu, and arranges for Cao Xi to give her a flying sword, teach her his technique, and serve as her Dao guardian.Chapter 235 (2) He arranges for Zheng Dafeng to act as Chen Ping'an's Dao mentor in Old Dragon City, and later accepts the cost of Zheng Dafeng's martial cultivation in exchange for Fan Junmao becoming the Great Li Empire's second great mountain god. === Chen Ping'an's Trial === During Chen Ping'an's crisis of the heart at Bamboo Scroll Lake, Old Man Yang discusses him with Ruan Qiong and Zheng Dafeng. He says that had Chen Ping'an's bonded porcelain not been shattered, he would have been talented enough to become a mediocre earth immortal, and he observes that neither the Scholarly Sage nor Lu Chen can solve this test for him. Zheng Dafeng accuses his master of deliberately letting the "evil flood dragon" in Chen Ping'an's heart rear its head. Old Man Yang does not deny it, and remarks that to stay alive and live well, one must compete with the entire world. When eager parents swarm the shop believing he is an immortal, he charges a snowflake coin per child to test their aptitude, rejects every one, and lets rumours spread that he is a fraud until no one comes. === Later Years === Old Man Yang takes on two new disciples: Shi Lingshan, a bleary-eyed young shop attendant, and his senior sister, a former kiln worker on [[Dragon Riding Alley]] who becomes a martial arts prodigy. He tells the young woman to inform Chen Ping'an that he will chat with him, but will do no more business with him. When Li Huai visits with tobacco and lectures him, Old Man Yang smiles and tells him there are a few items set aside for him. He meets Li Liu, whose rebirth he arranged, and urges her to set aside her ancient grudge with Ruan Xiu, asking what point there is in battles between Great Daos when no Dao remains. He tells her that Chen Ping'an has begun quietly investigating the matter of bonded porcelain, and that the hairpin the old scholar gave Chen Ping'an is a critical item of "that stinky Daoist temple master".Chapter 530 (1) He also told Li Liu that if she kept cultivating in her old way, changing bodies each life, she would be stuck at the Immortal Tier forever as someone who "couldn't even act like a human". == Abilities == His full power is never shown, but hints include: * '''Bonded porcelain:''' He once made the bonded porcelain of Jewel Small World's children. * '''Guidance of reincarnated beings:''' He can unlock past-life memories and set beings on their ancient paths. * '''Authority over spirits and deities:''' Water goddesses, Yin gods and river spirits obey him without question. He can kill the Yin god from a vast distance. * '''Presence:''' He can face down Upper Five Tier cultivators with nothing but pipe smoke. * '''Insight:''' He helped Ning Yao advance a tier with a few words. Li Er and Zheng Dafeng, both trained by him, became formidable martial artists. == Trivia == * He blames his rare displays of helplessness on the constant nagging of Li Er's wife, "detested by both gods and ghosts alike". * Chen Ping'an often went into the mountains with him as a boy and learned to observe mountains and taste clay. * He told Chen Ping'an that all medicines are poison to some degree, and that martial artists should avoid elixirs. * Chen Ping'an is one of the many people he has placed bets on, though held in far lower regard than [[Ma Kuxuan]]. * He trades secrets and favours with [[Ruan Qiong]]. * Although he mocks [[Cui Chan]], he admits that his philosophies taught him valuable things. * [[Li Huai]] is one of the very few people he genuinely likes. == References == [[Category:Characters]] [[Category:Male]] [[Category:Alive]]

pages.title: Old Man Yao
pages.content:
{{Character|Titles=Overseer of the Treasure Creek dragon kiln|Aliases=Master Yao
Old Man Yao|Vital_status=Dead|Gender=Male|Species=Human|Disciple(s)=[[Liu Xianyang]] (favourite disciple)|Allies=[[Old Man Yang]]|Occupation=Master potter
Dragon kiln overseer|Current_affiliation(s)=Treasure Creek dragon kiln|Continent=[[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]]|Empire=Great Li Empire|City=[[Small Town]]|Novel=1}}

'''Old Man Yao''' was the master potter who ran the Treasure Creek dragon kiln outside the [[Small Town]]. He took in [[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]] as an apprentice and made [[Liu Xianyang]] his favourite disciple. He had already died when the story opens, but his lessons and sayings stay with Chen Ping'an long after the kilns close.

==Appearance==
He was an old man who liked to keep to himself, often standing with his hands tucked into the opposite sleeves. Out in the mountains he seemed to come alive, climbing with more energy than a healthy young man. His hair and eye colour are never described.

== Personality ==
Old Man Yao was gruff, short-tempered and sparing with his words. When he did speak, it was usually to curse someone, and his remarks were either cutting or so cryptic that nobody could make sense of them. He beat and insulted his apprentices freely. Even Liu Xianyang, whom he plainly favoured, was not spared. Yet anyone could see that he meant well. After he once split Liu Xianyang's forehead open, he paced his room most of the night and finally sent Chen Ping'an over with a bottle of ointment.Chapter 4

He was harder on Chen Ping'an than on anyone. Thinking the boy had no talent, he refused to teach him the real secrets of pottery and set him to manual labour instead. Once, disgusted with him, he left the boy alone in the wilderness and walked back to the kiln. Chen Ping'an had to find his own way home through about 60 kilometres of mountains in the pouring rain.Chapter 6 Still, Old Man Yao trusted him with the kiln's money for buying medicine, because he knew the boy was honest.

He took his craft very seriously. A single firing could waste half a year of work if it went wrong, so he insisted on watching the fire himself and sat up through whole nights on his stool beside the kiln.Chapter 564 (2) When a worker let the kiln fire go out and fled into the mountains, Old Man Yao sent men after him and broke his arms and legs when he was dragged back.Chapter 268 He could be kind in quieter ways too. While other kilns allowed three days off at harvest time, he always gave four or five.Chapter 249 (2)

When he drank, he became a different man. He would boast that their kiln made porcelain for the emperor himself, and he told strange stories about gods in the mountains and rivers that his apprentices loved to hear.Chapter 211 (1)

== Background==

=== The kiln ===
Old Man Yao was the most skilled potter among the town's dragon kilns. As a young man he was the only potter in dozens of kilns who could make a difficult kind of underglaze porcelain favoured by an earlier Great Li emperor.Chapter 585 (1) His jumping burin technique won praise from everyone who saw it. He took several disciples, but none of them truly met his standards.

Liu Xianyang became his best disciple and learned in half a year what took Chen Ping'an three years.Chapter 1 Old Man Yao clearly preferred him and expected him to take over the kiln someday. That favour had limits. When he overheard Liu Xianyang calling himself a prodigy, he flew into a rage and beat him, and Liu Xianyang never used the word again.Chapter 42

=== Chen Ping'an ===
Liu Xianyang brought the orphaned Chen Ping'an to the kiln, and Old Man Yao took the boy in without ever accepting him as a true disciple. Instead he made Chen Ping'an carry his tools on long trips into the mountains to search for clay. Along the way he taught the boy to judge soil by chewing it, until Chen Ping'an could tell a kiln and its master from a broken shard just by holding it. On one trip they reached a high peak and saw an even taller mountain to the east. In a rare talkative mood, Old Man Yao told him to look but not to talk about it afterwards, because a person should keep his head down and work.Chapter 35

On their last trip into the mountains, he pointed out the burial ground of the other branch of the Chen Clan. He also told Chen Ping'an that not even immortals could find where his own branch's ancestors lay.Chapter 36 Chen Ping'an never held his treatment against him and remained grateful to him all his life. He later calls Old Man Yao his "half-teacher," and one of his sayings became a guiding principle for Chen Ping'an: if something is meant to be yours, hold on to it and don't let go, and if it isn't, don't even think about it.Chapter 134 (2)

According to Song Jixin's mother, Old Man Yao also told the young Chen Ping'an the truth about the superstition surrounding his birth on the fifth day of the fifth month. The boy ran back from the kiln in a fury, cornered Song Jixin outside Clay Vase Alley and nearly strangled him. She blames Old Man Yao for the fear Song Jixin carried for years afterwards.Chapter 90

=== Death and legacy ===
Old Man Yao died some time before the story begins, and the dragon kilns were shut down afterwards. 

When [[Qi Jingchun]] asked the town's old locust tree for a blessed leaf to protect Chen Ping'an, a single leaf fell bearing the golden character "Yao." Qi Jingchun confirmed it was the same Yao as the boy's old master and asked whether he would repay the Yao Clan's kindness. Chen Ping'an vowed to save any member of the Yao Clan connected to him, even at the cost of his life.Chapter 23 He later used that leaf to keep Liu Xianyang alive.

Years later, Cui Chan and Cui Dongshan review the scenes of Chen Ping'an's past that involve Old Man Yao and study the fall of that leaf closely. Cui Dongshan concludes that Old Man Yao had hidden a plan of his own extremely well, and that [[Old Man Yang]] must have been part of it.Chapter 455 (7)

== Trivia ==

* Old Man Yao believed that all mountains, tall or short, grow from the same roots and are related to each other like members of a clan.
* He taught that every kind of clay has its own fate, much like people do.
* He called True Jewel Mountain's soil the most flavourful he knew, but said the mountain was too small, like a man trapped in a cage.
* He passed on an old potters' custom that Chen Ping'an kept up for years, though he never explained what it meant.
* When the kiln supervision official visited in his robes, Old Man Yao kept the other apprentices out of sight and had only Liu Xianyang show off the jumping burin technique.
* [[Old Man Yang]] reacts with an odd expression whenever Old Man Yao is mentioned.
* Even [[Pei Qian]], watching scenes from her master's childhood years later, wonders why Old Man Yao was always scolding him.

==References==

pages.title: Pang Yuanji
pages.content:
{{Character |header1=Pang Yuanji |Aliases=Hundred Schools Pang |Vital_status=Alive |Gender=Male |Species=Human |Master(s)=Lord Hidden Official |Friend(s)=Gao Yehou
Gao Youqing
[[Chen Ping An]] |Occupation=Sword cultivator
Direct disciple of the Hidden Official |Current_affiliation(s)=[[Sword Qi Great Wall]] |Cultivation_rank=Golden Core Tier (peak stage) |Novel=Chapter 575 }} == Appearance == Pang Yuanji is an elegant young man dressed in white, carrying himself with a jaded maturity that seems well beyond his twenty-five years of age.Chapter 575Chapter 576 Unlike many of his sword immortal peers, he wears no Dao robe and carries no celestial weapon or Militarian armor pellets, relying on a single bonded flying sword instead.Chapter 577 == Personality == He is composed, self-possessed, and carries a deep-seated disdain for the prosperous, complacent Majestic World, a resentment that is kept from curdling into outright hatred only by his admiration for figures like A’Liang and Zuo You, along with the swordsmen of the Northern Complete Reed Continent.Chapter 576 He has no interest in romance and, despite being considered one of the two young prodigies most suited to become Ning Yao’s Dao partner, could not care less who she ends up liking.Chapter 575 He cares deeply about his standing as a swordsman of the Sword Qi Great Wall and as the Hidden Official’s disciple, and he prefers to keep his attention on cultivation rather than get tangled up in political disputes among the sword immortals.Chapter 586 With his master he drops his usual composure, bickering and grumbling like any ordinary disciple rather than standing on ceremony.Chapter 586 == Background == Pang Yuanji is one of the three most exceptional young sword talents of the Sword Qi Great Wall, alongside Qi Shou and Gao Yehou, and is widely regarded as the strongest of the three, with the greatest hopes of inheriting the title of Hidden Official from his master in the coming century. Born into a middle-class family, he showed signs of extraordinary potential from the moment he was born and has cultivated under the erratic Lord Hidden Official ever since, making him technically only half her formal disciple. He is also on close terms with the sages of the Three Teachings stationed on the wall, regularly seeking them out to learn and ask questions.Chapter 575 His bonded flying sword, called Time, has no fixed shape or form, much like the concept it is named for, and its true value lies not in raw destructive power but in how it lets him master an enormous range of immortal techniques and accelerates his cultivation and soul refinement. This versatility earned him the nickname Hundred Schools Pang from a young age.Chapter 577 When Chen Ping’an arrived at the Sword Qi Great Wall and challenged its young sword cultivators one after another, Pang Yuanji agreed to fight him once Qi Shou had taken his turn, with the winner of their own sparring match first deciding who would face the outsider. After Chen Ping’an defeated Qi Shou, Pang Yuanji accepted the challenge himself, deploying a dozen or more illusory copies of himself to slowly envelop the entire street in a sword formation and transform it into his own small world. Chen Ping’an broke through the scheme at the last moment, and the two traded a final, decisive blow each, with Pang Yuanji ultimately conceding the match rather than letting the fight turn fully lethal. Chen Ping’an later admitted privately that he had won only through careful strategy and the rules of engagement, not because he was genuinely stronger, and that Pang Yuanji had deliberately held back just as he had.Chapter 577Chapter 578 Despite losing, Pang Yuanji bore Chen Ping’an no ill will, and the two gradually became friends, with Pang Yuanji becoming a regular, if begrudging, customer at Die Zhang’s wine shop alongside his friend Sword Immortal Gao Kui.Chapter 578 He remained close to his master even after this, often visiting her and even being asked by her to weigh in on political disputes involving the Scholarly Sage’s and Second Sage’s lineages, matters he openly admitted he had little talent for navigating.Chapter 586 When the Savage World launched a renewed assault on the Sword Qi Great Wall, Pang Yuanji watched from the city wall as the Hidden Official, his own master, suddenly turned on the wall’s defenders, grievously wounding the nearly invincible swordsman Zuo You before defecting to the Savage World alongside the sword immortals Zhu An and Luo Shan. The betrayal left him shattered, collapsing to the ground in tears and sitting in a daze for a long while afterward, unable to understand why it had happened.Chapter 609Chapter 625 His friend Gao Yehou urged him to one day challenge the Hidden Official and demand an explanation for her betrayal, but Pang Yuanji could only murmur that he was not the kind of person who could do such a thing.Chapter 626 == Trivia == * The Hidden Official had reportedly considered two potential heirs to her title before her betrayal: Pang Yuanji and, surprisingly, the young swordswoman Guo Zhujiu.Chapter 575 * He once asked his master why she kept such a close watch on Chen Ping’an, since he clearly wasn’t a spy for the demon tribe, and received only a typically cryptic non-answer for his trouble.Chapter 609 * He was the only person to win money on the city wall’s informal betting pool regarding the outcome of Chen Ping’an’s challenge matches.Chapter 578 == References ==

pages.title: Parasol Leaf Continent
pages.content:
'''Parasol Leaf Continent''' is one of the nine continents of the [[Majestic World]], lying southeast of the [[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]]. It is a large and inward-looking continent with few immortal forces, most of them very powerful. It is home to the [[Lotus Flower Blessed Land]], where [[Chen Ping An]] spent much of his early travels.

== Geography ==
The continent is far larger than the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent, and larger even than Circling Ascension Continent.Chapter 261 The seas around it are rough, with strong winds and high waves. For that reason almost all of its ferry stations lie in the north.Chapter 281 The Parasol Leaf Sect and the Jade Tablet Sect hold the two ends of the continent, and each is said to hold half of its fortune.Chapter 287 The Jade Tablet Sect's southern lands are green and rich in spiritual energy.Chapter 631

The central region holds the Planchette Writing Sect, [[Sects#Peace and Tranquility Mountain|Peace and Tranquility Mountain]] and Great Subduing Academy.Chapter 296 The [[Great Quan Empire]] is one of the stronger empires there and was rising to lead the region.Chapter 344 Burial River was once one of the three great rivers of the continent that flowed into the sea.Chapter 349 The continent has four Confucian academies, one each in the north and south, Great Subduing Academy in the centre, and the little-known Literary Profundity Academy.

== History ==
Chen Ping An arrived at the Planchette Writing Sect's ferry station on his way to find the Observing Dao Temple. Soon after, a great demon of the Upper Five Tiers hidden in the central region destroyed almost half of the Planchette Writing Sect. At the same moment, the well prison of Peace and Tranquility Mountain opened, and more than half of the demons held there for thousands of years escaped. The central region fell into chaos, and the academies and sects of the continent joined forces to hunt them down.Chapter 345

Du Mao, an Ascension Tier cultivator of the [[Sects#Parasol Leaf Sect|Parasol Leaf Sect]], nearly killed Chen Ping An in [[Old Dragon City]]. In return, Chen Ping An's senior brother [[Zuo You]] brought the Parasol Leaf Sect to the worst crisis in its history.Chapter 369 The sect fell from grace, and the [[Sects#Jade Tablet Sect|Jade Tablet Sect]], second on the continent for thousands of years, rose to the top almost without effort.

[[Cui Chan]] believed that once the [[Sword Qi Great Wall]] fell, the demon tribe would strike Parasol Leaf Continent and that few of its Upper Five Tier cultivators would survive.Chapter 479 In time great demons were indeed wreaking havoc there.Chapter 626

== Cultivation world ==
Unlike the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent, which is crowded with small forces, Parasol Leaf Continent has few sects. Most of them are very strong, and the leading cultivators of its two great sects reached the Immortal Tier centuries ago. For a thousand years the Planchette Writing Sect was counted third after the two great sects, though Peace and Tranquility Mountain was said to be at least its equal. Its cultivators are known for their pride and for belittling the elites of other continents.Chapter 339

== Trivia ==

* The continent is very conservative and does not welcome outsiders. An outside power like [[Xie Shi]] would have been beaten half to death there.Chapter 293
* It is so reluctant to deal with other continents that it has never built a single intercontinental ship of its own.
* Its many dialects make learning the official dialect of its imperial courts the easiest way for an outsider to travel.
* One passage places the Parasol Leaf Sect in the south and the Jade Tablet Sect in the north, the reverse of the rest of the novel.

pages.title: Pei Qian
pages.content:
{{Character |header1=Pei Qian |Vital_status=Alive |Gender=Female |Species=Human |Age=9 (Chapter 329) |Master(s)=[[Chen Ping An]] (opening disciple)
[[Cui Cheng]] (martial arts teacher) |Friend(s)=[[Li Baoping]]
[[Li Huai]]
[[Zhu Lian]]
[[Chen Nuanshu]] |Occupation=Pure martial artist |Current_affiliation(s)=[[Downtrodden Mountain]] |Cultivation_rank=Fourth-tier pure martial artist }} {{Spoilers}} '''Pei Qian''' is [[Chen Ping An]]'s first disciple, his "opening disciple". She is a street urchin from the capital of the Southern Garden Nation in the Lotus Flower Blessed Land, who was dragged out of that world by its old Daoist master and left in Chen Ping'an's care. At first greedy, deceitful and cruel, a girl Chen Ping'an genuinely detested, she gradually grows into a fiercely loyal, comedic and big-hearted young martial artist who idolises her master. She has mysterious eyes containing the light of the sun and moon, an extraordinary talent for martial arts, and a love of money, treasures, sunflower seeds and her "self-created" Deranged Demon Sword Techniques. After the death of her martial arts teacher [[Cui Cheng]], she inherits half of his martial fortune. ==Appearance== Pei Qian is a skinny, heavily tanned girl, described as being as thin as a bamboo pole when Chen Ping'an meets her. For years she barely grows taller, to the point that Li Baoping asks why she isn't growing. Her most striking feature is her eyes, which Zhong Kui compares to the sun rising over the eastern seas and the moon over the western mountains. She is almost always seen with her bamboo hiking pole, a small bamboo bookcase, a bamboo sword and saber made by Chen Ping'an hanging at her hip, and a Treasure Pagoda Demon-Suppressing Talisman stuck to her forehead. ==Personality== When she first leaves the blessed land, Pei Qian is lazy, greedy, a habitual liar and a petty thief. Having survived alone on the streets, she treats a hostile world with hostility in return, resents anything good she cannot have, and would rather destroy it than leave it to someone else. She is extremely skilled at reading people, and she casually compares killing people to eating rice. Under Chen Ping'an's patient but strict guidance, especially the daily transcriptions he makes her write, she slowly changes. She remains mischievous, boastful, theatrical and obsessed with money. She calls her master "Father" in private and "Master" in public, flatters shamelessly, invents stories about being a lost princess, and loves novels about the martial world. But she becomes sincere, protective of her friends and deeply devoted to Chen Ping'an. By the end of Volume 8, she no longer needs her eyes to read people's hearts. ==Background== Pei Qian grew up alone and impoverished in the capital of the Southern Garden Nation. She occasionally sneaked out of the city to look at a small, overgrown grave mound. She first appears unnamed as a skinny little girl sitting on a stool during the great battles that shook the capital.Chapter 314 (1) She steals and sells books, and eventually lives in the courtyard of the boy [[Cao Qinglang]], where Chen Ping'an is staying. When the master of the Lotus Flower Blessed Land, an old Daoist priest, plucks the sun from the sky in front of her, her eyes are seared with pain. Looking at her, he recognises her identity: she is a "Go piece" secretly planted in his blessed land by the old scholar ([[Scholarly Sage]]), who had won from him a token and a promise to protect whoever held it.Chapter 321 (1) When Chen Ping'an leaves the blessed land, the old Daoist reaches into the air and drags Pei Qian out after him, leaving her face-down on the road.Chapter 327 (2) == Plot == === Journey Through Parasol Leaf Continent === On the road north, Pei Qian complains constantly, lies, tries to wheedle money out of Chen Ping'an, and kills butterflies and insects when he is not looking. Chen Ping'an genuinely detests her and refuses to teach her even his walking meditation.Chapter 329 (1) When she foolishly stares at a ghostly wedding procession, he protects her, and when they must escape through a dangerous mountain, she runs several kilometres with talismans in both hands. Her stamina surprises Chen Ping'an, and the translator notes that her name is a pun on "losing money".Chapter 329 (2) At Fox Town, she lies about borrowing money and stealing a kite, and accuses Chen Ping'an of preferring Cao Qinglang to her. Zhong Kui first notices her remarkable eyes.Chapter 337 (2) Later, at the Burial River's water residence, a water goddess offers her a treasure in exchange for the book Chen Ping'an makes her read. Pei Qian silently refuses to give it up. Chen Ping'an tells her it is fine, and she bursts into tears, apologising to him on his back as they leave.Chapter 347 (3) From then on, she gradually changes. Chen Ping'an's four companions from the blessed land, [[Zhu Lian]], [[Wei Xian]], [[Lu Baixiang]] and [[Sui Youbian]], join them. Pei Qian spends years watching them, learning Go rules, music and cooking from them, and pestering them for martial arts lessons. === Old Dragon City and Beyond === At [[Old Dragon City]], Chen Ping'an apologises to her for wrongly blaming her in an earlier quarrel over a pancake. Pei Qian is moved and tells him she no longer wants to explore the world now that she has met him.Chapter 362 (2) He makes her write transcriptions every day, and she slowly comes to do them willingly. He also teaches her A'Liang's Eighteen Stops breathing technique, which she picks up with astonishing speed.Chapter 377 She meets [[Cui Dongshan]], whom she nicknames the "big white goose" and grudgingly accepts as her "senior brother", then travels with Chen Ping'an through the Azure Phoenix Nation. At Mountain Cliff Academy, she befriends [[Li Huai]], who believes her lost-princess stories and loses to her in a treasure showdown. She also comes to worship [[Li Baoping]], whose mountains of transcriptions humble her. When she finally gets her hands on her own savings, she spends them on a present for her master. === Downtrodden Mountain and Dragon Riding Alley === Chen Ping'an leaves her at [[Downtrodden Mountain]] with Zhu Lian while he goes to Bamboo Scroll Lake. She spends years running the shops on Dragon Riding Alley, scaring customers by putting her head on the counter, and avoiding Cui Cheng, who believes Chen Ping'an is wasting her talent. When Chen Ping'an becomes the strongest fifth-tier martial artist and receives a jewel of martial fortune, he gives it straight to Pei Qian, and it vanishes into her hands.Chapter 466 (2) Chen Ping'an enrols her in the private school in the small town, which she resists with every delaying tactic she can bargain for.Chapter 483 (2) While he is away on [[Northern Complete Reed Continent]], she takes charge of the little water monster [[Zhou Mili]], whom Chen Ping'an had sent to Downtrodden Mountain, and makes her a loyal follower and "right guardian".Chapter 513 (4) === Cui Cheng's Disciple === After Zhu Lian takes her back to the Southern Garden Nation, Pei Qian climbs to the second floor of the bamboo building for the first time and asks Cui Cheng to teach her. He asks why, and she replies that there is one person she absolutely cannot lose to. That person is Cao Qinglang. Cui Cheng accepts her as his direct disciple.Chapter 522 (4) She leaves the private school and endures beatings as savage as her master's, being carried down to medicinal baths by [[Chen Nuanshu]] and [[Zhou Mili]], then insisting on writing her transcriptions anyway. Eventually, she lands a punch on Cui Cheng that makes him dodge. Before his death, Cui Cheng takes her on a long journey through the Lotus Root Blessed Land, encouraging her to face her fears and telling her that the Bodhisattvas did hear her prayers, by sending Chen Ping'an to her. When she finds him dead in the Heart Manifestation Temple, her Deity Drumming fist intent stirs his one last time. Half of his martial fortune is left for her, and she accepts it with trembling hands.Chapter 560 (3) She refuses to leave the blessed land until Chen Ping'an returns, then weeps in his arms. === Later Events === Pei Qian reaches the fourth tier, though Cui Cheng had complained that her progress was like a crawling tortoise. Cui Dongshan worries that her rapid breakthroughs and inherited fortune draw attention, and Wei Bo hides her from prying eyes.Chapter 567 (1) Chen Ping'an promises that once she reaches her fifth-tier bottleneck, she may travel on her own, with the little donkey he promised her, and decide whether to take Li Huai along. She visits Mountain Cliff Academy with him, where Li Baoping hands her the title of alliance leader of the martial arts world, to Li Huai's horror. == Abilities == * '''Eyes of the sun and moon:''' Ever since the old Daoist plucked the sun from the sky in front of her, her eyes have held the light of the sun and moon. She can see spirits invisible to others, stare at the sun without pain, and read people's hearts. At times her eyes cause her agony. * '''Martial arts:''' She has extraordinary aptitude. Zhu Lian considers her talent beyond the Five Elements, and she learns techniques simply by watching. As of ch. 567 she is a fourth-tier pure martial artist, trained in Cui Cheng's Deity Drumming Technique, and she holds half of his martial fortune as well as the jewel of martial fortune Chen Ping'an gave her. * '''Eighteen Stops:''' A'Liang's breathing technique, which she learned quickly. * '''Deranged Demon Sword Techniques:''' her "self-created" and wildly flailing sword style, performed with her hiking pole. == Possessions == * '''Hiking pole''': her most cherished item, which she lets no one touch. * '''Bamboo sword and saber''': made for her by Chen Ping'an. * '''Little bamboo bookcase.''' * '''Treasure Pagoda Demon-Suppressing Talisman''': which she keeps stuck to her forehead. * '''Nine-grid treasure box''': gifted by the Yao Clan's Yao Jinzhi, filled with a wooden ganoderma, rare coins, a Daoist badge and an osmanthus branch. * '''Embroidered pouch''': from Lady Gui of Old Dragon City, used as her money pouch. ==Trivia== * 裴钱 (Péi Qián) is a homonym of 赔钱 (péi qián), meaning "losing money", which is ironic given her love of it. * She detested Go because players take turns instead of placing several stones at once. ==References==

Scholarly Sage lineage |Continent=[[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]] |Region=[[Jewel Small World]] |Cultivation_rank=Upper Five Tiers (Confucian sage) |Novel=Chapter 6 |Donghua=Episode 1 }} '''Qi Jingchun''', known to the people of the small town simply as '''Mr. Qi''', was the schoolteacher of the town in [[Jewel Small World]] and a disciple of the [[Scholarly Sage]]. Outside the town he was the mountain master of Mountain Cliff Academy and a Confucian sage of the Upper Five Tiers. He spent his last years keeping the town safe and died holding off the powers that came to break it. == Appearance == Qi Jingchun is a middle-aged scholar with graying sideburns.Chapter 61 He dresses plainly in a scholar's robe, often an azure one, and keeps his hair in a bun held by an ordinary green jade hairpin that once belonged to his teacher. People in town found him quiet and a little dull, and most of the time he carries a calm, faint smile. In the days before his death his hair went gray very quickly, and by the end it had turned completely white.Chapter 68 When his soul leaves his body, it takes the form of an immortal in flowing white robes. == Personality == Qi Jingchun is gentle, patient and very hard to provoke. Bai Yuan, the Mountain-Moving Ape, insulted and humiliated him again and again, and he simply let it pass. He would rather explain than argue, and he treats the poorest boy in Clay Vase Alley with the same courtesy he shows visiting nobles. He once told [[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]] that he, too, had started out as a poor village youth who made up his mind to read.Chapter 24 Under that softness sits a will that does not bend. When [[Zhi Gui]] tested him, he made her kowtow three times. When the four great powers came for their treasures and his enemies closed in, he could have saved himself by giving up the town, but he chose to stay. He is also far sharper than he lets on. His teacher said he beat the Scholarly Sage himself at Go not long after learning the game, and he saw through the trap laid for him well before it was sprung. He does not judge people by where they come from. Having traveled widely with his senior brother [[Zuo You]], he knew there were hypocrites among scholars and admirable people among demons, and he treated the great demon Liu Chicheng with a fairness that surprised even Liu himself. == Background == === Mountain Cliff Academy === Qi Jingchun was one of the Scholarly Sage's disciples, alongside [[Cui Chan]] and [[Zuo You]]. Before sending him to Mountain Cliff Academy, his teacher told him that one must never stop learning and that the student should surpass the teacher, which showed how much hope the old man placed in him.Chapter 67 (2) He rose to become the mountain master of the academy, one of the three schools and seventy-two academies of Confucianism. Confucian sages normally have one kindred character, a word that adds a sliver to the sage's cultivation every time someone writes or speaks it. Qi Jingchun had two: "Tranquil" and "Spring". Their weight was so great that he was banished to the sealed small world of the town because of them.Chapter 58 === The small town === Qi Jingchun guarded the town for 59 years.Chapter 23 He worked as its schoolteacher the whole time, and the townsfolk never realized that every teacher who had come and gone over the years was the same man.Chapter 22 A regal jade tablet, left by one of the Second Sages, sat on his desk and anchored the formation over the town. While it remained, he could see everything that happened inside the small world. When a secret letter told him his teacher had been humiliated and had "passed away", he wept alone at his desk and blamed himself for doing nothing while he clung to his post.Chapter 11 The Scholarly Sage was in fact still alive. During the final months he quietly arranged a future for the town's children. He took Chen Ping'an to the old locust tree and asked it for a leaf carrying the character "Yao". Later he gave the boy his jade hairpin as a farewell gift, along with four seals. He carved a spring seal for [[Zhao Yao]], his book boy, and left six books for [[Song Jixin]]. When Chen Ping'an struck down [[Cai Jinjian]] in an alley and nearly killed [[Fu Nanhua]], Qi Jingchun stepped in. He sent Fu Nanhua away from the small world with a gift of opportunity, and he brought Cai Jinjian back to life, then sat with her in the school and talked about everyday things like the price of rice and oil before answering questions about her cultivation that even her master could not.Chapter 253 (2) He also arranged an excursion to Mountain Cliff Academy for his last five students, the trip the old janitor [[Ma Zhan]] later led in his place. Ma Zhan, who counted as half a disciple of the same teacher, betrayed him, and the Scholarly Sage later said this hurt Little Qi more than all of Cui Chan's schemes. === Death === The fall of the town was a trap. Cui Chan set the board and used Chen Ping'an as one of his pieces, while Lu Chen, walking the town as a young Daoist priest, was the real crux of the plot and hoped to cut off the Scholarly Sage's lineage for good.Chapter 405 Qi Jingchun had worked most of this out but would not change course. When the end came, he refused to call on his full power, knowing it would tear the town apart and could sink Eastern Treasured Vial Continent into the sea. He fought the celestial immortals who came for him with nothing but his two kindred characters and held out until

pages.title: Qi Jinglong
pages.content:
{{Character |header1=Qi Jinglong |Aliases=Liu Jinglong
Terrestrial Flood Dragon |Vital_status=Alive |Gender=Male |Species=Human |Disciple(s)=[[Bai Shou]] |Friend(s)=[[Chen Ping An]] |Occupation=Sword cultivator
Direct disciple of the Great Emblem Sword Sect’s ancestral hall |Current_affiliation(s)=Great Emblem Sword Sect
[[Northern Complete Reed Continent]] |Continent=[[Northern Complete Reed Continent]] |Cultivation_rank=Nascent Tier
Sword Immortal |Novel=Chapter 523 }} == Appearance == Qi Jinglong is an elegant and refined young man who dresses in Confucian robes rather than the garb of an ordinary sword cultivator, and he carries no visible sword when traveling outside the mountains, relying instead on a single bonded flying sword and illusion techniques to disguise his true cultivation.Chapter 523Chapter 524 == Personality == He speaks with calm conviction and genuinely enjoys debating principles and philosophy rather than showing off his strength, to the point that Chen Ping’an felt he could easily have passed for a Confucian scholar even though he isn’t one.Chapter 523 He dislikes drinking wine and considers persuading others to drink a mark against his own character, though he can be talked into a sip or two.Chapter 523 As a teacher he is patient and even-tempered, never holding his disciple’s shortcomings against him and preferring to let him compare himself against his own past self rather than against others.Chapter 596 He keeps his word without fail, a trait his disciple grudgingly admits is his one unambiguously good quality, and he genuinely dislikes being too narrow-minded or small about money and favors.Chapter 596 == Background == Qi Jinglong’s name in the genealogical records of the Great Emblem Sword Sect’s ancestral hall is actually Liu Jinglong, a matter he considers a private clan affair he prefers not to explain to outsiders. Known as the Terrestrial Flood Dragon of the Northern Complete Reed Continent, he was not born with innate sword talent and his own Dao mentor was only a middling Dragon Gate Tier sword cultivator whose Great Dao eventually decayed with age. His true Dao guardian was instead an older senior sister who had been stuck at the peak of the Golden Core Tier since before Qi Jinglong even entered the mountains, and whom he personally helped save from a crisis that nearly drove her to demonic cultivation, suffering severe wounds of his own in the process. Despite the odds against him, the sect took the unusual step of naming him a direct disciple of its ancestral hall once he reached the Abode Tier, a decision that was eventually proven correct many times over.Chapter 526 Qi Jinglong first crossed paths with Chen Ping’an and his disciple Sui Jingcheng by a riverside pavilion in the Northern Complete Reed Continent, where the two debated at length over the nature of strength, rules, and whether might could ever truly be called right. Chen Ping’an came away deeply impressed, bowing to him with full Confucian courtesy even though Qi Jinglong held no formal standing in any Confucian school, and privately hoping that Cao Qinglang might grow up to think in a similarly balanced way.Chapter 523Chapter 524 At the time he held Nascent Tier cultivation and was ranked third among the Northern Complete Reed Continent’s top ten young cultivators, a tier below the continent’s top two prodigies and well ahead of peers such as Gu Mo and Rong Chang.Chapter 524Chapter 526 When Deer Cutter Mountain made repeated attempts on Chen Ping’an’s life, Qi Jinglong intervened and negotiated a deal with the mountain’s master, agreeing that the master’s young assassin apprentice would become his own disciple if a final assassination attempt failed. The boy, later known as Bai Shou, did fail and was bound by the agreement, cursing his new master even as he reluctantly accepted him, in no small part because his old master had clearly wanted this outcome for him all along.Chapter 536 Qi Jinglong later solidified his standing as a sword immortal of the Northern Complete Reed Continent through three consecutive sword duels forced upon him by other cultivators, including one against Sword Immortal Li Cai of Duckweed Sword Lake, emerging from the battles with his Sword Dao measurably strengthened. The Great Emblem Sword Sect’s sect leader, Han Huaizi, openly spoke of wanting to help him ascend even further, hoping Qi Jinglong might one day become the sect’s first Ascension Tier sword immortal.Chapter 582 He later traveled with [[Bai Shou]] to Stalactite Mountain aboard Osmanthus Island, posing as an ordinary traveling scholar and his attendant, quietly fending off at least two groups secretly tailing them without ever revealing his full strength or raising concern. During the trip he secured a Sword Nurturing Gourd for Bai Shou as a gift befitting a new direct disciple of the sect’s ancestral hall.Chapter 595Chapter 596 == Trivia == * Despite being a renowned sword immortal, he is afraid of ghostly apparitions in water, having once gone pale with fright after a corpse-like face surfaced from a clump of river grass.Chapter 593 * He purchased a replica sword called Lightning Devourer from Hatred Sword Mountain for Bai Shou.Chapter 571 * Though he appears young, cultivators who reach his level live far longer than ordinary mortals, and he jokingly told Sui Jingcheng his true age would put him in his eighties by mortal reckoning.Chapter 523 == References ==

pages.title: Qi Refinement
pages.content:
Qi refinement is a fundamental practice in the sources, involving the manipulation and cultivation of spiritual energy, or Qi, to achieve higher levels of power and longevity.

'''Core Principles''':

* '''Qi as the Foundation''': Qi is seen as the basic building block of life and cultivation. Cultivators manipulate their own Qi and the Qi of the world to gain power.
* '''Body as a Vessel''': The physical body is viewed as a vessel for Qi, which must be strengthened and refined to support higher levels of cultivation.
* '''Mind and Will''': Cultivating the mind is also an important component of Qi refinement.
* '''Acupoints and Meridians''': Acupoints are key locations in the body that serve as pathways for Qi. Opening and refining acupoints is crucial for absorbing and storing spiritual energy. Meridians are like paths for the flow of Qi and the wider and stronger they are, the better.
* '''External vs. Internal''': Qi refiners may draw Qi from within themselves or from the outside world.
* '''Balance and Harmony''': The goal of Qi refinement is to balance internal and external energies, to nurture and refine Qi.

'''Tiers of Qi Refinement''':

* The sources describe a tiered system of Qi refinement, generally divided into '''Lower, Middle, and Upper Five Tiers'''.
* '''Lower Five Tiers''': Also known as the '''Mountain Ascending Five Tiers''', these tiers focus on refining the body. They are the Copper Skin Tier, Grass Root Tier, Willow Tendon Tier, Bone Qi Tier, and Furnace Molding Tier.
** The first four tiers focus on cultivating the flesh and nurturing a tough physique.
** At the peak stage of the Mud Molding Tier, one's Qi descends to their Dantian.
** The final tier of the Physique Refining Tier is the Mercury Tier, where one's blood becomes like mercury.
* '''Middle Five Tiers''': These tiers are the Cave Abode Tier, the Sea Observation Tier, the Dragon Gate Tier, the Golden Core Tier, and the Nascent Tier.
** The '''Golden Core Tier''' marks a significant step, where a cultivator's sea of Qi condenses into a golden core. This allows them to store more energy, and even borrow spiritual energy from heaven and earth.
** After reaching the Golden Core Tier, one is regarded as a genuine immortal.
* '''Upper Five Tiers''': The sources mention the '''Unpolished Jade Tier''' as a level of great accomplishment, where cultivators return to a state of natural simplicity.
** At the Unpolished Jade Tier, one's body is like gold and jade, resistant to natural elements, and one can enjoy a lifespan of 500 to 1000 years.
** Female Qi refiners at this tier are said to have the ability to beautify themselves without detrimentally affecting their fate.
** Those at the Upper Five Tiers are much more flexible and free than those at the Nascent Tier.
* There is also mention of an '''11th tier''', but this is not discussed in detail in the sources.

'''Methods and Practices''':

* '''Meditation and Breathing''': Specific breathing techniques are used to gather and refine Qi.
* '''Acupoint Development''': Activating and refining acupoints allows for increased absorption of spiritual energy.
* '''Visualization''': Visualization is an important component of cultivation, especially for cultivators of Dawn Cloud Mountain.
* '''Scriptures and Mantras''':  These can help guide the flow of Qi and enhance cultivation.
* '''Talismans''': Drawing talismans is a way to channel spiritual energy for various purposes.
* '''Sword Qi''': Qi can be imbued into swords, with sword cultivators focusing on both sword techniques and refining the sword.

'''Challenges and Obstacles''':

* '''Internal Demons''': Cultivators must overcome their inner demons, which can hinder progress.
* '''Tribulations''':  Cultivators face tribulations or challenges at various stages, and these must be overcome to advance.
* '''Impurity''': Over time, impurities can accumulate and obstruct the pursuit of the Great Dao.
* '''Qi Deviation''': Incorrect methods can lead to Qi deviation, which can severely damage a cultivator.
* '''Bottlenecks''': There are difficulties in advancing to higher tiers.
* '''External Interference''': Some cultivators can be harmed by others.

'''Key Concepts''':

* '''Dao Heart''':  Those with a strong Dao Heart, aspiring to the Dao, will be able to progress more quickly in their cultivation.
* '''Fated Opportunities''': Cultivators may encounter fated opportunities, which can accelerate their growth.
* '''Mental Cultivation''': Mental cultivation is just as important as the development of one's powers.
* '''The Great Dao''': This is the ultimate goal of cultivation, but there are many different paths to achieving it.
* '''Longevity''': Qi refinement can allow cultivators to extend their lifespans.
* '''Inner World''':  Cultivators can create a small world within their bodies, like a blessed land.

'''Heritage''': The concept of heritage, which is an intangible concept that's impossible to explain, seems to be connected to Qi refinement.

'''Differences from Martial Arts''':

* '''Qi Refiners''': Rely on the bestowal of the heavens, and their progress is often linked to luck and fated opportunities. They focus on nurturing and refining Qi.
* '''Martial Artists''': Progress step-by-step and rely on breaking through obstacles. They focus on tempering Qi and converting the auras in their acupoints.
* Qi refiners focus on the body only as a vessel, while martial artists focus on the body as a tool.
* Martial artists and Qi refiners take virtually the exact opposite route when it comes to qi refinement.
* Qi refiners at the lower tiers focus on refining their body, which overlaps with martial arts training.

'''Tools and Resources''':

* '''Flying Swords''': Swords are a way to channel Qi, and swordsmen often refine their swords.
* '''Talisman Paper''': Talisman cultivators need to use large amounts of talisman paper.
* '''Immortal Treasures''': These can greatly enhance cultivation, with some being linked to the five elements.
* '''Jade Slips''': These can contain powerful mantras and provide insights into cultivation.
* '''Bonded Items''':  Refining items to become bonded items is an important step in cultivation, and it allows for the storage of spiritual energy.

Qi refinement is a complex and multifaceted practice that involves the manipulation of spiritual energy to achieve greater power, longevity, and understanding of the Great Dao. It is a core element of the world depicted in the sources, with its own set of practices, challenges, and goals. The tiered system, various cultivation methods, and the distinction between Qi refiners and martial artists all contribute to the rich tapestry of this fictional world.

pages.title: Red Candle Town
pages.content:
Red Candle Town is a bustling and complex location within the narrative, serving as a significant point of transit and a microcosm of the larger world.

'''Location and Geography:'''

* '''Three Rivers:''' Red Candle Town is situated at the confluence of three rivers: '''Rushing Tranquil River''', '''Embroidered Flower River''', and '''Fine Wine River'''. This location makes it a busy hub for river traffic.
* '''Near Go Table Mountain:''' It's located near Go Table Mountain, and is close to the border of the mountain.
* '''Border Town''': It is near the border of the Great Li Empire.
* '''Former Jewel Small World:''' Red Candle Town is located near where Jewel Small World landed after it fell.
* '''South of Great Li Empire:''' Red Candle Town is situated to the south of the Great Li Empire.

'''Transportation and Trade:'''

* '''Busy Dock:''' Red Candle Town has a busy dock with numerous ships coming and going. It serves as a major point of transit for goods from all corners of the Great Li Empire.
* '''Relay Station:''' The town features a relay station called the Pillow Relay Station, which serves as a place for travelers and officials to stay.
* '''Official Post Road:''' The town is located on one of the three main post roads leading from the southern regions of the Great Li Empire to the capital. This makes it a vital stop for merchants, officials, and scholars.
* '''Escort Boats:''' There are escort boats that are available for travel, and the town has many merchant ships.
* '''Fu Inlet''': There is an inlet called the Fu Inlet where many decorative boats dock.

'''Commerce and Entertainment:'''

* '''Street Market:''' The town has a street market on the west side, offering a variety of goods and trinkets.
* '''Night Market:''' Red Candle Town is known for its lively night market.
* '''Taverns and Wine Shops''': There are many wine shops and taverns in town.
* '''Decorated Boats:''' The town is known for its decorated boats, which are unique to the area. These boats offer entertainment and companionship.
* '''Brothels:''' The town has brothels with hostesses and prostitutes, some of whom are managed by the capital's Imperial Music Office.
* '''Bookstores''': There are bookstores in Red Candle Town, including one known for its high prices and eccentric owner.
* '''Variety of Goods''': Red Candle Town has a wide variety of goods available for sale, including medicinal ingredients, ointments, and more.

'''Culture and Society:'''

* '''No Curfew:''' Red Candle Town does not have a curfew.
* '''Diverse Population:''' The town's population includes merchants, officials, scholars, and people from various backgrounds.
* '''Stories and Legends:''' The town has its own local stories and legends.
* '''Temples:''' There are two temples, a Wenchang pavilion and a martial sage temple.

'''Notable Features:'''

* '''Beacon Towers:''' The town has beacon towers, that are used to signal messages.
* '''River Gods:''' Two river gods are worshipped in shrines along the riverbanks.
* '''Fu Inlet:''' A crescent-shaped river bend is where the decorated boats are found.
* '''A Money Sink''': Fu Inlet is known to be a money sink due to the cost of the entertainment provided there.
* '''Unique Local Products:''' The town is known for its apricot blossom wine.

'''Political and Historical Context:'''

* '''Former Jewel Small World:''' It is near the location where the Jewel Small World fell, which gives it a unique historical context.
* '''Great Li Empire:''' Red Candle Town is part of the Great Li Empire, and the empire's influence is felt in the town’s administration and culture.
* '''Imperial Music Office''': The Imperial Music Office manages some of the boat hostesses and prostitutes, indicating the town's connection to the empire's central government.
* '''Mountain Lord Wei Bo''': A mountain lord of Go Table Mountain protected the ancestors of Red Candle Town's residents, but was later demoted for it.
* '''Site of conflict:''' Red Candle Town is the location of a conflict between a palace minister and a swordsman.

'''Specific Individuals and Groups:'''

* '''Cheng Sheng:''' The relay station deputy at the Pillow Relay Station, who assists travelers and is familiar with the town.
* '''A’Liang:''' He is familiar with Red Candle Town, particularly the area around the two river banks.
* '''Li Jin''': A man who has lived in the town for two hundred years, and is familiar with the waterways and customs.
* '''Old Man Yang''': A man who came to the town with a travel diary and is familiar with the history of the town.
* '''Officials and Scholars:''' Many officials and scholars pass through Red Candle Town on their way to the capital.

'''Challenges and Problems:'''

* '''Corruption:''' The possibility of corruption within the town's administration is implied.
* '''Uneven Application of Law:'''  The application of laws may vary depending on the type of officials, with scholars being more strict and martial artists being more lenient.
* '''Potential for Trouble:''' The presence of various types of people, including merchants, officials, and possibly unsavory characters, creates the potential for conflicts and problems.
* '''Ghosts''': There are rumors of ghosts in Red Candle Town who have driven some people insane.

Red Candle Town is a vibrant and crucial location, serving as a nexus for trade, travel, and cultural exchange within the Great Li Empire. Its unique geographical position, combined with its bustling economy and diverse population, make it a significant setting in the narrative.

== Appearance ==
Ruan Qiong is a tall, broad-shouldered man.

== Personality ==
Ruan Qiong is direct and unyielding. He does not grant special treatment to those he considers unworthy of it and holds firm under pressure, as shown during the Great Mo Villa incident when he refused to yield even while severely injured.Chapter 95 He enforces his own rules without exception, killing cultivators who violated the no-fly rule in Dragon Spring Prefecture on his first day as overseer and continuing to do so afterward.Chapter 74Chapter 420

He is selective about disciples and places character above talent. He turned down cultivators sent by the imperial court who he felt lacked the right qualities, and half of his unofficial disciples eventually left for Sun Scorch Mountain.Chapter 641 He declined to take Chen Ping'an as a disciple not because of any personal failing on Chen Ping'an's part, but because they are not walking the same path.Chapter 286

Despite his stern exterior, Ruan Qiong is capable of warmth in private. He visited Old Man Yang with a bottle of wine and found the company better than he had expected.Chapter 428 He secretly travelled to Downtrodden Mountain to watch Ruan Xiu meet with Chen Ping'an, then claimed to Wei Bo that he had only been taking a stroll.Chapter 460

His deepest ambition is to forge a truly living sword, one capable of cultivation, death, and reincarnation, something no swordsmith before him has achieved.Chapter 291

== Background ==
Ruan Qiong was formerly affiliated with Wind Snow Temple and forged swords for its members before leaving to establish his own sect.

When Qi Jingchun died, Ruan Qiong became the overseer of Jewel Small World, a role backed by the Yingyin Chen Clan.Chapter 85 On the first day he took up the post, he killed cultivators who violated the rules he had set, making clear from the outset that no exceptions would be made.

The Great Mo Villa incident took place while he was still a 9th-tier cultivator. A terrestrial sword immortal expected Ruan Qiong to step aside and queue-jumped in front of him. Ruan Qiong refused. The sword immortal attacked, injuring Ruan Qiong severely, but Ruan Qiong did not back down. The sword immortal was ultimately detained.

He later left Jewel Small World and founded Dragon Spring Sword Sect at Divine Elegance Mountain in Dragon Spring Prefecture on the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent. His three opening disciples included Dong Gu, a former mountain creature who became the sect's first Golden Core cultivator, and Xu Xiaoqiao, known as Third Senior Sister.Chapter 283 The imperial court of Great Li sent twelve unofficial disciples to train under him, though Ruan Qiong's standards meant not all remained.

He enforced a strict no-fly rule across Dragon Spring Prefecture and wounded or killed those who broke it, including Cao Jun. Dragon Spring Prefecture came to be regarded as a forbidden area, and Ruan Qiong was considered the undisputed top-tier guest elder of the Great Li Empire across two successive reigns.Chapter 533

Among the swords he forged for Chen Ping'an was one called Subduing Demons, which Chen Ping'an used against a flood dragon.Chapter 262 Ruan Qiong has vowed to one day forge a sword unlike anything that has come before.

== Trivia ==
* At the time of his confrontation at Great Mo Villa, Ruan Qiong was a 9th-tier cultivator. By the time he founded Dragon Spring Sword Sect, he had reached the 11th tier.Chapter 254
* He is widely regarded as the finest swordsmith on the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent.Chapter 94
* When Ruan Xiu and Chen Ping'an met at Downtrodden Mountain, Ruan Qiong watched from a distance and asked Wei Bo afterward whether Chen Ping'an was blind.

== References ==
