== Appearance ==

Ruan Xiu is a young woman with a slender build and an appearance described as unforgettable by those who meet her.Chapter 420 She typically wears green clothes and keeps her hair in a ponytail. Despite her slight frame, she has a famously large appetite, particularly for sweets and desserts.

When perceived through spiritual sight, she appears radically different from her unassuming exterior. [[Pei Qian]], who could see the true nature of people, once saw Ruan Xiu as a vast sea of bright red flames with the figure of a regal woman holding a radiant sun at its center.Chapter 460

== Personality ==

Ruan Xiu is quiet and easygoing on the surface. At Dragon Spring Sword Sect, she is amicable to everyone but genuinely close with no one, preferring to sit apart eating desserts while the other disciples train. She routinely shirks her duties at the sect, showing little interest in the formalities of her position despite being called "Senior Sister Ruan" by the other disciples.

Beneath this relaxed demeanor is a person of deep feeling who keeps her emotions private. When a young girl once asked her if she had someone she liked, she answered simply, "I do. He's always in my heart."Chapter 631 She is not one for grand declarations or dramatic gestures, preferring to express care through quiet, practical actions, such as looking after Chen Ping'an's shop and even his hens while he was away on his travels.Chapter 180

She possesses a stubborn streak inherited from her father. In her youth, she went into town to help Chen Ping'an despite [[Ruan Qiong]] explicitly forbidding it.Chapter 63 She is also direct when it matters. When a persistent admirer tried to win her affection with gifts and gestures, she refused him plainly without entertaining the attention.Chapter 94

== Background ==

Ruan Xiu is the daughter of [[Ruan Qiong]], the Militarian Sage and one of the greatest swordsmiths in the world. She originally grew up at Wind Snow Temple before her father relocated to the Jewel Small World. Ruan Qiong's decision to leave was partly motivated by a desire to protect his daughter, whose extraordinary innate talent made her a potential target for dangerous forces.

Ruan Xiu was born with a fire god constitution, making water her natural enemy, and she carries a fire dragon bracelet. She is considered a one-in-a-thousand-year talent. Her constitution grants her a unique way of perceiving the world: she can see the purity of a person's mind, their karmic fate, and their fortune, and the world itself appears to her in different colors depending on these qualities.

She first encountered Chen Ping'an on Azure Cow Ridge in the Jewel Small World.Chapter 40 What drew her attention to him was the extraordinary purity of his mind, which she could perceive through her innate abilities.Chapter 46 Over time, she grew close to him in her own reserved way, looking after his affairs while he traveled far from home.

When Chen Ping'an was preparing to leave on his journey, Ruan Xiu asked her father to let her help forge his sword, but Ruan Qiong refused.Chapter 198 She later delivered the finished sword to Chen Ping'an at [[Downtrodden Mountain]], along with a bag of peach cakes, as a quiet farewell.Chapter 204

After Dragon Spring Sword Sect was established, Ruan Xiu took on the role of senior disciple in practice if not in formal title. She later traveled south alongside Great Li sticky rod officials and resolved matters at Bamboo Scroll Lake through her own power and ability, without needing to resort to fighting.Chapter 478

Years later, when she and Chen Ping'an met again at Downtrodden Mountain, she addressed the unspoken tension between them directly. She told him, "The way I like you is not the way that you think I like you," and they parted on clear terms as friends. Her father Ruan Qiong, who had been waiting at the foot of the mountain and claimed he was merely "taking a stroll," said nothing about the conversation.

In later years, Ruan Xiu traveled north to the former Central Mountain territory to negotiate on behalf of Dragon Spring Sword Sect, handling sect affairs with quiet competence despite her reputation for avoiding responsibilities.Chapter 641

== Trivia ==

* Ruan Xiu's enormous appetite is a running detail throughout the story. She is especially fond of desserts and peach cakes, and [[Cui Dongshan]] was once noted to be visibly nervous around her when she had sweets in hand.Chapter 455
* Despite telling Chen Ping'an that her feelings were not what he assumed, she later confirmed to a young girl that she does have someone she likes, saying he is "always in my heart."
* Her fire god constitution means she perceives the world in a fundamentally different way from ordinary cultivators, seeing people and their fates as colors and light.
* Before leaving on his journey, Chen Ping'an considered leaving Immortal Herb Mountain in Ruan Xiu's care if he could not return.Chapter 84

== References ==

pages.title: Savage World
pages.content:
The Savage World is a distinct and dangerous realm, characterized by its harsh environment and the powerful demons that inhabit it. It is in constant conflict with the Majestic World, particularly with the sword cultivators of the Sword Qi Great Wall.

'''Geographic and Environmental Characteristics''':

* The Savage World is located '''south of the Sword Qi Great Wall'''. This wall serves as a border between the Savage and Majestic Worlds.
* It has a '''harsh environment with thin spiritual energy''', making it difficult for beings to cultivate. This is in stark contrast to the Majestic World, which has more abundant spiritual energy.
* The Savage World is described as a '''breeding ground for powerful demons''' due to its unforgiving nature.

'''Inhabitants and Their Nature''':

* The primary inhabitants are '''demons''', who are physically powerful and skilled in battle.
* These demons are characterized by their '''recklessness, violence, and lack of benevolence, righteousness, or morality'''. Reason is not effective in this world, and might makes right.
* They are driven by their need for survival and expansion and are constantly seeking ways to invade the Majestic World.
* It's mentioned that '''demon prodigies seem to be in hiding''', which is unusual and suggests the Savage World is planning something significant.

'''Conflict with the Majestic World''':

* The Savage World is in '''constant conflict''' with the Majestic World.
* The demons frequently launch attacks on the '''Sword Qi Great Wall''', which acts as a crucial defense for the Majestic World.
* The demons view the Majestic World as a '''source of resources''', comparing it to "a big piece of fatty meat". They seek to expand their territory and take the resources of the Majestic World for their own survival.
* The fighting is extremely brutal, and it is said that '''"everything is settled by the sharpness of one's sword or the hardness of one's fists"'''.

'''Unique Celestial Features''':

* The Savage World is distinguished by its night sky having '''three moons''': one full, one half-full, and one crescent. This is a unique feature that separates it from the Majestic World, which has one moon.

'''Lack of Reason''':

* In the Savage World, '''reason does not work''', and normal moral standards are nonexistent. This contributes to its violent and chaotic nature.

'''Training Ground for Swordsmen:''' Despite the dangers, the Savage World serves as a training ground for sword cultivators. By fighting in this harsh environment, they temper their sword dao and grow stronger.

'''No United Front''': The sources indicate that the rulers of the Savage World haven't considered combining their power to overcome the Sword Qi Great Wall.

The Savage World is a realm of '''intense conflict and brutal power dynamics'''. It is a hostile and desolate place, populated by powerful demons who seek to conquer the Majestic World. The lack of morality and reason, combined with the constant violence, makes it a highly dangerous place. Despite this, the Savage World plays a crucial role in the story as a constant threat and a training ground for sword cultivators from the Majestic World.

pages.content:

'''Contains Spoilers'''

The '''Scholarly Sage''', usually called '''the old scholar''', is a [[Confucianism|Confucian]] sage who was once the fourth most revered sage in the Confucian temples, after the Supreme Sage, the [[Etiquette Sage]] and the [[Second Sage]]. After losing a secret contest of doctrines known as the "battle between third and fourth", his statues were demoted and finally smashed, his works were banned and burned across the seventy-two academies, and he imprisoned himself in the [[Forest of Virtue]] to await death.

He is the teacher of [[Cui Chan]], [[Zuo You]] and [[Qi Jingchun]]. After Qi Jingchun's death, he acknowledges [[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]] as his final, "closing" disciple. Though he looks like a short, shabby, wine-loving old man who would rather argue than fight, he is one of the most formidable figures in the world, and his lineage is famed for producing few disciples who are all exceptional.

== Appearance ==
The old scholar is short, skinny and white-haired. He usually wears azure robes and dresses like a poor travelling scholar, with a bundle of luggage wrapped in cotton cloth on his back. Chen Ping'an notes that he looks even more shabby and impoverished than the noble scholar Zhong Kui. He likes to drink other people's wine and feigns drunkenness to avoid paying. Only on rare occasions does he look like a towering sage, such as when he stands against the mountain wind on Tassel Mountain.Chapter 151 His portraits in old books show a dignified, magnificent figure, and the people who meet him in person are often surprised.

== Personality ==
The old scholar is talkative, playful, boastful and openly shameless when it suits him. He is famous for winning arguments. He won a precious token from the old Daoist priest of the Lotus Flower Blessed Land by rolling on the ground and wailing, and he pestered the god of Tassel Mountain for a month to hear him praise his final disciple. When Chen Qingdu asked why he, rather than a more fitting sage, had come to the Sword Qi Great Wall, he answered simply that he was shameless enough.Chapter 579 (1) He is also fiercely protective of his disciples, so much so that others call his whole lineage "unbelievably protective of their own." The old Daoist calls him "the most biased person" he has ever met.

Beneath this, he is a profound thinker. His central idea is the "theory of sequential order", a way of finding the proper order in which to judge any matter. He believes human nature must be educated and guided towards goodness, and that principles do not belong to books alone. He readily admits that Confucian teachings have flaws, and that even a small child can speak reason. Spiritual Master Fire Dragon calls him "unmatched" in his assessment of human nature.

He carries a good deal of guilt. He believes that many of the wrongs that befell his lineage trace back to him, and he regrets having taught his closing disciple so little beyond a few brief sentences and some drunken remarks.Chapter 594 (2)

== Background ==
The old scholar began life as an impoverished, nameless scholar. He spent forty years passing the imperial examinations, and lived in a dilapidated alley on the [[Middle Earth Divine Continent]] with his first disciples, Cui Chan, Zuo You and later Qi Jingchun, so poor that they sometimes dug worms to fish for food. A'Liang also spent time with them. The old scholar later wrote his books and rose to become the Scholarly Sage. At his height he defeated the sages of Buddhism and Daoism in debate, and he once went to the border of two worlds to hurl abuse at the Dao Ancestor's second disciple.

He then lost the "battle between third and fourth" with the Second Sage. As agreed, he imprisoned himself in the Forest of Virtue, watching helplessly as his statues were demoted and smashed. His first disciple Cui Chan betrayed him, and his lineage fell into disarray. When his favourite disciple, Qi Jingchun, died challenging the Heavenly Dao on a distant continent, the old scholar made an unprecedented deal with the sages of every teaching to break his vow. In exchange, he gave up his physical body and his powers as a Confucian sage, and now travels the world as a soul.Chapter 149

== Plot ==
=== Meeting Chen Ping'an ===
The old scholar first appears drifting on a small boat, describing himself to a boatman as "half a teacher" of a certain boy.Chapter 117 (2) He arranges for the young Cui Chan, a split-off half of the imperial preceptor, to become Chen Ping'an's student, and places a restriction on Cui Chan's mind that punishes any ill thought towards Chen Ping'an. Unknown to Cui Chan, Qi Jingchun had already taken Chen Ping'an as a disciple on his teacher's behalf and given him the old scholar's final relic, a jade hairpin.Chapter 148

When the sword spirit, the tall woman in white bound to Chen Ping'an, wants to kill Cui Chan, the old scholar arrives and tries to talk her out of it. She addresses him as the Scholarly Sage and challenges him. He scolds Cui Chan over his betrayal and over Ma Zhan's death, reminding him that he himself taught Cui Chan Go, and that Qi Jingchun once beat Cui Chan but chose not to tell him.

He then fights the sword spirit and Chen Ping'an inside a picture scroll that is also his own consciousness. He conjures an illusion of Tassel Mountain, one of the Five Mountains of the Middle Earth Divine Continent, and stands on its summit while Chen Ping'an unleashes the sword spirit's strikes. One strike splits the mountain, drawing the anger of its golden-armoured god, an old acquaintance whom the old scholar talks into giving his "final disciple" a gift.

At the Autumn Reed Inn, he discusses the Great Dao with Chen Ping'an, Li Baoping and Cui Chan. He sets out his theory of sequential order, explains why Qi Jingchun spared Cui Chan, draws out the shadow of Chen Ping'an's worries from his body, and asks whether Chen Ping'an is willing to follow Qi Jingchun's arrangement and become his disciple.Chapter 154 (2) He takes Chen Ping'an and Li Baoping to bookshops and a tavern, gets drunk on cheap wine, tells them stories about his life, and makes Chen Ping'an carry him home on his back, slapping his head and insisting that youths must drink. Before leaving, he gives Chen Ping'an a silver ingot that is really a sword billet, which he calls "Little Capital" and Chen Ping'an later renames "First". He gently points out to Li Baoping that, as Qi Jingchun's teacher, he is her grandmaster, and accepts her formal bow.Chapter 158 (1)

Chen Ping'an initially declines to become his disciple, feeling unworthy since he was not even a student. The old scholar takes it in good humour.Chapter 232 (1) Qi Jingchun, appearing to Chen Ping'an later, tells him that he regards him as his junior brother regardless.

=== Guarding His Disciple from Afar ===
At the Sword Qi Great Wall, the old scholar appears before the Chen Clan's Chen Chun'an, spinning a small sun in his palm and asking his opinion of "my final disciple", then answering his own question: very good.

In the Lotus Flower Blessed Land, it is revealed that he once won a token from its master, the old Daoist priest, together with a promise that the Daoist would protect whoever held it. The old scholar then secretly planted that "Go piece", [[Pei Qian]], in the blessed land.Chapter 321 (1) He spends a month pestering the god of Tassel Mountain to praise Chen Ping'an.

When the Ascension Tier cultivator [[Du Mao]] attacks Chen Ping'an and Zheng Dafeng at [[Old Dragon City]], the old scholar senses it through divination on Tassel Mountain and rushes over. He freezes the city in time, lectures two disciples of the Second Sage on shame and justice, and agrees to clean up the mess in exchange for a golden jade pendant from an almighty figure in the heavens. When that figure lingers, the old scholar threatens to explain how he really lost the battle between third and fourth, then bites the pendant to check that it is real.Chapter 365 (2) He beats a young Daoist priest who had a hand in the trouble with a tree branch, and finds his second disciple Zuo You, who had been nearby, then lets him go to the Sword Qi Great Wall as he had always wanted.

Through the Zhao Clan's yin soul, he passes on the Parasol Leaf Sect's compensation to Chen Ping'an, including Du Mao's Ascension Tier fragments, and gives him copies of two mountain-protection formations, from Peace and Tranquility Mountain and Planchette Writing Sect.

During Chen Ping'an's crisis of the heart at [[Bamboo Scroll Lake]], the old scholar stays on Tassel Mountain day after day watching events, ignoring the Confucian temple's envoys. To the mountain god, he describes his disciples: Cui Chan was the most literary but pessimistic, Qi Jingchun the most knowledgeable and optimistic, and Zuo You the most stubborn but the best-balanced, learning the sword so quickly that the old scholar feared he would become the first fourteenth-tier sword cultivator in thousands of years. He adds that his fourth disciple is only "half a disciple", because the man feels his background is too lowly and does not want to cause his master trouble.Chapter 450 (2)

=== The Sword Qi Great Wall ===
The old scholar later comes to the Sword Qi Great Wall in person. Zuo You bows to him as "Master." He goes to Chen Qingdu's thatched cottage and announces that the scholarly temple needs to borrow three people. Chen Qingdu refuses. The old scholar keeps going back to haggle, at one point declaring he will roll on the ground and shout if he cannot win this time, until the strain nearly makes his insubstantial body vanish.

Afterwards he goes to the wine shop where Chen Ping'an works, eats and drinks happily on a stool with his two disciples, and scolds Zuo You for not treating his junior brother better. For the first time, Chen Ping'an calls him simply "Master." Chen Ping'an explains that he refused before because he had not yet studied, and that he now accepts the Scholarly Sage as his teacher. Before leaving, the old scholar thanks [[Ning Yao]], who has no idea why.Chapter 580 He also quietly passes a book Chen Ping'an had given him on to Zuo You.

He escorts Chen Ping'an's sword spirit back to the Majestic World and conceals her aura on the road. Along the way he uses up a store of merit that belongs to Chen Ping'an, explaining that it would be a waste to leave it, and that he would rather spend it before his disciple ever learns it existed.Chapter 589 (1)

=== Downtrodden Mountain ===
When Downtrodden Mountain's ancestral hall is founded, three portraits are hung inside. The old scholar's occupies the centre, flanked by those of Qi Jingchun and Cui Cheng.Chapter 568 (2)

He later pays a secret visit to the hall, his third visit to the mountain. Pei Qian greets him as "Senior Senior Scholarly Sage" and tells him he looks far more dignified in person than in his portrait, which pleases him enormously. He asks Pei Qian, [[Chen Nuanshu]] and [[Zhou Mili]] to keep his visit to themselves. Looking around the hall his closing disciple built, he smiles for the first time in a long while, even as he feels more guilty than ever about how little he

pages.title: Sects
pages.content:
'''Sects''' are the immortal forces of the cultivation world in Sword of Coming. They range from small temples and villas to sect-level forces that hold mountains, blessed lands and the loyalty of whole nations. Most are tied to one of the major teachings, such as Daoism, Buddhism or the Militarians, and many are lower sects of a larger force on another continent. This page lists them by continent, in the order [[Chen Ping An]] encounters them.

== Eastern Treasured Vial Continent ==

=== Sun Scorch Mountain ===
Sun Scorch Mountain is one of the oldest sword sects of the [[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]]. Besides the main path to its summit, the mountain has a series of "sword paths" opened by its sword immortals. Six had been completed by the start of the story, and two more were expected within a century.Chapter 35 Its peak is filled with sword intent, and the sword spirits of past ancestors are said to appear there.Chapter 37

The sect began small and weak. After its founder died in battle, its guardian, the great demon known as the [[Mountain-Moving Ape]], became its strongest fighter.Chapter 49 It shares the same origins as the Wind Lightning Field, and the two have been sworn enemies for centuries. The remains of a Sun Scorch Mountain matriarch lie on the sword arena of the Wind Lightning Field, left in the open with a sword driven through her head.Chapter 45 For hundreds of years the Wind Lightning Field's master Li Tuanjing held the sect down on his own.

The sect sent the Mountain-Moving Ape into the small town of Jewel Small World to guard [[Tao Zi]], granddaughter of the Pure Yang Sword Patriarch Tao Kui. While there, the ape struck down [[Liu Xianyang]] to keep his family's sword scripture away from the Wind Lightning Field. In a later public duel on the Divine Platform of Wind Snow Temple, its celestial maiden Su Jia was defeated by Huang He of the Wind Lightning Field in three exchanges.Chapter 213 After Li Tuanjing's death the balance turned, and Sun Scorch Mountain began to rise while its rival was forced to lie low.Chapter 457 It became a firm ally of the Xu Clan of Light Breeze City and one of the leading powers serving the [[Great Li Empire]].Chapter 533

=== Dawn Cloud Mountain ===
Dawn Cloud Mountain is one of the few sects on the continent that follows Buddhism. It was founded by Patriarch Dawn Cloud and traces its roots to one of the five branches of Buddhism.Chapter 10 Its wealth comes from the Cloud Root Stone mined on the mountain, a pure material prized by Daoist alchemists across several continents. It is not counted among the top sects, but it never lacks resources.Chapter 253 It sent [[Cai Jinjian]] into the small town in search of a fated opportunity, and she met her end there. The sect later became one of four sects-in-waiting under the Great Li Empire.Chapter 642

=== Wind Lightning Field ===
The Wind Lightning Field is a sword sect and the sworn enemy of Sun Scorch Mountain. A sword prodigy who betrayed Sun Scorch Mountain was given shelter there for most of his life, and the sword scripture handed down in Liu Xianyang's family came from him. Its master Li Tuanjing reached the tenth tier at forty and was long regarded as the strongest cultivator on the continent below the Upper Five Tiers. He died at the end of a later battle between the two sects, and his disciple Huang He took over, alongside the swordsman [[Liu Baqiao]].Chapter 250

=== Wind Snow Temple ===
Wind Snow Temple and True Martial Mountain are the two great Militarian sects of the continent, one in the north and one in the south.Chapter 88 Wind Snow Temple has six branches and places great weight on refining the body. It is fiercely protective of its own. When a villa in the Water Talisman Empire wronged [[Ruan Qiong]], all six branches struck back until the villa fell to a second-rate sect.Chapter 95 Its smallest branch, the Divine Platform, produced [[Wei Jin]], the youngest swordsman on the continent to reach the Upper Five Tiers. The temple's Divine Platform also served as neutral ground for the duel between Sun Scorch Mountain and the Wind Lightning Field.

=== True Martial Mountain ===
True Martial Mountain is the other Militarian ancestral temple of the continent. It is more involved in mortal empires than Wind Snow Temple, and many of its cultivators serve as generals in the [[Great Li Empire]], [[Great Sui Nation]] and the fallen Lu Empire. It is said that people there can speak directly with ancient deities in one of its great halls.Chapter 488 [[Ma Kuxuan]] of Apricot Blossom Alley was taken there by one of its swordsmen and became its most famous young cultivator.Chapter 56

=== Divine Edict Sect ===
The Divine Edict Sect of [[Southern Stream Nation]] is the foremost of the continent's three Daoist sects and receives most of its incense and offerings. It owns one of the 72 blessed lands, the Limpid Pond Blessed Land. It is itself a lower sect of a larger Daoist branch.Chapter 176 Its sect master Qi Zhen became the continent's only Heavenly Lord and holds the authority to recognise Daoist True Lords across it.Chapter 191 The sect is also home to [[He Xiaoliang]], its Jade Girl. Its elder Zhao Liu once led a group to punish the former disciple Yang Huang and his wife.Chapter 219

=== Sword Water Villa ===
Sword Water Villa is a martial arts villa in [[Water Combing Nation]], home of the sword saint Song Yushao and a large waterfall deep in its mountains.Chapter 239 It hosts the election of the alliance leader of the nation's martial world.Chapter 237 Chen Ping'an stayed there with [[Xu Yuanxia]] and [[Zhang Shanfeng]] on his first trip south.

=== Golden Osmanthus Temple ===
The Golden Osmanthus Temple is a Daoist temple at the top of Azure Waist Mountain near [[Azure Phoenix Nation]]. It is closed to outsiders for most of the year. Its master is regarded as a true immortal close to the Golden Core Tier, and martial artists from several nations climbed the mountain when it opened its doors to take nine disciples.Chapter 379

=== Dragon Spring Sword Sect ===
The Dragon Spring Sword Sect was founded by Ruan Qiong in Dragon Spring Prefecture after he left Wind Snow Temple. It holds Divine Elegance Mountain and many surrounding peaks.Chapter 283 It began with very few disciples. Later the Great Li court chose a dozen talented children to train there.Chapter 420

=== True Realm Sect ===
The True Realm Sect was founded at [[Bamboo Scroll Lake]] as a lower sect of the Jade Tablet Sect of Parasol Leaf Continent. Under its sect leader Jiang Shangzhen, it brought the lake's islands and their vagrant cultivators under its rule. Many of them became guest elders and official immortals.Chapter 530

=== Downtrodden Mountain ===
{{Main|Downtrodden Mountain}}Downtrodden Mountain in Dragon Spring Prefecture is Chen Ping An's own mountain. It grew from a single purchase into a sect with its own ancestral hall, and it later came to own the Lotus Root Blessed Land.

== Northern Complete Reed Continent ==

=== Ceremony Mountain ===
Ceremony Mountain is a large force in the southwest of the [[Northern Complete Reed Continent]]. At its peak it had two immortals of the Upper Five Tiers, but none had appeared there for over 120 years. Its Kun ship makes a yearly round trip across three continents, carrying passengers and cargo, and [[Chen Ping An]] travelled on it to the [[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]]'s south.Chapter 207 The ship was later struck down over the Luminous Vermilion Empire by Mr. Sword Urn, a sacrifice planned so that [[Xie Shi]] could move against Lake View Academy.Chapter 235

=== Flax Robe Sect ===
The Flax Robe Sect stands above Skeleton Shoal in the far south of the continent, with Mural City at its foot. It runs an intercontinental ship and is home to many righteous ghostly cultivators.Chapter 482 Its long-standing enemy is Gao Cheng, the ghostly lord of Skeleton Wall City in Malicious Ghost Valley. Even the sect's past leaders admitted he was a great figure among ghosts.Chapter 497

=== Lofty Cloud Palace ===
The Lofty Cloud Palace belongs to the Yang Clan of the Great Origin Empire's Esteemed Mystery Department. Its owner is both the department's leader and the empire's imperial preceptor, and three of his ancestors reached the Upper Five Tiers. The clan is known across the continent for repaying kindness many times over. Its young heir Yang Ningxing is one of the continent's ten dragons and phoenixes.Chapter 496

=== Spring Dew Garden ===
The Spring Dew Garden sits between Skeleton Shoal and the Fine Wood Mountain Range. It earns its living from an immortal ship that sells rare plants it raises. It keeps three heirloom treasures, one of them a ten-thousand-year-old locust tree. Every New Year's Eve it hosts the Farewelling the Year Banquet, where thousands of wandering merchants gather.Chapter 500 Its patriarch is a Nascent Tier cultivator.

=== Jade Forest Sect ===
The Jade Forest Sect grew rich through trade. It used that wealth to push its founder to the Unpolished Jade Tier, which made it a sect-level force, though other cultivators mocked how he got there.Chapter 501 It is the home of Bai Shang, the strongest sword immortal of the north, and his only disciple Xu Xuan.Chapter 526

=== Refreshing Sect ===
The Refreshing Sect was founded by [[He Xiaoliang]] of the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent. She found a small world on the continent and tamed many great demons and spirits there, and with Xie Shi's support she quickly established it as a powerful sect.Chapter 510 After she clashed with Xu Xuan and offended Bai Shang, the sect was left isolated, and Xie Shi sent her to apologise to the Jade Forest Sect.Chapter 555

=== Golden Scale Palace ===
The Golden Scale Palace lies deep in the mountains on the border of the Great Seal Script Empire, and it is on very bad terms with that empire.Chapter 516 Its talismans grant the power of flight. Its chief guest elder is a Golden Core Tier swordsman, and Chen Ping An once passed himself off as one of its swordsmen.Chapter 518

=== Deer Cutter Mountain ===
Deer Cutter Mountain is an assassin sect in the south of the continent. Its founder's rule is that it sends assassins only once per job. If the attempt fails, it returns half the payment and never tries again.Chapter 523 Its assassins, led by a Nascent Tier cultivator, made an attempt on Chen Ping An and failed.Chapter 532

=== Duckweed Sword Lake ===
Duckweed Sword Lake is a sword sect led by the sword immortal Li Cai. Her disciple Rong Chang is a Nascent Tier sword cultivator, though she has said he will not be the next sect leader.Chapter 524

=== Great Emblem Sword Sect ===
The Great Emblem Sword Sect is a sect-level sword sect in the north of the continent. Its sect leader and another senior sword immortal travelled to the Sword Qi Great Wall to fight, leaving the sect in a dangerous position.Chapter 525 It is home to the sword immortal Han Huaizi and to [[Qi Jinglong]], its newest sword immortal, who travelled with Chen Ping An under the name Qi Jinglong.Chapter 553

=== Ground Lying Peak ===
Ground Lying Peak is the home of [[Spiritual Master Fire Dragon]], who oversees four other major branches through disciples who founded their own peaks. Its disciples include [[Zhang Shanfeng]]. Few outside know how strong the peak truly is.Chapter 536 Zhang Shanfeng once called it Heavensoar Sect.

=== Lightning God Manor ===
The Lightning God Manor is known for its five lightning talismans. Their full power depends on the five ancestral seals of its ancestral hall, and its earth immortal spiritual masters inscribe them by hand.Chapter 540

=== Water Dragon Sect ===
The Water Dragon Sect is an ancient sect built on the great river that runs east to west through the centre of the continent. Its ancestral hall was once one of the river's three ancient water temples.Chapter 542 It owns the Dragon Palace Small World, one of the thirty-six small worlds, and Paddling Island, where Chen Ping An refined a bonded item.Chapter 548 Its sect leader is Sun Jie.

== Parasol Leaf Continent ==

=== Parasol Leaf Sect ===
The Parasol Leaf Sect in the north and the Jade Tablet Sect in the south are the two most powerful sects of the [[Parasol Leaf Continent]].Chapter 261 Almost all of the continent's ferry stations lie in the north, which is part of why the Parasol Leaf Sect can keep the Jade Tablet Sect in check.Chapter 281 It is on good terms with the Ding Clan of [[Old Dragon City]], and one of its cultivators once helped that clan recover from near collapse.Chapter 262

=== Jade Tablet Sect ===
The Jade Tablet Sect is the leading power of the south. Its Jiang Clan has controlled the Cloud Cave Blessed Land for generations. [[Jiang Shangzhen]] of the clan entered the Lotus Flower Blessed Land under the name Zhou Fei and later became the first leader of its lower sect, the True Realm Sect of Bamboo Scroll Lake.

=== Planchette Writing Sect ===
The Planchette Writing Sect is a sect-level force in the central region of the continent. Its two Unpolished Jade Tier cultivators are Dao partners. The sect leader spent his whole fortune building the bustling Sky Calling Street for his partner, who loved raising spirits.Chapter 287 Later a great demon of the Upper Five Tiers destroyed almost half the sect, killing one of the two and wounding the other.Chapter 344

=== Peace and Tranquility Mountain ===
Peace and Tranquility Mountain is the most powerful sect in the central region, at least the equal of the Planchette Writing Sect, but so secluded that it almost never appears in the world. It gathers the knowledge of every branch of alchemy.Chapter 296 For thousands of years it held demons captive in a well, guarded for over three thousand years by the [[Mountain-Moving Ape]]. When its sect master left to stop a twelfth tier great demon from reaching the sea, the prison opened. More than half the captive demons escaped, and the central region fell into chaos.Chapter 345 Its Daoist priests led the fight that followed. Many of them died, earning the respect of the Confucian academies that came to help.Chapter 349 The Daoist nun Huang Ting, who lived in the Lotus Flower Blessed Land as Tong Qingqing and Fan Wan'er, belongs to this sect.Chapter 323

=== Golden Summit Daoist Temple ===
The Golden Summit Daoist Temple is a small Daoist force regarded as heretical but well respected, with fewer than a hundred priests. Its priests like to cultivate their minds among mortals, often hiding who they are. Its abbot is a five-hundred-year-old Nascent Tier earth immortal renowned in the north of the continent.Chapter 342

=== Lotus Flower Blessed Land ===
The [[Lotus Flower Blessed Land]] has its own forces, which [[Chen Ping An]] met during his time there.

==== Observing Dao Temple ====
The Observing Dao Temple is the home of the old Daoist priest who owns the blessed land. Chen Ping An searched the capital of [[Southern Garden Nation]] for it without success. In truth the temple does not exist as a building, and the whole blessed land is the old Daoist's place for observing the Dao.Chapter 566

==== Mirror Heart Hall ====
The Mirror Heart Hall is a holy land of the martial world led by Tong Qingqing. Rather than chasing power among cultivators, it works to place its women in the courts of all four lands.Chapter 316 Its disciple Zhou Shuzhen rose to become empress of Southern Garden Nation.

==== Spring Tide Palace ====
The Spring Tide Palace was led by Zhou Fei, one of the Upper Ten Elites, who was in truth Jiang Shangzhen of the Jade Tablet Sect. The palace was later moved to Parasol Leaf Continent.Chapter 322

==== Lake Mountain Faction ====
The Lake Mountain Faction of [[Pine Song Nation]] was led by [[Yu Zhenyi]], the first person in the blessed land's history to switch from martial arts to cultivation.

==== Bird's Eye View Peak ====
Bird's Eye View Peak in [[Northern Jin Nation]] is the home of the sword immortal Lu Fang.Chapter 307

==== Reverence Pagoda ====
The Reverence Pagoda compiled the list of the Upper Ten Elites, the greatest fighters of the blessed land. Its leader was Zhou Shuzhen. After the great battles in Southern Garden Nation, it announced it would no longer rank the Upper Ten Elites.Chapter 325

== Middle Earth Divine Continent ==

=== Mount Longhu ===
Mount Longhu on the [[Middle Earth Divine Continent]] is a holy land of Daoism and the seat of the Heavenly Master Residence, which belongs to its Zhang Clan.Chapter 215 Its priests follow the talismanic branch of Daoism, relying on talismans and peach wood swords rather than the body.Chapter 214 Heavenly Masters are ranked in tiers. The first rank are immortals of the Upper Five Tiers, honoured in the ancestral hall, while external Heavenly Masters who do not carry the Zhang surname rank lower. [[Spiritual Master Fire Dragon]] of Ground Lying Peak is one of its external Heavenly Masters. When he asked the residence to recognise his disciple [[Zhang Shanfeng]] as a future external Heavenly Master, it declined.Chapter 527

=== White Emperor City ===
White Emperor City is a city among the iridescent clouds of the Middle Earth Divine Continent and one of the ten wonders of the world.Chapter 152 Its city lord is the greatest Go player in the world. [[Cui Chan]] lost to him but put up a strong fight. Because of the city lord, no empire dares to award the tenth dan in Go to any player.Chapter 169

== Heavenly World ==

=== White Jade Capital ===
The White Jade Capital of the [[Heavenly World]] is the seat of Daoism's three branches, known for its five cities and twelve towers.Chapter 113 [[Lu Chen]] is one of its three branch masters, and he once tried to draw Chen Ping An there. Not every Daoist sect falls under it. The Planchette Writing Sect, for example, does not. The [[Great Li Empire]] built a small replica of the White Jade Capital in its own capital as a weapon, able to strike down powerful cultivators north of Lake View Academy.Chapter 114

== Other sects ==

=== Rain Dragon Sect ===
The Rain Dragon Sect stands on an island far out at sea, so distant from the three nearest continents that its word is law in its waters. Its ancestor rebuilt the statue of an ancient rain god said to have commanded the True Dragons that brought rain. By old tradition, its female cultivators choose their Dao partners by tossing down embroidered balls made by the sect.Chapter 620 Fu Ke is the youngest Golden Core Tier cultivator in its history.Chapter 631

=== Green Goat Palace ===
Green Goat Palace stands on Heavenly Palace Peak, which hosts a large immortal ferry station. Its six branch palaces each worship a different Daoist immortal. Its master Lu Yong is a Nascent Tier cultivator known for refining pills and for being one of the most peaceful cultivators alive. After Jiang Shangzhen settled an old grievance there, the Jade Tablet Sect agreed to buy and sell every pill the palace makes.Chapter 358

=== Golden Crow Palace ===
The Golden Crow Palace is led by a Golden Core Tier swordsman known for fearing his wife, the daughter of a great mountain lord.Chapter 509 He badly wounded the patriarch of the nearby Yellow Wind Valley.Chapter 510

}} == Appearance == Shi Rou is a beautiful skeletal ghost, a rack of bones from the neck down concealed beneath an exquisite, colorful dress with large sleeves that hide her bony arms, with only her face appearing lifelike and lovely.Chapter 384 After gaining control of an unoccupied Immortal Tier immortal body that had once belonged to the Ascension Tier cultivator [[Du Mao]], she took on that body’s appearance instead, which left her feeling self-conscious about performing dainty, feminine gestures in such an unfamiliar visage.Chapter 465 While keeping shop she sometimes disguises herself to appear as an old man, though she has occasionally forgotten to also disguise her voice.Chapter 567 == Personality == She is sly and teasing by habit, quick to make thinly veiled jabs, but underneath that she is anxious, deferential, and still shaped by centuries of abuse, often reacting to new situations with instinctive fear before settling down.Chapter 384 She genuinely cares for those around her despite her awkward, uncertain place in the world, secretly setting aside money for Pei Qian out of guilt over not earning enough for Downtrodden Mountain, even though Pei Qian always insists on doing things properly instead.Chapter 639 She is self-conscious about small vanities, such as secretly buying makeup and hiding it so no one will tease her over it.Chapter 639 She can be quietly protective of her dignity, refusing to curry favor with guest elders who try to win her over only when it is convenient for them.Chapter 639 == Background == Shi Rou was once a living woman of the Colorful Garment Nation on the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent, long since dead and bound as a ghost in service to a lecherous old cultivator who collected beautiful female ghosts and forced them to assist him in sinister, malicious deeds. Several of her fellow captive ghosts suffered horrific fates at his hands, their souls burned down like candle wicks through a cruel immortal technique as punishment, yet Shi Rou was the only one among them who ever dared to defy him.Chapter 384 Eventually she came into Chen Ping’an’s possession, established through a contract that Aunt Gui and the Golden Core Tier sword cultivator Ma Zhi helped arrange while Chen Ping’an was traveling aboard Osmanthus Island. Wary of ghosts and yin entities after a bad experience with a vengeful female ghost in his youth, Chen Ping’an kept her sealed inside a yellow paper talisman for a long time before finally releasing her again.Chapter 384 When Chen Ping’an offered her an unoccupied body, essentially at the Immortal Tier, to inhabit so that she could finally walk freely in the world of the living, Shi Rou was overwhelmed and repeatedly kowtowed in gratitude, swearing lifelong servitude in return. With Cui Dongshan’s help, she succeeded in transforming the colored glaze golden body of the deceased Ascension Tier cultivator Du Mao into a blessed land for her own soul, though tension between the body and her soul took time to fully settle, and her own cultivation talent proved to be far less remarkable than the fated opportunity that brought her this body in the first place.Chapter 385Chapter 386 Shi Rou went on to serve as one of Chen Ping’an’s stewards on Downtrodden Mountain, following him and Wei Bo around while adjusting to a far more restrictive and rule-bound life than she was used to, and she grew wary of Cui Chan’s grandfather after witnessing the sheer force of his fist intent firsthand.Chapter 457 She later ran a pastry shop on Dragon Riding Alley alongside a general goods shop, overseeing both while Pei Qian attended a private school nearby, and the two of them developed a close, sisterly bond, with Pei Qian visiting often under the pretense of checking the account books but really just to make sure Shi Rou wasn’t feeling left out.Chapter 464Chapter 465 She continued managing the pastry shop for years afterward, keeping Downtrodden Mountain’s books in order and quietly caring for the people who passed through her life there, including the once-renowned pure martial artist Zheng Dafeng, who came to help out around the shop in his old age.Chapter 527 Chen Ping’an later gifted her the Snowflake Dao Robe, taken from a female ghost of Meticulous Skin City, as a token of his continued regard for her.Chapter 571 == Trivia == * She secretly buys makeup and hides it carefully so that Pei Qian will not find it and tease her.Chapter 639 * Despite her unassuming role, she is treated with notable generosity by the young mountain master of Downtrodden Mountain, something she has come to recognize only after many years of peace finally let her stop living in constant fear.Chapter 639 * She shares her current body with the lingering, unresolved remnants of its original owner, Du Mao, making for an occasionally strange sight when she performs delicate, ladylike gestures in his visage.Chapter 465 == References ==

pages.title: Small Town
pages.content:
The Small Town is the settlement where [[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]] was born and raised, located inside [[Small Worlds|Jewel Small World]] before it fell to the ground and was annexed by the [[Great Li Empire]]. The town now sits inside Locust Yellow County, the subordinate county carved out when the surrounding territory was elevated into [[Dragon Spring Prefecture]]. The town itself kept its old boundaries and its own long, hidden history even after the annexation.

== General Characteristics ==
The town has no walls around it. What people call the town gate is really just a stretch of makeshift fencing where visitors are checked before being let in or sent away.Chapter 3 Fewer than 700 clans live there, adding up to around 5,000 people once servants are counted, and the Lu, Li, Zhao, and Song clans are the most prominent among them. One resident describes the town as deceptive in its modesty, saying it "may only be a small town, but it's like a small puddle that appears to be innocuous from the outside, but actually holds unfathomably deep water."Chapter 9

The town's recorded history stretches back 3,000 years, and it has carried several names over that time. It appears on old maps of the Great Li Empire as Great Marsh Village before a sage personally renamed it Dragon Den. The town was renamed again later, to avoid sharing a character with the reigning Great Li emperor's name, but the sentence revealing that name is cut off before it is given, so the town's name in the period just before annexation is not stated outright.Chapter 23

Nearly every generation born in the town produces people of notable talent, and most of them are taken away from the town while still young. [[Song Jixin]], who has read through the town's local chronicle more than once, noticed that almost none of these children ever return to the town once they leave it.Chapter 24 Mystical abilities and cultivation are also suppressed inside the town, and the rule holds for residents and visitors alike: the stronger someone's cultivation, the more backlash they take on by using it there.Chapter 7

== Key Locations within the Town ==

=== Clay Vase Alley ===
Chen Ping'an's home sits on Clay Vase Alley, a cramped and narrow stretch that he grew up thinking of as ordinary until he saw how differently the wealthier clans lived. It is the poorest part of the Town.

=== Apricot Blossom Alley ===
Apricot Blossom Alley holds the Iron Lock Well, where a thick metal chain hangs down into the water for no reason anyone in town can explain. One curious resident once tried to pull the whole chain out, and died of unexplained bleeding the same night, a fate only undone once his family carried his body back to the well and let the chain sink back down.

=== Fortune Street and Peach Leaf Alley ===
Fortune Street and Peach Leaf Alley are where the town's wealthiest clans live, paved with bluestone slabs and lined with peach trees whose blossoms strike at least one visiting student as nothing like the peach blossoms described in his books.Chapter 11

=== Dragon Riding Alley ===
Dragon Riding Alley is home to a blacksmith's forge, as well as a pastry shop known for a peach blossom wine cake, and the general store Burclover next door where Chen Ping'an later buys ink and writing supplies.Chapter 70

=== Other landmarks ===
* At the edge of town stands the stone archway that locals call the Crab Archway, after the twelve stone pillars that hold it up, though Song Jixin insists its official name is the Grand Secretary Archway, bestowed by an emperor to honor a military official.Chapter 2 Nine of its twelve pillars are carved with dragons, and the remaining three carry the White Tiger, the Black Tortoise, and the Vermillion Bird.Chapter 27
* The covered bridge crosses the creek on the town's south side. Beneath it lies a rusted iron sword three thousand years old, and the Great Li Empire spent a great deal of money building the bridge for the sole purpose of containing what remains of the sword's power.Chapter 30
* The old locust tree is another fixture of the town, said to sway and rustle even when the air is completely still, and it has long served as a gathering spot where an old storyteller sets up to tell tales to the local children.
* The private school, funded jointly by the town's most affluent clans, was where [[Qi Jingchun]] taught for decades, limiting his lessons to just three foundational texts: "Principles of Life for Children," "Rites and Music," and "An Anthology of Literary Essays."Chapter 6
* The office of the kiln supervision official, once the seat of authority over the town's dragon kilns, is occupied by [[Song Changjing]] during his time in the town.Chapter 41

== Unique Aspects and Mysteries ==
No one in the town, however old, can explain who hung the chain in the Iron Lock Well or why. Song Jixin has taken to calling the town's local chronicle the "Sixty-Year Chronicle," since it is updated roughly every sixty years, and "Beyond the Wall," after noticing how the people it describes almost never return home once they leave the town.

The deeper mystery behind the town is its origin. Qi Jingchun tells Chen Ping'an that the town is the burial site of the last true dragon in the world, and that the clash which killed it, three thousand years ago, drew enough cultivators to the area that many of them stayed, married, and settled, eventually growing into the town that exists now. Afterward, four Sages, representing the Confucianist, Buddhist, Daoist, and martial artist traditions, agreed to take turns guarding the town in rotations of sixty years each.

Every child born in the town is given a secret code name, and a drop of their heart's blood is sealed into a piece of porcelain fired specially for them, six years for girls and nine for boys, in what the town calls [[Natal Porcelain|bonded porcelain]]. These pieces are later bought and sold by outside parties, and someone tampering with a bonded porcelain can upend the life of the person it belongs to, as happened to Chen Ping'an's own father.

== Social and Economic Aspects ==
Wealth in the town runs along clan lines, with the Lu, Li, Zhao, and Song clans at the top and their servants and poorer neighbors well below them. The town's economy was long built around its dragon kilns, with the Lu Clan alone owning more of them, and better ones, than any other clan. The imperial court eventually shut all of the kilns down, ending that trade in the town.

== The Town's Fate ==
Qi Jingchun describes the town as a 3,000-year-old piece of chinaware worn down to the point of shattering, and warns that if it finally breaks, the thousands of people living there will not simply die, but face what he calls "a great death, a death where there is no next life."Chapter 32 He goes on to call the town's nature "innately discordant with the Great Dao," the price the Sages agreed to pay in exchange for the town's three thousand years of fortune.

When that reckoning finally arrives, Qi Jingchun chooses to take the full weight of it onto himself rather than let the town's people suffer, declaring simply, "I will shoulder it all."Chapter 66 Had he not done so, every one of the town's more than 6,000 residents would have been made to answer for it, and [[Ruan Qiong]], set to take over as the next Sage, would have been bound by his role to see that none of them escaped that reckoning.Chapter 68

== References ==

pages.title: Small Worlds
pages.content:
Small worlds are one of two categories of alternate realms that exist alongside the nine continents, the other being the ten large worlds. There are 36 small worlds in total, and Jewel Small World, the floating realm that was home to [[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]]'s small town before it fell to the ground, is one of them.Chapter 70

== Definition and Nature ==
Qi refiners commonly call small worlds "mystical realms" to set them apart from the ten large worlds. Unlike large worlds, which run through heaven and earth with an abundance of spiritual energy and are considered true immortal abodes, small worlds tend to feel comparatively damaged and incomplete, since many of them were born from the wreckage of ancient ruins or old battlefields.Chapter 102 [[Ning Yao]] describes the 36 small worlds as concealed, secret places, "like a shy woman hiding behind a fan."

== Size and Scope ==
Small worlds vary enormously in size. Jewel Small World is the smallest and most insignificant of the 36, measuring only around 500 kilometers across. At the other extreme, legend holds that a single lotus leaf inside the Dao Ancestor's Lotus Flower World, itself counted as one of the 36 small worlds, is larger than the entire capital city of the Great Li Empire.

== The 36 Small Worlds ==
Among the named small worlds, Paradise Small World is said to be the most beautiful and scenic, and Astral Winds Small World the most strange and perilous. Island Small World is a mystical realm holding a number of ancient islands that mysteriously vanished from the outside world, and it is unusual in that it sits inside the abdomen of a primordial beast known as the island-engulfing whale. A damaged realm called the Ascending True Immortal Mystical Realm, derived from one of the 72 blessed lands rather than from a small world directly, also measures around 500 kilometers across, rivaling Jewel Small World in size; the Five Weapon Sect that controls it charges entrance fees in much the same way outsiders once paid to enter Jewel Small World.Chapter 286

=== Jewel Small World ===
Jewel Small World was never particularly rich in spiritual energy or valuable medicinal herbs, unlike many other small worlds. Instead, it became known across [[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]] for its "[[Natal Porcelain|bonded porcelain]]" system, its treasures, and the unusually high number of gifted cultivators its small town produced each generation.Chapter 62 Within the small world, Qi refiners were handicapped more than almost anyone else; even a minor lapse in concentration while using cultivation there could damage a Qi refiner's cultivation base, with more advanced cultivators suffering more for it.Chapter 67

For most of its 3,000-year history, entry into Jewel Small World was restricted and came at a price, but this was set to change once its guardianship passed out of the hands of the Sages: the small world was due to be downgraded into an unrestricted blessed land that anyone could enter freely, without paying the old entrance fee.Chapter 63 That transition never had the chance to run its natural course. Jewel Small World eventually fell out of the sky following the death of its final guardian Sage, Qi Jingchun, and the territory was subsequently annexed by the Great Li Empire and reorganized into what is now Dragon Spring Prefecture.

== Domains ==
A separate category from both large and small worlds is the domain, a small storage space, known to Buddhists as an "all-encompassing seed" and to Daoists as a "world up the sleeve." A domain can hold any number of objects but, unlike a true small world, cannot contain living beings. One example mentioned is a domain inside a jade bracelet, roughly the size of a single house.

== Significance and Cultivation ==
Small worlds are frequently tied to fated opportunities, drawing cultivators who hope to find rare treasures or accelerate their cultivation, though the risks inside can be just as great as the rewards. The Great Li Empire's White Jade Capital, a tower housing a dozen floors of flying swords powerful enough to deter any cultivator on the continent, was itself built using the wealth the empire's ruling Song Clan extracted over generations from managing Jewel Small World.Chapter 113 Elsewhere, the Fictionists maintain a realm called the White Paper Blessed Land, which grows or shrinks depending on how many characters and stories its members have written into being.Chapter 394

'''Song Changjing''' is the younger brother of the Great Li emperor and the most feared general in the empire. He arrived in the [[Small Town]] as the new kiln supervision official, revealed himself as [[Song Jixin]]'s uncle, and left the Jewel Small World as one of only a handful of tenth tier martial artists on the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent.

==Appearance==
Song Changjing usually wears a white robe and a jade belt, and he has a habit of resting his hand on the belt as he talks. The robe is the Flowing Water Robe, one of the finest immortal artifacts in the Great Li Empire.Chapter 114 His most recognisable item is an expensive but very old fox fur coat that he keeps wearing long after anyone else would have replaced it. Even his own coach driver teases him about it.Chapter 66 Years later, standing at the head of a Mohist war fleet, he is still wearing the same shabby coat. 

==Personality==
Song Changjing is bold, blunt and openly arrogant. It is said that his three great pleasures in life are winning glory on the battlefield, killing prodigies and fighting gods.Chapter 49 When [[Mountain-Moving Ape|Bai Yuan]], the Mountain-Moving Ape, picked him as a target to vent his anger on, Song Changjing charged straight at him down Fortune Street and forced the ape back a step. He looks down on scholars as all talk and no action, though he grudgingly admits that some of their sayings hold truths a soldier could never put into words.

He is hard and ruthless. He has massacred cities, and he nearly killed Chen Dui on the spot for talking back to him, stopping only when Song Jixin pointed out it would hurt his reputation.Chapter 50 (2) He also has a sense of honour. After years of fighting the Lu Empire's general Ye Qing, whom he cursed as a stubborn old fart, the first thing he did on breaking into Lu territory was offer wine and incense at Ye Qing's grave.Chapter 93 (1)

He is sharp at reading people. He saw at once that Chen Ping'an was the root of Song Jixin's inner demon, and he pushed his nephew hard to face it.Chapter 47 Under the teasing he cares about Song Jixin, and once, on the road out of the small town, he patted the boy's head with unexpected gentleness. Above all he is devoted to martial arts. He tells Song Jixin his only ambition is to see the scenery that lies beyond the End Tier.

==Background==

=== The small town ===
Song Changjing joined the army as a young prince and spent more than twenty years fighting on the empire's borders. Within a single year he conquered the Lu Empire, the Great Li's former overlord. He came to the small town as the new kiln supervision official and introduced himself to Song Jixin with the words "I'm an extremely unfortunate person. I'm actually your uncle!"Chapter 33

In the town he sized up [[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]] and gave him two tasks, the first being to find a chance to kidnap the little girl travelling with the old ape of Sun Scorch Mountain. He also explained to Song Jixin, with cold frankness, why [[Liu Xianyang]] had been struck down: the boy had attracted envy with his great fortune and had no backers to protect him. That night he exchanged three punches with Bai Yuan on Fortune Street and taunted Qi Jingchun to step in.

=== Li Er and the tenth tier ===
On the road out of the Jewel Small World, a plain middle-aged man blocked the path. It was [[Li Er]]. Song Changjing sent the carriages on ahead and fought him in the pouring rain until his white robe was soaked with mud, feeling that the fight would decide whether he lived or died, and whether he would wake up at the ninth tier or the tenth.Chapter 62 The battle was savage. At one point Song Changjing crashed down from the sky into a crater near the carriages, and at another he punched Li Er into a hillside. Li Er had the upper hand the whole time and could have beaten him to death. On Old Man Yang's secret instructions he held back, and the fight became the catalyst that let Song Changjing break through. He became only the second End Tier grandmaster on the continent, while still under forty.Chapter 168 (2)

He reached the capital pale and wrapped in his fox fur coat. His brother greeted him warmly, pleased that he had reached the tenth tier.Chapter 112 When a deadly attack struck during Song Jixin's trial at the White Jade Capital, Song Changjing refused to retreat even after a golden thread sliced open his robe. [[A'Liang]] tossed him his own saber, Auspicious Talisman.

=== Interim ruler ===
Song Changjing won great loyalty in the army and was allowed to act on the emperor's behalf. During a night of upheaval in the capital, he sat guard on the outer city road from dusk until dawn beside Luan Changye. Many officials would not have been surprised if he had declared himself emperor the next morning.Chapter 206 (3)

After the emperor's death he became interim ruler. The late emperor had actually wanted Song Changjing to take the throne, but Song Changjing refused and burned the will in front of Cui Chan. In the succession dispute he backed Song Jixin, while Cui Chan backed Song He.Chapter 479 (2) Song He became emperor, and Song Changjing remained the true master of the Great Li military. He led the southward campaign himself. When a mountain god's Dao Manifestation swung a giant sword at his flagship, he shattered its godly body with a single punch.Chapter 456 (2)

Years later, when Song Jixin is struggling as feudal lord of Old Dragon City, Song Changjing visits him and promises to do one thing for him.Chapter 631 (6)

==Trivia==

* Song Changjing is still at the Thriving Qi Tier, the first of the tenth tier's three minor tiers. Li Er, who reached the tenth tier after him, has already moved on to the Simplification Tier.Chapter 385 (1)
* The Daoist Saber Room on Stalactite Mountain once posted a bounty on his head. The reason given was that a continent as small as the Eastern Treasured Vial did not deserve a tenth tier martial artist.
* Li Er later said Song Changjing's aptitude was very good, but his punches were too soft.
* A general of the Water Combing Nation, Chu Hao, regards Song Changjing as his teacher in military strategy, though the two have never met.
* He killed a cultivator from the School of Naturalists in the capital after the man tried to turn the emperor into a puppet.

==References==

pages.content:
{{Character|Chinese=宋和|Pinyin=Sòng Hé|Titles=Emperor of the Great Li Empire

Song Mu (name taken over from his elder brother in the imperial records)|Vital_status=Alive|Gender=Male|Species=Human|Master(s)=[[Cui Chan]]|Relatives=Song Zhengchun (father, late emperor)

'''Song He''' is the younger son of the Great Li emperor Song Zhengchun and an imperial concubine. Raised at his mother's side in the capital while his elder brother [[Song Jixin]] was hidden in the [[Small Town]], he becomes the Great Li Empire's new emperor and [[Cui Chan]]'s student.

== Personality ==
In public Song He is courteous and humble, and he has a fine reputation among the empire's officials. Some of that comes from his mother's careful upbringing, and some from his own ability.Chapter 484 (1) In private he is sharper and more cynical. Talking with his mother, he wondered aloud whether his uncle meant to seize the throne, and he pointed out that Song Changjing could simply arrange an assassination if he wanted to.Chapter 417 (3)

He has a competitive streak. After meeting [[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]], he told his mother that he would not have done much worse in Chen Ping'an's place. She snapped back, asking whether Qi Jingchun would ever have chosen him. He apologised at once and admitted he had only said it out of envy. Even as emperor he stood and took her scolding without a trace of resentment.

He is respectful toward the past. After taking the throne he did not remove a single item his father had left in the imperial study, and he quietly took out a few things he had added himself once the room felt cluttered. He also has firm opinions on art. He thinks the paintings of Bian Ye, a favourite of earlier emperors, are poor in both skill and character.Chapter 640 (3)

== Background ==

=== The younger son ===
For the sake of the clan and the empire, Song He's mother sent her eldest son away to the Jewel Small World as an infant and had him recorded as dead. Song He took over his brother's name and his place as eldest son. She kept Song He by her side in the capital, where he won over the officials on her behalf, and she poured all her hopes into him.Chapter 117 (2) When she was later banished to the Palace of Eternal Spring, Song He went with her.Chapter 206 (3)

When Song Jixin came out of the Jewel Small World and met his mother for the first time, Song He wept openly beside them. Song Jixin found the reunion awkward for all three of them.Chapter 255 (1)

=== Becoming emperor ===
Song He was Cui Chan's student. After the old emperor's death, the succession split the two most powerful men in the empire. Song Changjing supported Song Jixin, and Cui Chan supported Song He.Chapter 479 (2) Song He won the throne and became the emperor ruling more territory than any before him on the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent. Cui Chan worried that someone so newly crowned could easily be goaded into rash decisions by those around him.Chapter 481

He travelled with his mother on an intercontinental ship to meet Chen Ping'an, carrying himself with great humility. Privately he was not much interested in Chen Ping'an and had only come because his mother insisted.

=== Reign ===
Song He visited the Dragon Spring Prefecture in person with two of his chief ministers to congratulate [[Wei Bo]] when the mountain god broke through to the Upper Five Tiers. He presented Wei Bo with a pseudo-celestial treasure from the imperial vault.Chapter 550 (4)

When they are alone, Song He treats Cui Chan as a pupil treats his teacher. After one small court meeting, Cui Chan stayed behind and laid out a plan reaching a hundred years into the future. Song He said he had been waiting for this day all along. He was a little disappointed when Cui Chan advised him that the Song Clan should never try to conquer other continents. He bowed and promised to remember his teacher's words when Cui Chan told him he would only be truly capable once his father's old ministers stayed loyal to him even without Cui Chan in the room.Chapter 555 (2)

== Trivia ==

* An old boxwood chair has stood in the imperial study for about a hundred years. Like his father, Song He touched it as a child but never sat in it.Chapter 547 (3)
* His father's paintings in the study are kept in a porcelain brush holder made in a Jewel Small World dragon kiln.
* His mother told him that even as emperor he would have to learn to play dumb, in front of his uncle and in front of the scholarly officials.

== References ==

'''Song Jixin''' grew up next door to [[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]] on [[Clay Vase Alley]], where the town believed he was the illegitimate son of the kiln supervision official. He is in fact the eldest son of the Great Li emperor, and he later becomes a prince and the feudal lord of [[Old Dragon City]].

== Appearance ==
Song Jixin is a good-looking young man, and Chen Ping'an counts him among the handsome people of his own age he has known. As a boy he liked to sit with his legs crossed and play with a bamboo folding fan, tapping it against his knee or his palm as he talked.Chapter 47 He grows taller than Chen Ping'an after leaving the small town. 

== Personality ==
As a boy Song Jixin was sharp, proud and quick with a cutting remark. He loved fine and pretty things and looked down on anything crude or plain. When he saw something good that he could not have, he tended to sneer at it. He mocked Chen Ping'an constantly and was sure his neighbour would stay poor all his life.

Much of that scorn grew out of envy. Cui Dongshan explains that Song Jixin had money, books and a maidservant, yet he could never understand why someone as poor as Chen Ping'an had at least had two loving parents when he had none he could claim.Chapter 161 Later he learns that the rumours he grew up with were worse than he knew. The things the women of the small town said about him left him with inner demons that even immortals cannot remove.

He is clever and reads people well. He knows how to bargain, and he flew into a rage when [[Fu Nanhua]] tried to buy his Mandrill Teapot for far less than it was worth.Chapter 17 He can also be cold. He once thought about having Fu Nanhua kill [[Liu Xianyang]] simply because it would cost him very little.Chapter 39 He has a playful streak too. In the Fu Clan gardens he spent a happy few minutes teaching a parrot to insult his own royal name.

As he grows older he loosens up. By the time he meets Chen Ping'an again as a prince, he jokes and laughs easily and admits he still does not like the look of his old neighbour. As feudal lord he chooses his own staff and cares only about their ability, not their background.

== Background ==

=== Clay Vase Alley ===
Song Jixin was born Song Mu, the eldest son of the Great Li emperor Song Zhengchun and an imperial concubine. For the sake of the clan and the empire, his mother sent him to the Jewel Small World as an infant to gather as much fortune and fated opportunity as he could for the Song Clan. The imperial records said he had died soon after birth. His name was crossed out of the genealogy, and his younger brother Song He took both the name and the place of the eldest son.Chapter 484 (1)

[[Song Yuzhang]], the kiln supervision official, raised him in the small town. Townsfolk whispered that Song Jixin was Song Yuzhang's illegitimate son, and Song Yuzhang never denied it. He even showed the boy something close to a father's affection. Song Jixin resented him and admired him at the same time, and part of him wished the rumour were true.Chapter 641 (4) He studied under [[Qi Jingchun]] at the town's private school.

When the girl who would become [[Zhi Gui]] escaped from a dragon locking well, she collapsed in the snow outside Chen Ping'an's house. She was drawn by the dragon qi coming from Song Jixin's home next door, so she declared herself Song Jixin's maidservant, and she served him from then on.Chapter 86 (1)

Song Jixin told the young Chen Ping'an that being born on the fifth day of the fifth month had cursed his parents, and that they could not be reborn while he lived in their house. Chen Ping'an broke a promise to his mother because of it. When [[Old Man Yao]] told him the truth, he ran back to town in the rain and nearly strangled Song Jixin against a wall. The memory haunted Song Jixin for years.Chapter 89 Chen Ping'an later says what truly turned him against Song Jixin was something else. When [[Liu Xianyang]] was being beaten nearly to death as a child, Song Jixin squatted on a wall and cheered the attackers on.

=== Discovering his identity ===
When the Jewel Small World opened to outsiders, Song Jixin befriended Tao Zi of Sun Scorch Mountain, who called him "Firewood Collecting Brother." He even had his uncle force the Li Clan to let her out so she could visit him.Chapter 57 The new kiln supervision official, [[Song Changjing]], turned out to be his uncle, and Song Changjing revealed the truth of his birth.

Qi Jingchun left him six books as a parting gift. Song Jixin looked down on the three elementary ones and left them behind, and they eventually went to Chen Ping'an, just as Qi Jingchun had foreseen. Song Jixin threw the keys to his house into Chen Ping'an's yard and left for the capital with Song Changjing and Zhi Gui.

In the capital his father took him to the White Jade Capital tower, where he struggled up level after level and won the recognition of its twelve flying swords. Moments later the swords were gone, and he broke down in tears. That night his father sat with him and told him plainly that he was his son. As the emperor walked away, Song Jixin called after him, "Father!"Chapter 116

=== Prince of the Great Li Empire ===
Song Jixin was presented to the world as a new prince and sent on a visit to Old Dragon City. Reunited with his mother, he found he could not return her feelings, and the meeting with her and Song He was awkward for all three of them. Later he visited Chen Ping'an at Mountain Cliff Academy. He spoke frankly about how distant he was from his mother and asked Chen Ping'an for help with the struggling mountain god temple on [[Downtrodden Mountain]].Chapter 413 (1)

After the old emperor died, the question of succession split the court's most powerful men. Song Changjing backed Song Jixin, while Cui Chan backed his own disciple Song He.Chapter 479 (2) Song He took the throne. Song Jixin was made a first-rank king and feudal lord of Old Dragon City, with the task of overseeing the empire's new secondary capital from afar. The Fu Clan gave up half of the inner city for his residence, and he won goodwill by leaving the way the city was run unchanged.Chapter 528 (2) By the time of the war in the Savage World, he is buried in the work of governing. He has to deal with the Fu Clan, Sun Scorch Mountain and Light Breeze City, and he senses that Zhi Gui is becoming harder to read.

== Trivia ==

* Song Mu is his name in the imperial genealogy. Those who knew him in the small town still call him Song Jixin.
* He kept a large red chest of curios. A green gourd left behind by Song Yuzhang was the piece he felt mattered most.
* When Gao Xuan tried to buy Zhi Gui years later, Song Jixin reminded him that he had once asked 10,000 taels of gold for her, then asked how much the whole Great Sui Nation cost.
* He kept a small four-legged snake as a pet. A horn-like bump later grew on its forehead.
* Qi Jingchun left a wisp of spring wind on three of the town's children: Chen Ping'an, Zhao Yao and Song Jixin.
* There are very few people he resents as much as [[Ma Kuxuan]].
* [[Pei Qian]], watching scenes from her master's childhood, declared that Song Jixin and Zhi Gui both deserved to die.

== References ==

pages.content:
