'''Song Yuzhang''', known in the [[Small Town]] as '''Master Song''', was the kiln supervision official who raised [[Song Jixin]] on Clay Vase Alley. The town believed Song Jixin was his illegitimate son. After his death he became the mountain god of [[Downtrodden Mountain]].

== Appearance ==
When he returned to the small town as an official of the Ministry of Rites, his complexion had grown a little fairer than in his years there.Chapter 83 

== Personality ==
Song Yuzhang was a bookish, mild official who made himself well liked. Of all the kiln supervision officials sent to the town over the years, he was the most popular with ordinary people, though he was not much good at actually running the kilns.Chapter 33 He adapted to circumstances without fuss. When the ministers he travelled with laughed at the townsfolk, he alone did not join in.

He was loyal to the Great Li Empire to the point of foolishness, and he knew it. Cui Chan thought his devotion was ridiculous but still could not help admiring him a little.Chapter 117 (2) Even as a god he kept the habits of a careful official. He insisted on bowing to [[Wei Bo]] according to the rules, even when Wei Bo tried to wave it off.Chapter 189 (2)

His one great weakness was the boy he raised. He let the rumour that Song Jixin was his son spread unchecked, and he treated the prince with something very close to a father's love.

== Background ==

=== Kiln supervision official ===
Song Yuzhang was sent to the small town to serve as kiln supervision official at the same time the infant Song Jixin was hidden there.Chapter 484 (1) He held the post for fifteen years. Before he was recalled to the capital, he spent all his money funding the covered bridge outside town, and he left Song Jixin behind to be looked after by his successor.Chapter 5 The bridge he built hid the Imperial Song Clan's greatest scandal, and he oversaw that bloody piece of clan history from beginning to end.Chapter 641 (4)

The late emperor first meant to let him live quietly, placing him in the Ministry of Rites and later in some unimportant post. Song Yuzhang ruined that by acting as Song Jixin's father. He never denied the rumours in town, and he kept showing the boy affection even after he returned as a Ministry of Rites official. Song Jixin resented him, yet part of him wished the rumour were true. That fatherly love was the one line the emperor would not allow anyone to cross.Chapter 484 (2)

=== Death ===
Song Yuzhang knew too many of the Song Clan's secrets, and he had always expected to be killed someday.Chapter 189 (1) When the emperor picked him to go back to the Jewel Small World, he understood it as the gift of a dignified death, one that would not happen in the capital or under a false charge. He accepted it calmly.

He returned to the town with a group of officials from the Ministry of Rites and stayed alone in a house on Dragon Riding Alley. One night Wang Yifu, a general from the fallen Lu Empire, appeared in his yard. Song Yuzhang greeted him as though he had been expecting him and asked to finish his drink first. He asked Wang Yifu to tell Song Jixin that all those years he had wanted a pair of couplets from him. Wang Yifu refused. Song Yuzhang then remembered reading as a young man about the great waves of the South Sea crashing against Old Dragon City, raised his bowl to them, and drank. Wang Yifu broke his neck and laid him gently on the table as if he had only passed out drunk.Chapter 89 On the orders of Song Jixin's mother, his head was then cut off and sent to the capital in a wooden box.

=== Mountain god ===
After his death the emperor made Song Yuzhang's heroic spirit the mountain god of Downtrodden Mountain. Whether this was a reward for a loyal servant or a final punishment is hard to say. His new colleagues mocked him as the "Gold Head Mountain God."

As a god he remained just as loyal. He met [[Cui Chan]], a man he had admired since his student days, in his mountain temple, and was moved simply to talk with him about virtue.Chapter 199 He grew increasingly at odds with [[Wei Bo]], his superior as god of the Northern Mountain, and he accepted the imperial court's limits on his powers over Downtrodden Mountain without complaint.Chapter 222 (1) When Song Jixin later visited [[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]] at Mountain Cliff Academy, he asked for help with Song Yuzhang's struggling temple.

[[Cui Dongshan]] once summoned him at the summit and called him a fool who had died for nothing. Song Yuzhang bowed respectfully but stood his ground. He told Cui Dongshan that he saw no reason a man could not seek his own moral fulfilment and serve the empire and its people at the same time.Chapter 480 Cui Dongshan later told Song Jixin that his grief over Song Yuzhang was laughable, and that the true mastermind behind the death was neither the man who killed him nor the mother who sent his head to the capital.Chapter 528 (3)

== Trivia ==

* As a young man he loved reading travel chronicles, which is how he knew about the waves at Old Dragon City.
* The great Great Li emperor remarked that Song Yuzhang chose tacky names for people but put real thought into them.
* The green gourd Song Jixin treasured most in his chest of curios was something Song Yuzhang had left behind.
* When outsiders are away from Downtrodden Mountain, he likes to appear and listen to [[Pei Qian]]'s stories, and he shares small memories from his years as kiln supervision official.Chapter 556 (1)

== References ==

pages.title: Southern Garden Nation
pages.content:
'''Southern Garden Nation''' is one of the four lands of the [[Lotus Flower Blessed Land]] on the [[Parasol Leaf Continent]]. Founded by [[Wei Xian]] and ruled by the Wei Clan, it was regarded as the most powerful nation in that world. It was the setting of the great battles of the Upper Ten Elites during [[Chen Ping An]]'s time in the blessed land. When the blessed land was later divided, Southern Garden Nation became the land owned by Downtrodden Mountain.

== Geography ==
The Lotus Flower Blessed Land held four regions. These were Southern Garden Nation, Pine Song Nation, [[Northern Jin Nation]] and the grasslands beyond them.Chapter 566 Though it was the strongest of these, Wei Xian later admitted that it was only the size of a few counties of the [[Great Li Empire]].Chapter 404 It had a population of around twenty million.Chapter 530

The capital is divided into eighty-one districts. As in many other capitals, the north is wealthy and the south poor, martial artists cluster in the east and scholars in the west.Chapter 308 Notable places in and around the city include Champion Scholar Alley and Bull Mountain, which stands just outside the walls.Chapter 307 The capital is also home to the Vajra Temple, the largest temple in that world and the one with the most monks.Chapter 311 The White River Temple, one of the capital's four major temples, and the small Heart Manifestation Temple are there as well. The nation has its own Five Mountains.

== History ==
Southern Garden Nation was founded by Wei Xian, who rose from a poor family through the army to become its first emperor. He was remembered as the greatest martial artist of the past thousand years at breaking enemy lines.Chapter 314 Under him, the nation's mounted troops became famous across that world. They drove the grassland horsemen back, and the rulers of the grasslands nearly surrendered.Chapter 330

After Wei Xian, the nation enjoyed several centuries of peace under rulers who were neither brilliant nor incompetent.Chapter 306 About sixty years before Chen Ping An arrived, the capital was the scene of a chaotic battle among martial artists. During it, [[Ding Ying]] won the silver lotus flower hat and fought [[Zhu Lian]]. Some time afterwards [[Zhong Qiu]] settled in the nation and became its imperial preceptor. He spent decades strengthening it, and the court came to openly hope to unite the four lands.Chapter 320

Chen Ping An came to the capital searching for the Observing Dao Temple.Chapter 304 The Reverence Pagoda chose Bull Mountain as the site of that era's ascension. The great battles that followed, involving Ding Ying, [[Yu Zhenyi]], Zhong Qiu, Chen Ping An and others, tore through the capital and its city wall. The emperor placed the city under martial law whenever grandmasters fought. Afterwards Yu Zhenyi built a cottage on the ruins of Bull Mountain, and the court threatened to remove him by force unless he moved his Lake Mountain Faction into the nation.Chapter 323

The Lotus Flower Blessed Land was later split into four, and the part containing Southern Garden Nation passed to Downtrodden Mountain. There it was called the Lotus Root Blessed Land.Chapter 527 Only the people of Southern Garden Nation kept their souls whole. The inhabitants of the other three regions became like blank paper, alive but without intent. Downtrodden Mountain fed the land immortal coins until it rose to a mid-grade blessed land. It then planned to teach the court how to appoint mountain gods and river gods. Zhong Qiu later said that if the blessed land had not been divided, the nation would have been on course to unite the whole world.Chapter 602

== Government ==
The nation is ruled by the Wei Clan. At the time of the great battles the emperor was Wei Liang, and his family included Empress Zhou Shuzhen, Crown Prince Wei Yan, a second prince and a young princess. The empress was secretly a disciple of the Mirror Heart Hall. That sect had agents in the courts of all four lands, and through her it had placed its own people deep inside the palace. She was also the leader of the Reverence Pagoda, which publishes the list of the Upper Ten Elites.Chapter 316

The imperial preceptor Zhong Qiu lives beside the palace and was the real force behind the court for many years. The nation also kept a network of spies who worked between the court and the martial world. After the blessed land was divided, Wei Liang decided to take up cultivation and stepped down. He was succeeded by Wei Yan, a man of great ambition.

== Culture ==
Buddhism is favoured over Daoism in Southern Garden Nation. Buddhist temples are everywhere, while Daoist temples are rare and there are none at all in the capital. When the abbot of the White River Temple was caught in a scandal, the emperor had most of its three hundred monks imprisoned and banished the rest. The capital has no Confucian temple honouring the seventy-two sages. Martial arts hold a high place in society, and the grandmasters of the world are closely watched by the court.

Local specialities include bamboo wine and golden ball jujube paste cakes. Statues of the Ba Xia can be found under bridges throughout the nation.

== Trivia ==

* [[Pei Qian]] grew up as a beggar in the capital after her parents died.
* One legend says Wei Xian's mother was found by the roadside with a white dragon coiled around her, shortly before she gave birth to him.
* Chen Ping An learned to speak the capital's dialect fluently while searching for the Observing Dao Temple.
* Chen Ping An took a copy of a building manual from the nation's Ministry of Works back with him and later gave it to Zhu Lian.
* [[Cao Qinglang]], a boy from the capital, became a student of Zhong Qiu and [[Lu Tai]].

pages.title: Southern Stream Nation
pages.content:
Southern Stream Nation is a powerful and influential nation within the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent, known for its strong Daoist traditions and the presence of the Divine Edict Sect, which is one of the top immortal forces on the continent. The nation's religious and political landscapes are closely intertwined, with the sect leader holding significant spiritual and political authority. The nation's wealth and resources contribute to its standing, and it has connections with other nations, both on the continent and beyond. The nation is the location of the Limpid Pond Blessed Land, an important location for cultivation. The nation is also a destination for people from all around the world to come and attend ceremonies.

'''General Characteristics:'''

* '''Daoism:''' Southern Stream Nation is primarily known for '''promoting Daoism above all else'''. This is a central aspect of the nation's identity and culture.
* '''Central Location''': It is located in the central region of the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent.
* '''Resources''': The southern region of Eastern Treasured Vial Continent is described as being '''abundant with resources''', which suggests that Southern Stream Nation likely benefits from this.
* '''Proximity to Lake View Academy:''' Southern Stream Nation is not far from Lake View Academy, one of the 72 Confucian academies.
* '''Unique Identity''': It is suggested that the nobles of Southern Stream Nation are happy to establish ties with Great Sui Nation, perhaps because of their mutual northern location.
* '''Geographic Traits''': Southern Stream Nation has some distinct geographic features, such as a mountain that extends all the way up into the clouds, and behind that mountain is a forest.
* '''Ceremony''': There is a Daoist ceremony that is held in the nation which draws people from outside of the nation to attend. It is mentioned that this ceremony recently concluded.
* '''Wealthy''': It is implied that it is a wealthy nation

'''Daoist Influence:'''

* '''Divine Edict Sect:''' The '''Divine Edict Sect''' is the leading Daoist sect of Eastern Treasured Vial Continent, and it's located near the border of Southern Stream Nation. This sect is extremely influential.
* '''Limpid Pond Blessed Land:''' The Divine Edict Sect possesses the '''Limpid Pond Blessed Land''', one of the 72 blessed lands. This indicates the sect's importance and spiritual power. The sect has sole ownership of the land.
* '''Incense and Offerings:''' The Divine Edict Sect receives the vast majority of incense and offerings among the three Daoist sects of Eastern Treasured Vial Continent.
* '''Heavenly Lord:''' The sect leader of the Divine Edict Sect, Qi Zhen, was promoted to the position of '''Heavenly Lord'''. He is a spiritual master and is also recognized as a True Lord in four different nations.
* '''Daoist Temples''': There are many Daoist temples located in the nation, and they are described as being top-notch.
* '''Other Daoist Sects''': The presence of multiple Daoist temples and priests suggests a strong Daoist culture and practice within the nation.

'''Political and Social Aspects:'''

* '''Imperial Preceptor:''' The sect leader of the Divine Edict Sect is also the imperial preceptor of Southern Stream Nation. This highlights the close relationship between the religious and political power within the nation.
* '''True Lord:''' The sect leader is honored as the highest-ranking True Lord in four different nations, demonstrating the widespread recognition of their spiritual authority.
* '''Rulers of Surrounding Nations:''' The rulers of several surrounding nations have visited the sect to confer the title of True Lord on the sect leader.
* '''Powerful Immortal Force:''' The Divine Edict Sect is considered one of the top immortal forces.
* '''Respect for Immortals:''' The mortal emperors, True Lords, and terrestrial gods encountered by travelers from the nation are treated with the utmost respect without exception.
* '''Wealthy Rulers''': The emperor of the nation is described as wealthy.

'''Key Figures:'''

* '''Qi Zhen:''' The sect leader of the Divine Edict Sect, who is also the imperial preceptor and a highly respected True Lord. He is a Dao Master of the continent. He has profound Dao powers.
* '''Old Immortal Qi:''' This is another name for Qi Zhen.
* '''Daoist Priests''': Daoist priests are mentioned in multiple contexts, showing that they are important members of the culture. A young Daoist priest in the Divine Edict Sect, who has a surprisingly senior status, was invited to a sect that controlled the Divine Edict Sect.
* '''Daoist Nun:''' There is a young Daoist nun mentioned in the text.

'''Interactions with the Wider World:'''

* '''Eastern Treasured Vial Continent:''' Southern Stream Nation is a key player in Eastern Treasured Vial Continent, with its dominant Daoist sect and its influence on surrounding nations.
* '''Other Continents''': The Divine Edict Sect receives funding from the Middle Earth Divine Continent, which shows a connection between the two places.
* '''Travel''': People travel to the nation to attend ceremonies.

pages.title: Stalactite Mountain
pages.content:
'''Stalactite Mountain''' is a hovering mountain in the sea off [[Southern Whirl Continent]], made from the largest mountain seal in the world. It belongs to the lineage of the Dao Ancestor's second disciple and stands on the border between the Majestic World and the Savage World, serving as the gateway to the [[Sword Qi Great Wall]]. [[Chen Ping An]] first came there to deliver a sword to [[Ning Yao]].

== Geography ==
The mountain began as a small, finely made seal. Once it came down from the sky, it grew into a towering mountain.Chapter 198 It hangs upside down above the sea, its peak pointing toward the earth and its base toward the sky.Chapter 613 It measures about fifty kilometers in radius, but as a lone mountain in the sea it controls a wide region around it. Ships cannot fly straight to it. Even those that can fly have to come down to the sea and follow one of the paths of cloud and water that hang in the air between the mountain and the sea.Chapter 268 Southern Whirl Continent is the closest continent, and several islands nearby are home to righteous cultivators who keep watch on the criminals hiding on the mountain.Chapter 269

The Daoist lineage owns nine structures on the mountain, and the rest of the land, buildings and shops have been sold to people from all over the world. Eight of the nine sit on eight different sides of the mountain. They are the Catch and Release Pavilion, the Sword Reverence Pagoda, the Incense Offering Tower, the Lightning Lake Platform, Ganoderma Inn, Milu Cliff, the Daoist Seal Hall and the Daoist Saber Room. Lone Peak, a restricted area at the center, holds the tallest building on the mountain, and the gate to the Sword Qi Great Wall stands at its foot.

The four great private residences on the mountain are the Ape Havoc Estate of the Liu Clan of Pure White Continent, the Spring Banner Inn, the Plum Blossom Garden and the Water Essence Palace, which belongs to the Rain Dragon Sect.Chapter 619

== History ==
The second disciple of the Dao Ancestor, True Invincible, made the mountain and drove it into the Majestic World like a nail. [[Wei Bo]] describes it as indestructible and as the first defensive pass between the two worlds, and perhaps the last.Chapter 189 Confucian sages take it as an insult, and the Daoist branch master even made the Qi refiners passing through to the [[Sword Qi Great Wall]] sign a "mountain alliance". It is also treated as forbidden ground for Confucian disciples, so much of the news from beyond it never reaches the rest of the world.Chapter 115

The Catch and Release Pavilion is named for an event from the mountain's early days. A twelfth tier great demon slipped past the Sword Qi Great Wall to the newly placed mountain seal, expecting it to be empty, but the first person it met was the branch master himself. The mountain once came close to destruction when a sword spirit split it with a single slash. Only the Second Sage stepping in stopped it from collapsing.Chapter 588

When the war at the Sword Qi Great Wall grew worse, the Great Heavenly Lord of Lone Peak worked with two sword immortals to open a second gate to the wall for traders. After a serious incident that the mountain kept secret, it brought in a curfew and checked the badge of every cultivator on the mountain in a single day.Chapter 571

== Administration ==
The Great Heavenly Lord who lives on Lone Peak is a direct disciple of the second disciple and is called the embodiment of the mountain's rules. His junior, a young-looking Daoist priest from White Jade Capital, is second in command. Lu Chen tricked him into coming, and after a quarrel with his senior brother he left all affairs to the Great Heavenly Lord and simply guarded the gate.Chapter 271 The third in command is the Flood Dragon True Lord, the Great Heavenly Lord's first disciple, famed for slaying flood dragons in the South Sea. A sword-hugging man from the Sword Qi Great Wall also guards the gate as punishment for losing a battle to a young great demon.Chapter 281

The first rule of the mountain is that anyone who injures another person dies. The Daoist saber priests will pursue a case even decades later, which makes the mountain unusually peaceful. Because the rule also protects wanted men, many evil cultivators flee there to escape pursuit and sell their spoils. Stalactite Mountain does not regard itself as part of the Majestic World and observes the fasting days of the Heavenly World.

Passage to the Sword Qi Great Wall is closely controlled. Visitors are given time slots at the gate and are turned away if they miss them. The Sword Qi Great Wall forbids its own cultivators below the Golden Core Tier from going to the mountain to cultivate, so Ning Yao was criticized for sneaking there as a girl.Chapter 594

== Trade ==
Swordsmen from across the world are summoned to the mountain whenever the demon tribe goes to war, and merchants gather there to sell swords and supplies to the wall at steep prices. Intercontinental ships from eight continents trade there. The first ever to arrive was the Water Pillow of Southern Whirl Continent, and the early ships carried goods to the wall with no thought of profit. 

== Trivia ==
* [[Qi Jinglong]] saw that the mountain's eight attractions are the eyes of a formation, and that the mountain is a celestial weapon with both offensive and defensive power, not just a seal.Chapter 596 Later the narration states that the eight attractions and Lone Peak form an ancient formation from the Master of Three Mountains and Nine Lords, something close to an ancient ascension platform.
* The wine shop that sells Forgetting Sorrow Wine is the last surviving mystical realm of the Golden Millet Blessed Land. Three Pure Incense is a local specialty.Chapter 284
* People born and raised there tend to be well informed and speak with confidence about sages and heavenly lords alike.
* Fewer than one in ten people there understand the official dialect of Eastern Treasured Vial Continent.
* The Daoist Seal Hall displays every kind of seal except mountain seals, since the mountain is one itself. This is why it is also called the Missing One Hall.
* The Daoist Saber Room once put up a bounty for Song Changjing, on the grounds that Eastern Treasured Vial Continent did not deserve an eleventh tier martial artist.
* It was said that if the Sword Qi Great Wall fell, the second disciple would take the mountain back to the Heavenly World.

pages.title: Sword Qi Great Wall
pages.content:
{{Spoilers}}
The '''Sword Qi Great Wall''' is a vast city wall on the edge of the [[Savage World]], reached from the [[Majestic World]] through the gate on [[Stalactite Mountain]]. For ten thousand years its sword cultivators have held back the demon tribe, led by the old great sword immortal [[Chen Qingdu]]. Its people are descended from convicts and refugees of the Majestic World. [[Chen Ping An]] first came there to deliver a sword to [[Ning Yao]], and he later served as its Hidden Official.

== Geography ==
The Savage World lies south of the wall, and the city where the clans live lies north of it.Chapter 277 The top of the wall carries a wide carriageway running from the southern edge to the northern edge.Chapter 610 Three moons hang in the sky, a sight unknown in the Majestic World.Chapter 280

Great sword immortals have carved huge characters into the southern face of the wall. The strokes are so large that cultivators live inside them, and some sword cultivators who keep out of the city's affairs make their homes there. A sage of the Confucian Sect and one of the Buddhist Sect guard the two ends of the wall, while a Daoist sage watches the sky.Chapter 612

The wall is a land without Dao, like the heavens beyond heavens faced by the Heavenly World. Even Ascension Tier sword cultivators are not forced to ascend, and in Ning Yao's words, not even the Heavenly Dao cares about the place.

== History ==
{{Spoilers|This section covers the origins of the wall and the later war, including events the donghua has not reached.}}
Ten thousand years ago, humans rose to the top of the world and drove the demon tribe into barren lands. Late in that war, conflict broke out among the humans, and the sword cultivators were exiled as prisoners to the place that became the wall. They built it and stood guard over it, while the lands beyond became the Savage World.Chapter 588 When the Savage World was still young, three of these prisoner sword cultivators, Chen Qingdu, Long Jun and Guan Zhao, went to challenge the demons atop Holding Moon Mountain. After that battle the demon ancestor vanished, and the two sides have fought ever since.Chapter 613

Since the wall was raised, Chen Qingdu has never left it, not even for the weddings or funerals of his own clan.Chapter 575 In the most dangerous battle in its history, when close to half the throne holders of the Savage World joined forces, he was the only one left standing on the wall. A demon of the Savage World once complained that its side had never won a single battle against the wall in ten thousand years.Chapter 622

Before Chen Ping'an's arrival, the two sides held a wager of thirteen duels. The Hidden Official went first, and her opponent surrendered without fighting. The wall nearly collapsed during the middle duels until A'Liang stepped in and carried it to victory.Chapter 279 In the war that followed, the Hidden Official Xiao Xun defected to the Savage World along with Luo Shan and Zhu An, badly wounding Zuo You on the way. Chen Ping'an was named the new Hidden Official, the youngest and weakest in the post's history.Chapter 626

== Society ==
More than a hundred thousand sword cultivators have lived there generation after generation, cut off from the outside world. Except for the few who can travel to Stalactite Mountain, they keep to their ancestors' teachings and never set foot in the Majestic World.Chapter 253 Liu Youzhou points out that the population is made up of convicts and refugees from the Majestic World, so their feelings toward the other side of the gate are not as warm as outsiders assume.Chapter 274

The major clans have long histories. The Yan Clan acts much like an empire's Ministry of Revenue and controls nearly half of the resources moving through the wall.Chapter 572 The Hidden Official is an ancient title passed down for generations, responsible for governance and punishment. On the wall, Chen Qingdu is the highest principle of all.Chapter 576

Outsiders who come to temper their swords must face three trials against local sword cultivators. Ning Yao explains that this is a mark of respect, and that daring to climb the wall and look out at the Savage World already proves someone a sword cultivator.Chapter 592 The wall also forbids its own cultivators below the Golden Core Tier from going to Stalactite Mountain to cultivate.

== Trivia ==
* The Dong Clan's founding ancestor once returned after more than two centuries away. He carried the head of a thirteenth tier great demon in a bamboo case and engraved the character "Dong" on the wall.Chapter 272
* A'Liang carved a character on the wall that Chen Ping'an calls "badass".
* Yuan Zaohua's list of the wall's ten strongest sword immortals is Chen Qingdu, Dong Sangeng, A'Liang, the Hidden Official, Chen Xi, Qi Tingji, Zuo You, Nalan Shaowei, the old deaf guy and Lu Zhi.
* Chen Ping'an later learns from Chen Qingdu that the wall naturally suppresses the Great Dao of martial arts.
* The generation of young sword cultivators in Chen Ping'an's time is described as the most bountiful in ten thousand years, though another chapter says it has the second-largest number of innate sword talents in that span.

pages.title: Tao Zi
pages.content:
{{Character |header1=Tao Zi |image1=Tao Zi.png |Aliases=Peach |Vital_status=Alive |Gender=Female |Species=Human |Relatives=Tao Kui (grandfather) |Allies=[[Bai Yuan]]
[[Song Jixin]] |Occupation=Cultivator of Sun Scorch Mountain |Current_affiliation(s)=[[Sun Scorch Mountain]] |Continent=[[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]] |Novel=Chapter 7 |Donghua=Episode 1 }} '''Tao Zi''' is the granddaughter of Tao Kui, the Pure Yang Sword Patriarch of Sun Scorch Mountain, and is regarded as the sect's most gifted young cultivator in five centuries. She travels to [[Jewel Small World]] under the protection of [[Bai Yuan]], who serves as her guardian throughout the visit. Her name is a homonym for the word meaning "peach", which is how she came to be affectionately nicknamed Peach. == Appearance == Tao Zi is a young girl whose skin is so fair and delicate that she is repeatedly compared to fine porcelain, with faint veins visible beneath the surface in strong light.Chapter 7 == Personality == Tao Zi is lively and warm, quick to make friends and genuinely curious about the world. She struck up a fast friendship with Song Jixin and kept up an easy, natural conversation with him that surprised both of them with how long it lasted.Chapter 57 She is not soft, however. When Chen Ping'an's slingshot shattered the food containers in the birdcage and her taller maidservant panicked and ran toward the wall to look, Tao Zi grabbed the maidservant's wrist, stopped her, and then slapped her across the face to snap her out of the panic and order her to raise the alarm.Chapter 48 She read the situation quickly, noted that the shots had not been aimed at her, and warned Bai Yuan not to drop his guard regardless. She was raised strictly and was not a child who made trouble for her seniors, even when left alone and bored.Chapter 45 == Background == Tao Zi's physical constitution, cultivation aptitude, personality, and natural gifts were said to rank near the top of every Sun Scorch Mountain sword immortal born in the past five hundred years. The sect viewed her as a prodigy with enormous upside and no apparent weaknesses, and invested heavily in her development.Chapter 45 She grew up hearing about her family's ancestral humiliation at the hands of Wind Lightning Field and knew the history of the ancestor whose body still sits on Wind Lightning Field's sparring arena with a sword through her skull. The adults in her family always told the story in as neutral a tone as they could manage, but Bai Yuan never did.Chapter 45 Her family owns three Sword Nurturing Gourds. Her grandfather's is gray. Another elder's is small and releases dozens of miniature flying swords. A third, belonging to a senior called Big Sister Su, is golden-purple in color and rarely taken out.Chapter 57 == Plot == Tao Zi arrived in [[Jewel Small World]] with Bai Yuan, who had come to retrieve a sword scripture. She was placed in the care of the Li Clan during his activities in the town and stayed within their manor as instructed, though she found the people there thoroughly incompetent.Chapter 48 When Chen Ping'an used a slingshot to smash the food containers in a birdcage inside the courtyard, her maidservants were thrown into confusion. Tao Zi kept her head, assessed that the boy had not been shooting at her, and promptly slapped the taller maidservant back to her senses before ordering the alarm raised. She then warned Bai Yuan, when he returned, not to assume everything was fine.Chapter 48 Song Jixin arranged to have her brought out of the Li Clan's residence so they could spend time at the kiln supervision office. He gave her an emerald-green Sword Nurturing Gourd as a gift. She called him "firewood collecting brother" because of the characters in his name, and he did not mind.Chapter 57 She was disappointed that Bai Yuan was unable to carry a mountain out of the small world for her. He had done this once before, bringing a mountain from a distant place all the way to Sun Scorch Mountain as a private estate for another person she admired, and Tao Zi had always wanted one of her own.Chapter 48 == Trivia == * She had to beg her senior Big Sister Su many times before being allowed to touch her golden-purple Sword Nurturing Gourd, and it was put away again quickly afterward.Chapter 57 * Even though she was very young, she had already heard enough about the dangers of cultivation to understand the stakes involved in what Bai Yuan was doing in the town.Chapter 45 == References == [[Category:Characters]] [[Category:Female]] [[Category:Alive]]

pages.title: Wei Bo
pages.content:
{{Character |header1=Wei Bo |image1=Wei Bo.jpg |Vital_status=Alive |Gender=Male |Species=Mountain God |Friend(s)=[[Chen Ping An]]
[[Zhu Lian]]
[[Zheng Dafeng]] |Allies=Xu Ruo |Enemie(s)=Jin Qing |Occupation=Northern Mountain God of the Great Li Empire
Mountain lord of Go Table Mountain (former) |Current_affiliation(s)=[[Great Li Empire]]
[[Downtrodden Mountain]] (partner) |Former_affiliation(s)=Divine Water Nation |Continent=[[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]] |Cultivation_rank=Unpolished Jade Tier |Novel=Chapter 98 }} '''Wei Bo''' is a mountain deity. Once the formal god of the Divine Water Nation's Northern Mountain, he was demoted to the lowly mountain lord of Go Table Mountain after the [[Great Li Empire]] conquered his nation. After a fateful encounter with [[A'Liang]] and [[Chen Ping An]], he rose to become the formal god of the Great Li Empire's Northern Mountain, seated on Cloud Drape Mountain beside the small town. He later became the first mountain god in the history of [[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]] to reach the Upper Five Tiers. Handsome, ethereal and seemingly carefree, Wei Bo is one of Chen Ping'an's most dependable friends and allies. He is a frequent visitor to [[Downtrodden Mountain]], and Chen Ping'an's partner in Ox Horn Mountain. == Appearance == Wei Bo's true form is a strikingly handsome young man, sometimes described as more beautiful than a woman, in white robes with large flowing sleeves that billow like clouds. He wears a pale gold earring with illusion powers and, as mountain lord, carried a green bamboo cane signifying his status. When first encountered, he hides behind the form of a tiny, white-haired, dishevelled old man who barely reaches Zhu He's waist. Even [[Zhu Lu]] admitted he was the living embodiment of "spirited and handsome", and others say that only [[Cui Dongshan]], Lu Tai and [[Cao Ci]] can compare with him in looks. == Personality == At Go Table Mountain, Wei Bo appears cowardly and obsequious, grovelling before A'Liang and scheming to survive the two pythons that bullied him for centuries. Once restored to power, his true personality emerges: relaxed, witty, generous and extremely sociable. He remembers everyone's name and background, and is renowned for being easy to approach despite his status. He describes himself as easily persuaded by reason but impossible to cow by force, and as someone who will refuse to do anything if he can be idle. Beneath his charm, he is shrewd and politically astute. The little boy in azure accuses him of "hiding blades behind his smiles". He keeps a careful balance between his loyalty to the [[Great Li Empire]] and his friendship with Chen Ping'an, and will firmly discipline subordinates and rivals when needed. He reveres A'Liang deeply, and is said to carry a long-held, quiet devotion to a woman from his past. == Background == Wei Bo was made the formal god of the Northern Mountain by the final emperor of the Divine Water Nation. When the Great Li Empire conquered the nation, he secretly protected refugees fleeing the war, including the ancestors of the people of Red Candle Town, who still tell stories praising him.Chapter 105 This enraged the founding emperor of the Great Li Empire. Wei Bo's golden statue was shattered and thrown into the water, and someone painstakingly pieced his body back together. He was demoted to a mere mountain lord of Go Table Mountain, with his territory cut by 150 kilometres in radius.Chapter 102 Records in the Great Li Empire's Ministry of Rites say that he had delayed forming his godly body for many years for the sake of a certain woman, and that he refused to let her go.Chapter 115 (1) He feels guilt towards the [[Clans|Liu Clan]] of the Divine Water Nation. He is also the last surviving deity of that nation, and secretly kept 15,000 litres of its spring water before it fell. == Plot == === Go Table Mountain === When [[Zhu He]] accidentally summons him with a Soil Molding Technique, the "old" mountain lord appears and furiously beats Zhu He's calf with his cane. He reveals that he has spent centuries hiding from a black python and a white python that rule his mountain, and as the black python closes in, he even urges it to eat the children instead.Chapter 98 A'Liang then appears beside him unnoticed and runs him through with his bamboo saber. Being a deity, Wei Bo is unharmed, but he is struck by lightning when he tries to flee.Chapter 100 (1) Wei Bo then reveals his true, handsome form and fawns on [[A'Liang]], whom he calls "great immortal". A'Liang kills the white python and makes Wei Bo and the black python pay a "farewell gift" from their hoard: a yellow ebony box full of treasures, from which Li Huai, Li Baoping, Lin Shouyi, Zhu He and Zhu Lu each pick an item. Chen Ping'an takes a withered golden lotus seed. A'Liang also cuts down a great swathe of Wei Bo's precious courage bamboo, descended from the famed bamboo of the Bamboo Sea Small World's Azure Divine Mountain. Wei Bo agrees to build a bamboo building for Chen Ping'an on Downtrodden Mountain, make A'Liang a new bamboo saber, and move the black python there. After A'Liang's departure, Wei Bo saves the life of the Great Li cultivator Liu Yu, whom A'Liang had struck down. He is also approached by Xu Ruo, a Mohist swordsman serving the Great Li Empire. Wei Bo trades valuable information about the newly promoted river goddess of the Iron Talisman River, [[Yang Hua]], asking in return only for a smoother path to immortality for a certain new disciple of the Palace of Eternal Spring.Chapter 125 The Great Li Empire then offers him the position of god of its new Northern Mountain, which he accepts, joking that surviving A'Liang's saber surely qualifies him.Chapter 145 (1) === Northern Mountain God === When Chen Ping'an returns from Great Sui, Wei Bo greets him as his new neighbour on Cloud Drape Mountain and shows him the finished bamboo building.Chapter 179 He deliberately takes Chen Ping'an on a tour of the surrounding mountains, including the ferry station on Parasol Tree Mountain and Ox Horn Mountain's Cloth Wrapper Shop. This is a clear signal to every immortal sect in the area that Chen Ping'an is under the protection of the new Northern Mountain God.Chapter 189 (2) He brings Chen Ping'an medicine worth tens of thousands of taels of silver during Cui Cheng's brutal training, finds him the Sword Nurturing Gourd "Jiang Hu", carves locust wood scabbards for his swords, and tells him stories of the Sword Qi Great Wall and A'Liang's legendary battles. Wei Bo comes to understand that the strike from A'Liang's bamboo saber at Go Table Mountain greatly strengthened his godly body, allowing him to govern the thirty-odd mountains of the region with ease. Looking south, he quietly wishes a certain someone a good life, adding that she should never fall for a scholar again.Chapter 190 He plants Chen Ping'an's golden lotus seed in a pond behind the bamboo building, filled with water from the fallen Divine Water Nation. The seed is revealed to be a relic of the Daoist [[Lu Chen]] that keeps the nation's remnant fortune alive. Lu Chen himself visits and pins Wei Bo helplessly to the ground. Wei Bo's relationship with Downtrodden Mountain's own mountain god, the loyal Great Li official Song Yuzhang, gradually sours. While Chen Ping'an is away, Wei Bo writes him detailed secret letters, sending him two secret techniques from the Divine Water Nation's imperial clan and armoury. He also brokers his purchases of mountains in Dragon Spring Prefecture and oversees the pond's growing lotus spirit. === Partnership with Downtrodden Mountain === When Chen Ping'an returns from Bamboo Scroll Lake, Wei Bo becomes the go-between for his mountain purchases. Ox Horn Mountain and its immortal ferry station are placed under Wei Bo's name, and the two privately agree to split the profits evenly. Chen Ping'an lends him a valuable jade tablet for a hundred years in exchange for courage bamboo, and gives him the larger of two colored glaze golden body fragments of the Ascension Tier cultivator Du Mao. Such fragments are priceless, and even more valuable to deities than to cultivators.Chapter 461 (2) Wei Bo later quietly confirms that he can refine it within ten years. Wei Bo witnesses Chen Ping'an's land contract with the Great Li Empire at Forest Deer Academy and hosts his first Night Travel Banquet for the deities of his territory. When the river goddess Yang Hua tries to provoke Chen Ping'an, Wei Bo stops her. On a walk along the river, he calmly lectures her on respect and then strips her temple's incense essence and river fortune to make his point.Chapter 477 (1) That same night, he helps Chen Ping'an with a crisis of conscience, telling him that "one's heart must contain both a sun and a moon". Wei Bo becomes close friends with [[Zhu Lian]], whom he regrets not having met sooner, and with [[Zheng Dafeng]]. The three play Go together often and jointly run Downtrodden Mountain's affairs during Chen Ping'an's absence. After Downtrodden Mountain acquires part of the shattered Lotus Flower Blessed Land, they negotiate how to fund raising it to a medium-grade blessed land. Wei Bo hosts three Night Travel Banquets in quick succession and opens a Cloth Wrapper Shop branch to raise immortal coins, taking only a 10% share. === Upper Five Tiers === Wei Bo enters seclusion, guarded by Xu Ruo, and breaks through. Ruan Qiong observes that the barrier he should have faced had been shattered long ago in a very subtle way, so the challenge for Wei Bo was not breaking through, but reaching a more flawless Unpolished Jade Tier.Chapter 528 (2) His breakthrough fills his territory with auspicious phenomena and makes him the first Upper Five Tier mountain god in the history of the continent. The new emperor, Song He, personally climbs Cloud Drape Mountain with two head ministers to congratulate him and gives him a pseudo-celestial tool that lets him command the water fortune of his territory.Chapter 550 (4) Wei Bo then travels to the new Central Mountain to confront its god, Jin Qing, who had neglected to show proper respect to the Northern Mountain. When Jin Qing defies him, their Dao Manifestations clash on the Central Mountain's summit. Wei Bo's manifestation, over five hundred feet taller even on enemy ground, forces Jin Qing's to its knees. Wei Bo tells him to visit Cloud Drape Mountain, with generous gifts.Chapter 560 (2) He later explains that he intervened because Jin Qing is the only Central Mountain candidate he can stand. He then visits Xu Ruo, telling him he brought no gift because the favour he owes him is too great to repay. Wei Bo welcomes Chen Ping'an home, takes him into the Lotus Root Blessed Land, keeps Pei Qian hidden from prying eyes after her rapid martial breakthroughs, and helps choose the site for Downtrodden Mountain's ancestral hall. He privately warns Chen Ping'an to stay true to himself now that he rules a blessed land of forty million people. At the hall's founding, Wei Bo leaves first, implicitly granting Chen Ping'an authority over decisions concerning Cloud Drape Mountain. == Abilities == * '''Mountain god powers:''' As Northern Mountain God, he can sense everything within his territory, transport people instantly across it, summon the black python, manipulate mountain mist, and channel the fortune of all mountains and rivers under his jurisdiction. * '''Cultivation:''' He reached the Unpolished Jade Tier, the first mountain god of Eastern Treasured Vial Continent to enter the Upper Five Tiers. His godly body was greatly strengthened by A'Liang's saber strike. * '''Dao Manifestation:''' He overpowered the Central Mountain God's manifestation on the latter's own ground. * '''Illusions:''' His pale gold earring hides his true form, and he can conceal treasures from cultivators below the tenth tier. * '''Knowledge:''' He has encyclopaedic knowledge of treasures, the cultivation world, mountains and rivers, and politics. He is also a skilled Go player. == Possessions == * '''Pale gold earring''': an illusion treasure. * '''Green bamboo cane''': the symbol of his status as mountain lord. * '''Courage bamboo forest''': descended from the bamboo of Azure Divine Mountain. * '''Colored glaze golden body fragment''': from Du Mao, gifted by Chen Ping'an. * '''Jade tablet''': on loan from Chen Ping'an for a hundred years. * '''Pseudo-celestial tool''': gifted by Emperor Song He, granting control of water fortune. * '''Parasol leaf umbrella''': the entrance to the Lotus Root Blessed Land, held for Downtrodden Mountain. * '''Share of Ox Horn Mountain''': co-owned with Chen Ping'an. == Trivia == * Despite his lofty status, he picked up a children's folk song about stinky tofu from Pei Qian. * Others on Downtrodden Mountain joke that he is vain and easily offended, and they take care not to hurt his pride over money. * In Go games among Wei Bo, Zhu Lian and Zheng Dafeng, whoever Zheng Dafeng helps always wins. == References ==

pages.title: Wei Jin
pages.content:
{{Character |header1 = Wei Jin |image1 = Wei Jin.png |Vital_status = Alive |Gender = Male |Species = Human |Aliases = Drunken Sword Immortal |Master(s) = Patriarch of the Divine Platform |Love_interest(s) = [[He Xiaoliang]] (One-sided) |Friend(s) = [[A'Liang]]
[[Chen Ping An]] |Occupation = Sword immortal |Current_affiliation(s) = [[Wind Snow Temple]] (Divine Platform) |Continent = [[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]] |Cultivation_rank = Unpolished Jade Tier }} {{Spoilers}} == Appearance == Wei Jin is a sword immortal who wears white robes. He carries his renowned sword, High Radiance, in a scabbard at his waist.Chapter 127 In his earlier years, he was known for traveling with a white donkey and a silver-white Sword Nurturing Gourd, though both items eventually ended up in [[A'Liang]]'s possession. To the children he encounters during his travels, he cuts an impressive figure: his sword arrives before he does, sword qi hovering around his white robes as he descends from the sky. == Personality == Wei Jin has a cold personality. He likes to keep to himself and wanders from place to place, which [[Ruan Qiong]] attributes to peculiar idiosyncrasies.Chapter 88 Even after becoming a sword immortal, he prefers to ride his white donkey rather than fly on his sword, often swaying drunkenly on its back and sharing wine with the animal from his palm. A'Liang once teased him for being pedantic about riding such a slow mount.Chapter 93 Despite his aloof reputation, he is polite and patient even toward children. [[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]] once called him "a very good person" for being willing to explain things to them despite his status. [[Lin Shouyi]], however, noticed that Wei Jin seemed to look down on Chen Ping'an and was the least optimistic about his prospects among the children.Chapter 130 Years later, Chen Ping'an still recalled Wei Jin's apathetic gaze toward him but continued to consider him a good person.Chapter 524 He is a passionate swordsman who longs for battle. After hearing A'Liang's stories about the Sword Qi Great Wall, he yearned to visit Stalactite Mountain. Following his clash at Lady Chu's residence, he sighed that he had not fought to his heart's content.Chapter 128 In matters of the heart, however, he is helpless. He fell in love at first sight with the Daoist nun [[He Xiaoliang]], widely lauded as one of the brightest talents on the continent, and pursued her for years. His feelings were completely unrequited, and the story became an amusing tale that spread through the cultivation circles of Eastern Treasured Vile Continent. At the Sword Qi Great Wall, he remained frank and honest in dealing with others. When Chen Qingdu offered him guidance, Wei Jin admitted openly that he had always felt guilty about attributing the lucky circumstances of his advancement to his own abilities.Chapter 649 He told the old great sword immortal that as the only sword immortal from the Eastern Treasured Vile Continent, he wanted to come to the Sword Qi Great Wall without selfish desires and hoped to leave in a gallant manner. == Background == Wei Jin is the pillar of the Divine Platform, a small branch of [[Wind Snow Temple]] with very few disciples. At a young age, he was found by one of Wind Snow Temple's patriarchs during the patriarch's travels and taken on as a disciple. Despite being only around twenty when he arrived at the sect, his seniority through this master meant that cultivators over a hundred years old had to refer to him as grandmaster. After his master perished during a failed breakthrough attempt, the Divine Platform branch had few bright talents left, and Wei Jin became increasingly detached from the main sect. He spent seven or eight years traveling the world, returning only on his master's death anniversaries. He used his prized Sword Nurturing Gourd not to nurture flying swords but to carry wine, and was often so drunk that he would lie on his donkey's back and let it carry him wherever it pleased. This earned him the reputation of a drunken sword immortal. At barely forty years old, Wei Jin broke through to the Upper Five Tiers as a terrestrial sword immortal, becoming the youngest Upper Five Tier cultivator on Eastern Treasured Vile Continent. He broke the record previously held by [[Wind Lightning Field]]'s Li Tuanjing, and together with Song Changjing, the two were regarded as the undisputed "jade walls" of the south and north among the continent's young cultivators. His rapid advancement was partly thanks to guidance from A'Liang, who had sought him out specifically to teach him swordsmanship. A'Liang used a risky method of utilizing Wei Jin's future potential to allow him to break through earlier than expected. Right after exiting seclusion, Wei Jin rushed to Lady Chu's residence and shattered its night sky barrier with a single strike that severed a mountain range. The Mohist swordsman Xu Ruo blocked his follow-up strike by pushing his own sword just one inch from its scabbard. Wei Jin then accompanied Chen Ping'an and the children on part of their journey north, giving them a Peace and Safety Tablet from Wind Snow Temple and gifting [[Li Huai]] five small clay statues before departing to sharpen his swords at the Dragon Slaying Platform in Jewel Small World. He later challenged Heavenly Lord [[Xie Shi]] of the [[Northern Complete Reed Continent]], who was cultivating in seclusion on the Eastern Treasured Vile Continent. Wei Jin lost the fight, but the cultivators of his home continent felt no resentment toward him. Instead, they took pride in his willingness to stand up for their lands.Chapter 452 Afterward, he left the continent alone, flying on his sword toward Stalactite Mountain and the Sword Qi Great Wall. At the Sword Qi Great Wall, Wei Jin was given the small thatched cottage behind Chen Qingdu's own dwelling, a privilege previously reserved for Cao Ci and Chen Ping'an. He was fond of Zuo You, one of the few swordsmen on the wall that Zuo You would bother speaking to, and grew to respect Chen Ping'an after witnessing his role as the Hidden Official. When the sword immortals of the Majestic World gathered at the Spring Banner Inn on Stalactite Mountain to negotiate with the intercontinental ship administrators, Wei Jin met with the administrators from his home continent and declared that if he reached the Immortal Tier and survived the war, he would travel to the Northern Complete Reed Continent to challenge Xie Shi again.Chapter 633 [[Chen Qingdu]] told Wei Jin that he should not remain at the Sword Qi Great Wall forever and offered him three continents to choose from after the war: the Southern Whirl Continent, the Circling Ascension Continent, and the Golden Armor Continent. When Wei Jin asked if this was his only option, the old great sword immortal replied: "Why are you asking me? Go and ask your sword."Chapter 585 Wei Jin chose the Circling Ascension Continent, but resolved to first earn enough battlefield contributions for the Divine Platform to match Xie Songhua's. He felt he owed that much to his late master's memory. == Trivia == * [[Li Baoping]] later said that the small gourd she owned was "swindled" from Wei Jin, and that it was better than her saber, Auspicious Talisman. * Chen Ping'an long regarded Wei Jin's strike against Lady Chu's barrier as one of the flying sword strikes that left a lasting mark on his understanding of the sword, alongside Zuo You's and Fan Junmao's. * Li Huai felt Wei Jin was "not as good as A'Liang" and made his clay swordsman statue kneel and beg for forgiveness. * * Wei Jin was the only sword immortal from the Eastern Treasured Vile Continent at the Sword Qi Great Wall. Chen Qingdu noted that things he did not wish for often came to him in abundance, while things he sorely desired always seemed to pass him by. * A'Liang's reason for seeking out Wei Jin and teaching him swordsmanship was not out of charity. As Chen Qingdu explained, A'Liang sincerely hoped that Wei Jin could one day stand shoulder to shoulder with him, and he felt the same way toward all like-minded cultivators walking the same path behind him. == References ==

'''Xie Shi''' is a Daoist cultivator who grew up on Peach Leaf Alley in the small town of Jewel Small World. He became the most powerful Daoist on the Northern Complete Reed Continent and is known there as its Dao Master. He is the ancestor of Xie Ling and one of the town's most famous descendants, along with [[Cao Xi]].

== Appearance ==
Xie Shi looks like a middle-aged man.Chapter 187 Despite his standing, he looks much like one of the rough farmers of the small town. Few would guess that he has read widely and knows the teachings of all three schools.Chapter 235

== Personality ==
Across several continents Xie Shi is known as an honest and upright man who never acts against his conscience. People compare him to the sun in the sky.Chapter 185 Even his enemies respect him. He speaks little and dislikes chatter. He has no patience for Cao Xi's teasing and tells him plainly that he does not trust him.

He takes others seriously regardless of their age. Even with a child many generations younger, he gives his full attention and never lets his mind wander. He holds his descendants to a high standard. He would have given up on Xie Ling if the boy had shown any wish to leave his teacher [[Ruan Qiong]] for a more powerful one.Chapter 201

Being forced into a task he finds dishonourable weighs on him. He admitted to Xie Ling that he felt guilty, and told him that the Daoist path is one where examining one's own conscience matters most. Before his branch master [[Lu Chen]] he is nervous and obedient, quick to stand and quick to obey.Chapter 204

== Background ==
Xie Shi was born into the Xie Clan of Peach Leaf Alley. As a child he wrote his name on the wall of the small temple along with other children such as Cao Xi.Chapter 51 He came close to dying twice in the town, and both times he was saved by [[Zhi Gui]]. She once said he would have been swept away by a flood if not for her.Chapter 39 Like everyone born in the town, he has a bonded porcelain held by a buyer outside, which gives that buyer power over his life.Chapter 61

He left the small world and rose to become the Dao Master of the Northern Complete Reed Continent. Several of the Five Mountains of various empires there hold sects of his lineage, and his faction is the strongest Daoist one on the continent. That continent has no full Heavenly Lord, and he is described as being half of one.Chapter 191

After [[Chen Ping An]]'s bonded porcelain was broken, the buyer's backers used Xie Shi's own porcelain to make him travel south and press the Great Li Empire. He returned to the town on New Year's Day. When a girl at his clan's door did not believe him, he told her to check the genealogy, where his name was written with one stroke missing. He then offered incense in the ancestral hall and chose the long-browed boy, Xie Ling, as the only descendant worth his attention.

At the relay station, he demanded that the Great Li Empire hand over He Xiaoliang, Ma Kuxuan or [[Li Xisheng]]. He offered to guard Summer Resort Mountain against Lake View Academy if they agreed, and threatened trouble on the empire's northern border if they refused. Cao Xi, Xu Ruo, Ruan Qiong, Cui Chan and an old martial artist all gathered around him. When Xu Ruo challenged him to a fight to the death, an oriole sent by Xie Shi's elder landed on his shoulder and relayed an offer that eased the deal.Chapter 200

During this time, Lu Chen visited and gave Xie Ling a gift. He also ordered Xie Shi to keep He Xiaoliang alive for the next sixty years. Xie Shi then took Xie Ling to Old Man Yang's medicine shop and paid with his own promise for a treasure and a promise for the boy.

The sinking of Ceremony Mountain's Kun ship gave Xie Shi the reason he needed to move into the central region of the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent. There he stood guard north of Lake View Academy and cut the continent in two, so the Great Li Empire could conquer the north without interference. He held back the academy and took on three challengers in a row.Chapter 526 [[Wei Jin]] of Wind Snow Temple later fought him. The result was never made public, but Xie Shi stayed on the continent, so it was taken that he had not lost.Chapter 452

He eventually returned to the Northern Complete Reed Continent. He supported He Xiaoliang in founding the Refreshing Sect.Chapter 494 When she offended the Jade Forest Sect and Bai Shang, one of his direct disciples went to her sect in anger.Chapter 555 Xie Shi himself scolded her and sent her to apologize.Chapter 562

== Trivia ==
* The "Shi" in his name is written with one dot missing in the Xie Clan genealogy.
* Cao Xi taunts him by calling him Old Man Xie, and the two have never got along.
* He gave Xie Ling two treasures. One was the flying sword of a dead sword immortal, called Peach Leaf, for Xie Ling to refine into a bonded item. The other was a high-grade Sword Nurturing Gourd named Full Moon.Chapter 528
* He once taught Dao techniques to a young man from a powerful Daoist clan without taking him as a disciple, because he was said to be unable to take disciples. Elsewhere the novel mentions his direct disciples.
* He is ranked among the top ten cultivators of the Northern Complete Reed Continent.
* After his rise became known, the Xie Clan of Peach Leaf Alley went from a declining family to one of note in the town.

pages.title: Xie Xie
pages.content:
{{Character |header1 = Xie Xie |image1 = Xie Xie.png |Aliases = Xie Lingyue (real name) |Vital_status = Alive |Gender = Female |Species = Human |Age = 13 (Chapter 134) |Master(s) = [[Cui Dongshan]] |Relatives = Wind God Xie Clan |Friend(s) = [[Li Huai]] |Allies = [[Lin Shouyi]]
[[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]] |Occupation = Qi refiner
Maidservant and disciple of Cui Dongshan |Current_affiliation(s) = [[Mountain Cliff Academy]] |Former_affiliation(s) = Lu Empire
Wind God Xie Clan |Continent = [[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]] |Cultivation_rank = Fifth Tier Qi refiner (restored) |Novel = Chapter 131 }} '''Xie Xie''', whose real name is '''Xie Lingyue''', is a descendant of the Wind God Xie Clan of the fallen Lu Empire, the empire's foremost cultivating clan. She was once the youngest Qi refiner in the Lu Empire to reach the fifth tier. After the empire's fall, her cultivation was sealed with Dragon Restricting Nails, and she passed from the control of [[Song Jixin]]'s mother into the hands of the imperial preceptor [[Cui Chan]], who mockingly renamed her "Xie Xie", meaning "thank you". She joins [[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]]'s group on its journey to [[Great Sui Nation]] together with [[Yu Lu]]. At [[Mountain Cliff Academy]], she becomes Cui Dongshan's maidservant and disciple, enduring years of harsh treatment while quietly regaining her strength. == Appearance == Xie Xie is a slender, dark-skinned girl with a stern expression and a naturally seductive voice. She carries a bamboo flute at her waist. Cui Chan describes her appearance as unremarkable. == Personality == Xie Xie is proud, guarded and bitter about the fate of her clan and the Lu Empire. She hides her feelings behind a smile, and Chen Ping'an finds her unapproachable. She feels ashamed of cultivators being called "transcendent and carefree beings" when she herself is a prisoner. She is fiercely ambitious, and Cui Chan claims she is so jealous of Lin Shouyi's smooth cultivation path that she is close to going mad. She cares more about results than study, and Mao Xiaodong notes she is far too fixated on cultivation. Beneath her cold exterior, she can be warm with those who don't threaten her. She gets along well with [[Li Huai]], playing battle games with him and his toys, and later smiles openly when her old companions visit. She has a long-running, childish feud with [[Li Baoping]]. == Background == The Wind God Xie Clan was the Lu Empire's number one cultivating clan, and the only one in history whose members all chose to fight and die for an empire. Hundreds of its cultivators fell defending the Lu Clan. Xie Lingyue survived and, after the empire's fall, was imprisoned with Dragon Restricting Nails driven into her body to seal her cultivation. She was at first under the control of the Great Li Empire's imperial concubine, Song Jixin's mother, before falling into Cui Chan's hands, which the narrative calls jumping "out of the frying pan and into the fire".Chapter 167 (3) == Plot == === Joining the Journey === Cui Chan brings her to his manor, where Yu Lu already works as his servant. She is hopeless at housework and breaks many dishes. When she refuses to give her name, Cui Chan names her "Xie Xie", saying she should thank him for it.Chapter 131 (2) On the road, she mocks Yu Lu, asking whether he still thinks he is the revered prince of the Lu Empire.Chapter 132 She joins Chen Ping'an's group with Yu Lu and Cui Chan. She easily crushes Lin Shouyi at Go and becomes friends with Li Huai, but she and Li Baoping dislike each other intensely.Chapter 133 (2) Li Baoping accuses her of snoring so loudly she can be heard from far away. Xie Xie denies it, then retorts that she is a cultivator, someone people like Li Baoping revere as immortals.Chapter 140 Cui Chan secretly asks her to put in a good word for him with Chen Ping'an. She wanted his ownerless flying sword, but he only offers a Fish Bug Flute from the Lu Empire's secret imperial collection, a token of the alliance between a sect and the Lu Empire's first emperor. She tells Chen Ping'an all this frankly, admitting she is fond of beautiful things.Chapter 134 (1) At Cui Chan's urging, she and Yu Lu reveal their identities. When Yu Lu speaks calmly of the past, she explodes in tearful rage, declaring her true name, Xie Lingyue, and her clan's sacrifice for the "foolish and incompetent" royal family. Yu Lu coldly replies that she should die or assassinate Cui Chan if she truly has her ancestors' courage. Chen Ping'an tells them that grievances can be set aside without being forgotten.Chapter 155 Cui Chan later remarks on her jealousy of Lin Shouyi.Chapter 156 === Mountain Cliff Academy === When Lin Shouyi is beaten by the son of the late general Pan Maozhen, Xie Xie does not visit him. Instead, she seeks out the Pan boy the same day and beats him until he bleeds from every orifice.Chapter 165 (1) When Li Huai is bullied, though, she says she can do nothing against the Confucian prodigy Li Changying. Cui Chan, displeased, slaps her across the face. Cui Chan, now Cui Dongshan, removes half of the Dragon Restricting Nails from her body, and she quickly recovers to the fifth tier, light surging across her body.Chapter 170 (1) She becomes his disciple and maidservant, receiving a pile of treasures that only immortals could dream of, and becomes famous in the Great Sui capital under her real name.Chapter 206 (2) In return, she endures years of harsh treatment: kneeling at his door, serving tea, and being slapped across the room for setting down a Go stone too hard. Chen Ping'an, as Cui Dongshan's teacher, does not interfere, just as Cui Cheng never interfered with Pei Qian's training. It is later revealed that she and Yu Lu were pawns deliberately chosen by Cui Chan and the Great Li empress.Chapter 463 (1) === The Assassination Attempt === When Chen Ping'an returns, she sternly asks why he has come, but lets him in, and later invites Lin Shouyi to cultivate in Cui Dongshan's courtyard, which has some of the best feng shui in the academy. During the assassination attempt, she locks Li Baoping, Li Huai and Pei Qian in the study and uses Cui Dongshan's secret technique to turn the courtyard into a miniature small world. As its core, she holds firm against a Nascent Tier swordsman's flying sword until she coughs blood and collapses unconscious.Chapter 410 (1) Cui Dongshan praises her for making him look good. He is especially pleased that she let Pei Qian and Li Huai play with his precious Vibrant Cloud Stones, since stinginess would have reflected badly on him. For the first time, he gives her a genuine smile and offers her a reward of her choice.Chapter 412 The final Dragon Restricting Nail is removed, and Cui Dongshan suggests giving her the Li Fire flying sword taken from the assassin. === Later Years === Xie Xie continues to live in Cui Dongshan's old residence, cultivating wholeheartedly. With all the Dragon Restricting Nails removed, she progresses rapidly but hides it, and she leads the small-town students in cultivation.Chapter 570 (1) When Chen Ping'an and the others gather at her residence, she smiles at the visitors, glares at him for nearly taking off his boots, and is the most astonished of all at the news of Downtrodden Mountain's ancestral hall. Chen Ping'an invites her and Lin Shouyi to cultivate in the mountains of Dragon Spring Prefecture. == Abilities == * '''Qi refining:''' She was once the youngest fifth-tier Qi refiner in the Lu Empire. Her cultivation was sealed by Dragon Restricting Nails and restored once they were removed. * '''Formations:''' She can form a miniature small world using Cui Dongshan's secret technique. * '''Go:''' She is an exceptional player who easily beats Lin Shouyi. * '''Music:''' She plays the bamboo flute and the guqin. == Possessions == * '''Fish Bug Flute''': a bamboo flute from the Lu Empire's secret imperial collection, promised by Cui Chan. * '''Treasures from Cui Dongshan''': a pile of immortal treasures received as his disciple. * '''Li Fire flying sword''' (possibly): the assassin's sword, which Cui Dongshan suggested giving to her. == Trivia == * 谢谢 (xiè xie) means "thank you". Cui Chan chose the name to mock her. * Cui Dongshan once joked that she wanted to become Chen Ping'an's wife, to her silent mortification. * In Cui Dongshan's farewell performance, she plays the guqin across a lake from Yu Lu's flute, "like an immortal couple". == References == [[Category:Characters]] [[Category:Alive]] [[Category:Female]]

pages.title: Xu Yuanxia
pages.content:
{{Character|status=Alive|gender=Male|species=Human|master(s)=[[Old Yao]](previous)|enemies=[[Old Mountain Ape]]|friends/allies=[[Chen Ping An]]|donghua=Chapter 3}}
==Appearance==
Xu Yuanxia is described as a '''tall and sturdy''' man with a '''big beard'''. He has a '''rough''' and '''unrefined''' appearance. He has a '''muscular''' build and is often seen with a '''saber'''. He also is noted to have an '''unruly and untamed appearance'''.

Xu Yuanxia is frequently depicted wearing '''simple attire''', and he is also seen wearing '''armor''' on occasion. His clothing is sometimes described as '''old''' or '''worn'''. He is said to have '''sideburns like halberds''', and he has a '''dark and weathered''' complexion. His face is sometimes compared to that of a '''furious war deity'''. He is also described as having '''thick eyebrows''' and a '''wide mouth'''.

Despite his imposing appearance, Xu Yuanxia is not necessarily intimidating, and is seen as a '''hero''' by some. He is also portrayed as having a '''strong and healthy''' physique. His overall appearance is that of a '''rugged and powerful martial artist'''.

==Personality==
Xu Yuanxia is portrayed as a '''bold and straightforward''' individual with a '''strong sense of justice'''. He is '''unreserved and outspoken''', and does not hesitate to voice his opinions. Despite his rough exterior, he is '''kind-hearted and compassionate''', and is willing to help others in need. He is also described as being '''loyal''' and '''protective''' of his friends.

Xu Yuanxia is '''passionate about martial arts''' and is proud of his abilities. He can be '''boastful and arrogant''' at times, and he enjoys telling stories about his past exploits. He is also depicted as being '''somewhat naive''' and '''easily impressed''', and is easily swayed by flattery. While he can be '''quick to anger''', he is also quick to forgive. He is also '''shown to be quite perceptive''' of others. He is '''fond of drinking alcohol''' and enjoys the company of his friends.

Xu Yuanxia is also portrayed as being '''somewhat sentimental and nostalgic''', often thinking about his past and his family. He has a '''strong sense of responsibility''', and he feels a duty to protect the innocent and fight against evil forces. Though he is '''not particularly interested in romantic relationships''', he admits to having liked a woman before leaving home. In addition, it is mentioned that he is '''"not a stingy person"''' and also '''"not good with words,"''' and that he has a tendency to '''overthink things'''.

==Background==
Xu Yuanxia's background is that of a '''soldier''' who served in the border army, where he fought in many battles. He is also described as a '''fifth-tier martial artist'''. Although he is a skilled martial artist, he comes from a '''highly educated family''', which is considered a prominent clan in his county. Despite his family background, he chose to join the army, surprising many people.

Xu Yuanxia left the army to travel the world, but he continued to encounter death and suffering, which caused him some distress. He is said to have some knowledge of '''battle formations'''. He is also an '''earth immortal'''. He has a connection to the '''Azure Phoenix Nation''', and was involved in bringing an ash urn back to a person's family. He also attended the Liberation Rite of Water and Land and the Heavenly Worship Ceremony with Zhang Shanfeng.

Xu Yuanxia is said to be from a '''well-off family''' and had a marriage arranged for him before he left home, and he admits to liking the woman he was meant to marry. He is also described as being familiar with the local customs and traditions of the places he visits. He has traveled to the '''Azure Phoenix Nation''' and the '''Great Li Empire'''. It is also mentioned that he has been wandering around for more than ten years. While he is a skilled martial artist, he is also described as someone who is '''"not a stingy person"''' and '''"not good with words,"''' and that he has a tendency to '''overthink things''' [previous conversation].

==Trivia==

* Xu Yuanxia is a '''fifth-tier martial artist''' who was once a soldier in the border army [previous conversation].
* He comes from a '''highly educated family''', which is considered a prominent clan in his county, yet he chose to join the army [previous conversation].
* Despite his family background, he has a '''rough and unrefined appearance''', with a '''big beard''' and '''muscular''' build [previous conversation].
* He is described as having '''sideburns like halberds''' and a face like a '''furious war deity''' [previous conversation].
* He is '''bold and straightforward''', and doesn't hesitate to speak his mind [previous conversation].
* He is '''passionate about martial arts''' and enjoys telling stories about his past exploits, sometimes to the point of being '''boastful and arrogant''' [previous conversation].
* He is '''kind-hearted and compassionate''', willing to help others, and is '''loyal''' and '''protective''' of his friends [previous conversation].
* Though he can be quick to anger, he's also quick to forgive.
* He is '''somewhat naive and easily impressed''', and can be swayed by flattery [previous conversation].
* Xu Yuanxia is '''fond of drinking alcohol''' and enjoys the company of his friends [previous conversation].
* He has a '''strong sense of responsibility''' and feels a duty to protect the innocent and fight against evil [previous conversation].
* He is '''somewhat sentimental and nostalgic''', often thinking about his past and family [previous conversation].
* He admits to having liked a woman before leaving home, but is '''not particularly interested in romantic relationships''' [previous conversation].
* He is '''"not a stingy person"''' and also '''"not good with words,"''' and has a tendency to '''overthink things''' [previous conversation].
* He enjoys writing '''travel journals''' and recording the strange and dangerous natural sceneries he encounters.
* He is '''perceptive''' of others and notices details that others might miss [previous conversation].
* He is said to have knowledge of '''battle formations''' [previous conversation].
* He is an '''earth immortal''' [previous conversation].
* He was involved in bringing an '''ash urn''' back to a person's family [90, previous conversation].
* He attended the Liberation Rite of Water and Land and the Heavenly Worship Ceremony with Zhang Shanfeng [previous conversation].
* He has traveled to the '''Azure Phoenix Nation''' and the '''Great Li Empire''' [previous conversation].
* He has been wandering around for '''more than ten years''' [previous conversation].
* He is '''always unwilling to take transcontinental ships''' from ferry stations.
* He did not notice anything special about a white bowl but did recognize the value of a piece of lightning-struck ebony.
* Xu Yuanxia once '''smiled and shook his head''' when Chen Ping'an offered to split wine with him, implying he had already noticed Chen Ping'an's Sword Nurturing Gourd.
* He once had a long-standing grudge against a man, which led him to initially think ill of the man's grandson, only to later learn to appreciate the grandson as a good person.
* He is a good judge of character and can quickly assess a person's abilities, such as with Chen Ping'an and Ma Zhi.
* He enjoys a good challenge and was eager to bet with Mr. Hong, offering to have a drink whether he won or lost.
* He thinks a single sip of medicinal wine is enough for most martial artists to see amazing results.
* He believes that Chen Ping'an is the "least ambitious sword immortal in history".
* Xu Yuanxia '''enjoys bragging''', sometimes making grand pronouncements about his abilities [previous conversation].
* He sometimes '''recites Chan comments''' when excited.
* He is '''good at remembering details''' from the places he has visited [previous conversation].
* He '''overthinks things''' and has a tendency to get caught up in his own thoughts [previous conversation].
* He is '''always willing to offer praise''' and encouragement to his friends, especially Chen Ping'an [previous conversation].
* He once made up a line of poetry to describe himself, saying: "With sideburns like halberds, the hero raises his saber against all forces of evil," which was clearly dedicated to himself.
* He has a '''strong sense of humor''', and often makes jokes and teases his friends [previous conversation].
* He was '''once tricked into buying a fake Daoist talismanic sword'''.
* He once said, “But when it comes to wives, even two are too many.”.
