pages.title: Yang Hua
pages.content:
{{Character |header1 = Yang Hua |Aliases = Iron Talisman River Goddess |Vital_status = Deceased (deified) |Gender = Female |Species = River deity (formerly human) |Eye_color = Golden (godly body) |Master(s) = Empress dowager (Dao mentor) |Allies = Empress dowager |Enemie(s) = [[Liu Baqiao]] (rival for Talisman) |Occupation = Formal river goddess of the Iron Talisman River
Former maidservant of the imperial concubine |Current_affiliation(s) = [[Great Li Empire]] |Former_affiliation(s) = Imperial concubine's household |Continent = [[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]] |Cultivation_rank = Formerly near the Upper Five Tiers |Novel = Chapter 88 }} '''Yang Hua''' is the formal river goddess of the Iron Talisman River and the highest-ranking river deity of the Great Li Empire. She was once the personal sword-bearing maidservant of the empire's imperial concubine, the mother of [[Song Jixin]], and a talented Qi refiner on the verge of the Upper Five Tiers. When her mistress crossed the emperor, Yang Hua was punished in her place: she was forced to give up her human body and her path to immortality to become a river deity. Proud, cold and fiercely loyal to her former mistress, she is known for the golden-tasselled ancient sword "Talisman" that she always carries. == Appearance == Yang Hua was extremely beautiful as a human, despite a name considered crude and basic for someone of her looks. As a river goddess, she has golden hair three metres long, golden eyes, and a face concealed by armour. She is always seen holding her golden-tasselled sword. Shortly after becoming a goddess, she deliberately cut a deep gash into her own cheek with it. == Personality == Yang Hua is haughty, aloof and intensely proud. She almost never appears before others. She ignores her subordinate [[Ma Lanhua]]'s greetings, refuses to show proper respect even to the Northern Mountain God [[Wei Bo]], and crushes a gift he sends her in contempt. She is extremely confident in her swordsmanship and quick to lash out at anything she cannot see through. Her one unwavering loyalty is to her former mistress, who saved her life and became her Dao mentor. She endured death and excruciating torture for the slim chance of becoming a deity, and she resents the fate forced upon her by the emperor. Still, she has a quieter side. She long admired [[Mountain Cliff Academy]], and when its scholars later pass her temple, she breaks her usual seclusion to show them respect. == Background == Yang Hua was born in the countryside with a unique physique that gave her a strong affinity for water. A travelling Daoist priest once warned that she attracted dark and dirty things in the water and should never approach sourceless water alone. A geomantic official of the [[Great Li Empire]] noticed her and brought her before the imperial concubine. Under her, Yang Hua cultivated a top-notch water-element technique, making as much progress in three years as others made in thirty. She then won the recognition of "Talisman", the capital's famous talismanic sword that no one else could unsheathe, before the [[Wind Lightning Field]] swordsman [[Liu Baqiao]] could claim it.Chapter 118 (1) Liu Baqiao later complains bitterly that Song Changjing, rather than giving him the sword, told him to take it from Yang Hua by force.Chapter 133 (1) == Plot == === Maidservant of the Imperial Concubine === Yang Hua first appears in the small town as one of the attendants of the imperial concubine, alongside Xu Hunran and Wang Yifu. When her mistress asks her the price of a children's book in the capital, Yang Hua answers with flattery about the prince's upbringing. She obeys every strange order, such as walking 63 steps matching the stride of the seven-year-old Song Jixin. She knows that serving a powerful mistress is like serving a tigress.Chapter 89 She also reports on the empire's intelligence efforts, while carefully avoiding the power struggles at the top of the imperial court.Chapter 93 (1) === Forced Deification === On the advice of "Mr. Lu", the empire planned to use Talisman as the thirteenth flying sword of the replica White Jade Capital. It was instead used to split the Dragon Slaying Platform in Jewel Small World, and it cracked beyond repair after two strikes. The emperor then gave the broken sword back to Yang Hua, and at the same time appointed her river god of the Iron Talisman River. Cui Chan observes that this was a warning to her mistress, depriving the concubine of one of her most loyal and capable assistants.Chapter 117 (1) Cui Chan reflects that the concubine had crossed the emperor's bottom line by "collecting" the head of Song Yuzhang, and that Yang Hua's hasty appointment was her punishment.Chapter 117 (2) Becoming a river deity was regarded by orthodox Qi refiners as "taking a severed path" with no way to immortality. Yang Hua, who had been close to the Upper Five Tiers, understood that she was being punished for her achievements. Gazing at the damaged sword, she murmurs that in the end only it never abandoned her, and slashes a deep gash into her own cheek with its edge. === River Goddess === Wei Bo, now Northern Mountain God, sends her a precious ball of cloud root aura as a goodwill gift. Suspicious of his motives, she smiles coldly and crushes it, absorbing its energy.Chapter 190 Considered perhaps the youngest high-ranking river god on Eastern Treasured Vial Continent, she patrols her subordinate Dragon Whisker River for the first time and leaves without acknowledging Ma Lanhua's timid greeting.Chapter 201 (2) It is later noted that she abandoned her human body and died in order to become a deity.Chapter 463 (2) When Mao Xiaodong leads Mountain Cliff Academy's students past her temple, Yang Hua appears before them and pays her respects, though the academy has lost its official status. She admired the academy while still a maidservant, and once visited it with her mistress.Chapter 471 (1) === Confrontation with Chen Ping'an === When Chen Ping'an walks along the Iron Talisman River, Yang Hua appears in her godly body and sizes him up. She is suspicious of what she cannot see through in him, and hostile because of her devotion to her mistress, whose history with Chen Ping'an runs deep. She grows furious when he touches on that devotion. Her sword, she reflects, was formidable enough to have almost been placed in the replica White Jade Capital. Wei Bo arrives and quells her aura. She sneers that Chen Ping'an should hide under the protection of the martial artist in the bamboo building, and the river rumbles with her anger.Chapter 477 (1) Afterwards, Wei Bo takes her on a walk along the river, lectures her on respect, and strips her temple of incense essence and river fortune to drive the point home. == Abilities == * '''Water affinity:''' She was born with a physique deeply attuned to water, and was a prodigy of water-element cultivation. * '''Swordsmanship:''' She won the recognition of the sword Talisman and is extremely confident in her sword skills. * '''River goddess powers:''' She has authority over the Iron Talisman River and its subordinate waters, including the Dragon Whisker River. She can stir the river into violent turbulence. == Possessions == * '''Talisman''': a golden-tasselled ancient sword, once the most famous talismanic sword of the Great Li capital and renowned as the toughest sword on the continent. It was cracked beyond repair after striking the Dragon Slaying Platform, but she still carries it. == Trivia == * 杨花 (yáng huā) refers to willow or poplar catkins, which drift wherever the wind takes them, a symbol of being toyed with by fate. * She is described as a river goddess "who almost never appeared in front of other people". * Years later, [[Ma Kuxuan]] returns home and confronts Yang Hua at the waterfall where the two rivers meet. He tells her that, although he is only the grandson of a river guardian beneath her, he has heard she has not been kind to his grandmother. He threatens to refine her godly body at True Martial Mountain for a thousand years if she does not make amends. == References == [[Category:Characters]] [[Category:Female]]

pages.title: Yao Zhen
pages.content:
[[Category:Characters]]
{{Character|image1=Zhao Yao.PNG|status=Alive|gender=Male|species=Human|master(s)=[[Mister Qi]]|donghua=Chapter 2}}
==Appearance==
Yao Zhen is an old general who is described as being serious and unsmiling when in the army and at home. However, he becomes more relaxed and talkative when he interacts with Chen Ping'an. Despite his age, he is '''healthy and strong'''. 

==Personality==
Yao Zhen is portrayed as a complex character with a blend of strictness and warmth. He is described as an old general who is '''serious and unsmiling''' when in the army and at home. However, his demeanor changes when he interacts with Chen Ping'an, becoming more '''relaxed and talkative'''. Despite his age, he is still physically robust, as he is described as '''healthy and strong'''. A recent disaster has left him '''heartbroken''', leading to a change in his temperament. Yao Zhen is also incredibly '''stubborn''' and adheres strictly to hierarchical relationships, more so than even pedantic Confucian scholars. He is a subordinate of the Imperial Liu Clan. He is also very fond of Chen Ping'an, considering him a young benefactor and enjoying his company. He is also willing to reveal secrets about the Great Quan Empire to Chen Ping'an that he would not have shared before. Additionally, Yao Zhen demonstrates a sense of loyalty and protectiveness towards those he cares about and is willing to risk his life for Chen Ping'an. Although he is generally serious, he also has a sense of humor, as seen when he jokes with Chen Ping'an, and there are moments when he shows a "youthful shamelessness".

==Background==
Yao Zhen is an old general who is a subordinate of the Imperial Liu Clan. He and his clan have lived in the '''rough border regions for many generations'''. The Yao Clan is a large military clan. They are known for their mounted troops. Yao Zhen is a capable military leader, and his family is very focused on military strategy and literary studies. Despite their martial background, they place a heavy emphasis on literary studies, which is necessary for setting up military formations and employing military strategies.

Yao Zhen's ancestors were from the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent. According to a fortune teller, one of their ancestors had the character "Zhi" in their name and that this character had a strong affinity with Yao Zhen's grandchildren's generation. Because of this, all the children of Yao Zhen's grandchildren's generation have "Zhi" in their names, including Yao Jinzhi, Yao Lingzhi, and Yao Xianzhi.

He is also described as being very familiar with the rules and schemes of officialdom. The Yao clan has a long history of making contributions and being rewarded by the imperial court, with some members dying in battle, leaving behind widows. Yao Zhen is very strict about the hierarchical relationships between rulers and officials. He is also very protective of his family. He has become heartbroken after a recent disaster that his clan experienced. Despite his serious nature, Yao Zhen is also capable of showing a sense of humor and "youthful shamelessness".

pages.title: Yellow Court Nation
pages.content:
Yellow Court Nation is a significant, though not the most powerful, political entity in the sources, and it presents a complex picture of a nation navigating its place in a world dominated by larger empires.

'''Political Status and Relationships:'''

* '''Subsidiary Nation:''' Yellow Court Nation is a '''subsidiary nation of the Great Sui Empire'''. This status significantly limits its autonomy and influences its internal and external policies.
* '''Tribute:''' As a subsidiary nation, it is implied that Yellow Court Nation pays tribute to Great Sui.
* '''Influence of Great Sui:''' The influence of Great Sui is considerable, impacting the appointment of mountain and river gods within Yellow Court Nation, which are few.
* '''Relationship with Great Li:''' Yellow Court Nation is located south of the Great Li Empire, making it a neighbor and a point of interest for the expanding Great Li Empire.
* '''Observing the Great Li Empire:''' Yellow Court Nation, along with other nations to the north and south, is carefully observing the Great Li Empire’s expansion.
* '''Potential Annexation''': There is a possibility that Yellow Court Nation will become a subsidiary nation of the Great Li Empire in the future, which is why they are giving preferential treatment to traveling scholars from the Great Li Empire.

'''Geographical and Resource Limitations:'''

* '''Limited Territory:''' The northern region of Yellow Court Nation has limited territory, and mountain and river gods are quite rare.
* '''Lack of Resources:''' Compared to the southern region of the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent, Yellow Court Nation is implied to be lacking in resources.

'''Cultural and Social Aspects:'''

* '''Confucianism:''' Like the Great Sui Empire, Yellow Court Nation appears to have a culture influenced by Confucianism, but there are also other influences.
* '''Academies:''' The nation has some academies of Confucianism, but they do not seem to have the same status as those in Great Sui or Great Li.
* '''Treatment of Scholars:''' Traveling scholars from the Great Li Empire are given preferential treatment.
* '''Corruption:''' It is suggested that the Hong Clan, which has a strong influence in Yellow Court Nation, is "rotten to the core," implying systemic corruption.
* '''Limited Cultivation''': The cultivation paths available are limited, and even if the Hong Clan could appoint as many gods as they pleased, they would still be limited by the nation.

'''Military and Defense:'''

* '''Weak Armies''': The armies of Yellow Court Nation are not very strong. They are not a match for the Great Li Empire.
* '''Reliance on Great Sui''': As a subsidiary nation, they rely on Great Sui for protection.
* '''Lack of Assigned Gods:''' Yellow Court Nation lacks mountain and river gods assigned by the emperor of the Great Sui Empire.

'''Key Figures and Groups:'''

* '''Hong Clan:''' The founding clan of Yellow Court Nation. They appear to hold significant influence and are possibly corrupt.
* '''Chu Clan:''' The Chu Clan is mentioned as the family that owns the Great Water Palace, but this is proclaimed to be a front to the public.
* '''Cold Food Great River God:''' A high-ranking god of Yellow Court Nation who has a lavish palace outside the cities and towns. He is powerful within the nation.
* '''Gao Xuan:''' A prince of Yellow Court Nation.
* '''Spies:''' The Great Sui Nation has spies within the Great Li Empire.

'''Specific Locations and Structures:'''

* '''City God Temple:''' The nation has city god temples, and the wall murals within them are said to be very realistic.
* '''Great Water Palace:''' A lavish palace owned by the Cold Food Great River God, but proclaimed to be owned by the Chu Clan.
* '''Pillow Relay Station''': A relay station at Red Candle Town where guests of the empire can stay.
* '''Mountain Forests in the North''': A villa in the northern forests near a river that features cliff carvings.

'''Challenges and Internal Issues:'''

* '''Internal Strife:''' There is a possibility of internal conflict and instability.
* '''Limited Potential''': Due to their limited territory and resources, there is a limit to the potential achievements of those within the nation.
* '''Unease about the Great Li Empire:''' The nation is aware of the growing power of the Great Li Empire and its potential threat.
* '''Fear of Collapse:''' There is an implied fear that the nation could collapse, much like the Lu Empire before it.

'''Interactions with Others:'''

* '''Great Li Empire:''' They are trying to maintain good relations with scholars from Great Li Empire.
* '''Great Sui Nation:''' They are a subsidiary nation and subject to the will of the Great Sui Empire.
* '''Cultivators''': Cultivators from other nations and sects have entered Yellow Court Nation.
* '''Chen Ping'an's impact''': Chen Ping'an, though not from Yellow Court Nation, interacts with people in Yellow Court Nation, influencing local events and relationships.

Yellow Court Nation is a nation that is trying to maintain stability and navigate its place in a world dominated by larger empires. It is subject to the will of the Great Sui Empire, and it is also under the watchful eye of the Great Li Empire. The nation struggles with internal corruption, limited resources, and a weak military. Despite these challenges, the people of Yellow Court Nation, like those in other nations, have their own culture and pride.

{{Character |header1=Gu Tao (Yin god) |image1=Yin god.png |Aliases=The yin god |Vital_status=Alive |Gender=Male |Species=Yin spirit (formerly human) |Relatives=[[Gu Can]] (son)
Gu Can's mother (wife) |Master(s)=[[Old Man Yang]] |Allies=[[Chen Ping An]]
[[Lin Shouyi]] |Occupation=Yin god
Deity of the Great Li Empire |Current_affiliation(s)=[[Great Li Empire]] |Continent=[[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]] |Novel=Chapter 112 (as the yin god) }} '''Gu Tao''' is a yin god of the [[Great Li Empire]], the husband of Gu Can's mother and the father of [[Gu Can]]. He once lived in the small town of [[Jewel Small World]] and never made it home, and his soul has been wandering as a yin god since. He secretly protected [[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]] and his companions on the road to White Emperor City without revealing who he was. == Appearance == Gu Tao appears as a man whose face closely resembles [[Gu Can]]'s.Chapter 426 In his yin god form he is hazy and faint, and he can make himself entirely invisible or sharpen his appearance at will. == Personality == Gu Tao is restrained and steady. He kept his identity hidden from Chen Ping'an for the entire journey, bound by his duty and unwilling to break the rules of his station even when he burned to reveal himself. When he finally did, he bowed deeply and apologized for leaving without a word.Chapter 426 He is unafraid of punishment and speaks plainly even with a lance skewering him to the ground. He is also quietly shrewd. The Embroidered Flower River God learned that Gu Tao and Chen Ping'an had outmaneuvered him without making a single obvious move.Chapter 435 (2) == Background == Gu Tao was a man from the small town who died before [[Gu Can]] ever knew him, yet his soul never left. He became a yin god under [[Old Man Yang]]'s authority and was drawn into the service of the Great Li Empire. When Chen Ping'an left the town heading north, Gu Tao was already trailing behind him unseen. == Plot == === Journey to White Emperor City === On the road north, Gu Tao followed Chen Ping'an's group from a distance, shielding them from dangers they never knew about. [[Lin Shouyi]] made contact with him first, and Gu Tao began passing the boy quiet warnings about approaching threats.Chapter 119 (1) When enemies closed in near the Embroidered Flower River, he swam alongside the ship like a fish, keeping watch.Chapter 119 (2) At the inn on the long corridor, he rested a heavy hand on Chen Ping'an's shoulder to hold him back from running into a dangerous scene, then faded away once the moment passed.Chapter 112 He never spoke his name and made sure Chen Ping'an could not look at him directly. He was with them all the way to [[White Emperor City]], standing in the corridor above when A'Liang's clash with the sky lit up the night, staring up at it in a daze.Chapter 112 === Reunion === Years later, when Chen Ping'an visited the Chu Clan's riverside residence in the Great Li Empire, he found that its new master was the very yin god who had walked with him all those years ago. Gu Tao revealed himself, told Chen Ping'an about Gu Can's fated opportunity, and thanked him for looking after Little Can back in the town.Chapter 426 The Embroidered Flower River God had forbidden him from leaving the residence, and for slipping away to find Chen Ping'an, Gu Tao was run through the stomach with a golden lance and pinned to the ground. He did not cry out. The river god chose to delay further punishment only because he still needed Gu Tao's help to repair the residence's water fortune.Chapter 426 The river god later discovered that Gu Tao and Chen Ping'an had quietly talked circles around him, and he was not pleased about it.Chapter 435 (2) === Later === By the time [[Lin Shouyi]] had advanced far in his cultivation, he and Gu Tao had grown into genuine friends and kept in regular contact.Chapter 476 (1) Gu Tao also crossed paths with [[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]] again during a later visit, and the two parted on warm terms. By the later volumes, Gu Tao had risen from yin god to full deity and held a proper divine post in the empire, though he still carried the wound the river god had put through him.Chapter 567 (3) == Abilities == * '''Yin god body:''' He can become invisible, drift through water and solid barriers and project his presence at a distance. * '''Deific form:''' After becoming a proper deity of the Great Li Empire, his body hardened against spiritual attacks, though a river god's golden lance could still injure him severely. * '''Stealth and sensing:''' He tracked Chen Ping'an's group over a long journey without being detected by cultivators far above his level. == Relationships == * '''[[Gu Can]]:''' His son, whom he never met while alive. He watched over Gu Can from a distance and felt genuine joy hearing that the boy was thriving.Chapter 426 * '''[[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]]:''' He protected Chen Ping'an on the road north out of gratitude for everything Chen Ping'an had done for Gu Can. He thinks of him as a genuinely good person.Chapter 426 * '''[[Lin Shouyi]]:''' The first person to make contact with him on the road. By the later chapters they are close friends who keep in touch across great distances.Chapter 476 (1) * '''[[Old Man Yang]]:''' His master and the one who set him on the path of a yin god. The full nature of what Old Man Yang asked of him remains unclear. * '''Embroidered Flower River God:''' His superior in the empire's divine hierarchy, who holds Gu Tao to strict rules and is quick to punish him when he steps out of line. == Trivia == * Chen Ping'an said "I never would have expected that Uncle Gu actually became a yin god" when he recognized him at the Chu residence. * The river god almost destroyed his soul entirely at their confrontation, and only held back because the residence repair needed him. * He obtained news about Bamboo Scroll Lake from Red Candle Town several times, though the Great Li Empire fed him only what it wanted him to know.Chapter 426 * Lin Shouyi's ability to communicate with him on the road north was one of the first signs of Lin Shouyi's unusual spiritual sensitivity. == References == [[Category:Characters]] [[Category:Male]] [[Category:Alive]]

pages.title: Yu Lu
pages.content:
{{Character |header1 = Yu Lu |image1 = Yu Lu.png |Aliases = Yu Shilu
Crown prince of the Lu Empire |Vital_status = Alive |Gender = Male |Species = Human |Age = 14 (Chapter 134) |Relatives = Lu Clan (former imperial family) |Friend(s) = [[Gao Zhen|Gao Xuan]]
[[Zhu Lian]] |Allies = [[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]]
[[Li Huai]]
[[Cui Dongshan]] |Occupation = Pure martial artist
Student |Current_affiliation(s) = [[Mountain Cliff Academy]] |Former_affiliation(s) = Lu Empire |Continent = [[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]] |Cultivation_rank = Vajra Body Tier pure martial artist |Novel = Chapter 131 }} '''Yu Lu''' is the former crown prince of the fallen Lu Empire, conquered by the Great Li Empire. He survived by hiding among the empire's prisoners. He was taken in by the imperial preceptor [[Cui Chan]], who renamed him "Yu Lu", and he joined [[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]]'s group on its journey to [[Great Sui Nation]] together with [[Xie Xie]]. Easy-going, courteous and tirelessly helpful on the surface, he is also shrewd, calm and capable of startling ruthlessness. He becomes a powerful pure martial artist and studies at [[Mountain Cliff Academy]], where he quietly protects the children from the small town. == Appearance == Yu Lu is tall and extremely handsome, with skin as smooth and fair as jade, angular features and bright eyes. He dresses simply. The founding matriarch of the Purple Sun Residence practically salivates at the abundant dragon qi she senses in him. == Personality == Yu Lu is cheerful, patient and polite, the kind of person teachers call "the pick of the bunch". He is obsessively clean, polishing every dish, scrubbing everyone's shoes and fretting over the mess in Li Huai's bookcase, and he is even good at sewing. He seems to enjoy humble chores, and Chen Ping'an marvels that anyone could be so busy. Beneath this, he is calm and detached to the point of seeming cold. He can see into the hearts of those around him and wants little, which lets him live carefree even as Cui Chan's pawn. When Xie Xie confronts him over the Lu Empire's fall, his polite manner gives way to cutting remarks. [[Li Er]] considers him sly and scheming, while Chen Ping'an comes to trust him. He has a childish streak, too: he once boasts to Xie Xie that his part of Chen Ping'an's letter had twenty-four more characters than hers. == Background == Yu Lu was the prince of the Lu Empire. His father, the emperor, distrusted him because of baseless rumours and sent him to study at an academy in the enemy Great Li Empire, so he never wielded real power. After the empire fell, he hid among the survivors forced into a mountain-clearing team, under the pseudonym '''Yu Shilu''', meaning a "remnant evil" of the Lu Clan, to remind himself that everything was in the past. == Plot == === Cui Chan's Servant === Cui Chan takes him out of the prisoners and renames him Yu Lu, much to his reluctance. Living in Cui Chan's manor, he cheerfully takes on servants' chores, and soon has to look after the clumsy girl Xie Xie as well.Chapter 131 (2) Cui Chan then takes both of them to join Chen Ping'an's group, introducing Yu Lu as "the tall idiot... Lu as in fortune". Through the Yin god, Old Man Yang advises Chen Ping'an to take the pair in, and Chen Ping'an agrees to accept them, though not Cui Chan.Chapter 133 (1) At the time, Yu Lu is fourteen years old.Chapter 134 (2) He drives the group's carriage, cooks and cleans, and plays Go with Lin Shouyi. One night he offers to share lookout duties so Chen Ping'an can practise his meditation, and from then on he takes the second half of the night.Chapter 136 At Cui Chan's urging, he and Xie Xie reveal their true identities. Xie Xie, really Xie Lingyue of the Wind God Xie Clan, tearfully accuses the royal family of letting her clan die for them. Yu Lu coldly replies that if she has the courage of her ancestors, she should go and die, or assassinate Cui Chan. He then asks Chen Ping'an to lend him a hundred taels to build "Martyr Xie" a tomb. Chen Ping'an tells them that grievances can be set aside without being forgotten.Chapter 155 When Cui Chan asks them to follow him wholeheartedly, Yu Lu replies that he has been following the imperial preceptor all along and has enjoyed the journey.Chapter 156 At the end of the journey, the founding matriarch of the Purple Sun Residence is visibly drawn to his dragon qi.Chapter 159 (1) === Mountain Cliff Academy === At the academy, teachers praise Yu Lu and Xie Xie as talented and respectful.Chapter 162 (1) He spends hours fishing at the lake, later revealing that his posture is a form of martial training: he has never practised fist techniques, yet he is always training.Chapter 162 (2) When Li Huai is bullied and Lin Shouyi is injured, Yu Lu asks the children what Chen Ping'an would do in his place. He then goes to the scripture library and confronts the Confucian prodigy Li Changying, warning him to look out so he isn't beaten half to death in one punch.Chapter 166 He fights Li Changying and a gray-robed old man to a standstill, and all three have to be carried out. Li Er later remarks that Yu Lu went too far in that fight, proving himself malicious, aggressive and scheming.Chapter 169 Over the following years, he becomes inseparable from the Great Sui prince [[Gao Zhen|Gao Xuan]], who becomes his roommate. Fishing together, he confides that he was the Lu Empire's prince and is a seventh-tier martial artist, and Gao Xuan is proud to have chosen such a friend.Chapter 304 (1) When Gao Xuan leaves as a royal hostage, Yu Lu sees him only to the foot of the mountain. He also escorts Li Huai to the Lantern Festival and remains quietly protective of the children. === Chen Ping'an's Visit === When Chen Ping'an returns, he visits Yu Lu late at night, and Yu Lu greets him as a rare guest. Chen Ping'an thanks him for stepping in when Li Huai was bullied, and gives him the ''Mountain and Sea Chronicle''. He trusts Yu Lu enough to leave him guarding Pei Qian, Li Baoping and Li Huai. Yu Lu reads Zhu Lian's drafts in secret, and the two get along well as "like-minded" souls. During the assassination attempt on the academy, Yu Lu, described as a Vajra Body Tier martial artist, leaps into the air to punch an incoming flying sword, and later digs the injured Shi Rou out of the floorboards.Chapter 410 (1) In Cui Dongshan's farewell performance for Chen Ping'an, Yu Lu plays a "frail scholar" beaten by bandits, then plays the flute across a lake from Xie Xie's guqin. === Later Years === It is later revealed that Yu Lu and Xie Xie did not merely slip through the cracks. They were pawns deliberately selected by Cui Chan and the empress of the Great Li Empire.Chapter 463 (1) On an academy excursion, he and Xie Xie visit the Cao Clan's ancestral residence, where they once served as the young Cui Chan's servants. Yu Lu has spent years steadily consolidating the Vajra Body Tier and nurturing his fist intent. Mao Xiaodong notes that he understands the Confucian classics well.Chapter 570 (1) Chen Ping'an suggests he seek sparring practice with Zhu Lian on Downtrodden Mountain, which inexplicably sends a chill down Yu Lu's spine. == Abilities == * '''Pure martial arts:''' The translation is inconsistent about his tier. He tells Gao Xuan he is seventh tier (ch. 304), Shi Rou believes he is eighth tier (ch. 406), and he is called a Vajra Body Tier martial artist from ch. 410 onward. He claims he trains even while sitting and fishing. * '''Combat:''' He fought a Confucian prodigy and a gray-robed old man to a standstill, and can punch a flying sword out of the air. * '''Go:''' a skilled player who plays only modest tricks against Cui Chan, earning his grudging approval. * '''Dragon qi:''' As a former crown prince, he carries abundant dragon qi. == Relationships == * '''[[Cui Chan]] / [[Cui Dongshan]]''': the man who saved and renamed him, and whom he served. Cui Dongshan once beat him badly, and Yu Lu did not dare fight back. * '''[[Xie Xie]]''': fellow survivor of the Lu Empire, who loathes him. * '''[[Gao Zhen|Gao Xuan]]''': his closest friend, a prince in a similar situation. * '''[[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]]''': whom he respects and helps. * '''[[Li Huai]]''': whom he protects and guides. * '''[[Lin Shouyi]]''': a Go opponent, who is not fond of him. * '''[[Zhu Lian]]''': a like-minded friend. == Trivia == * 禄 (lù) means fortune or official salary, which Cui Chan uses in introducing him. * Pei Qian and Li Huai once agreed that each could have Yu Lu make three moves for them in a game. * A girl's father secretly revealed to her that the tall young man "using the pseudonym Yu Lu" was the Lu Empire's crown prince. == References == [[Category:Characters]] [[Category:Male]] [[Category:Alive]]

'''Zhang Shanfeng''' is a young Daoist priest from Ground Lying Peak on the Northern Complete Reed Continent and the youngest disciple of Spiritual Master Fire Dragon. He met [[Chen Ping An]] on the Ceremony Mountain Kun ship and became one of his closest friends.

== Appearance ==
Zhang Shanfeng is a young man who wears a Daoist hat and robe and carries a peach wood sword on his back. When he first travels with Chen Ping'an, his clothes are so worn that he feels embarrassed next to the well-dressed Daoist priests of the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent.Chapter 218 He has unusually long arms, which make his sword stances look smooth and natural.Chapter 239 He is taller than Chen Ping'an and has to bend down to put an arm around his shoulders.Chapter 552

Because he follows the talismanic branch of Daoism, he relies on talismans and his sword more than on his body. As a result he is physically frail. A heavy storm once drained him so badly that Chen Ping'an had to carry him on his back.Chapter 214 In later years he also carries the bronze sword True Martial alongside his peach wood sword.Chapter 415

== Personality ==
Zhang Shanfeng is kind, generous and honest. Shortly after meeting Chen Ping'an he insisted on giving him his own Bai Ze Album, and he would only accept one minor snow coin for it. He is shy and gentle by nature, and he tends to dwell on his mistakes until he drives himself into a corner.Chapter 211 He took it hard when he failed to protect a family that had paid him to drive away a demon, and he blamed himself even though the surviving children did not.Chapter 210

He hates being in debt. After learning that the armor pellet Chen Ping'an gave him was worth far more than Chen Ping'an claimed, he could not rest until he had paid something back.Chapter 242 Despite his mild manner, he does not shy away from danger. When a group of Divine Edict Sect priests came to punish Yang Huang and Zhuo Jing, he stood up to them, even after one of them tied him up with a rope.Chapter 219

He knows his cultivation is slow but never gives up. What disappoints him is only that he is not yet strong enough to protect people from demons.Chapter 379 He cares little for status. When he learned that he had missed the chance to become an external Heavenly Master of Mount Longhu, he barely minded. He was far sadder about having parted with Chen Ping'an twice.Chapter 536 He has always felt out of place in the wider world. He is at ease only when cultivating at Ground Lying Peak, travelling with his friends, or walking alone among quiet mountains and rivers.

== Background ==
Zhang Shanfeng once held a scholarly title from the imperial examinations but gave it up to pursue the Dao. He had nowhere to go, and Spiritual Master Fire Dragon took him in as his final disciple. Zhang Shanfeng believed his aptitude was mediocre. He grew up as the youngest disciple at Ground Lying Peak, knowing little about how strong his master and senior brothers really were. When he left to slay demons, his master told him there were none nearby, so he travelled across continents to find some. Several of his senior brothers secretly watched over parts of his journey without his knowledge.

He reached the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent on the Ceremony Mountain Kun ship with almost no money left. Chen Ping'an lent him his jade badge so he could watch a battle from the premium seats, and the two became friends. At first he introduced himself as Zhang Shan, a member of a distant branch of Mount Longhu's Zhang Clan that was not recorded in its genealogy. They left the ship together at Southern Stream Nation and travelled south. At that time he was a third tier Qi refiner practising the Five Lightning Righteous Technique.

At an old estate during a storm, he and [[Xu Yuanxia]] tried to protect the ghost couple Yang Huang and Zhuo Jing. When Zhao Liu's group from Divine Edict Sect called him a fraud, he named himself a disciple of Spiritual Master Fire Dragon of Heavensoar Sect. Later he admitted to Chen Ping'an that his real name was Zhang Shanfeng. Chen Ping'an then gave him the damaged armor pellet, saying he could pay later. In the fighting at Blusher Prefecture, the armor saved Daoist Chong Miao from a fatal blow.

At a ferry station on the border of Water Combing Nation, he sold a pair of bamboo chopsticks and gave the money to Chen Ping'an to repay part of his debt. Chen Ping'an then bought him the sword True Martial. Zhang Shanfeng wanted to attend a Liberation Rite of Water and Land in the southeast but was ashamed to break his promise to accompany Chen Ping'an to Old Dragon City. Chen Ping'an sent him off with Xu Yuanxia anyway.Chapter 248

He spent about two years travelling the Azure Phoenix Nation with Xu Yuanxia. When vagrant cultivators hunted a gentle earth bull, he and Xu Yuanxia defended it. They feared its death would set off a deadly earthquake, and Zhang Shanfeng's shoulder was pierced by a bonded flying sword.Chapter 375 Chen Ping'an arrived and settled the matter. Soon after, Spiritual Master Fire Dragon appeared, and Chen Ping'an gave Zhang Shanfeng a city god seal made by a former Great Heavenly Master. His master then took him away to visit Mount Longhu. On the way they visited a man in azure living on an island, who praised the fist technique Zhang Shanfeng had created himself.

At Mount Longhu his master hoped he would be recognized as a future external Heavenly Master, but the Heavenly Master Residence declined. Master and disciple then travelled the Middle Earth Divine Continent on foot and obtained water elixir at Mirage Lake.Chapter 527 At the Pure Confucian Chen Clan, Zhang Shanfeng met Chen Ping'an's friend [[Liu Xianyang]] and told him about their journey together.

He later found Chen Ping'an at Paddling Island in the Water Dragon Sect, gave him a bottle of water elixir and stayed nearby while Chen Ping'an refined his bonded item. Back at Ground Lying Peak he told the young Daoist priests stories about slaying demons. Afterwards he set out again with his senior brother Yuan Lingdian.Chapter 554

== Trivia ==
* He has a low tolerance for alcohol and does not really like drinking, yet he is easily talked into it.
* He made up short verses for Xu Yuanxia and himself, and promised to come up with something grand for Chen Ping'an later.
* He once called Chen Ping'an's name a little tacky, thinking it was a false name like his own.
* His fist technique is deliberately slow. Chen Ping'an could not copy it, though he later practised its stances to calm his mind.
* He sometimes calls himself a Great Heavenly Master in his sleep.
* He believes his master is a mediocre cultivator, unaware of his master's true standing on the Northern Complete Reed Continent.

== References ==

pages.title: Zhao Yao
pages.content:
{{Character|Chinese=赵繇|Pinyin=Zhào Yáo|Vital_status=Alive|Gender=Male|Species=Human|Master(s)=[[Qi Jingchun]] (teacher)|Friend(s)=[[Song Jixin]]|Occupation=Scholar
Cultivator
Former scholarly attendant to [[Qi Jingchun]]|Former_affiliation(s)=Zhao Clan of Fortune Street|Continent=[[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]] (origin)|Empire=Great Li Empire|City=[[Small Town]] (Fortune Street)|Novel=Chapter 6|image1=Zhao Yao.png}}

'''Zhao Yao''' is the eldest grandson of the Zhao Clan, one of the four great families of the [[Small Town]]. He was [[Qi Jingchun]]'s student and scholarly attendant at the private school, and he left the town carrying his teacher's most important seal.

==Appearance==
Zhao Yao is a neat, refined young scholar who usually dresses in azure.Chapter 27 At the Go board he sits with a serious face and his back ramrod straight.Chapter 6 Chen Ping'an counts him among the good-looking people of his own age. 

==Personality==
Zhao Yao is gentle, earnest and well mannered, the opposite of [[Song Jixin]]'s sharp tongue and pride.Chapter 11 Elders across the town held him up as the model their own children should follow. That left him with few real friends, since the rowdy young masters of Fortune Street thought him a dull bookworm. Song Jixin, his regular Go partner, was about the only person he could call a friend. Zhao Yao admired Song Jixin and always lost to him at Go. Song Jixin privately thought Zhao Yao was not as clever as he was, but stayed friendly with him because of their shared teacher.Chapter 161

He is diligent and memorised every book Qi Jingchun gave him. He is also prone to embarrassment and blushes easily. The first time he saw [[Ning Yao]], he stood frozen in the street, staring at her until his teacher had to pull him away, then blurted out that she smelled really good. Qi Jingchun later told him not to fall for her.Chapter 280

He has a strong sense of obligation. When a stranger saved his life, he insisted on giving the man his most treasured possession, saying he could not simply ignore such a debt.

==Background==

=== Fortune Street ===
Zhao Yao served Qi Jingchun as both student and scholarly attendant, and he spent more time with his teacher than any other child at the private school. Qi Jingchun carved a seal for him that bore the words "the world welcomes spring."Chapter 8 Song Jixin tried to trade for it several times, and Zhao Yao refused every time. Shortly before everything changed in the town, Qi Jingchun walked him past the stone archways and warned him to guard his tongue from then on, telling him that careless words would only bring trouble.

On the night before he left, Zhao Yao brought Song Jixin a pouch of Good Fortune Coins as a farewell gift and drank with him until he could barely stand. When he got home, his grandmother sat him down in the study before a wooden carving of a resting dragon and solemnly made him take the seat behind the desk. The next morning he left the town on a cart, reciting poetry at the top of his voice. He passed Chen Ping'an on the road as he went.Chapter 28

=== The spring seal ===
Following his grandfather's plans, Zhao Yao set out by ox cart for an immortal sect in the west of the Eastern Treasured Vial Continent. Halfway there he met a boy with a red birthmark between his brows who called himself the Embroidered Tiger. It was [[Cui Chan]]. Zhao Yao gave up the spring seal in exchange for a secret cultivation technique and two immortal tools, and those gifts carried him through every danger on the road.Chapter 138 Qi Jingchun had foreseen this and told him not to worry about the seal. Chen Ping'an later realised that his teacher had probably wanted Zhao Yao to lose the seal so that he would be free of any ties to him.Chapter 370

When he finally reached the foot of the sect's mountain, Zhao Yao changed his mind. He untied the ox, set it free and headed west to the sea alone. From there he took ship after ship toward the Middle Earth Divine Continent.

=== The island ===
More than halfway into the voyage, a swarm of flying fish smashed his ship apart. Zhao Yao survived on a plank of wreckage until he passed out. He woke on a small island in a thatched cottage piled with books, cared for by a quiet man in azure robes. A rusted sword stood driven into the island's peak. In his despair Zhao Yao walked to the edge of a cliff meaning to jump, and the man stopped him with a few gentle words.Chapter 415 (2)

He stayed on the island for nearly two years, reading and staring out to sea, until his spirits recovered. Before leaving on a raft he had built himself, he tried to give the man his wooden dragon paperweight as thanks. The man refused it, remarking that the world could not be too bad yet.

Zhao Yao never learned the rest. A remnant of Qi Jingchun's soul had guided him to the island and asked its master, a scholar who had once split the Yellow River Small World with a single sword strike, to save him. Qi Jingchun chose not to show himself, believing the boy would only feel guiltier. He had hidden his own kindred character inside the wooden dragon paperweight, waiting for the day Zhao Yao's heart found a new spring. He said that whether Zhao Yao ever inherited his lineage mattered far less than letting him seek knowledge in peace.Chapter 417 (2)

=== Later ===
Qi Jingchun left a wisp of spring wind on three of the town's children, Chen Ping'an, Song Jixin and Zhao Yao. He also revealed that Zhao Yao found another fated opportunity on his journey to another continent.Chapter 238 Of his two students from the small town, Qi Jingchun actually held Zhao Yao in somewhat higher regard than Song Jixin.

==Trivia==

* The wooden dragon carving his grandmother gave him is counted among the great fated treasures to come out of the Jewel Small World, alongside Gao Xuan's golden carp and Ruan Xiu's fire dragon bracelet.
* An old man from the Zhao Clan who still lives in the small town is the ancestor of Zhao Yao's branch of the family.
* At the private school's Go table, Song Jixin always sat on the north seat and Zhao Yao always sat on the south.
* Cui Dongshan once told Song Jixin that his disposition was slightly better than Zhao Yao's.Chapter 528 (3)

pages.content:
{{Character |header1=Zheng Dafeng |image1=Zheng Dafeng.png |Vital_status=Alive |Gender=Male |Species=Human |Master(s)=[[Old Man Yang]] |Friend(s)=[[Chen Ping An]]
[[Fan Er]]
[[Zhu Lian]] |Allies=[[Li Er]]
[[Old Man Yang]] |Occupation=Gatekeeper
Shopkeeper |Current_affiliation(s)=[[Downtrodden Mountain]] |Former_affiliation(s)=Jewel Small World, Dust Medicinal Shop |Donghua=Ep 1 }} == Appearance == Zheng Dafeng is a hunchbacked man. By the time he takes up residence at Downtrodden Mountain, his posture has worsened noticeably compared to his years in Jewel Small World.Chapter 461 == Personality == Zheng Dafeng is foul-mouthed, lecherous, and cheerfully shameless, yet underneath all of that he operates by a strict personal code that he rarely advertises. He is a habitual thief of small things, a compulsive gossip, and an unembarrassed admirer of women, but he pays his debts in full when they matter. When a young woman who worked at his Dust Medicinal Shop was killed because of circumstances tied to him, he picked a fight with the entire city of Old Dragon City rather than walk away owing her a book.Chapter 361 He is slow to trust and quicker to needle than to praise. He spent years dismissing Chen Ping'an as a boring country boy with whom he had nothing in common, only to eventually acknowledge him as his Dao mentor.Chapter 254 He is candid about his own weaknesses, admitting that his broad knowledge, while an advantage in many areas, narrowed the purity of his fist intent and made his ninth tier breakthrough far harder than it needed to be. He enjoys wine, Go, and the company of people who can match him in banter. At Downtrodden Mountain he falls into an easy companionship with Zhu Lian and Wei Bo, bickering over Go games and sharing wine late into the night. == Background == Zheng Dafeng is a disciple of [[Old Man Yang]] and the junior martial brother of [[Li Er]]. Old Man Yang never formally identified himself as their Dao mentor, only their master, and kept both disciples at arm's length regarding the details of his plans.Chapter 252 In Jewel Small World, Zheng Dafeng worked as the gatekeeper of the eastern gate, collecting pouches of copper coins from outsiders seeking entry. He also taught Chen Ping'an a basic breathing technique during this period, though he considered it rudimentary and did not hold Chen Ping'an in particularly high regard at the time. After the small town was absorbed into Dragon Spring Prefecture, Zheng Dafeng relocated to Old Dragon City, where he ran the Dust Medicinal Shop and served as Dao guardian to a young man from the Fan Clan, guiding him toward a breakthrough past the third tier bottleneck. He was also secretly responsible for ensuring things went smoothly for Chen Ping'an in the city, on Old Man Yang's instructions. When a female employee at his shop was killed after being caught up in a conflict tied to him, Zheng Dafeng challenged the Fu Clan and fought his way through a succession of their fighters. He defeated Chu Yang, a Golden Core Tier cultivator who broke through to the Nascent Tier mid-battle, and then severely wounded a Nascent Tier Fu Clan ancestor wielding a pseudo-celestial tool, taking heavy injuries himself in the process. The confrontation forced every major clan in Old Dragon City to choose sides and sent the city into upheaval. At the year's end he met Fu Qi, the city lord, in a battle to the death on the Dragon Scaling Platform. Chen Ping'an arrived beforehand and gave him a vial of Seated Meditation Pills to help suppress his injuries. Zheng Dafeng prevailed, trapping Fu Qi's pseudo-celestial sword with an azure sword-suppressing talisman inscribed by Zhong Kui until Fu Qi surrendered.Chapter 373 It was only after the battle, upon reading the book he had taken from her, that Zheng Dafeng fully understood what that text had meant to him in terms of his own cultivation. He recognized then that Chen Ping'an had played a role in his ninth tier breakthrough, and that he was in fact his Dao mentor. After the events in Old Dragon City, Zheng Dafeng returned to the small town for a time before eventually settling at the foot of Downtrodden Mountain, where he took on the role of gatekeeper once again. He became a regular part of life there alongside Zhu Lian and Wei Bo, helping to plan the development of the Lotus Root Blessed Land and acting as one of the mountain's official guest elders.Chapter 527 == Trivia == * Zhu Lian once speculated that, in a past life, Zheng Dafeng may have been one of the four divine generals of the Heavenly Court. * Despite his appearance and manner, Zheng Dafeng was considered by those who knew him to be, at heart, the most scrupulous of men.Chapter 820 * He gave Chen Ping'an a jade tablet minimization treasure and a copy of the Proper Sword Scripture while in Old Dragon City.Chapter 283 == References ==

pages.title: Zhi Gui
pages.content:
{{Character|image1=Zhi Gui.jpg|Chinese=稚圭|Pinyin=Zhì Guī|Aliases=Wang Zhu (true name)
Court Lady Zhi Gui
Young Mistress (by Fu Qi)|Vital_status=Alive|Gender=Female|Species=True Dragon|Eye_color=Golden, with vertical pupils |Allies=[[Song Jixin]] (young master)
[[Fu Nanhua]]
Fu Qi
[[Lu Chen]]
[[Ma Kuxuan]]|Enemie(s)=[[Qi Jingchun]]
[[Cao Xi]]|Occupation=Maidservant to [[Song Jixin]]|Continent=[[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]]|Empire=Great Li Empire|City=[[Small Town]] (Clay Vase Alley); later [[Old Dragon City]]|Novel=Chapter 1}}

'''Zhi Gui''' is [[Song Jixin]]'s maidservant on [[Clay Vase Alley]]. To the town she looks like a sweet, shy servant girl. In truth she is Wang Zhu, a jewel formed from the soul of the last true dragon in the world, who spent thousands of years trapped in the Jewel Small World.

==Appearance==
Zhi Gui looks like a slender young girl with large, round eyes. Her face is only just losing its childhood softness, and she grows taller and lovelier with every year.Chapter 113 In front of most people she wears a timid, wide-eyed expression that makes onlookers feel sorry for her. Every so often her true nature shows through, and golden pupils flash in her eyes before vanishing again.Chapter 10 Later, when she lets her guard down, her eyes are golden with vertical pupils. 

==Personality==
Zhi Gui shows the world a gentle, obedient face, but it is a mask. On her own or with people she does not fear, she is cold, proud and sharp-tongued. When Granny Ma made one remark too many at the well, the quiet little maid walked over and slapped the old woman twice, saying she had put up with her for long enough.Chapter 31 She once hacked an old wooden figure in the house to pieces with a meat cleaver, and she stamps on Song Jixin's four-legged snake whenever it annoys her.Chapter 36

She carries a deep and lasting anger toward the cultivators and sages who kept her imprisoned. She refuses to bow her head to anyone who tries to lecture her, and she says openly that she does not care for scholars' sermons. She thinks mostly of herself. When [[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]] came begging for help to save [[Liu Xianyang]], she turned him away with a mocking smile, then burped and remarked that she had eaten a little too much.Chapter 47

She is not without feeling. She stays at Song Jixin's side through his worst days, and she fusses over the hen and chicks they left behind in the small town. She is also capable of real fear. As [[Song Changjing]]'s carriages passed through the gate out of the Jewel Small World, she curled up in a corner and sobbed that she could sense terrifying things beyond it that even he could not handle.Chapter 66

==Background==

=== The well ===
Zhi Gui's true name is Wang Zhu. The two characters together form the character for "pearl," the most precious part of a true dragon.Chapter 63 (1) She is a jewel formed from the soul of the world's final true dragon.Chapter 191 (2) For 3,000 years she lay sealed in the small town, beneath the Iron Lock Well. She describes endless sixty-year cycles of Buddhist chanting, Daoist talismans, righteous light and sword qi tearing at her, without a single day of rest.Chapter 15

The town's children never knew what lay in the well. When Cao Xi relieved himself into it as a boy, the iron chain clanked and the water surged up to his feet, and he fled in terror. Years later Zhi Gui told him she would have made him drink the well dry if he had been slower. Xie Shi, on the other hand, thanked her for saving his life twice.

=== Clay Vase Alley ===
When she finally broke free, she was drawn to Chen Ping'an at first. Then she sensed the rich dragon qi in Song Jixin's house next door. Too weak to reach it, she collapsed in the snow outside Chen Ping'an's gate, and he saved her life. The accounts of what happened next differ. [[Qi Jingchun]] says she had no choice but to bind herself to a human, and that she repaid her rescuer by slowly devouring what little good fortune Chen Ping'an had. [[Old Man Yang]] says she refused to bind herself to a mortal like him and declared herself Song Jixin's maidservant instead, and Chen Ping'an unknowingly handed the greatest opportunity in the Jewel Small World to his neighbour.Chapter 86 (1) Liu Xianyang always insisted that her real name was Wang Zhu and that "Zhi Gui" was a name Song Jixin picked up somewhere on a whim. The town's wealthier families took the name as proof that Song Jixin was the kiln official's son.Chapter 5

Before leaving the small town, Qi Jingchun confronted her in Clay Vase Alley. She mocked him, defended what she had done to Chen Ping'an as simple hunger, and refused to repent. He forced her to kowtow three times, to the world, to all living beings and to the Great Dao. Then he warned her that somewhere beyond the town there would always be someone more unreasonable than she was. She thanked him for his teaching, then spat on the ground as soon as he was gone.

=== Leaving the Jewel Small World ===
Zhi Gui left for the capital with Song Jixin and Song Changjing, who warned her that her fate was now tied to his nephew's and that she should not push her luck. She followed Song Jixin to the White Jade Capital tower. Later she returned briefly to the small town with Cui Chan, who told her she was the true owner of that small world and that he was only there to watch over her.

On the trip to [[Old Dragon City]], she was the real focus of the visit, not Song Jixin. The Fu Clan treated her as an honoured guest, and Fu Qi told [[Fu Nanhua]] that her opinion had decided who would inherit the city. She climbed the Dragon Scaling Platform alone and broke through the sea of clouds above it. When she reached the top, blood ran from her golden eyes as she looked out over a world filled with the tombs of her kind.Chapter 255 (1) Coming down, she spoke coldly to the Mohist swordsman Xu Ruo, who warned her not to go too far. She replied that this world was an ancient battlefield piled with more corpses than any mountain.Chapter 257 (2)

=== Later years ===
[[Lu Chen]] once arranged a promise with the Great Li emperor and planned to hand [[Ma Kuxuan]] over to Zhi Gui. She thought little of it until Ma Kuxuan began rising rapidly at True Martial Mountain. When he came to see her with the Divine Edict Sect's Qi Zhen, she brushed off his long devotion and told him to stop boasting before he had actually become powerful. That night she ate a grain rain coin whole and scolded Song Jixin's horned snake for being so timid.Chapter 415 (1)

She still wears a maidservant's clothes, only finer than before, and she stays at Song Jixin's side after he becomes feudal lord of Old Dragon City. Song Jixin feels her drifting further from him, and he senses that something is going on between her and the city's Fu Clan.Chapter 631 (6)

==Trivia==

* Both [[Liu Xianyang]] and [[Ma Kuxuan]] were in love with her. 
* Ma Kuxuan's [[Ma Lanhua|grandmother]] called her a poisonous vixen and warned him to stay away from her.
* She once told Song Jixin that she would curtsy ten thousand times if it earned her a bag of coins each time.
* Gu Can likes to call her a "bitch" and once promised to find Chen Ping'an a roomful of girls as pretty as she is.
* Fu Qi lent her the Old Dragon Robe, which she wrapped herself in like a blanket.
* [[Pei Qian]], watching scenes from her master's childhood, declared that Song Jixin and Zhi Gui both deserved to die.

==References==

pages.title: Zhong Kui
pages.content:
{{Character|image1=Zhao Yao.PNG|status=Alive|gender=Male|species=Human|master(s)=[[Mister Qi]]|donghua=Chapter 2}}
==Appearance==
Zhong Kui is a '''scholar''' who is often described as wearing '''azure robes'''. He is also referred to as a "noble scholar". At one point, he appears in red official garb. He is also described as being impoverished and is referred to as an impoverished scholar.

Despite his scholarly appearance, he is also presented as a complex figure who is not always serious and dignified. He is depicted as having a '''mischievous''' chuckle and a '''dazzling smile'''. He is also portrayed as being capable of acting theatrically, and at times, he is described as having a '''fearless''' and '''gallant''' expression.

While he often presents himself as an ordinary scholar, he is also capable of displaying a powerful aura and can appear solemn. He is described as having a "righteous" aura that he nurtures from reading sagely classics. He is also shown to be '''observant''' and '''thoughtful'''. He has a habit of leaning on the counter at the inn.

==Personality==
Zhong Kui is a complex character with a blend of scholarly and unconventional traits. He is a '''noble scholar''' from the Great Subduing Academy. Although he is a scholar, he is not always serious or dignified. He is portrayed as having a '''mischievous''' chuckle and a '''dazzling smile'''. He can be theatrical, and at times, he has a '''fearless''' and '''gallant''' expression. He is sometimes described as '''shameless'''.

Despite his sometimes frivolous behavior, Zhong Kui possesses a strong sense of '''righteousness''' that he nurtures by reading sagely classics. He is very knowledgeable about Confucian principles, and he understands the importance of respecting the rules established by the Confucian sect. He can be '''observant''' and '''thoughtful''', often contemplating the deeper meaning behind things. He is '''courageous''', and he does not hesitate to stand up for what he believes is right. He can be '''impulsive''', but he also possesses a strong sense of responsibility.

Zhong Kui's personality includes some contradictions:

* He is described as an impoverished scholar, yet he is also depicted as a noble scholar.
* He is a scholar who is familiar with the rules and etiquette of the Confucian sect, yet he does not always adhere to them.
* He is capable of displaying a powerful aura, yet he often presents himself as ordinary.
* He often expresses concern over his image, but then behaves in a way that might harm that image.

Zhong Kui is portrayed as being '''kind and generous''', and he is also someone who enjoys drinking and socializing. He is depicted as being particularly fond of Jiu Niang, and he goes out of his way to impress her. He can also be humorous, often joking with Chen Ping'an. He is aware of his own shortcomings, and is willing to admit them. Despite his flaws, Zhong Kui is presented as a likeable character who is capable of growth and change. He is not afraid to show his emotions, and he is not afraid to be himself. He is capable of acting in ways that are both noble and unconventional. He is sometimes described as having a "youthful shamelessness".

==Background==
Zhong Kui is a '''noble scholar''' from the '''Great Subduing Academy'''. He is from the most orthodox lineage of the Second Sage, and his master, the mountain master of Great Subduing Academy, also graduated from the Second Sage Residence in Middle Earth Divine Continent. He became a virtuous scholar at Great Subduing Academy before the age of twenty. Despite this, he had a "tattered" reputation due to his unrestrained behavior and was disliked by many pedantic old scholars. He is the youngest noble scholar in the history of the Great Subduing Academy. He is a Confucian scholar who is very knowledgeable about Confucian principles, and he understands the importance of respecting the rules established by the Confucian sect. He is also very familiar with the Scholarly Sage's works and philosophies. His knowledge of Confucian classics is profound.

Zhong Kui's family background is not mentioned in the sources. He is described as being an "impoverished scholar" at one point, but he is also referred to as a noble scholar, indicating that he is from a well-respected scholarly background. He is said to have a teacher who treats his azure talisman paper like his own child. His master was also said to have used one of his azure talisman papers when crossing the seas, and another one upon arriving in Parasol Leaf Continent.

pages.title: Zhong Qiu
pages.content:
{{Character |header1=Zhong Qiu |Aliases=Imperial Preceptor Zhong Qiu
Mr. Zhong |Vital_status=Alive |Gender=Male |Species=Human |Disciple(s)=[[Cao Qinglang]] (half-disciple) |Occupation=Scholar
Martial arts grandmaster
Calligrapher and painter
Imperial Preceptor of Southern Garden Nation (former) |Current_affiliation(s)=[[Downtrodden Mountain]] (guest elder) |Former_affiliation(s)=[[Southern Garden Nation]]
[[Lotus Flower Blessed Land]] / Lotus Root Blessed Land |Continent=[[Parasol Leaf Continent]] (origin)
Southern Whirl Continent (current) |Cultivation_rank=Vajra Body Tier |Novel=Chapter 307 }} == Appearance == Zhong Qiu is a thin, serious-looking man with a scholarly demeanor, dressed in an azure robe. His plain look belies his status, so much so that it was hard for those who first met him to believe he was the leading figure among the world’s four grandmasters.Chapter 307 == Personality == He carries himself with the discipline of both a scholar and a martial artist, insisting that every word he speaks and every punch he throws adhere strictly to principle.Chapter 315 He is blunt and not given to idle talk, but he is also fair-minded, candid, and willing to hold back in a fight rather than strike an opponent who is unprepared.Chapter 315 As a teacher he is strict and protective of his student’s foundation, growing visibly angry when he feels that foundation is being undermined.Chapter 388 Once freed from his old responsibilities he becomes noticeably more relaxed, unashamed to borrow money or enjoy small pleasures he once denied himself.Chapter 603 == Background == Zhong Qiu and Yu Zhenyi came from humble backgrounds in Pine Song Nation and grew up as neighbors and inseparable friends, traveling the world together and each obtaining their own fated opportunity that elevated them into renowned martial arts prodigies. The two eventually turned on each other and fought a mortal duel witnessed by only a handful of people, leaving both of them severely wounded. Afterward Zhong Qiu left for Southern Garden Nation and the two cut all ties, though the rivalry and mutual respect between them never fully faded. In Southern Garden Nation he rose to become Imperial Preceptor and was regarded as the strongest martial artist in the world, ranked among the four grandmasters of the Lotus Flower Blessed Land alongside Yu Zhenyi, Tong Qingqing, and Lu Fang.Chapter 307 When Old Demon Ding Ying revealed to him the existence of a world beyond their own, called Parasol Leaf Continent, and the possibility of ascending from the blessed land by killing or surviving other grandmasters, Zhong Qiu was shaken but kept his composure, pressing Ding Ying for his true intentions rather than reacting rashly.Chapter 314 During the chaos that followed, Zhong Qiu stepped in to save Lu Fang from a killing blow by Chen Ping’an, then challenged Chen Ping’an to a fight himself, deliberately holding back at first to test him. He created his own signature fist stance, called Mountain Peak, trained over many years to make him as immovable as a mountain, and was stunned when Chen Ping’an managed to grasp the essence of the stance after only a few exchanges. The two eventually traded a single decisive blow each, and Zhong Qiu was sent crashing backward and plowing a trench into the ground for dozens of meters. Though he only suffered minor injuries, it was the first time he had been defeated within an arm’s length, and from that day on he could no longer be called the strongest martial artist in that world.Chapter 315 He was soon after named to the renewed list of Upper Ten Elites alongside Chen Ping’an and several other new faces.Chapter 316 Zhong Qiu later became a teacher to Cao Qinglang, a boy from the capital whom Chen Ping’an had once looked after, sharing the role informally with Lu Tai. He confronted Lu Tai directly after learning that Lu Tai had been feeding the boy a flood of miscellaneous knowledge beyond his years, insisting that a Confucian education built on solid classical foundations would serve him far better in the long run.Chapter 388 Despite this friction, the two men respected each other and worked well together raising Cao Qinglang between them, Zhong Qiu grounding him in rigorous scholarship while Lu Tai broadened his worldview. He also personally guided the boy’s preparation for the imperial examination and gave him access to his own rare book collection.Chapter 483 Zhong Qiu came to think of Cao Qinglang as something close to a true disciple, and expressed hope that the boy would one day speak up for ordinary people in a world that too often treated them as disposable pieces on a game board.Chapter 530 When the old Daoist priest who secretly oversaw the Lotus Flower Blessed Land split it in two, with part of it becoming Downtrodden Mountain’s Lotus Root Blessed Land, Zhong Qiu resigned as imperial preceptor once the Great Dao’s hold over the land was lifted, finding himself a much freer and lighter person for it. In the years that followed he broke through to the Vajra Body Tier, and later made a further breakthrough after a stroke of fortune. He accepted a position as a guest elder of Downtrodden Mountain and set out with Cao Qinglang to see the wider world for the first time in his life, traveling across the Lotus Root Blessed Land before continuing on toward the Majestic World.Chapter 567Chapter 569 Alongside Cao Qinglang and Pei Qian, Zhong Qiu traveled onward to the Sword Qi Great Wall and then into the Majestic World proper, visiting Old Dragon City, Stalactite Mountain, and the Ning Manor in the company of Chen Ping’an and Cui Dongshan. Having spent nearly his entire life confined to the capital of Southern Garden Nation, he was humbled by how much larger the wider world was than anything he had known, and he continued to guide Cao Qinglang’s scholarship even as he admitted that true cultivation guidance was beyond his own expertise.Chapter 603Chapter 604 He went on to accompany Cao Qinglang further into the Majestic World, with Chen Ping’an entrusting them to continue their travels together through the Southern Whirl Continent.Chapter 612 == Trivia == * He created his own fist stance, Mountain Peak, built around training the back, shoulders, and elbows into a single immovable form. It took most of his own disciples decades to even approximate its outward form.Chapter 315 * Chen Ping’an later incorporated elements of Zhong Qiu’s teachings, including the Examining the Dragon method and the Mountain Peak stance, into his own fighting style.Chapter 315 * He once tried and failed to destroy an immortal item, the Five Mountains True Appearance Picture Scroll, out of concern that Yu Zhenyi would seize it, before eventually entrusting it to Cao Qinglang instead.Chapter 530 == References ==

pages.title: Zhou Mili
pages.content:
{{Character |header1=Zhou Mili |Aliases=Great Water Monster of Mute Lake
Little Mili |Vital_status=Alive |Gender=Female |Species=Water demon |Master(s)=[[Chen Ping An]] |Friend(s)=[[Pei Qian]]
[[Chen Nuanshu]]
[[Chen Lingjun]]
[[Shi Rou]] |Occupation=Right-hand guardian of Downtrodden Mountain's ancestral hall
Former temporary right guardian of Dragon Riding Alley's pastry shop |Current_affiliation(s)=[[Downtrodden Mountain]] |Continent=[[Northern Complete Reed Continent]] (origin, Mute Lake) |Novel=Chapter 509 }} == Appearance == Zhou Mili takes the form of a small girl dressed in black clothing. Chen Ping'an later gave her his Golden Sweet Wine robe to wear over her black outfit, turning her into what looked like a little girl in white, and she continued wearing this robe afterward. She has thin, slightly yellow eyebrows and stays notably short for her apparent age no matter how much she eats.Chapter 641Chapter 571 == Personality == Zhou Mili is cheerful, naive and easily excitable, prone to boasting about being a "great water monster" even though she is tiny and timid in practice. She loves roasted seeds and rice and dislikes fish intensely. She is devoted to Pei Qian, whom she calls Sect Sister or Senior Sister, and takes her duties as Downtrodden Mountain's right guardian very seriously despite frequently misunderstanding instructions or getting things backward. She is easily moved to tears but just as quickly cheered up, and she has a habit of hiding her own troubles so as not to worry the people she cares about.Chapter 527Chapter 641 == Background == Zhou Mili was originally a water monster living in Mute Lake on the Northern Complete Reed Continent, watching cultivators and travelers pass by without ever being able to fit in among humans. Disguised as a little girl selling newspapers, she was captured and passed between several parties aboard an intercontinental ship before Chen Ping'an bought her freedom. During a later confrontation on the ship involving a hidden enemy named Gao Cheng of the Malicious Ghost Valley, Chen Ping'an publicly named her Zhou Mili and disguised her further to shield her from danger, promising to protect her.Chapter 509Chapter 511 Chen Ping'an entrusted her to Sect Leader Zhu Quan of the Flax Robe Sect to escort her to the Ox Horn Mountain ferry station of the Dragon Spring Prefecture, telling her she could turn to Zhu Lian on Downtrodden Mountain if she ever needed help. She was brought to Downtrodden Mountain's Dragon Riding Alley and introduced to Pei Qian, who took her in on Chen Ping'an's instructions. She became Pei Qian's close companion, serving first as a temporary guardian of Dragon Riding Alley's pastry shop before Chen Ping'an formally approved her promotion to right-hand guardian of Downtrodden Mountain's ancestral hall at Pei Qian's recommendation.Chapter 511Chapter 551 She continued living on Downtrodden Mountain alongside Pei Qian, Chen Nuanshu and Chen Ruchu, accompanying Pei Qian on her travels to the Lotus Root Blessed Land and later to the Sword Qi Great Wall. During one return trip to Downtrodden Mountain, she was confronted and beaten by an official of the Fine Wine River's water palace after refusing to be recruited, but concealed Downtrodden Mountain's name out of caution rather than invoking Chen Ping'an's protection.Chapter 565Chapter 641 == Trivia == * The name Mili literally translates to "a grain of rice."Chapter 597 * She does not need to eat, being a water demon, but enjoys food anyway and keeps up the habit regardless.Chapter 559 * Cui Dongshan addressed her as his junior apprentice-sister, implying she holds some standing within Chen Ping'an's lineage alongside Pei Qian.Chapter 565 == References ==

pages.content:
{{Character
|header1=Zhu He
|image1=Zhu He.png
|Vital_status=Alive
|Gender=Male
|Species=Human
|Relatives=[[Zhu Lu]] (daughter)
|Allies=[[Li Baoping]]
|Occupation=Hereditary servant and martial arts instructor of the Li Clan
|Current_affiliation(s)=Li Clan of Fortune Street
|Continent=[[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]]
|Cultivation_rank=Fifth Tier (martial artist)
|Novel=Chapter 87
}}

== Appearance ==
Zhu He is a sturdy martial artist with rough features and a usually solemn face. On the road south, he walks beside his horse and carries a string of red Demon Chiming Bells given to him by the Li Clan's patriarch.Chapter 96 After his battle with the black python on Go Table Mountain, he sits cross-legged and drenched in blood, yet visibly glowing with energy.Chapter 100 (1)

== Personality ==
Zhu He is kind, generous and easygoing, described as "a kind and pure man". Although a fifth-tier martial artist, he apologises to the young Li Huai after [[Zhu Lu]] splatters him with mud, and promises to buy him new clothes.Chapter 97 He readily shares his knowledge, and patiently explains the early martial tiers to Chen Ping'an during their night watch.Chapter 100 (2) He is disciplined in his craft: when A'Liang offers him wine, he refuses, saying he cannot drink before reaching full mastery of martial arts.Chapter 88 He takes his duty to protect Li Baoping seriously and genuinely adores her.

In battle, he shows an extremely resolute will. Facing the black python, he declares that since he will die either way, he would rather die fighting, and his aura climbs higher the more he is injured.Chapter 99

His great weakness is his daughter. Her eyes resemble her mother's, so he can rarely bring himself to scold her, and Chen Ping'an later observes that Zhu He is a good person who does not know how to discipline his daughter. When Zhu Lu's assassination attempt fails, Zhu He begs A'Liang to let her go and offers to take his own life in her place.Chapter 110

He also has an innate dislike for scholars, picked up from Li Baozhen's habit of ridiculing them.Chapter 106

== Background ==
Zhu He is a hereditary servant of the Li Clan of [[Fortune Street]]. When his aptitude for martial arts was discovered, the Li Clan immediately invested heavily in his development, and later did the same for his daughter.Chapter 92 (1) His own aptitude is limited, but the Li patriarch privately praised him as a brilliant martial arts teacher, one who would be treated as an esteemed guest even by the affluent clans of the Great Li capital.Chapter 87 (1) He taught Zhu Lu that training fist techniques the wrong way ruins the body, while someone who grasps their true essence can slay gods with a single punch.Chapter 87 (2)

Having spent his whole life in the small town, Zhu He had never fought a true life-and-death battle before the journey. He firmly believed, like most martial artists, that the ninth tier was the very pinnacle of martial arts, unaware of the tenth.Chapter 134 (1) He was stuck at the peak of the fifth tier.

He and Zhu Lu were assigned to accompany Li Baoping to Mountain Cliff Academy. On Go Table Mountain, he performs a Soil Molding Technique to summon the mountain god, accidentally calling up the mountain lord Wei Bo, who thrashes his calf with a bamboo cane.Chapter 98 After surviving the black python, he feels he has found a catalyst for a breakthrough. When the treasures are shared out, he chooses the Purple Qi Guide for his daughter and a Hero's Gall Pill from True Martial Mountain, which leaves him dreaming of the seventh tier.Chapter 104 Both are later confiscated by A'Liang after Zhu Lu's assassination attempt, and the pair leave the group.

== Trivia ==

* Zhu He jokingly admits he would happily accept A'Liang as a son-in-law, or even call him father-in-law, if A'Liang's boasts were true.Chapter 90
* When sparring with Chen Ping'an on Go Table Mountain, Zhu He suppressed his strength to the third tier. The fight helped Chen Ping'an discover three acupoints that the "fire dragon" in his body dared not enter.
* Chen Ping'an often compared A'Liang to Zhu He, to A'Liang's great annoyance.
* One later passage describes Zhu He as having left Jewel Small World as a fourth-tier martial artist, contradicting the many passages that call him a fifth-tier martial artist.

== References ==
