pages.title: Zhu Lian
pages.content:
{{Character |header1=Zhu Lian |Aliases=Martial Arts Maniac
Old Cook |Vital_status=Alive |Gender=Male |Species=Human |Occupation=Senior steward of Downtrodden Mountain
Cook |Current_affiliation(s)=[[Downtrodden Mountain]] |Former_affiliation(s)=[[Lotus Flower Blessed Land]] |Continent=[[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]] |Cultivation_rank=Far Roaming Tier (pure martial artist) |Novel=Chapter 314 }} ==Appearance== Zhu Lian appears as a short, skinny, hunchbacked old man who usually walks with his hands clasped behind his back and his eyes squinted into a smile, looking much like an ordinary old man from the marketplace.Chapter 328 (1) He remains hunched even when riding a horse, and of Chen Ping'an's four companions from the picture scrolls he is the one who looks most like a humble servant. On Downtrodden Mountain he is often seen in an apron, wiping his hands as he comes out of the kitchen. This was not always his look. Before going mad in the Lotus Flower Blessed Land, Zhu Lian was known as a refined young master who could put otherworldly immortals to shame.Chapter 389 (2) He boasts that countless women of the blessed land spent their lives lovesick after a single glance at his portrait.Chapter 465 (2) When asked why he keeps his current appearance, he explains that he benefited too much from his looks in his hometown and grew tired of it, and that now he is a "senior citizen", he should act the part.Chapter 482 (2) Cen Yuanji, who reveres him, thinks that although he isn't very handsome now, he must have been very popular with women in his prime. ==Personality== Zhu Lian always wears a faint, kindly smile, yet he is the man who once almost turned the cultivation world of the Lotus Flower Blessed Land upside down.Chapter 333 (2) He is easy-going, humorous and shameless, constantly flattering Chen Ping'an, calling himself "this old servant", and making lecherous remarks that earn him the disgust of Shi Rou and many female deities. He openly declares that he wants to capture the heart of a beautiful woman. He reads racy romance novels, writes his own drafts about chivalrous heroines, and covers the walls of his residence with portraits of beautiful women he has seen.Chapter 478 Yet when Zheng Dafeng asks whether he ever truly loved anyone, he answers seriously that his feelings were always earnest, but that matters of his nation and the martial world kept him from controlling his own fate, and that it is all in the past.Chapter 462 (1) Beneath the clowning lie great insight and loyalty. Cui Dongshan judges him the one with the broadest outlook and highest ambition of the four picture-scroll people: adaptable, fond of good food, and the most likely to become truly loyal to Chen Ping'an.Chapter 387 (2) He is protective of Pei Qian and Cen Yuanji, a gentle guiding senior to the young people of Downtrodden Mountain, and willing to stand his ground against Chen Ping'an when he thinks his young master is wrong. When Pei Qian accuses him of being a fence-sitter, he describes his own shifts in loyalty as "adjusting to the circumstances like a wise and handsome individual". He is also more capable than he lets on. He pretended to be a poor Go player while watching Sui Youbian and Lu Baixiang play, but is in fact an extraordinary player.Chapter 467 (1) He is an excellent cook, earning the nickname "Old Cook" from Pei Qian, and his cursive calligraphy astonishes onlookers who assumed he was a mere servant. ==Background== Zhu Lian came from a truly wealthy clan in the Lotus Flower Blessed Land.Chapter 368 (4) He became known as the '''Martial Arts Maniac''', the strongest person in the blessed land for several decades before Ding Ying.Chapter 314 (2) He practised external martial arts, intending to turn inward only after reaching the pinnacle, and tried to kill the nine other superior grandmasters of his generation. In that brutal battle, he grew stronger and deadlier the more wounded he became.Chapter 348 He was ultimately killed by Ding Ying, who took his silver-coloured lotus flower hat. Ding Ying never spoke of that battle afterwards. Zhu Lian later remarks that Ding Ying was the most talented martial artist he ever met, and jokes that he should have killed him with a single punch back then.Chapter 396 (1) After the fall of the blessed land, Zhu Lian was one of the four legendary figures preserved in picture scrolls that Chen Ping'an obtained, along with Wei Xian, Lu Baixiang and Sui Youbian. Because of the death he suffered, the old Daoist priest's rules cap his potential at the tenth tier.Chapter 367 (1) Adapting to the Majestic World, he reaches the Far Roaming Tier quickly, making him the strongest of the four. Chen Ping'an considers his choice of a "shortcut" correct.Chapter 459 ==Trivia== * He introduces himself to the water goddess Xiao Luan as "Little Zhu, Zhu as in young and handsome". * He once told Pei Qian that when she grew up she would ward off evil spirits better than a door god, meaning she would be so ugly that ghosts would fear her. * Wei Bo felt that if he had met Zhu Lian years earlier, a long-held knot in his heart would have been untied much sooner. * He became the senior steward of Downtrodden Mountain, where Chen Ruchu, the "young steward", sometimes manages even him. * He deliberately provokes Cui Cheng so that he too can receive the old master's beatings. * After Cui Cheng's death, Zhu Lian could have claimed half of Cui Cheng's scattered martial fortune, but he deliberately declined it. ==References== [[Category:Alive]] [[Category:Male]]

pages.title: Zhu Lu
pages.content:
{{Character
|header1=Zhu Lu
|image1=Zhu Lu.png
|Vital_status=Alive
|Gender=Female
|Species=Human
|Relatives=[[Zhu He]] (father)
|Allies=Li Baozhen
|Enemie(s)=[[Chen Ping An]]
|Occupation=Hereditary maidservant of the Li Clan
|Current_affiliation(s)=Li Clan of Fortune Street
|Continent=[[Eastern Treasured Vial Continent]]
|Cultivation_rank=Second Tier (martial artist)
|Novel= Chapter 87
|Love_interest(s)=[[Li Baozhen]] (one-sided)}}


'''Zhu Lu''' is a young female martial artist and a hereditary maidservant of the Li Clan of [[Fortune Street]]. She is the daughter of the fifth-tier martial artist [[Zhu He]]. Assigned with her father to protect [[Li Baoping]] on the journey to [[Mountain Cliff Academy]], she grows increasingly hostile towards [[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]]. At Pillow Relay Station, she attempts to assassinate him on the secret instructions of Li Baoping's second brother, [[Li Baozhen]], whom she loves.

Proud, talented and sharp-witted, but cowardly in real danger and blinded by ambition and infatuation, she is one of the people Chen Ping'an detests most. He looks back on her as the person who first taught him the sinister subtleties of the human heart after he left the small town.

== Appearance ==
Zhu Lu is described as a pretty young woman. Her eyes closely resemble her mother's, which is why her father can rarely bring himself to scold her harshly. When she wishes, she can appear like a friendly neighbourhood girl with a dazzling smile.

== Personality ==
Zhu Lu is proud, haughty and quick to look down on others. She sneers at A'Liang as a braggart, calls Chen Ping'an a monkey unworthy of his jade hairpin, mocks Li Huai's poverty and his parents, and initially refuses Chen Ping'an's straw sandals as crude. She is fiercely protective of Li Baoping and her father, but in a crisis she freezes with fear and acts on impulse.

She is also highly intelligent and ambitious. She longs to escape her hereditary servant status and reach the heights of martial arts. When manipulated by Li Baozhen with promises of freedom and a noble future, she becomes completely single-minded and feels no guilt at all. The Yin god escorting the group judges that she would be an impressive prodigy in any ordinary force, but is inferior in every way to the children she travels with. Cui Chan calls her "foolish and evil at the same time", while Chen Ping'an later reflects that, setting aside good and evil, she had a very clear goal and an extremely resolute mind.

== Background ==
Zhu Lu was born into a family that has served the Li Clan for generations. The Li Clan treats its servants generously, and the elders of the manor joked that Zhu Lu was a maidservant living the life of a young mistress. She trained in martial arts under her father from childhood. The Li patriarch believed she had the aptitude to reach the seventh tier, and some expected her to surpass her father.Chapter 92 (1)

She was very close to the young Li Baoping, who followed her around, watched her practise walking on tall wooden poles, and absorbed her stories about martial arts. However, Zhu Lu stumbled at the bottleneck of the second tier. Twice her training went badly wrong, leaving her bedridden. The first time, she was frail for nearly half a year. The second time, Li Baoping saw her rolling on her bed in agony.Chapter 87 (2) She was also infatuated with Li Baozhen, Li Baoping's second brother, a fact the story later confirms.

She is also the maidservant whom Chen Ping'an struck with roof tiles and a punch when he infiltrated the Li Clan manor, as Chen Ping'an himself later suspects.Chapter 48Chapter 87 (1)

== Plot ==

=== Journey Begins ===
Zhu He and Zhu Lu join Chen Ping'an and Li Baoping on the road south. Zhu Lu is eager for her first real fight and openly scornful of A'Liang's boasting. She refuses A'Liang's offers to teach her swordsmanship and spits at him in disgust, and she is homesick and moody the further they travel.

She objects furiously when A'Liang suggests staying in [[Red Candle Town]], calling Chen Ping'an a disgrace who would shame all scholars if he were one. On the muddy slopes of [[Go Table Mountain]], she reluctantly accepts the straw sandals she had scorned, then splatters Li Huai with mud. When he breaks down in tears, she sneers that he is learning to extort others just like his parents.Chapter 97

=== Go Table Mountain ===
When the black and white pythons attack, Zhu Lu, despite being at the peak of the second tier, is paralysed with fear. The white python fixes its gaze on her and lunges to swallow her, and she is saved only because Chen Ping'an leaps from the black python's back and severs the white python's wing.Chapter 98 Even then she stays rooted to the spot until Li Huai screams at her to run.

The trapped mountain lord, Wei Bo, then begs a child to stamp out the 岳 talisman Zhu He had used to summon him. Chen Ping'an shouts at Zhu Lu not to do it, warning that the mountain lord is likely in league with the pythons. Sobbing that no one else cares about her father, she stamps it out anyway, freeing Wei Bo, who promptly reveals his treachery.Chapter 99 After A'Liang arrives and resolves the crisis, she screams at him to kill the mountain lord and the pythons. When her father gently suggests she was wrong, she asks whether she would still be his daughter if she had done nothing. Zhu He cannot bring himself to criticise her.Chapter 100 (1)

When Wei Bo's treasures are shared out, Zhu Lu initially refuses the "contemptuous handout" until her father drags her over. Zhu He then chooses the Purple Qi Guide for her, a martial manual that could carry her to the fifth tier, and a Hero's Gall Pill from [[True Martial Mountain]] that could push her to the sixth.Chapter 104

=== Pillow Relay Station ===
In Red Candle Town, a letter from Li Baozhen to Li Baoping mentions Zhu Lu, and she happily asks to take it away to read. In private, she grumbles to her father that Lin Shouyi and Li Huai have no right to treat Li Baoping as an equal, and tells him that the Second Young Master has promised a way for them to escape their servant status once they reach the capital.Chapter 107

Zhu Lu then buys three skewers of tanghulu, asks her father to fetch Chen Ping'an, and greets him in a corridor with a shy smile. She feints a punch and tries to drive the bamboo skewers into his heart, but Chen Ping'an seizes her throat and beats her down. Bleeding and pinned under his foot, she proudly explains that she found a hidden message in Li Baozhen's letter: the eldest grandson of the Chen Clan had won an honorary title, hinting that she could do the same by killing Chen Ping'an. Chen Ping'an realises she is deliberately baiting him into attacking her, to force Zhu He to choose between killing him and watching his daughter die.Chapter 109

Zhu He apologises to Chen Ping'an, but Chen Ping'an prepares to use one of the hidden wisps of sword qi in his body against him. A'Liang intervenes. He forces father and daughter to return the Hero's Gall Pill, the Purple Qi Guide and the Li Clan's talismans, then asks Zhu Lu which of the two she wants to live. Chen Ping'an insists that she must die, but when he strikes, his fist opens into a slap across her face. A'Liang deals with the pair, and they leave the relay station.Chapter 110

Chen Ping'an tells Li Baoping the truth, believing she needs to know what her clan's people have done. He explains that he forgave Zhu Lu's actions on Go Table Mountain as panic for her father, but not this. Li Baoping is deeply hurt, and Li Huai guesses that Zhu Lu acted for love of Li Baozhen.

=== Aftermath ===
Back in the small town, Li Baozhen suggests to his father, Li Hong, that Zhu He and Zhu Lu be removed from the Li Clan's hereditary servant registry and made commoners. This was the very reward he had dangled before them, and Li Hong complains that his second son acted first and asked later.Chapter 127 Li Xisheng, Li Baozhen's elder brother, later apologises to Chen Ping'an on his brother's behalf.

Years later, Li Baozhen reveals that Zhu Lu found him in the Great Li capital, weeping uncontrollably. He was so angry that she had failed such a "simple task", which cost him a scolding from the empress and his chance to rise in the imperial court, that he nearly killed her with a single slap.Chapter 397 (2) It is also revealed that she only barely advanced to the next martial tier by relying on medicinal ointments from the Yang Family Medicine Shop.Chapter 468 (2)

Chen Ping'an often recalls her as he matures. She comes to mind when he meets arrogant daughters of reasonable fathers, and when he warns a young woman named Liu Qingqing that a lover's affection may hide ulterior motives.

== Abilities ==

* '''Martial arts:''' peak of the second tier for most of the story, later reaching the next tier with the help of medicines. Her speed and agility are notable for her tier.
* '''Training:''' trained by her father, a skilled instructor; practised walking on high poles and bathing in medicinal concoctions.
* '''Intellect:''' sharp-witted and resourceful. She decoded Li Baozhen's hidden message after reading the letter only twice, and planned an assassination that left a way out for herself.

== Trivia ==

* 鹿 (lù) means deer.
* Even Zhu Lu had to concede that Wei Bo in his true form was the very picture of a handsome young god, though her memory of his cowardly old-man form coloured her opinion of him.
* Li Baoping's earliest ideas about martial artists and cultivators came from Zhu Lu's stories.
* She possessed a secret martial manual from the Go Table Mountain treasures, a Hero's Gall Pill from True Martial Mountain, and Li Clan talismans, all of which A'Liang confiscated.

== References ==

pages.title: Zuo You
pages.content:
{{Character |header1 = Zuo You |Aliases = Swordsman Zuo
Great sword immortal |Vital_status = Alive |Gender = Male |Species = Human |Master(s) = [[Scholarly Sage]] |Friend(s) = [[A'Liang]] |Allies = [[Qi Jingchun]] (junior brother)
[[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]] (junior brother)
[[Wei Jin]] |Enemie(s) = [[Du Mao]] |Occupation = Swordsman |Current_affiliation(s) = [[Sword Qi Great Wall]] |Cultivation_rank = Great sword immortal |Novel = Chapter 265 }} {{Spoilers}} '''Zuo You''' is the second disciple of the [[Scholarly Sage]], the senior brother of [[Qi Jingchun]], and, initiallty reluctantly, of [[Chen Ping An|Chen Ping'an]]. A swordsman in Confucian robes who cares nothing for debate, he is widely regarded as having perhaps the finest swordsmanship under the heavens. Even the Ascension Tier [[Du Mao]] praises him, and the swordsmen of [[Northern Complete Reed Continent]] revere him. He spent more than a century wandering the seas, far from the human world. He refused both his teacher's request to protect Qi Jingchun and Qi Jingchun's request to be Chen Ping'an's Dao guardian. Still, he steps in when he sees his junior brother being bullied, and his sword strikes at the Flood Dragon Trench and against Du Mao are among the most memorable in the story. == Appearance == Zuo You wears azure Confucian robes and carries a sword at his waist. He looks nothing like a scholar, with a temperament neither as elegant as Qi Jingchun's nor as friendly as A'Liang's. == Personality == Zuo You is blunt, stubborn and short-tempered. He dislikes speaking reason, asking what the point of a sword would be if one always had to reason with others. As a senior brother, he believes that lecturing a junior brother needs no further justification. As a boy, he found his teacher's boasting and Qi Jingchun's rapid page-turning the two most annoying things in the world. He is awkward around women, and finds a woman's heart harder to understand than his master's teachings. Despite this, he is fundamentally a good and principled person. He does not attack those who leave him alone, and he refuses to take lives without cause. During his entire assault on Parasol Leaf Sect, he does not kill a single person. The Scholarly Sage calls him the most balanced of his disciples, patient and focused, and secretly the one most afraid of loneliness, who never stopped thinking of his teacher and fellow disciples while wandering the seas.Chapter 450 (2) He once told Chen Ping'an that cultivators can no longer really be considered human, but have become something else.Chapter 278 (1) == Background == Zuo You was the Scholarly Sage's second disciple. In their impoverished days in a small alley on the Middle Earth Divine Continent, the Scholarly Sage put him in charge of their finances, since he managed money far better than his teacher. He would sneak over the wall at night and bring back snacks for the young Qi Jingchun. He was a late bloomer who advocated walking the path of the Great Dao alone. He began learning the sword late, yet progressed so astonishingly quickly that the Scholarly Sage feared he might become the first fourteenth-tier sword cultivator in thousands of years.Chapter 402 (1) Once, when a sage wronged their teacher, Zuo You secretly beat the sage up, then admitted it and went to apologise to his teacher. The Scholarly Sage scolded him in public and took him to apologise, but privately complained that he had hit the sage too lightly. After his teacher lost the battle between third and fourth, Zuo You stayed by his side, cheerful and unbothered, as he entered the Forest of Virtue. He then distanced himself from the mortal world and set off alone to sea. Over the following century, he shattered the sword hearts of many talented young swordsmen from every continent who came to challenge him, including Cao Jun of Southern Whirl Continent.Chapter 364 (3) The swordsman Ji Yue of [[Northern Complete Reed Continent]] was the first from that continent to seek him out at sea, and could not withstand even a single strike.Chapter 516 (3) == Plot == === The Flood Dragon Trench === While Chen Ping'an is crossing the sea on Osmanthus Island, a swordsman flies towards the Flood Dragon Trench, destroying a sect's rain god statue along the way when he is told to detour. From three to four hundred kilometres away he flicks his wrist, and sword qi pours down from the heavens into the trench like waterfalls. The elderly golden flood dragon threatening Chen Ping'an is pierced through all three hundred of its acupoints. Zuo You tells Chen Ping'an that he refused Qi Jingchun's request to be his Dao guardian, just as he once refused to protect Qi Jingchun, but that it isn't right for others to bully someone so young. He then introduces himself as "Little Qi's senior brother... and your senior brother, too".Chapter 265 He warns Chen Ping'an to cultivate earnestly and not disappoint Little Qi, or he will come to cause trouble, and declares that however strong Chen Ping'an becomes, Zuo You can still deal with him with a single slash. When a Daoist disciple of the Dao Ancestor's second disciple appears as a 300-metre golden Dao Manifestation to challenge him, Zuo You mocks him and shatters the manifestation instantly with a column of sword qi wider than Osmanthus Island. He leaves Chen Ping'an the flood dragon's golden robe, its whiskers and its pill-like jewel.Chapter 266 (1) === Parasol Leaf Continent === On Parasol Leaf Continent, Zuo You slays a great demon fleeing from Planchette Writing Sect with a single slash simply because he is in a foul mood, depriving a Parasol Leaf Sect cultivator of the kill.Chapter 356 (2) Chen Ping'an later tells Jiang Shangzhen that Zuo You admitted his sword intent is inferior to A'Liang's but his swordsmanship superior. He adds that Zuo You only accepted him as junior brother with extreme reluctance.Chapter 359 (2) When the Ascension Tier Du Mao of Parasol Leaf Sect attacks Chen Ping'an and Zheng Dafeng at Old Dragon City, partly hoping to lure Zuo You out, Zuo You does not come. Afterwards, the Scholarly Sage finds him and slaps him repeatedly for having vanished for so long and cared so little for everyone else. Zuo You takes the beating in silence, then asks his teacher what he should do, and flies off over the sea.Chapter 366 (2) He descends on Parasol Leaf Sect and calmly announces, as if he were a student come to learn, that his master told him to come and curse their ancestors in the most vulgar terms.Chapter 367 (3) For days he methodically destroys the sect's mountain and river fortune, waiting for Du Mao to come out. He does not kill anyone. When his sword qi frightens a young woman, he scratches his head in embarrassment, and he releases the pressure on a stubborn young swordsman who glares at him. He warns the sect that Du Mao will lead them to ruin.Chapter 368 (2) Zuo You believes there are only two swords at the pinnacle of the world: the one a Middle Earth scholar used to slice Yellow River Small World apart, and his own. Out at sea, the Scholarly Sage furiously asks why he did not use the rift to leave the world. Zuo You lowers his head without answering. His teacher sighs and tells him to go to Stalactite Mountain and the Sword Qi Great Wall, as he has always wanted. Zuo You bows in farewell, walks away step by step rather than flying, and tells his teacher that he accepted a great disciple in their junior brother.Chapter 369 (3) === Reputation === On Northern Complete Reed Continent, the swordsmen revere Zuo You for never wasting words, for having a temper shorter even than theirs, and for treating an Ascension Tier cultivator and a mortal alike. Zhu Quan of Wood Garment Mountain greatly admires him.Chapter 513 (1) == Abilities == * '''Swordsmanship:''' widely considered the best in the world. Zuo You himself says his sword intent is inferior to A'Liang's but his swordsmanship superior. * '''Sword qi:''' able to pour sword qi into the Flood Dragon Trench from hundreds of kilometres away, shatter a 300-metre Dao Manifestation instantly, and cut an Ascension Tier manifestation in half with a single languid slash. * '''Control:''' His sword qi can kill the flood dragons of an entire trench while leaving Chen Ping'an and the elderly flood dragon untouched, and he can destroy a sect's fortune without taking a single life. * '''Learning:''' Although he disliked studying, he is still more learned than most academies' noble scholars, thanks to the books his teacher forced on him. == Trivia == * Zuo You's name (左右) literally means "left and right". * The Burial River water goddess, a fan of the Scholarly Sage's lineage, calls his name "incredibly domineering". == References == [[Category:Characters]] [[Category:Male]] [[Category:Alive]]

templates.title: Template:Synopsis
templates.content:
{{Header |header = About the Series |content = A world of endless wonder, where myths and legends breathe. This is my journey—as a swordsman, as a dreamer. [[File:Poster 剑来动画 Jian Lai Chinese Donghua Animation Bilal My Art Collection.jpg|300px|left|link=]] '''Welcome to the Sword of Coming Wiki''', an open and collaborative platform dedicated to becoming a comprehensive English-language encyclopedia on everything related to '''[[Donghua|Sword of Coming]]'''!

Epic Tale

Chen Ping’an had grown up his entire life in a mundane little town, leading an impoverished yet peaceful existence. However, the arrival of a group of outsiders quickly turned his mundane life on its head. Before long, all types of strange occurrences were taking place in the town, and Chen Ping’an was made to realize that things are not what they seem. As it turned out, the stories of immortal cultivators, mighty dragons, and unfathomably powerful beings that had always been told in the town as folklore were all true, and Chen Ping’an was inadvertently swept up into this world that he had no business being a part of. Having been forced onto a path that Chen Ping’an had never thought he would walk, he commences his journey to the top… ''Please note that viewer discretion is advised when navigating this wiki, as it may contain '''unmarked spoilers''' that could reveal crucial plot details.'' extra_pages.title: Sword of Coming Wiki:Wiki rules
extra_pages.content:
Below is a suggested set of rules to follow when editing this wiki. Administrators of this wiki should read these rules and adapt them as necessary.


# '''Keep it civil''': Do not make personal attacks on other people. If you need to criticize another user’s argument, do so without attacking them as a person. Do not use bigoted language, including slurs which degrade another person or group of people based on gender, race, sexual orientation, nationality, religion, etc.
# '''Be a productive member of the wiki''': Contribute to the wiki in line with the established processes and conventions. Need help? Ask an [[Special:ListUsers/sysop|administrator]]! Disrupting the wiki with “edit warring” over differing opinions of a topic with another user or group of users is not productive.
# '''Do not engage in excessive self-promotion''': The wiki is a collaborative community resource for the topic at hand. It is NOT a free place to advertise your related website, YouTube channel, blog, social media account, etc. Have a question about whether your link would be welcome? Ask an administrator!
# '''Do not harass other users''': If somebody asks you to stop posting certain content on their wall, respect their wishes. It is their wall.
# '''Do follow community guidelines for formatting''': When a community has established formatting, it’s important to adhere to that, especially when spoiler content is involved.

extra_pages.title: User blog:RyūSeongX/Season 2 Announcement
extra_pages.content:
[[File:Season 2 Anouncement.webp|center|frameless|511x511px]]
'''Official Jian Lai ( GTL) :A letter from the animation creator'''
Life is a long journey. If you can be invincible with a sword and not be afraid of wind and rain, then how can such a life be ordinary? The second season of the animation is now in preparation, much earlier than we had planned, and we hope it can be achieved as we wish. The second season will have more adapted chapters than the first season, and the single episode will be longer. Let me tell you a little secret here, the first theatrical version that has been started is about the story of the Sword Qi Great Wall. "Swords come!" is a very encouraging phrase. I hope that when you encounter difficulties, you can encourage yourself first and don't be discouraged. A gentleman sits and discusses the truth, while a young man should get up and act. Let's go!

extra_pages.title: User blog:RyūSeongX/Season 2 Officially Released
extra_pages.content:
'''Jian Lai Season 2 Officially Released — New Journey Begins!'''
[[File:Season 2 preview.jpg|center|frameless|986x986px]] After months of excitement and anticipation, Season 2 of Jian Lai has officially premiered! The second season of this popular Chinese donghua adaptation of Feng Huo Xi Zhu Hou’s Jian Lai novel was released on December 25, 2025, exclusively on Tencent Video.
This new season continues the story from the conclusion of Season 1, following Chen Ping-an and his companions as they embark on a long and perilous journey south. Season 2 focuses heavily on Chen Ping-an’s travels with Li Bao-ping and others as they head toward the Daxiu cliffside academy, facing dangers such as the Dali cavalry’s attacks, demon spirits, and old adversaries along the way.
In the lead-up to the premiere, the official final trailer showcased intense action moments, including Chen Ping-an’s sword qi against a giant serpent and strategic confrontations, reinforcing the season’s themes of growth, challenge, and martial spirit.
The full season consists of 26 episodes and is being released weekly on Tencent Video. Leading up to launch, the series broke records with over 800 million reservations on the platform, indicating overwhelming fan enthusiasm and making it one of the most anticipated donghua releases of 2025.
Fans can now tune in to witness new character developments, expanded world-building, and more breathtaking cultivation battles as Jian Lai continues to unfold its epic tale of swordplay, honor, and personal transformation.
[[Category:Blog posts]]
